scope: Selected foundational sources, the main general KLS bound milestones, and the connected moment-map, slicing and thin-shell developments through July 2026; not an exhaustive bibliography or a paper-by-paper proof verification; the October 2026 Bizeul–Klartag–Lehec preprint is added after the cutoff as the pinned current formalization target.

groups.title: Analytic foundations and selected local coverage
General KLS bounds and stochastic localization

papers.title: Convex measures on locally convex spaces
papers.result: Convex/log-concave measures, inner measure and density representation on the affine support.
papers.remaining: The locally convex-space theory and the other convexity parameters are outside our finite-dimensional log-concave scope.

local_results.scope: Compact/Borel definitions with inner measure
Finite-dimensional intrinsic density representation

papers.title: Isoperimetric problems for convex bodies and a localization lemma
papers.locator: Theorem 5.1 (Main Theorem); needle reduction of Section 2
papers.result: For every convex body K, ψ(K) ≥ ln 2 / M₁(K), with M₁ the mean distance to the centroid; for isotropic bodies this is the dimension-scale bound ψₙ = O(n^(1/2)). States the KLS conjecture. The localization lemma is quoted from Lovász–Simonovits (1993) and extended to exponential needles.
papers.remaining: No statement of the paper is formalized. The localization lemma (Lemma 2.1) is only cited, so a Lean proof needs Lovász–Simonovits (1993) or a later proof. The paper proves no Poincaré or covariance bound; with the local Cheeger inequality, Theorem 5.1 would give C_P ≤ (16 / ln² 2) E‖X − EX‖² for convex bodies, the factor 2 coming from the product denominator, once the paper's boundary measure is matched with the local outer Minkowski content.

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: Convex bodies in R^n with Lebesgue (uniform) measure; the isoperimetric coefficient ψ(K) uses the product denominator vol(S)·vol(K∖S)/vol(K) of (1.1), within a factor 2 of the min-denominator form (1.2).
lemma_map.omitted: Remark 2.8 is a normalization comment. The paper proves no Poincaré or trace-of-covariance bound; those appear in later literature.

items.label: Localization lemma
items.statement: For lower semicontinuous integrable g, h on R^n with positive integrals, some needle (segment with a linear weight to the power n−1) has positive g- and h-integrals.
items.note: Cited from Lovász–Simonovits (1993); its proof is not in this paper.

items.label: Four-function needle reduction
items.statement: For nonnegative continuous f1..f4 and α, β > 0, an inequality between products of integral powers holds on every convex body iff it holds on every needle.

items.label: Semicontinuous extension
items.statement: Corollary 2.2 extends to upper semicontinuous f1, f2 and lower semicontinuous f3, f4.

items.label: Needle with an equality constraint
items.statement: On a bounded open convex T, if ∫g > 0 and ∫h = 0 for bounded lower semicontinuous g and continuous h, some needle in T has positive g-integral and zero h-integral.

items.label: Non-strict version
items.statement: Strict inequalities in Corollary 2.4 may be replaced by non-strict ones.

items.label: One-dimensional log-concave reduction
items.statement: On an interval, a four-function inequality holds for every log-concave weight iff it holds for every exponential weight on every subinterval.

items.label: Exponential needles
items.statement: For nonnegative continuous f1..f4 on R^n, the four-function inequality holds for every compactly supported log-concave F iff it holds on every exponential needle.

items.label: Reverse Hölder for linear functions
items.statement: For 0 < p < q there is C(p, q), independent of n and K, with ‖f‖_q ≤ C(p, q)‖f‖_p for every linear f on a convex body K.

items.label: Isotropic body contains and is contained in balls
items.statement: An isotropic convex body satisfies √((n+2)/n) B ⊆ K ⊆ √(n(n+2)) B.

items.label: Isoperimetric coefficient bound
items.statement: For every convex body K, ψ(K) ≥ ln 2 / M₁(K), where M₁ is the mean distance to the centroid.
items.note: Convex bodies only; the later log-concave version is quoted as Theorem 5.11 of Milman (2009).

items.label: Three-set partition form
items.statement: If K = K1 ∪ K2 ∪ K3 with dist(K1, K2) ≥ ε > 0, then ε·vol(K1)·vol(K2) ≤ vol(K)·vol(K3)·M₁(K)/ln 2.

items.label: Bound by the mean chord length
items.statement: ψ(K) ≥ 1/χ(K), where χ(K) averages the longest chord of K centred at each point.

items.label: KLS conjecture
items.statement: ψ(K) is of order 1/√a(K), where a(K) is the largest eigenvalue of the inertia matrix.
items.note: The repository states a covariance-normalized Poincaré version for log-concave laws (KLS.Conjecture); it is not a literal form of this convex-body conjecture.

items.label: Upper bound by hyperplane cuts
items.statement: ψ(K) ≤ 10/√a(K) for every convex body K.

items.label: Hyperplane cut through the centroid
items.statement: For b(K) = 0 and a unit vector u, the two halves of K cut by u^⊥ satisfy a product-volume bound against the section area and β = E(u·x)².

papers.title: Isoperimetric and analytic inequalities for log-concave probability measures
papers.result: Cheeger/Poincaré inequalities for log-concave laws; the one-dimensional comparison yields C_P ≤ 12 Var.
papers.remaining: Our one-dimensional proof uses a different analytic argument. The paper’s general isoperimetric theory is not fully formalized.

local_results.scope: One-dimensional upper bound, now strengthened locally to 4 Var; the independent 12 Var proof is retained

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: Absolutely continuous log-concave probability measures on R^n; μ⁺ is the Minkowski boundary measure; Is(μ) is the min-denominator Cheeger constant h, λ₁ = 1/C_P is the spectral gap and ρ the log-Sobolev constant.
lemma_map.omitted: The displayed consequences (1.8), (2.7), (2.8) and (2.10) are recorded with the statements they follow from.

items.label: Perimeter, entropy and ball mass
items.statement: For log-concave μ on R^n, every measurable A, x₀ and r > 0: 2rμ⁺(A) ≥ μ(A)log(1/μ(A)) + (1 − μ(A))log(1/(1 − μ(A))) + log μ{|x − x₀| ≤ r}.

items.label: Cheeger bound by the L² radius
items.statement: Is(μ) ≥ 1/(K‖|x − x₀|‖_{L²(μ)}) with x₀ the barycenter and K universal; hence λ₁ ≥ 1/(4K²‖|x − x₀|‖²_{L²}) by Cheeger.
items.note: The proof gives Is(μ) ≥ 1/(6r) with r the 2/3-quantile of |x − x₀| (3.3).

items.label: Gaussian isoperimetry, log-Sobolev and Gaussian moments
items.statement: For log-concave μ, Gaussian-type isoperimetry, a log-Sobolev inequality and ∫exp(ε|x|²)dμ < ∞ are equivalent, with ρ ≥ 1/(K‖|x − x₀|‖²_ψ) for ψ(u) = exp(u²) − 1.

items.label: Functional form of Theorem 1.1
items.statement: For locally Lipschitz f with values in [0, 1] and a symmetric convex body B: 2∫‖∇f‖_{B°}dμ ≥ Ent(f) + Ent(1 − f) + log μ(B(x₀)).
items.note: Proved by the Prékopa–Leindler inequality.

items.label: Measures supported in a ball
items.statement: If μ is concentrated in a ball of radius r, then 2r∫|∇f|dμ ≥ Ent(f) + Ent(1 − f) and 2rμ⁺(A) ≥ μ(A)log(1/μ(A)) + (1 − μ(A))log(1/(1 − μ(A))); hence Is(μ) ≥ log 2/r and λ₁ ≥ log²2/(4r²).

items.label: Log-Sobolev versus spectral gap in a ball
items.statement: If μ is concentrated in a ball of radius r, then λ₁/(1 + 2r√λ₁) ≤ ρ ≤ λ₁, so ρ ≥ 1/(10r²).

items.label: Borell's lemma
items.statement: For symmetric convex B with θ = μ(B) > 1/2 and t ≥ 1: 1 − μ(tB) ≤ (1 − θ)((1 − θ)/θ)^((t−1)/2).
items.note: For every log-concave law on a finite-dimensional real normed space. The Lean statement assumes B measurable, which the paper's μ(B) presupposes (a convex set need not be Borel).

items.label: Functional Gaussian isoperimetry
items.statement: If μ⁺(A) ≥ cI(μ(A)) for the Gaussian isoperimetric function I, then c[I(∫f) − ∫I(f)] ≤ ∫|∇f| for locally Lipschitz f with values in [0, 1].

items.label: Gaussian isoperimetry gives log-Sobolev
items.statement: Inequality (3.10) implies (c²/2)Ent(f²) ≤ ∫|∇f|² dμ.

items.label: Cheeger constant on the line
items.statement: For log-concave μ on R: 1/(3Var) ≤ Is²(μ) ≤ 2/Var, with equality cases the uniform and two-sided exponential laws; Is(μ) = 2f(m) at the median.
items.note: Formalized: Is(μ) = 2f(m) at a median, and the lower bound 1/(3 Var) ≤ Is² as Is⁻² ≤ 3 Var for every log-concave law on the line. Not formalized: the upper bound Is² ≤ 2/Var and the equality cases.

items.label: Hensley-type section ratio
items.statement: For a convex body satisfying the isotropy condition, central sections by hyperplanes cutting B into equal volumes have ratio at most √6.

items.label: Spectral gap on the line
items.statement: For log-concave μ on R: 1/(12 Var) ≤ λ₁ ≤ 1/Var, i.e. Var ≤ C_P ≤ 12 Var.
items.note: Sharper upper constant C_P ≤ 4 Var, proved by a different argument that does not use Proposition 4.1; the paper's 12 Var follows as a corollary, and Var ≤ C_P is the linear test.

items.label: Log-Sobolev constant on the line
items.statement: For log-concave μ on R: 1/(24‖ξ − Eξ‖²_ψ) ≤ ρ ≤ 8/(3‖ξ − Eξ‖²_ψ) with ψ(x) = exp(x²) − 1.

items.label: Cheeger bound for norms
items.statement: For a random vector X with log-concave law in a normed space, Is(μ_X) ≥ 1/(6r) with r the 2/3-quantile of ‖X‖, where μ_X is the law of ‖X‖.

items.label: Small-ball monotonicity
items.statement: With F(t) = P(‖X‖ ≤ t), the function F(t)/t^(1/(2e)) is nondecreasing where 0 < F(t) ≤ e/(e + 1).

papers.title: On the role of convexity in isoperimetry, spectral gap and concentration
papers.result: Under convexity, isoperimetry, spectral gap and concentration control one another up to universal constants.
papers.remaining: The full equivalence remains open locally; our forward infimum comparison is supporting infrastructure, not this theorem.

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: Metric probability spaces; "convexity assumptions" mean total-variation limits of weighted Riemannian manifolds with Ric + Hess ψ ≥ 0. D_Che is the min-denominator Cheeger constant h and D_Poin = 1/√C_P, so D_Poin ≥ D_Che/2 is C_P ≤ 4Ψ². Attributed statements are quoted from the cited authors.
lemma_map.omitted: Remarks 3.3, 4.4, 5.13, 6.3 and 6.7 are expository; the unnumbered regularity theorems for isoperimetric minimizers in the appendix are quoted background.

items.label: Cheeger constant D_Che
items.statement: Best D with Ĩ(t) ≥ D t on [0, 1/2], where Ĩ is the isoperimetric profile.
items.note: Finite-dimensional laws on their affine support, with outer Minkowski content.

items.label: Poincaré constant D_Poin
items.statement: Best D with D‖f − Ef‖₂ ≤ ‖|∇f|‖₂ for Lipschitz-on-balls f.
items.note: Stored as C_P = D_Poin^(−2) for finite-dimensional laws.

items.label: Exponential concentration D_Exp
items.statement: Best D with μ(|f − Ef| ≥ t) ≤ e·exp(−Dt) for 1-Lipschitz f.

items.label: First-moment concentration D_FM
items.statement: Best D with ‖f − Ef‖₁ ≤ 1/D for 1-Lipschitz f.

items.label: Cheeger inequality
items.statement: D_Poin ≥ D_Che/2.
items.note: Proved as C_P ≤ 4Ψ² for finite-dimensional log-concave laws; the paper states it on general metric probability spaces.

items.label: Poincaré implies exponential concentration
items.statement: D_Exp ≥ c·D_Poin for a universal c.

items.label: Buser inequality on closed manifolds
items.statement: For uniform measure on a closed manifold with Ric ≥ 0, D_Che ≥ c·D_Poin.

items.label: Buser–Ledoux inequality
items.statement: Under smooth convexity assumptions, D_Che ≥ c·D_Poin.
items.note: Euclidean case only, as Ψ² ≤ π C_P, i.e. c = 1/√π, for every finite-dimensional log-concave law including nonsmooth ones; weighted manifolds are not covered.

items.label: Cheeger, Poincaré and concentration are equivalent
items.statement: Under convexity assumptions, D_Che ≃ D_Poin ≃ D_Exp ≃ D_FM up to universal constants.

items.label: Lipschitz-distance form of D_Che
items.statement: D_Che ≃ inf over A with μ(A) ≥ 1/2 of 1/∫d(x, A)dμ.

items.label: Stability of D_Che for convex domains
items.statement: If vol(K ∩ L) ≥ v_K vol(K) and ≥ v_L vol(L), then D_Che(K) ≥ c·v_K²/log(1 + 1/v_L)·D_Che(L).

items.label: Concavity of the isoperimetric profile
items.statement: Under generalized smooth convexity the isoperimetric profile is concave on (0, 1); I^(n/(n−1)) is concave for uniform measures.

items.label: Mean versus median in Orlicz norms
items.statement: ½‖f − Ef‖_N ≤ ‖f − Mf‖_N ≤ 3‖f − Ef‖_N for every Orlicz norm.

items.label: Cheeger as an L¹ Poincaré inequality
items.statement: Cheeger's inequality with D_Che holds iff D_Che‖f − Mf‖₁ ≤ ‖|∇f|‖₁ for all f.

items.label: Metric gradient
items.statement: On metric probability spaces |∇f|(x) is the limsup of |f(y) − f(x)|/d(x, y) as y → x, and 0 at isolated points.
items.note: Same convention, including isolated points.

items.label: All (p, q) Poincaré inequalities are equivalent
items.statement: Under convexity assumptions, D_{p,q} ≤ C p′ D_{p′,q′} for 1 ≤ p ≤ q ≤ ∞ and 1 ≤ p′ ≤ q′ ≤ ∞.

items.label: Monotonicity of (p, q) constants
items.statement: If 1/p − 1/q = 1/p′ − 1/q′ with p ≤ p′, q ≤ q′, then D_{p′,q′} ≥ (p/p′) D_{p,q}, without convexity.

items.label: Maz'ya–Cheeger inequality, new proof
items.statement: D_Poin ≥ D_Che/2.
items.note: Same Lean result as Theorem 1.1, by a different proof; finite-dimensional log-concave laws only.

items.label: Gromov–Milman inequality, new proof
items.statement: D_Exp ≥ c·D_Poin.

items.label: Concentration from (r, r) Poincaré
items.statement: D_Exp ≥ c_r D_{r,r} for every r ≥ 1.

items.label: Poincaré versus profile decay
items.statement: Under smooth convexity, a (p, q) Poincaré inequality is equivalent to Ĩ(t) ≥ D′ t^r with r = 1 + 1/p − 1/q in [1/2, 2], with comparable constants.

items.label: L¹-type Poincaré versus isoperimetry
items.statement: For 0 < r ≤ 1, the (1/r, 1) Poincaré inequality is equivalent to Ĩ(t) ≥ D t^r, without convexity.

items.label: Uniform measures strengthen the results
items.statement: For uniform measures, concavity of I^(n/(n−1)) upgrades the main theorem to an (n/(n−1), 1) Poincaré inequality.

items.label: Reverse local Poincaré inequality
items.statement: Under Ric + Hess ψ ≥ −K, c(t)|∇P_t f|² ≤ P_t(f²) − (P_t f)² pointwise, with c(t) = 2t when K = 0.
items.note: K = 0 for smooth convex potentials on Euclidean spaces, integrated against nonnegative C_c^∞ tests (a.e. form for bounded data).

items.label: L¹ heat displacement
items.note: Indicator data of smooth domains with relative perimeter, smooth convex potential; a sharper coefficient 2√(t/π) is also proved.

items.label: Paley–Zygmund-type quantile bound
items.statement: If ‖f‖₂ ≤ D‖f‖₁ then the (1 − ε) quantile of |f| is at least θ‖f‖₁ with ε = (1 − θ)²/D².
items.note: Stated with the paper's hypotheses (D > 0, θ ∈ (0, 1)) and Q_δ as the real infimum; in the degenerate case f = 0 with 1 − ε < 0 the paper's quantile is −∞ and the real convention gives 0.

items.label: Optimal 1-Lipschitz functions behave like linear ones
items.statement: An essentially optimal 1-Lipschitz f₀ for first-moment concentration has ‖f₀‖_Ψ₁ ≤ C₀‖f₀‖₁ and a quantile lower bound.

items.label: Slow tail decay suffices
items.statement: An arbitrarily slow uniform tail decay of 1-Lipschitz functions implies the main theorem's statements with constants depending only on the decay.

items.label: Going down to a large convex subset
items.statement: If L ⊆ K is convex with vol(L) ≥ v vol(K), then D_FM(L) ≥ c/log(1 + 1/v)·D_Exp(K).

items.label: Going up to a convex superset
items.statement: If L ⊆ K are convex with vol(L) ≥ v vol(K), then D_Che(K) ≥ v² D_Che(L).

items.label: Stability under Banach–Mazur-close bodies
items.statement: If d_G(K, L) ≤ 1 + s/n for 1 ≤ s ≤ C₁n, then D_Che(K) and D_Che(L) agree up to a factor C₂ s.

items.label: Log-concave version of Lemmas 5.1–5.2
items.statement: Lemmas 5.1 and 5.2 hold for absolutely continuous log-concave measures with density domination dμ_K/dx ≥ v dμ_L/dx.

items.label: Total-variation stability of D_Che
items.statement: If d_TV(μ₁, μ₂) ≤ 1 − ε for log-concave μ₁, μ₂, their Cheeger constants agree up to c(ε) = c′ε²/log(1 + 1/ε).

items.label: Optimality of the stability exponent
items.statement: Products of cubes and ℓ₁-balls show the quadratic dependence in Theorem 1.7 is necessary.

items.label: Optimality of Corollary 5.3
items.statement: Truncated ℓ₁-balls show the linear dependence on s in Corollary 5.3 is necessary.

items.label: Sharper stability near the Euclidean ball
items.statement: Near B₂ⁿ the bound in Corollary 5.3 improves to 1/(C₂√s).

items.label: Lipschitz-on-average transport
items.statement: If T pushes μ to ν and ν satisfies convexity assumptions, then D_Che(ν) ≥ c/∫‖DT‖_op dμ·D_Che(μ).

items.label: Diameter bound for convex domains
items.statement: For locally convex smooth K with Ric ≥ 0, D_Poin ≥ π/(2 diam K), and π/diam K in Euclidean space.

items.label: KLS first-moment bound
items.statement: For log-concave μ on R^n, D_Che(μ) ≥ c/∫|x − x₀|dμ for every x₀.

items.label: First-moment bound under convexity assumptions
items.statement: Under convexity assumptions, D_Che ≥ c/∫d(x, x₀)dμ for every x₀.

items.label: Mean chord bound
items.statement: For log-concave μ with bounded support B, D_Che(μ) ≥ c/∫θ_B dμ, θ_B the longest symmetric chord.

items.label: Variance-of-norm bound
items.statement: For log-concave μ, D_Che(μ) ≥ c/Var_μ(|x − x₀|²)^(1/4).

items.label: Uniform bound for ℓ_p balls
items.statement: Normalized ℓ_pⁿ balls with p ∈ [1, 2] have D_Che bounded below uniformly in n.

items.label: Profile lower semicontinuity from above
items.statement: If μ_m tends to μ from above, liminf of I_{μ_m}(t) is at least the lower limit of I_μ near t.

items.label: Profile lower semicontinuity from within
items.statement: The same conclusion when μ_m tends to μ from within.

items.label: Profile versus capacity
items.statement: inf over [a, b] of I ≤ Cap₁(a, b) ≤ inf over [a, b) of I.

items.label: Profile symmetry
items.statement: If I is lower semicontinuous at t and 1 − t, then I(t) = I(1 − t).

items.label: Upper semicontinuity under concavity
items.statement: If μ_m → μ in total variation with concave profiles, the lower limit of I_μ near t dominates limsup I_{μ_m}(t).

items.label: Convergence of profiles
items.statement: Under total-variation convergence from above or within, with concave profiles, I_{μ_m}(t) converges to the lower limit of I_μ near t.

items.label: Hölder continuity of the profile
items.statement: For densities bounded above on balls, the profile is absolutely continuous and locally (n−1)/n-Hölder.

items.label: Approximation preserves concavity
items.statement: Smooth convex approximations from above or within give pointwise profile convergence, so the limit profile is concave.

items.label: Convex bodies satisfy the assumptions
items.statement: Uniform measures on convex domains satisfy the convexity assumptions, with I and I^(n/(n−1)) concave.

items.label: Log-concave measures satisfy the assumptions
items.statement: Absolutely continuous log-concave measures on R^n satisfy the convexity assumptions, with concave profile.

items.label: Borell-type tail bound
items.statement: If μ_m(B(x₀, R)) = θ > 1/2, then μ_m(M ∖ B(x₀, tR)) ≤ θ((1 − θ)/θ)^((t+1)/2) for t ≥ 1.

items.label: Riemannian Prékopa–Leindler
items.statement: Under Ric + Hess ψ ≥ 0, the weighted Prékopa–Leindler inequality holds along geodesic interpolation.

items.label: Concavity for uniform measures
items.statement: For locally convex smooth domains in manifolds with Ric ≥ 0, I and I^(n/(n−1)) are concave.

items.label: Concavity for weighted manifolds
items.statement: Under Ric + Hess ψ ≥ 0 the profile is concave.

items.label: Concavity on locally convex domains
items.statement: On locally convex C² domains with Ric + Hess ψ ≥ 0 the profile is concave.

items.label: One-dimensional log-concave profile
items.statement: For absolutely continuous log-concave μ on R, the isoperimetric profile is concave on (0, 1).

items.label: Half-lines are minimizers
items.statement: In dimension one the minimizers are half-lines, so I(t) = min(F′∘F⁻¹(t), F′∘F⁻¹(1 − t)).

papers.title: Interpolating thin-shell and sharp large-deviation estimates for isotropic log-concave measures
papers.result: Quantitative radial concentration across thin-shell and large-deviation scales for isotropic log-concave laws.
papers.remaining: Radial deviation estimates and their thin-shell/isoperimetric consequences are not locally formalized.

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: C, c, c_1, c_2, C' denote universal positive constants independent of n and all other parameters, changing between occurrences. X is an isotropic random vector in R^n (E X = 0, E X tensor X = Id) with log-concave density; X is psi_alpha with constant b_alpha (alpha in [1,2]) if (E|<X,y>|^p)^{1/p} <= b_alpha p^{1/alpha} (E|<X,y>|^2)^{1/2} for all p >= 2 and y (always true for alpha = 1 with b_1 <= C, and b_alpha >= 2^{-1/alpha}). A in M_n(R) with ||A||_HS^2 = n, eta = n/(||A||_op^2 b_alpha^2), G_n an independent standard Gaussian vector and Y = (AX + G_n)/sqrt 2 with density g. Throughout the proofs eta (hence n) is assumed larger than a universal constant. SO(n) carries the bi-invariant metric |B|^2 = ||B||_HS^2/2 on antisymmetric B; Z^+_q(w) is the one-sided L_q-centroid body h(y) = (2 int <x,y>_+^q w)^{1/q}, Z_q(w) the standard one with h(y) = (int |<x,y>|^q w)^{1/q}, K_q(w) Ball's body with gauge (q int_0^infty t^{q-1} w(tx) dt)^{-1/q}, and d(K,L) = inf{C_2/C_1 : C_1 L in K in C_2 L} the geometric distance.
lemma_map.omitted: Every numbered statement (Theorems 1.1, 1.2, 1.5, 2.1, 2.5, 3.1, 4.1; Lemmas 2.2, 2.3, A.1-A.4; Corollaries 1.4, 2.4; Proposition 2.6; Remarks 1.3, 3.2, 3.3) is listed; no numbered statement is purely expository. Not listed: the unnumbered Theorem in Section 2.2 (K. Ball, Klartag: K_q(w) gauge is a possibly non-even norm), the unnumbered conjectures in the Introduction (Anttila-Ball-Perissinaki thin shell, Bobkov-Koldobsky, KLS in Poincare form; none has a Lean declaration other than the target hole FunctionalInequalities.KLS.kls, which is deliberately not mapped), and cited displayed facts used in proofs: Paouris' estimates (1.3)-(1.5), Klartag's and Fleury's bounds, Borell's concavity (1.18), the SO(n) log-Sobolev inequality (1.19) and reverse Holder bound (1.20), the inclusions (2.2)-(2.3) and (2.7), the polar identity (2.8), Prekopa-Leindler, Bobkov's Cheeger-variance theorem, and Klartag's Gaussian-convolution reduction [KlartagCLP, Prop. 4.1]. The unnumbered definitions of isotropy and log-concavity are listed (DISO, DLC) because Lean declarations state them.

items.label: Isotropic random vector
items.statement: A random vector X in R^n (and its density) is isotropic if E X = 0 and E X tensor X = Id, i.e. barycenter at the origin and identity covariance; then E|AX|^2 = ||A||_HS^2 for every n by n matrix A.
items.note: Unnumbered definition, listed because a Lean declaration states it. Lean states the three conditions (MemLp id 2, zero mean, centered covariance operator equal to the identity) coordinate-free on a finite-dimensional real inner-product space and for arbitrary probability laws; in orthonormal coordinates this is the paper's definition. The paper always adds a log-concave density; that hypothesis is DLC.

items.label: Log-concave density
items.statement: A function g : R^n -> R_+ is log-concave if -log g : R^n -> R union {+infinity} is convex; the paper's random vectors X have log-concave densities with respect to Lebesgue measure on R^n.
items.note: Unnumbered definition, listed because Lean states a counterpart. Lean's LogConcave is Borell's compact-set inequality mu(tK0+(1-t)K1) >= mu(K0)^t mu(K1)^(1-t) for probability laws on a finite-dimensional normed space (degenerate supports allowed). IsBorellDensity.compactLogConcave proves that a law with a pointwise log-concave density is LogConcave (Prekopa-Leindler); the paper's full-dimensional density hypothesis is therefore a special case, but log-concavity of functions itself is not a separate Lean definition.

items.label: Deviation and thin-shell estimates
items.statement: If X is isotropic in R^n with log-concave density and psi_alpha (alpha in [1,2]) with constant b_alpha, and A in M_n(R) has ||A||_HS^2 = n, then P(||AX| - sqrt n| >= t sqrt n) <= C exp(-c eta^{alpha/2} min(t^{2+alpha}, t)) for all t >= 0, where eta = n/(||A||_op^2 b_alpha^2) (1.8), with universal c, C > 0. In particular sqrt(Var|AX|) <= C n^{1/2} eta^{-alpha/(2(2+alpha))} (1.9); the text adds the one-sided forms (1.10) without the prefactor C and (1.11) with max(t^{2+alpha}, log(c_2/(1-t))), and for alpha = 1, A = Id the thin-shell bound sqrt(Var|X|) <= C n^{1/3} (1.12).
items.note: Main theorem: it is the headline estimate of the abstract and of the register entry (Main deviation estimate), and contains the thin-shell bound sigma_n <= C n^{1/3} cited downstream (Eldan 2013, Lee-Vempala). The authors call the moment estimates of Theorem 1.2 the main result and say Theorem 1.1 is essentially equivalent to them; logically (1.7) is derived in Section 4 from Theorem 4.1 for Y = (AX+G_n)/sqrt 2 via Klartag's reduction [KlartagCLP, Prop. 4.1], (1.10) via the moment reduction (4.7) from Theorem 3.1, and (1.11) additionally uses Paouris' small-ball estimate (1.5), so the full Theorem 1.2 depends on Theorem 1.1 rather than conversely. No Lean counterpart: radial moments, psi_alpha, deviation and thin-shell bounds are not formalized. Marked main as the register's target (the deviation estimate); the authors call Theorem 1.2 their main result, and its proof uses this theorem.

items.label: Moment estimates for |AX|
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.1, for 1 <= |p-2| <= c_1 eta^{alpha/(2(alpha+2))} one has |(E|AX|^p)^{1/p}/(E|AX|^2)^{1/2} - 1| <= C |p-2|/eta^{alpha/(alpha+2)}, and for c_1 eta^{alpha/(2(alpha+2))} <= |p-2| <= c_2 eta^{alpha/2} one has |(E|AX|^p)^{1/p}/(E|AX|^2)^{1/2} - 1| <= C (|p-2|/eta^{alpha/2})^{1/(alpha+1)}, with the L_0-norm read as exp(E log|AX|).
items.note: Called the main result by the authors. Proved in Section 4: positive moments for p >= 3 from Theorem 3.1 via (4.7); the small-range positive moments via Fleury's Lemma 6 applied to the deviations of Theorem 1.1; negative moments by integrating (4.8), which combines (1.11)-type bounds with Paouris' small-ball estimate. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Scale-invariant normalization
items.statement: The assumption ||A||_HS^2 = n is only cosmetic: scaling X, all deviation estimates hold around (E|AX|^2)^{1/2} = ||A||_HS with the scale-invariant parameter eta = ||A||_HS^2/(b_alpha^2 ||A||_op^2).
items.note: Reformulation remark, no separate proof. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Cheeger bound n^{-5/12}
items.statement: If mu is a probability measure on R^n with isotropic log-concave density, then its Cheeger constant satisfies D_Che(mu) >= c n^{-5/12} for a universal c > 0 (improving to c n^{-3/8} when the density is psi_2).
items.note: Proved by combining Bobkov's theorem D_Che(mu)^2 >= c/(E|X| sqrt(Var|X|)) (cited, not proved) with the thin-shell bound (1.12). Not mapped: Lean's literatureConstant_le_four_mul_inverseScale_sq and inverseScale_sq_le_pi_literature compare the Poincare and Minkowski-Cheeger constants of a fixed log-concave law, but neither Bobkov's variance bound nor any dimension-dependent lower bound on the Cheeger constant is formalized, so no Lean statement states or restricts this corollary.

items.label: Improved log-Lipschitz bound
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.1, with Y = (AX + G_n)/sqrt 2 and h_{k,p}(u) = vol(S^{k-1}) int_0^infty t^{p+k-1} pi_{u(E_0)} g(t u(theta_0)) dt on SO(n) (g the density of Y), if p >= -k+1 then the log-Lipschitz constant satisfies L_{k,p} <= C ||A||_op b_alpha max(k,p)^{1/alpha+1/2}.
items.note: Introduction version of Corollary 2.4 (which uses ||A||_op >= 1, automatic when ||A||_HS^2 = n). No Lean counterpart; SO(n) Riemannian structure and h_{k,p} are not formalized.

items.label: Log-Lipschitz via centroid bodies
items.statement: For Y with log-concave density g on R^n and barycenter 0, integers 1 <= k <= n, real p >= -k+1, E_0 in G_{n,k} and theta_0 in S(E_0), the log-Lipschitz constant of h_{k,p} on SO(n) (metric |B|^2 = ||B||_HS^2/2) is at most C max(k,p) d(Z^+_{max(k,p)}(g), B_2^n), where Z^+_q is the one-sided L_q-centroid body h_{Z^+_q(w)}(y) = (2 int <x,y>_+^q w)^{1/q} and d is the geometric distance.
items.note: Proof via Type-1/2/3 movements using K. Ball's K_q(w) norm theorem (unnumbered, cited from Ball and Klartag), the inclusions (2.3) between the Z^+_q (uses Lemma 2.2), projection and Theorem 2.5. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Grunbaum half-line mass bound
items.statement: If X_1 is a real random variable with log-concave density and barycenter at the origin, then 1/e <= P(X_1 >= 0) <= 1 - 1/e.
items.note: Lean states it for a log-concave law on the line whose support has nonempty interior (equivalently, one with a log-concave density) and mean 0. Proof: the tail is log-concave and lies below its tangent exponential at 0; the layer-cake formula and the barycenter condition give P(X > 0) ≥ 1/e, and the reflected law gives P(X < 0) ≥ 1/e.

items.label: Centroid bodies of Gaussian convolution
items.statement: Let X be isotropic in R^n with log-concave density, A in M_n(R), Y = (AX + G_n)/sqrt 2 with density g. Then for all q >= 2: Z^+_q(g) contains c sqrt q B_2^n, and if X is psi_alpha (alpha in [1,2]) with constant b_alpha then Z^+_q(g) is contained in (C_1 ||A||_op b_alpha q^{1/alpha} + C_2 sqrt q) B_2^n.
items.note: Lower bound uses P(<AX,theta> >= 0) >= 1/e from Lemma 2.2 and Gaussian moments. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Distance and Lipschitz bound
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma 2.3 with X psi_alpha (alpha in [1,2]) with constant b_alpha, d(Z^+_q(g), B_2^n) <= C_1 (1 + ||A||_op b_alpha q^{1/alpha - 1/2}); consequently, when ||A||_op >= 1, L_{k,p} <= C_2 ||A||_op b_alpha max(k,p)^{1/alpha+1/2}.
items.note: Immediate from Lemma 2.3 and Theorem 2.1. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Distance of K_{m+p} to ball
items.statement: If w is log-concave on R^m with 0 < int w < infinity and barycenter at the origin, then for every p >= -m+1, d(K_{m+p}(w), B_2^m) <= C max(m/(m+p), 1) d(Z^+_{max(p,m)}(w), B_2^m).
items.note: Uses the cited inclusions (2.7) between K_q bodies, the polar identity Z^+_q(K_{m+q}(w)) = Z^+_q(w) (2.8), Proposition 2.6 and Stirling's formula. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Comparing K_{m+q} and Z^+_q
items.statement: With w as in Theorem 2.5 and any q >= 1, C_1 Z^+_q(K_{m+q}(w)) is contained in vol(K_{m+q}(w))^{1/q} K_{m+q}(w), which is contained in C_2 (Gamma(m+q+1)/(Gamma(m) Gamma(q+1)))^{1/q} Z^+_q(K_{m+q}(w)).
items.note: Proof in the Appendix; the non-even (non-centrally-symmetric) case is the new part. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Moment estimates for Y
items.statement: Let X be isotropic in R^n with log-concave density, psi_alpha (alpha in [1,2]) with constant b_alpha, A in M_n(R) with ||A||_HS^2 = n, and Y = (AX + G_n)/sqrt 2 with G_n an independent standard Gaussian. Then for |p| <= c eta^{alpha/2}, 1 - C (|p-2|/eta^{alpha/2})^{1/(alpha+1)} <= (E|Y|^p)^{1/p}/(E|Y|^2)^{1/2} <= 1 + C (|p-2|/eta^{alpha/2})^{1/(alpha+1)}.
items.note: Proof: Fleury's passage to SO(n) and Grassmann averaging, entropy decomposition of d/dp log (E|Y|^p)^{1/p}, the SO(n) log-Sobolev inequality and Herbst reverse Holder bound (cited), Borell's concavity of q -> log(int t^q w/Gamma(q+1)) (cited), Stirling, Corollary 2.4, optimization of k, and Fleury's argument near p = 0. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Sharpness of exponent balance
items.statement: For alpha = 1 and A = Id, if L_{k,p} <= C p^beta k^gamma for 2 <= p <= k, the proof recovers the sharp large deviation P(|X| >= C sqrt n) <= exp(-sqrt n) if and only if beta + gamma = 3/2; the paper's bounds give beta = 0, gamma = 3/2.
items.note: Proof-analysis remark, not proved in detail; speculates that beta = 1, gamma = 1/2 should hold. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Bobkov concavity alternative
items.statement: The Stirling computation behind (3.11) can be avoided using Bobkov's result that for any log-concave density w on R_+, q -> log(int_0^infty t^q w(t) dt / q^q) is concave on R_+.
items.note: Cited result of Bobkov; no proof in the paper. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Deviation estimates for Y
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 3.1, P(|Y| >= (1+t) sqrt n) <= exp(-c eta^{alpha/2} min(t^{2+alpha}, t)) for all t >= 0, and P(|Y| <= (1-t) sqrt n) <= C exp(-c eta^{alpha/2} max(t^{2+alpha}, log(c_2/(1-t)))) for all t in [0,1].
items.note: Markov-Chebyshev with optimized p from Theorem 3.1, plus Borell's lemma (cited) for t >= t_0. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Support of Z^+_q(K)
items.statement: For a convex body K in R^m, theta in S^{m-1} and f_theta the marginal of 1_K on span(theta): (f_theta(0)/||f_theta||_infty)^{1/q} (Gamma(m) Gamma(q+1)/Gamma(m+q+1))^{1/q} h_K(theta) <= h_{Z^+_q(K)}(theta)/(2 vol(K intersect H^+_theta))^{1/q} <= h_K(theta).
items.note: Left inequality follows Paouris [Lemma 4.1 of Small-Diameter] using (m-1)^{-1}-concavity of marginals; only sketched. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Log-concave density at zero
items.statement: If mu = f(x)dx is a log-concave probability measure on R and eps <= int_0^infty f <= 1 - eps for some eps > 0, then f(0) >= eps ||f||_infty.
items.note: Folklore (Fradelizi). Lean takes f to be the Borell representative of a LineDensity (continuous on the interior of the support, which contains 0 here) and ‖f‖_∞ the essential supremum eLpNorm f ⊤; the proof uses the existing hazard-rate monotonicity, the paper's route.

items.label: Half-space mass of K_{m+q}
items.statement: If w is log-concave on R^m with barycenter at the origin, then for every theta in S^{m-1}, (vol(K_{m+q}(w) intersect H^+_theta)/vol(K_{m+q}(w)))^{1/q} >= c > 0.
items.note: Uses the cited inclusions (2.7), Stirling and Lemma 2.2 for the marginal of w. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Lower bound for Z^+_2
items.statement: If g : R^m -> R_+ is a log-concave isotropic density, then Z^+_2(g) contains c B_2^m, e.g. with c = (3 e^2 (1 + (e-1)^3))^{-1/2}.
items.note: Proof compares one-dimensional moments via (2.7) and uses Lemma 2.2. No Lean counterpart.

papers.title: Thin shell implies spectral gap up to polylog via a stochastic localization scheme
papers.result: Introduces stochastic localization and transfers thin-shell control to KLS with logarithmic losses.
papers.remaining: The paper's uncut stochastic-localization construction, covariance estimates and transfer theorem are not locally formalized. The separate BKL finite-horizon cutoff process and its generator/Dynkin estimates do not certify those Eldan source statements.

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: Universal constants c, C change from line to line. G_n^{-1} = inf over isotropic log-concave measures mu on R^n and Borel A with mu(A) <= 1/2 of mu^+(A)/mu(A), with mu^+ the lower Minkowski boundary measure of the closed eps-extension A_eps (the printed definition omits y in A); sigma_n^2 = sup E(|X| - sqrt n)^2 and K_n = sup ||E[X tensor X X_1]||_HS over isotropic log-concave X; kappa = liminf log sigma_n / log n, tau_n = max(1, max_j sigma_j j^{-kappa}). From Section 2 on the isotropic log-concave density f is assumed WLOG to satisfy supp f in n B_n (justified only by citing concentration bounds). Gamma_t(f) = f_t = f F_t is the stochastic localization driven by an n-dimensional standard Wiener process W_t, with barycenter a_t, covariance A_t, B_t = int_0^t A_s^{-1} ds; ||A||_OP is the largest eigenvalue of a positive semidefinite A.
lemma_map.omitted: Remarks 1.4 (connection to the hyperplane conjecture and Ball-Nguyen), 2.2 (heuristic discrete-step interpretation) and 2.7 (comparison with Lehec's drift construction) are expository and listed here instead of as items. Unnumbered displayed claims are covered inside the items that use them: the Ledoux Cheeger/spectral-gap comparison (4), the bounds (14)-(15) and the W_2 convergence (16) after Proposition 2.6, the Gaussian worked example at the end of Section 2, and the dA_t computation in Section 3. There is no appendix.

items.label: KLS conjecture
items.statement: There is a universal constant C with G_n < C for all n, where G_n^{-1} is the infimum of mu^+(A)/mu(A) over isotropic log-concave measures mu on R^n and Borel A with mu(A) <= 1/2.
items.note: Stated as an open conjecture, not proved in the paper. Deliberately not mapped to FunctionalInequalities.KLS.kls; the paper's G_n is the uniform Minkowski-Cheeger constant of isotropic laws.

items.label: Thin-shell conjecture
items.statement: There is a universal constant C with sigma_n < C for all n, where sigma_n^2 = sup E[(|X| - sqrt n)^2] over isotropic log-concave random vectors X in R^n.
items.note: Open conjecture, used only as a hypothesis in the corollary discussion after Theorem 1.1. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Thin shell implies Cheeger polylog
items.statement: There is a universal constant C > 0 such that for all n >= 2, G_n <= C sqrt((log n) sum_{k=1}^n sigma_k^2 / k). In particular sigma_k <= k^kappa for all k gives G_n <= C sqrt(log n) n^kappa, and the thin-shell conjecture gives G_n <= C log n.
items.note: Main theorem: the title result, thin shell implies the Cheeger (equivalently, via Ledoux's comparison (4), spectral gap) constant up to polylog. Proof is the two-line combination of Lemma 1.6 and Proposition 1.7. The spectral-gap reading uses the unnumbered comparison (4) quoted from Ledoux; the Lean Cheeger half literatureConstant_le_four_mul_inverseScale_sq (KLS/Geometry/Cheeger/Inequality.lean) gives only the direction C_P <= 4 Psi^2 of that comparison and is not a restricted case of this theorem, so no declaration is mapped.

items.label: Polylog bound with GM thin shell
items.statement: Combined with the Guedon-E. Milman bound sigma_n <= C n^{1/3}, Theorem 1.1 gives G_n <= C n^{1/3} sqrt(log n), improving the bound G_n <= C n^{5/12} obtained from Guedon-Milman and Bobkov.
items.note: Corollary of T11 plus an external thin-shell estimate that is not proved in the paper.

items.label: Bobkov variance bound
items.statement: For every log-concave random vector X and smooth phi, Var[phi(X)] / E[|grad phi(X)|^2] <= C E[|X|] sqrt(Var[|X|]); under the thin-shell hypothesis this gives G_n <= C n^{1/4}.
items.note: Quoted from Bobkov for comparison only; not proved and not used in the proofs.

items.label: K_n bounded by thin shell
items.statement: There is a universal constant C > 0 such that for all n >= 2, K_n <= C sqrt(sum_{k=1}^n sigma_k^2 / k), where K_n = sup over isotropic log-concave mu and unit theta of the Hilbert-Schmidt norm of int x tensor x <x,theta> dmu.
items.note: Proved in Section 6 by projecting onto k-dimensional eigenspaces of A = E[X tensor X <X,theta>] and Cauchy-Schwarz with Var|P X|^2 <= C k sigma_k^2. Purely deterministic; the opening sentence of Section 6 mistakenly says the bound is in terms of tau_n and kappa.

items.label: Cheeger bounded by K_n polylog
items.statement: There is a universal constant C > 0 such that for all n >= 2, G_n <= C K_n sqrt(log n).
items.note: Core result of Section 4. For an isotropic f and E with f-mass 1/2, the martingale property (Lemma 2.4(iv)), the event F of Proposition 3.1, Lemma 4.1 at time T and Corollary 3.3 give f(E_{Theta/delta} minus E) >= c with delta = 1/(K_n sqrt(log n)); Theorem 4.2 converts this concentration bound into the isoperimetric bound.

items.label: K_n controlled by ellipsoids
items.statement: There is a universal c > 0 with K_n^{-1} >= c inf_mu inf_E mu^+(E)/mu(E), the infimum over isotropic log-concave mu and ellipsoids E with mu(E) <= 1/2; that is, K_n <= C R_n.
items.note: Restates the second inequality chain of Fact 6.1; with Proposition 1.7 it reduces the Cheeger constant to ellipsoids up to sqrt(log n).

items.label: Dimension-sensitive Brunn-Minkowski stability
items.statement: For every epsilon > 0 there is C(epsilon) such that for convex bodies K, T in R^n of volume 1 with barycenters at the origin and Cov(uniform on K) = L_K Id, with V = Vol_n((K+T)/2) and delta = C(epsilon) L_K V^5 tau_n n^{2(kappa - kappa^2) + epsilon}, one has Vol_n(K_delta cap T) >= 1 - epsilon.
items.note: Second main result, independent of Theorem 1.1. kappa = liminf log sigma_n / log n and tau_n = max(1, max_j sigma_j / j^kappa). The statement says covariance L_K Id but the proof uses L_K^2 Id and concludes Vol_n(K minus T_delta) <= 2 epsilon with delta = L_K Theta / sqrt(epsilon); the roles of K and T in the conclusion differ between statement and proof.

items.label: Comparison with Eldan-Klartag bound
items.statement: By Theorem 1.4 of Eldan-Klartag, the estimate of Theorem 1.2 also holds with delta = C(epsilon) sqrt(tau_n) n^{1/4 + kappa/2} V^{5/2}; the bound of Theorem 1.2 is tight up to C(epsilon) n^epsilon under thin shell, as shown by the cube and the cube truncated by the ball of radius sqrt n.
items.note: Quoted external bound and an asserted tightness example; neither is proved in the paper.

items.label: Brunn-Minkowski stability with GM
items.statement: With sigma_n <= C n^{1/3}, Theorem 1.2 holds with delta = C(epsilon) n^{4/9 + epsilon} V^5 L_K; without the volume assumption on (K+T)/2, even with equal covariances, the best possible bound is delta = C sqrt(n) L_K, as for a cube and a ball.
items.note: Specialisation kappa = 1/3 of T12 plus an asserted optimality example.

items.label: FMP quantitative stability
items.statement: Figalli-Maggi-Pratelli prove Vol_n((K + x_0) symmetric-difference T)^2 <= n^7 (Vol_n((K+T)/2) - 1) for some x_0.
items.note: Quoted for comparison; not used. The quoted exponent is as printed in the paper.

items.label: Linear-tilt localization SDE
items.statement: For the solution (c_t, B_t) of the SDE (11) on [0, t_0], F_t(x) = V_t^{-1} exp(<c_t,x> - <B_t x,x>/2) satisfies F_0 = 1 and dF_t(x) = <x - a_t, A_t^{-1/2} dW_t> F_t(x) for every x, where a_t and A_t are the barycenter and covariance of f F_t.
items.note: Proof is Ito's formula for G_t(x), V_t^{-1} and the product V_t^{-1} G_t(x), with an interchange of stochastic differential and spatial integral justified by the compact-support assumption supp f in n B_n.

items.label: Direct infinite SDE definition
items.statement: The process F_t may alternatively be defined directly by the infinite system of SDEs dF_t(x) = <x - a_t, A_t^{-1/2} dW_t> F_t(x), with existence and uniqueness following from Kallianpur-Xiong Theorem 5.2.2 after verifying its hypotheses.
items.note: Asserted without proof (the paper notes extra work is needed); not used later.

items.label: Basic properties of localization
items.statement: (i) Gamma_t(f) is almost surely well defined, finite and log-concave for all t > 0 (the explosion time t_0 is infinite); (ii) int f_t = 1; (iii) the semigroup property Gamma_{s+t}(f) ~ det(A_s)^{-1/2} Gamma_t(sqrt(det A_s) Gamma_s(f) o L^{-1}) o L with L(x) = A_s^{-1/2}(x - a_s); (iv) for every x the process f_t(x) is a martingale.
items.note: (ii) and (iv) follow from (13); t_0 = infinity uses Lemma 2.5 and a restart argument at the hitting times of ||A_t^{-1}||_OP = c(n)^{-1}, i.e. a strong Markov renewal argument. (iii) is equality in law. Martingale (not merely local martingale) status is asserted from (13) without a separate integrability argument.

items.label: Covariance nondegenerate at small times
items.statement: For every n there is c(n) > 0 such that P(A_t >= c(n) Id for all 0 <= t <= c(n)) >= c(n).
items.note: Proved in Section 6 with dimension-dependent constants: a lower bound on A_f(c,B) for |c| < c_4 and B <= Id from log-concave density and exponential moment bounds (Lovasz-Vempala Theorem 5.14, Lemma 5.7), Ito's formula for |c_t|^2, Dambis-Dubins-Schwarz and stopping times T_1, T_2.

items.label: Gaussian-tilted concentration and variance
items.statement: There is a universal Theta > 0 such that if phi is convex, K > 0 and dmu = Z exp(-phi(x) - |x|^2/(2K^2)) dx is a probability measure with barycenter 0, then (i) mu(A_{K Theta}) >= 0.95 for every Borel A with 0.1 <= mu(A) <= 0.9, and (ii) int <x,theta>^2 dmu <= Theta K^2 for every unit theta.
items.note: Proof via the parallelogram law and the Prekopa-Leindler inequality, then log-concavity of the tail function for (ii). Lean has Prekopa-Leindler (prekopaLeindler in Probability/BrunnMinkowski.lean) as an ingredient, but no declaration states this proposition, so nothing is mapped. The proof applies (i) to a half-space of measure 1/2. The printed display has |x|^2 twice where |y|^2 is meant.

items.label: Covariance operator norm bound
items.statement: There are universal C, c > 0 such that for n >= 2 and isotropic log-concave f, with A_t the covariance of Gamma_t(f): (i) the event F = {||A_t||_OP < C K_n^2 (log n) e^{-ct} for all t > 0} has P(F) >= 1 - n^{-10}; (ii) E[Tr A_t] <= n for all t > 0; (iii) on F, for every t > 1/(K_n^2 log n), f_t(x) = exp(-|x/(C K_n sqrt(log n))|^2 - phi_t(x)) with phi_t convex.
items.note: Proof: dA_t formula by Ito, the dominating process tilde A_t without drift, Ito for S_t = Tr(tilde A_t^p) with p = ceil(log n), Dambis-Dubins-Schwarz and the reflection principle on [0, 1/(K_n^2 log n)], then the deterministic bound (14) A_t <= Theta ||B_t^{-1}||_OP Id from P26(ii) and exponential growth of B_t. The proof only establishes ||A_t||_OP <= C' on the initial interval and C delta^{-2} e^{(delta^2 - t)/Theta} afterwards; the prefactor K_n^2 log n arises as delta^{-2}.

items.label: Bounds on the xi vectors
items.statement: For the vectors xi_{i,j} of (19) one has (i) |xi_{i,i}| < C for a universal C and every i, and (ii) sum_j |xi_{i,j}|^2 <= K_n^2 for every i.
items.note: Deterministic: after normalising f_t to the isotropic tilde f_t, (i) is Cauchy-Schwarz with the universal fourth-moment bound for isotropic log-concave marginals (Lovasz-Vempala Lemma 5.7) and (ii) is the definition of K_n.

items.label: Concentration for localized measure
items.statement: There are universal c, Theta > 0 such that on the event F, with delta = 1/(K_n sqrt(log n)), every t > delta^2 and every measurable E with 0.1 <= int_E f_t <= 0.9 satisfy int_{E_{Theta/delta} minus E} f_t >= c.
items.note: Immediate from P31(iii) and P26(i) with K = C K_n sqrt(log n).

items.label: Mass of E stays balanced
items.statement: If f is isotropic log-concave, int_E f = 1/2 and g(t) = int_E f_t, then there is a universal T > 0 with P(0.1 <= g(t) <= 0.9) > 0.5 for all t in [0, T].
items.note: dg = <int_{E_t} y tilde f_t(y) dy, dW_t> with integrand of norm at most 1 by isotropy, so d[g]_t/dt <= 1, E[(g(t) - 1/2)^2] <= t by Ito, and Chebyshev's inequality.

items.label: Concentration implies isoperimetry
items.statement: If a log-concave probability measure mu has constants 0 < lambda < 1/2 and Theta > 0 with mu(E_Theta) >= 1 - lambda for all measurable E with mu(E) >= 1/2, then mu^+(E)/mu(E) >= (1 - 2 lambda)/Theta for all measurable E with mu(E) <= 1/2.
items.note: Quoted from E. Milman in a weakened form and not proved here; it is the only deep non-stochastic input of Theorem 1.1. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Bakry-Emery alternative route
items.statement: Proposition 2.6 can be replaced by the Bakry-Emery result that a density of the form (12), log-concave relative to a Gaussian, has a corresponding Cheeger constant, which would bound the surface area of every set under f_t directly and avoid Theorem 4.2.
items.note: Alternative proof sketch, asserted without proof.

items.label: Covariance comparison via sup-convolution
items.statement: There are universal C, C_1 > 0 such that for log-concave probability densities f, g on R^n, with A = Cov(f)^{-1/2} Cov(g) Cov(f)^{-1/2} - Id and eigenvalues delta_i ordered so that |delta_i - 1| decreases, |delta_i - 1| <= C K(f,g)^4 for all i and |delta_i - 1| <= C K(f,g) tau_n i^{kappa - 1/2} for (log K(f,g))^{C_1} <= i <= n, where K(f,g) = int sup_y sqrt(f(x+y) g(x-y)) dx.
items.note: Stated without proof as a variant of a lemma of Eldan-Klartag. As printed the subtraction of Id and the quantity |delta_i - 1| are inconsistent, and the use in Lemma 5.2 (with K^5 and j^kappa/sqrt j) does not match the printed exponents; recorded as printed.

items.label: Coupled localization Wasserstein bound
items.statement: For epsilon > 0 and log-concave densities f, g with f isotropic and g centred, there are subdensities tilde f <= f, tilde g <= g with equal mass at least 1 - epsilon and W_2(tilde f, tilde g) <= C epsilon^{-6} tau_n K(f,g)^5 n^{2(kappa - kappa^2) + epsilon}.
items.note: Coupled localizations of f and g driven by the same W_t with the drift matrix A_t of f, the sup-convolution martingale S_t, Doob's maximal inequality, optional stopping, a trace inequality of Tam, Hoelder and the convergence of f_t to a point mass. The final display of the proof gives W_2^2 <= C epsilon^{-11} K^{10} tau_n^2 n^{4 kappa - 4 kappa^2 + epsilon}, whose square root carries epsilon^{-11/2}; this implies the stated epsilon^{-6} for epsilon <= 1.

items.label: Improved bound under Gaussian log-concavity
items.statement: If instead f and g are log-concave with respect to the Gaussian measure, the same argument with Proposition 2.6 gives W_2(tilde f, tilde g) <= C(epsilon) K(f,g) sqrt(log n).
items.note: Asserted without proof.

items.label: K_n Q_n R_n comparison
items.statement: There are universal C_1, C_2 with K_n <= C_1 Q_n <= C_2 R_n, where Q_n^2 = sup Var[Q(X)]/E|grad Q(X)|^2 over isotropic log-concave X and quadratic forms Q, and R_n^{-1} = inf mu^+(E)/mu(E) over isotropic log-concave mu and ellipsoids E with mu(E) <= 1/2.
items.note: The left inequality is proved by duality for the Hilbert-Schmidt norm and Cauchy-Schwarz (giving K_n <= sqrt 2 Q_n); the right inequality is called standard (coarea formula and Cauchy-Schwarz) and not proved.

items.label: Conjectured K_n versus sigma_n
items.statement: The author suspects that K_n <= C sigma_n for a universal C but cannot prove it.
items.note: Open question; recorded so that the paper's conjectural claims are complete.

papers.title: Density of Lipschitz functions and equivalence of weak gradients in metric measure spaces
papers.result: Identifies weak-gradient notions and relaxed energies in metric measure spaces.
papers.remaining: The general metric-space theorem and unrestricted singular-law comparison are not formalized here. Our absolutely-continuous Euclidean identity is an independent restricted counterpart.

local_results.scope: Intrinsic absolutely-continuous E^can = 2 Ch in the local-slope convention

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: q ∈ (1, ∞) with dual exponent p = q/(q − 1). Section 3: (X, d) compact, f Lipschitz, no reference measure. Sections 4–5: (X, d) complete and separable, m a nonnegative σ-finite Borel measure. Section 6: m finite. Section 7: (X, d) compact and m a finite Borel measure; Section 8 relaxes this to bounded complete separable spaces with finite m and to locally finite spaces.
lemma_map.omitted: Nothing numbered is omitted: the source has 33 numbered statements (Lemma 2.1 to Theorem 7.4; Section 8 and the introduction have none, and there is no appendix). Unnumbered expository passages are omitted: the introduction's outline, the independence-of-q conjecture in Section 5, the Orlicz–Wasserstein outlook of Section 8.4, and the acknowledgement. Unnumbered displayed claims are listed only where a local Lean declaration states them; 21 other unnumbered claims (Sections 1–8) are not listed.

items.label: Slope of a function
items.statement: For f : X → R on a metric space, the slope (local Lipschitz constant) is |∇f|(x) = limsup_{y→x} |f(y) − f(x)|/d(y, x).
items.note: Lean takes values in [0, ∞] on any metric space and is 0 at isolated points, where the paper's limsup is left unspecified.

items.label: Subadditivity of the slope
items.statement: For Lipschitz f, g : X → R and α, β ∈ R: |∇(αf + βg)| ≤ |α||∇f| + |β||∇g|.
items.note: Lean proves |∇g|(x) ≤ |∇a|(x) + |∇b|(x) whenever every secant of g near x is bounded by the sum of the secants of a and b; this gives the case α = β = 1 (for any functions), but scalar homogeneity |∇(αf)| = |α||∇f| is not stated with it.

items.label: One-dimensional Sobolev criterion
items.statement: If f : (0,1) → R, q ∈ [1, ∞] and 0 ≤ g ∈ L^q(0,1) satisfy |f(s) − f(t)| ≤ |∫_s^t g| for L²-a.e. (s, t) ∈ (0,1)², then f ∈ W^{1,q}(0,1) and |f′| ≤ g a.e.

items.label: Lifting W_p curves to path measures
items.statement: If (X, d) is complete and separable with d bounded, p ∈ (1, ∞) and μ_t ∈ AC^p([0,T]; (P(X), W_p)), there is π ∈ P(C([0,1], X)) concentrated on AC^p([0,1], X) with (e_t)_#π = μ_t for all t and ∫|γ̇_t|^p dπ = |μ̇_t|^p for a.e. t.
items.note: Quoted from Lisini (2007); no proof in the paper.

items.label: Monotonicity of D^±
items.statement: For compact (X, d), Lipschitz f and every x: D⁺(x, t) ≤ D⁻(x, s) for 0 ≤ t < s; hence D^±(x, ·) are nondecreasing and coincide outside a countable subset of [0, ∞).
items.note: The printed proof says nonincreasing; nondecreasing is what is stated and proved.

items.label: Semicontinuity of D^±
items.statement: For compact (X, d) and Lipschitz f, D⁺ is upper semicontinuous and D⁻ is lower semicontinuous on X × [0, ∞).

items.label: Time derivative of Q_t f
items.statement: For compact (X, d) and Lipschitz f, t ↦ Q_t f is Lipschitz from [0, ∞) to C(X) and, for every x, d/dt Q_t f(x) = −(1/q)[D^±(x, t)/t]^p for all t > 0 outside a countable set.

items.label: Asymptotic Lipschitz constant
items.statement: Lip_a(f, x) = inf_{r>0} Lip(f, B_r(x)) = lim_{r↓0} Lip(f, B_r(x)); it satisfies Lip(f) ≥ Lip_a(f, x) ≥ |∇f|*(x), the upper semicontinuous envelope of the slope, with equality in length spaces.
items.note: The definition is the same (open balls, values in [0, ∞]); the comparison with the u.s.c. envelope of the slope is not stated in Lean, only the pointwise bound LocalSlope.apply_le_asymptoticLipschitz.

items.label: Asymptotic Lipschitz bound for Q_t f
items.statement: For compact (X, d), Lipschitz f and (x, t) ∈ X × (0, ∞): Lip_a(Q_t f, x) ≤ [D⁺(x, t)/t]^{p−1}; in particular Lip(Q_t f) ≤ p Lip(f).

items.label: Hopf–Lax subsolution of Hamilton–Jacobi
items.statement: For compact (X, d), Lipschitz f and every x: d/dt Q_t f(x) + (1/q)|∇Q_t f|^q(x) ≤ 0 for all t ∈ (0, ∞) outside a countable set.

items.label: Hopf–Lax supersolution in geodesic spaces
items.statement: If (X, d) is also geodesic, equality holds in Proposition 3.4, hence d/dt Q_t f(x) + (1/q)|∇Q_t f|^q(x) = 0 for every x and all t > 0 outside a countable set.
items.note: Stated without proof (analogous to the cited q = 2 argument); not used later.

items.label: q-relaxed upper gradient
items.statement: g ∈ L^q(X, m) is a q-relaxed upper gradient of f ∈ L^q(X, m) if f_n → f in L^q with upper gradients g_n of f_n converging weakly in L^q to some g̃ ≤ g m-a.e.; |∇f|_C,q is the one of minimal L^q norm.

items.label: Minimal q-relaxed slope
items.statement: g ∈ L^q(X, m) is a q-relaxed slope of f ∈ L^q(X, m) if Lipschitz f_n → f in L^q with |∇f_n| converging weakly in L^q to some g̃ ≤ g m-a.e.; |∇f|_*,q is the one of minimal L^q norm.
items.note: Well posed: by Mazur's lemma and (2.1a) the q-relaxed slopes form a closed convex set, and L^q is uniformly convex. Lean defines no relaxed-slope function, only relaxed energies.

items.label: Strong density in energy
items.statement: If f ∈ L^q(X, m) has a q-relaxed slope, there are Lipschitz f_n with ∫|f_n − f|^q dm + ∫||∇f_n| − |∇f|_*,q|^q dm → 0.
items.note: Proof only sketched (uniform convexity, as in the cited q = 2 case). Not mapped: the generic Lean recovery sequences of Energy/Relaxation/Recovery.lean give energy convergence only, with no relaxed-slope function to converge to.

items.label: Integrability of f versus gradient
items.statement: The L^q integrability of f could be decoupled from that of the gradient or replaced by m-a.e. convergence; by locality and truncation the relaxed definitions extend beyond L^q, see (6.2).
items.note: Mainly expository.

items.label: Fuglede's observation
items.statement: If Mod_q(Γ) = 0 and ε > 0, there is ρ ∈ L^q(X, m) with ‖ρ‖_q < ε and ∫_γ ρ = ∞ for every γ ∈ Γ.

items.label: Test plans and q-negligible curves
items.statement: A p-test plan is π ∈ P(C([0,1], X)) concentrated on AC^p with ∫∫_0^1 |γ̇_t|^p dt dπ < ∞ and (e_t)_#π ≤ C(π) m for all t; a Borel set of curves is q-negligible if it is π-null for every p-test plan.

items.label: Representative independence along curves
items.statement: If m-measurable f, g agree m-a.e. and T ⊂ [0,1] is countable, then f∘γ = g∘γ on T and L¹-a.e. on (0,1) for q-a.e. γ.

items.label: q-weak upper gradient
items.statement: A Borel g : X → [0, ∞] is a q-weak upper gradient of f : X → R if |f(γ_1) − f(γ_0)| ≤ ∫_γ g for q-a.e. curve γ.

items.label: Sobolev along q-a.e. curve
items.statement: f : X → R is Sobolev along q-a.e. curve if for q-a.e. γ, f∘γ agrees a.e. in [0,1] and at 0, 1 with an absolutely continuous f_γ.

items.label: Weak upper gradients give Sobolev curves
items.statement: If g is a q-weak upper gradient of f with ∫_γ g < ∞ for q-a.e. γ (e.g. g ∈ L^q), then f is Sobolev along q-a.e. curve and |d/dt(f∘γ)| ≤ g∘γ |γ̇| a.e. for π-a.e. γ, for every p-test plan π (4.11).

items.label: Minimal q-weak upper gradient
items.statement: For f Sobolev along q-a.e. curve, |∇f|_w,q is the q-weak upper gradient with |∇f|_w,q ≤ g m-a.e. for every q-weak upper gradient g; it exists and is unique up to m-null sets when m is σ-finite.
items.note: Existence is proved after the definition by minimizing ∫θ arctan g dm.

items.label: Mod_q-null sets are q-negligible
items.statement: For Borel Γ and a p-test plan π: π(Γ) ≤ C(π)^{1/q} Mod_q(Γ)^{1/q} (∫∫|γ̇|^p)^{1/p}; hence every q-upper gradient is a q-weak upper gradient and |∇f|_w,q ≤ |∇f|_S,q m-a.e. (4.14).

items.label: Pointwise minimality of relaxed slope
items.statement: If g_1, g_2 are q-relaxed slopes of f, so is min{g_1, g_2}; hence |∇f|_*,q ≤ g m-a.e. for every q-relaxed slope g of f.
items.note: Proof by reference to the cited sources.

items.label: Locality and chain rule
items.statement: If f ∈ L^q(X, m) has a q-relaxed slope: (a) |∇h|_*,q = |∇f|_*,q m-a.e. on {h = f} for every h with a q-relaxed slope; (b) |∇φ(f)|_*,q ≤ |φ′(f)||∇f|_*,q for C¹ Lipschitz φ, with equality for nondecreasing φ.
items.note: Proof by reference to the cited q = 2 case.

items.label: Stability of weak upper gradients
items.statement: If f_n are m-measurable and Sobolev along q-a.e. curve with q-weak upper gradients g_n ∈ L^q, f_n → f ∈ R m-a.e. and g_n ⇀ g weakly in L^q, then g is a q-weak upper gradient of f and f is Sobolev along q-a.e. curve.

items.label: Cheeger q-functional
items.statement: For finite m, Ch_q(f) = (1/q)∫|∇f|_*,q^q dm on L²(X, m), set to +∞ outside 𝒞.
items.note: Only q = 2, on a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with a Borel probability law. Lean defines Ch directly as one half of the sequential L²-lower-semicontinuous relaxation of ∫|∇f|² over locally Lipschitz L² tests of finite slope energy; agreement with the relaxed-slope definition (via Proposition 4.3, Theorem 6.1, (5.1) and the reduction to Lipschitz tests) is not stated in Lean.

items.label: Cheeger functional convex and lsc
items.statement: For complete separable (X, d), finite m and q ∈ (1, ∞), Ch_q is convex and lower semicontinuous on L²(X, m).
items.note: Only lower semicontinuity, for q = 2 on a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with a Borel probability law; convexity is not stated. In Lean the functional is by definition a sequential L² relaxation (see E63), so lower semicontinuity holds by construction rather than by the paper's weak-compactness argument. Not mapped: the local relaxation is lower semicontinuous by construction, which does not state this theorem.

items.label: Lsc of weighted energies
items.statement: For every α > 0, f ↦ ∫|∇f|_*,q^q / |f|^α dm is lower semicontinuous on 𝒞 in L²(X, m).

items.label: q-Laplacian
items.statement: For f ∈ L²(X, m) with ∂⁻Ch_q(f) ≠ ∅, −Δ_q f is the element of minimal L² norm of ∂⁻Ch_q(f); D(Δ_q) is the set of such f.

items.label: Laplacian is homogeneous, not linear
items.statement: Even for q = 2, Δ_q need not be linear; v ∈ ∂⁻Ch_q(f) implies λ^{q−1}v ∈ ∂⁻Ch_q(λf), so Δ_q and the gradient flow are (q − 1)-homogeneous.

items.label: Integration by parts inequality
items.statement: For f ∈ D(Δ_q) and g ∈ D(Ch_q): −∫ g Δ_q f dm ≤ ∫ |∇g|_*,q |∇f|_*,q^{q−1} dm, with equality for g = φ(f), φ ∈ C¹(R) with bounded derivative on the image of f.

items.label: Properties of the Ch_q gradient flow
items.statement: For the gradient flow (f_t) of Ch_q from f_0 ∈ L²(X, m): ∫f_t dm = ∫f_0 dm; f_0 ≤ C (resp. ≥ c) implies f_t ≤ C (resp. ≥ c); and if 0 < c ≤ f_0 ≤ C and Φ ∈ C²([c, C]), then t ↦ ∫Φ(f_t) dm is locally absolutely continuous with derivative −∫Φ″(f_t)|∇f_t|_*,q^q dm a.e.
items.note: Not mapped: the Lean heat semigroup of KLS/LogConcave/HeatSemigroup/Markov.lean (mass preservation, sub-Markov bounds) is generated by the closed weighted-gradient form, and no Lean statement identifies it with the gradient flow of Cheeger.energy.

items.label: Entropy dissipation along W_p curves
items.statement: For compact (X, d), finite m and μ_t = f_t m ∈ AC^p([0,1], (P(X), W_p)) with c ≤ f_t ≤ C and f_0 Sobolev along q-a.e. curve with |∇f_0|_w,q ∈ L^q, every convex Φ ∈ C²([c, C]) satisfies ∫Φ(f_0) − ∫Φ(f_t) ≤ (1/q)∫∫_0^t (Φ″(f_0)|∇f_0|_w,q)^q f_s ds dm + (1/p)∫_0^t |μ̇_s|^p ds.

items.label: Kuwada's lemma
items.statement: For compact (X, d), finite m and the gradient flow (f_t) of Ch_q from f_0 with c ≤ f_0 ≤ C and ∫f_0 dm = 1, μ_t = f_t m is W_p-absolutely continuous and |μ̇_t|^p ≤ ∫ |∇f_t|_*,q^q / f_t^{p−1} dm for a.e. t.
items.note: The idea is credited to Kuwada (2010).

items.label: Weak gradient equals relaxed slope
items.statement: For compact (X, d) and finite m, if f : X → R is Borel, Sobolev along q-a.e. curve and |∇f|_w,q ∈ L^q(X, m), then f ∈ 𝒞 and |∇f|_*,q = |∇f|_w,q m-a.e.

items.label: Equivalence of weak gradients
items.statement: For compact (X, d), finite m and f ∈ L^q(X, m), the following are equivalent: f has a q-relaxed upper gradient; a q-relaxed slope; a q-upper gradient in L^q; a q-weak upper gradient in L^q. The four minimal gradients |∇f|_C,q, |∇f|_*,q, |∇f|_S,q and |∇f|_w,q then coincide m-a.e.
items.note: Section 8 extends it to bounded complete separable spaces with finite m and to locally finite spaces (S81, S82). No Lean declaration states weak, Mod_q or test-plan gradients.

items.label: Density with asymptotic Lipschitz constants
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 7.3 there are Lipschitz f_n → f m-a.e. with |∇f_n| → |∇f|_w,q in L^q, and even with Lip_a(f_n, ·) → |∇f|_w,q in L^q: the Cheeger energy relaxed from Lip_a coincides with Ch_q.
items.note: Lean proves the energy-level identity (relaxation of ∫Lip_a² equals relaxation of ∫|∇f|², and the two Cheeger conventions agree) only for q = 2 and Borel probability laws on finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, by a different route (McShane patches and mollification, not Hopf–Lax); weak upper gradients and the L^q convergence of Lip_a(f_n) are not stated. The paper only sketches the argument.

papers.title: Analysis and Geometry of Markov Diffusion Operators
papers.locator: Corollary 4.8.2 (Poincaré P(1/ρ) for e^{-W} dx with ∇∇W ≥ ρ Id); Propositions 4.1.1 and 4.3.1 as background
papers.result: Tensorization and Gaussian functional inequalities within the diffusion/Dirichlet-form framework.
papers.remaining: Corollary 4.8.2 is certified in a reviewed stronger form (thm:bakry-emery-poincare): C² potential, any normalization, any finite-dimensional real inner product space, through the semigroup route in the Euclidean heat model. The general Markov-triple, diffusion and Γ-calculus framework of the book is not formalized: Proposition 4.8.1 under CD(ρ, ∞) stays partial, and CD(ρ, n), Theorem 4.8.4, Riemannian versions and log-Sobolev inequalities are not covered. Coverage refers to the selected Corollary 4.8.2 only.

lemma_map.source_version: Springer 2014, Grundlehren der mathematischen Wissenschaften 348 (DOI 10.1007/978-3-319-00227-9), Chapter 4
lemma_map.standing_assumptions: Unless stated otherwise, the Full Markov Triple (E, μ, Γ) of Sect. 3.4 (called a Markov Triple): state space E, invariant reversible measure μ (a probability measure wherever a Poincaré inequality is stated), carré du champ Γ on an algebra A₀ of bounded measurable functions (smooth compactly supported functions in examples) with extended algebra A ⊃ A₀ for the Γ-calculus, Dirichlet form E(f) = ∫Γ(f) dμ with domain D(E) (A₀ dense in it), diffusion generator L with domain D(L), Markov semigroup P_t = e^{tL} with kernels p_t(x, dy), and Γ₂(f) = ½(LΓ(f) − 2Γ(f, Lf)). Var_μ(f) = ∫f² dμ − (∫f dμ)²; P(C) means Var_μ(f) ≤ C E(f) for f ∈ D(E) (Definition 4.2.1); CD(ρ, n) means Γ₂(f) ≥ ρΓ(f) + (Lf)²/n on A₀ (Definition 3.3.14), with CD(ρ, ∞) for n = ∞. Sect. 4.5.2 uses Diffusion Markov Triples, Sect. 4.6 allows infinite μ for local inequalities, Sect. 4.7 needs no invariant probability, and Sects. 4.10.1–4.10.2 use the minimal triple of Sect. 3.1. Repository counterparts (not identified with these notions): Poincare.SmoothTest.constant and Poincare.LocalSlope.Intrinsic.constant are ENNReal optimal constants over smooth L² finite-energy (resp. locally Lipschitz local-slope) tests with Γ(f) = |∇f|² on finite-dimensional real inner product spaces, and no Dirichlet-domain equivalence is asserted; the heat semigroup model in formalization/FunctionalInequalities/KLS/LogConcave/HeatSemigroup takes a full-dimensional log-concave law ν = m.tilted (−U) with smooth convex potential U, the closed weighted gradient T̄ and P_t = exp(−tT̄†T̄), whose generator is ℒf = Δf − ⟨∇U, ∇f⟩ on C_c^∞.

Page numbers are the printed pages where each statement begins.

items.locator: Proposition 4.1.1 (Poincaré inequality for the Gaussian measure), p. 180
items.label: Gaussian Poincaré inequality
items.statement: For the standard Gaussian measure μ on ℝⁿ and every f in the Dirichlet domain D(E): ∫f² dμ − (∫f dμ)² ≤ E(f) = ∫|∇f|² dμ, i.e. P(1). For a centered Gaussian with covariance matrix Q, Var_μ(f) ≤ ∫ Q∇f·∇f dμ for every smooth f.
items.note: The one-dimensional case (4.1.1) is proved by the Hermite expansion (Sect. 2.7.1); the n-dimensional case by multiple Hermite polynomials or tensorization (Proposition 4.3.1, see the remark after Remark 4.3.3); the covariance form by a change of variables. Affine functions are extremal. P(1) for the standard Gaussian on any finite-dimensional real inner product space, for smooth L² tests of finite energy (a dense class, as Definition 4.2.1 allows). The covariance clause is covered only in dimension one (holds_gaussianReal, with arbitrary variance v).

items.label: Poincaré inequality P(C)
items.statement: A Markov Triple (E, μ, Γ) with μ a probability measure satisfies a Poincaré (spectral gap) inequality P(C), C > 0, if Var_μ(f) ≤ C E(f) for all f ∈ D(E); the best such C is the Poincaré constant.
items.note: Variance (4.2.1). It suffices to check P(C) on a dense subfamily of D(E), typically A₀. Under P(C) the spectrum of −L lies in {0} ∪ [1/C, ∞) (Sect. A.4).

items.label: Poincaré inequalities are tight
items.statement: Under a Poincaré inequality, E(f) = 0 forces f to be μ-a.e. constant (tightness, strengthening ergodicity and connexity); a non-tight form ∫f² dμ ≤ a(∫f dμ)² + C E(f) on a probability space forces a ≥ 1 and reduces to the case a = 1.
items.note: Refers to Definition 3.1.11 (ergodicity), Definition 3.3.7 (connexity), Sect. 1.8 and the Nash-type inequalities of Sect. 7.4.1.

items.label: Poincaré for functions vanishing outside A
items.statement: Under P(C), if f ∈ D(E) vanishes outside a set A ∈ F with μ(A) < 1, then ∫ f² dμ ≤ (C/(1 − μ(A))) E(f).
items.note: Proof by Cauchy–Schwarz: (∫f dμ)² ≤ μ(A)∫f² dμ, so (1 − μ(A))∫f² dμ ≤ Var_μ(f).

items.label: Faber–Krahn-type inequalities
items.statement: Inequalities ∫_A f² dμ ≤ Θ(μ(A)) E(f) for f ∈ D(E) supported in A, with a function Θ of the measure of A, hold in various contexts, e.g. the Faber–Krahn inequalities associated with Nash inequalities.
items.note: Cross-references Remark 6.2.4 and Remark 8.2.2. The function symbol in front of μ(A) is lost in the extracted text; Θ is a placeholder.

items.label: Variance decay equivalent to Poincaré
items.statement: For a Markov Triple with semigroup (P_t)_{t≥0}, the following are equivalent: (i) P(C); (ii) Var_μ(P_t f) ≤ e^{−2t/C} Var_μ(f) for all f ∈ L²(μ) and t ≥ 0; (iii) for every f ∈ L²(μ) there is c(f) > 0 with Var_μ(P_t f) ≤ c(f) e^{−2t/C} for all t ≥ 0.
items.note: (ii)⇒(i) by a first-order expansion at t = 0; (i)⇒(ii) from d/dt Var_μ(P_t f) = −2E(P_t f) (4.2.2) and Gronwall; (iii)⇒(ii) by Lemma 4.2.6. Uses Proposition 3.1.6 and Remark 3.1.7 (P_t maps L² into D(Lᵏ)). The unnumbered consequence (4.2.3), ∫(f − P_t f)² dμ ≤ 2t E(f) for f ∈ D(E), is recorded here. Only (i) ⇒ (ii), for the heat semigroup of a full-dimensional log-concave law with the Poincaré hypothesis on the form domain.

items.label: Log-convexity of the L² norm
items.statement: For every non-zero f ∈ L²(μ), the map t ↦ log ‖P_t f‖₂ is convex on ℝ₊.
items.note: With Λ(t) = ∫(P_t f)² dμ, Λ″(t) = 4∫(LP_t f)² dμ and Cauchy–Schwarz gives Λ′² ≤ ΛΛ″.

items.label: Bounded perturbation
items.statement: If (E, μ, Γ) satisfies P(C) and μ₁ is a probability measure with density h with respect to μ such that 1/b ≤ h ≤ b for some b > 0, then μ₁ satisfies P(b³C) with respect to Γ.
items.note: Proof via the duplication formula (4.2.4), Var_ν(f) = ½∬(f(x) − f(y))² dν(x)dν(y). The text adds that Lemma 5.1.7 improves b³ to b², and to e^{osc(k)} when h = e^k. The preceding unnumbered observation (Γ ≤ aΓ₁ and P(C) for Γ give P(aC) for Γ₁) is recorded here.

items.label: Tensorization of Poincaré inequalities
items.statement: If (E₁, μ₁, Γ₁) and (E₂, μ₂, Γ₂) satisfy Poincaré inequalities with constants C₁ and C₂, then the product Markov Triple (E₁ × E₂, μ₁ ⊗ μ₂, Γ₁ ⊕ Γ₂) satisfies a Poincaré inequality with constant max(C₁, C₂).
items.note: Product Dirichlet form E(f) = ∫E₁(f) dμ₂ + ∫E₂(f) dμ₁ and the variance decomposition Var(f) = Var_{μ₁}(g) + ∫∫(f − g)² dμ₂ dμ₁ with g = ∫f dμ₂. Exact constant max(C₁, C₂), but for the Euclidean carré du champ on Hilbert spaces and smooth tests rather than general Markov Triples; finite products and the reverse bound are proved separately (constant_pi_eq, constant_prod_eq).

items.label: Partial integration and Dirichlet energy
items.statement: If f(x₁, x₂) is measurable in x₂ and f(·, x₂) ∈ D(E₁) for every x₂ ∈ E₂, then g(x₁) = ∫ f(x₁, x₂) dμ₂(x₂) lies in D(E₁) and E₁(g) ≤ ∫ E₁(f(·, x₂)) dμ₂(x₂).
items.note: Only sketched in the book: convexity of the Dirichlet form and Jensen's inequality, 'under suitable integrability properties'.

items.label: Tensorization via heat kernels
items.statement: With ν_t(dx, dy) = p_t(x, dy)μ(dx), ∬(f(x) − f(y))² dν_t = 2(∫f² dμ − ∫f P_t f dμ), and P(C) is equivalent to ∬(f(x) − f(y))² dν_t ≥ (1 − e^{−t/C}) ∬(f(x) − f(y))² dμ(x)dμ(y) for all t ≥ 0; this condition is stable under products since ν_t = ν_t¹ ⊗ ν_t², giving another proof of Proposition 4.3.1.
items.note: The following paragraph notes that Proposition 4.3.1 recovers Proposition 4.1.1 from (4.1.1).

items.label: Exponential measure on half-line
items.statement: For dμ(x) = e^{−x}dx on ℝ₊ and every f in the Dirichlet domain for Γ(f) = f′², Var_μ(f) ≤ 4 ∫_{ℝ₊} f′² dμ.
items.note: Proof: reduce to f(0) = 0, then ∫f² dμ = 2∫ff′ dμ and Cauchy–Schwarz. The book notes that this Dirichlet domain generates a sub-Markov semigroup (no ESA). Recorded here: the Laguerre form (4.4.1) Var_μ(f) ≤ ∫x f′² dμ, and P(4) for ½e^{−|x|}dx on ℝ (4.4.3) via h = |x|; the constant 4 is optimal (Proposition 4.4.2 with f = |x|).

items.label: Exponential integrability of Lipschitz functions
items.statement: If μ satisfies P(C) for some C > 0, then every 1-Lipschitz f (‖Γ(f)‖_∞ ≤ 1) satisfies ∫ e^{sf} dμ < ∞ for every s < 2/√C; more precisely ∫ e^{sf} dμ ≤ e^{s∫f dμ} ∏_{ℓ≥0} (1 − Cs²/4^{ℓ+1})^{−2^ℓ} (4.4.4).
items.note: Proof: apply P(C) to e^{sf/2} and iterate s → s/2; integrability of Lipschitz functions by truncation. Recorded here: (4.4.5) ∫e^{s(f − ∫f dμ)} dμ ≤ (2 + s√C)/(2 − s√C), the concentration bound (4.4.6) μ(f ≥ ∫f dμ + r) ≤ 3e^{−r/(√C‖f‖_Lip)}, and its dimension-free tensorized form via Proposition 4.3.1. The bound s < 2/√C is read from the proof (1 − Cs²/4 > 0); the extracted statement is garbled.

items.label: Lipschitz functions lie in D(E)
items.statement: Lipschitz functions lie a priori in A or D(E); part of Proposition 4.4.2 is that they belong to L²(μ), hence to D(E), and the proof (by truncation in D(E)) adapts to A by smooth truncation.

items.label: Contraction principle
items.statement: If (μ, Γ) satisfies P(C) on E and F : E → ℝ is 1-Lipschitz with respect to Γ, then the image measure μ_F of μ by F satisfies P(C) with respect to the usual carré du champ g′² on ℝ.
items.note: Var_{μ_F}(g) = Var_μ(g ∘ F) and Γ(g ∘ F) = g′(F)² Γ(F) ≤ g′(F)².

items.label: Concentration versus Poincaré
items.statement: Exponential integrability (Proposition 4.4.2) or the tail bound (4.4.6) do not imply a Poincaré inequality in general, but under CD(0, ∞) the concentration bound (4.4.6) implies P(C′) with a proportional constant.
items.note: Forward reference to Sect. 8.7, based on the reverse local inequalities of Theorem 4.7.2; no proof in this chapter.

items.label: Muckenhoupt criterion
items.statement: Let μ be a Borel probability measure on ℝ with Lebesgue density p and median m, and set B₊ = sup_{x>m} μ([x, ∞)) ∫_m^x dt/p(t) and B₋ = sup_{x<m} μ((−∞, x]) ∫_x^m dt/p(t). Then μ satisfies a Poincaré inequality for Γ(f) = f′² iff B = max(B₊, B₋) < ∞, and B ≤ 2C ≤ 8B where C is the Poincaré constant of μ.
items.note: Sufficiency (C ≤ 4B) by a weighted Cauchy–Schwarz with k = √h₊·p, proved with suprema over the smallest closed interval carrying μ (general case left to the reader); necessity (B ≤ 2C) by Lemma 4.2.3 with A = [m, ∞) and test functions ∫_m^x 1_{[m,r]}/(p + ε).

items.label: Integrable Hardy weights suffice
items.statement: If μ has density p and median m, and ∫_m^∞ h₊ p dx < ∞ and ∫_{−∞}^m h₋ p dx < ∞, where h₊(x) = ∫_m^x dt/p(t) (x ≥ m) and h₋(x) = ∫_x^m dt/p(t) (x ≤ m), then μ satisfies a Poincaré inequality with constant C = max(∫_m^∞ h₊ p dx, ∫_{−∞}^m h₋ p dx).
items.note: Proof by Cauchy–Schwarz on (f(x) − f(m))², as for Proposition 4.4.1.

items.label: Dirichlet Poincaré on an interval
items.statement: For Lf = f″ + (w′/w)f′ on a bounded interval I with w smooth, w ≥ a > 0 and invariant probability dμ = w dx, there is C > 0 with ∫_I f² dμ ≤ C ∫_I f′² dμ for all smooth f compactly supported in I (4.5.1); the best constant is 1/λ₀, where −λ₀ is the lowest eigenvalue of L with Dirichlet boundary conditions.
items.note: Proof via the Friedrichs extension and the discrete spectrum (Sect. 2.6); positivity and simplicity of λ₀ are stated without proof. Diffusion (not Full) Markov Triples in Sect. 4.5.2.

items.label: Neumann Poincaré on an interval
items.statement: In the setting of Proposition 4.5.3, there is C > 0 with Var_μ(f) ≤ C ∫_I f′² dμ for every smooth f on I (restriction of a smooth function on a neighbourhood of I) (4.5.2); the best constant is 1/λ₁, where −λ₁ is the first non-zero eigenvalue of L with Neumann boundary conditions.
items.note: As for Proposition 4.5.3 plus an approximation by functions with vanishing boundary derivatives; details left to the reader.

items.label: Sharp constants on [0, 1]
items.statement: For Lf = f″ on [0, 1] with Lebesgue measure: (i) ∫f² dx ≤ π^{−2}∫f′² dx if f(0) = f(1) = 0, sharp for sin(πx); (ii) Var(f) ≤ π^{−2}∫f′² dx for all smooth f, sharp for cos(πx); (iii) Var(f) ≤ (4π²)^{−1}∫f′² dx if f(0) = f(1), sharp for a cos(2πx) + b sin(2πx) + c (Wirtinger).
items.note: (iii) by Fourier series; (i) from (iii) by odd reflection and periodization; (ii) by even reflection (the text says 'from (i)', but the even extension satisfies the periodic condition of (iii)). (i) is the Dirichlet case of Proposition 4.5.3, (ii) the Neumann case of Proposition 4.5.4.

items.label: Local Poincaré equals Neumann Poincaré
items.statement: On ℝⁿ (or a manifold with a measure locally equivalent to Lebesgue measure) and K compact with smooth boundary, the local Poincaré inequality (4.6.1), ∫_K (f − m_K)² dμ ≤ C_K ∫_K Γ(f) dμ, is the Poincaré inequality on K with Neumann boundary conditions; the Dirichlet-type inequality (4.10.1) on a larger L ⊃ K gives the weaker form (4.6.2).
items.note: Approximation argument only sketched (normal coordinates near the boundary).

items.label: Lyapunov criterion
items.statement: Let (E, μ, Γ) be a Markov Triple with μ a probability measure satisfying the completeness property (Definition 3.3.9). If J : E → [1, ∞) in A satisfies 1 ≤ −LJ/(λJ) + b1_K with λ, b > 0, where K satisfies the local Poincaré inequality (4.6.2) ∫_K (f − m_K)² dμ ≤ C_{K,L} ∫_L Γ(f) dμ for some L ⊃ K, then μ satisfies P(C) with C = 1/λ + bC_{K,L}.
items.note: Proof: −∫(LJ/J)g² dμ = ∫Γ(g²/J, J) dμ ≤ ∫Γ(g) dμ by the diffusion property and Cauchy–Schwarz (1.4.3), with m = m_K; completeness justifies the integration by parts. Examples: the Gaussian with J = 1 + |x|², the exponential law with J = e^{c|x|}.

items.label: Log-concave measures satisfy Poincaré
items.statement: Every log-concave probability measure dμ = e^{−W}dx on ℝⁿ (W smooth and convex) satisfies a Poincaré inequality with respect to Γ(f) = |∇f|².
items.note: The source proof uses Theorem 4.6.2 with J = e^{c|x|} outside a ball; the convex-potential tail condition is left as an exercise. The declarations mapped here prove the one-dimensional bound C_P ≤ 4 Var. Separately, the certified BKL main line and KLS.kls supply a covariance-normalized bound in every finite dimension; this does not formalize the book's proof of Theorem 4.6.3 or its quoted Payne–Weinberger bound C_P ≤ D²/π². This item retains its mapped one-dimensional scope.

items.label: Glueing local Poincaré constants
items.statement: If K, L ⊂ E are measurable with μ(K ∩ L) > 0 and μ(K ∪ L) < ∞, then the local Poincaré constants of (4.6.1) satisfy C_{K∪L} ≤ (μ(K ∪ L)/μ(K ∩ L)) max(C_K, C_L).
items.note: μ need not be a probability measure; the local inequalities are assumed on a class A₁ of functions.

items.label: Mean-square glueing lemma
items.statement: In a measure space with μ(K ∩ L) > 0 and μ(K ∪ L) < ∞, every measurable f with ∫_{K∪L} f² dμ < ∞ and ∫_{K∪L} f dμ = 0 satisfies (1/μ(K))(∫_K f dμ)² + (1/μ(L))(∫_L f dμ)² ≤ (1 − μ(K ∩ L)/μ(K ∪ L)) ∫_{K∪L} f² dμ.
items.note: Cauchy–Schwarz on K \ L, L \ K and K ∩ L; the final optimization is left as 'tedious details'.

items.label: Gaussian heat kernel inequalities
items.statement: Since the Brownian and Ornstein–Uhlenbeck heat kernels are Gaussian, the local inequalities (4.7.2) P_t(f²) − (P_t f)² ≤ (1 − e^{−2t})P_tΓ(f) and (4.7.4) 2tΓ(P_t f) ≤ P_t(f²) − (P_t f)² ≤ 2tP_tΓ(f) are variants of Proposition 4.1.1 with other means and variances.
items.note: The semigroup-interpolation proofs of (4.7.1)–(4.7.4) precede the remark; the point is the approach via commutation and Γ₂.

items.label: Local Poincaré under CD(ρ, ∞)
items.statement: For a Markov Triple with semigroup (P_t) and ρ ∈ ℝ, the following are equivalent: (i) CD(ρ, ∞); (ii) Γ(P_t f) ≤ e^{−2ρt} P_tΓ(f); (iii) P_t(f²) − (P_t f)² ≤ ((1 − e^{−2ρt})/ρ) P_tΓ(f); (iv) P_t(f²) − (P_t f)² ≥ ((e^{2ρt} − 1)/ρ) Γ(P_t f); each for all f ∈ A₀ and t ≥ 0, the constants being read as 2t when ρ = 0.
