items.note: (i)⇔(ii) is Corollary 3.3.19; (ii)⇒(iii),(iv) by the interpolation s ↦ P_s((P_{t−s}f)²); (iii) or (iv)⇒(i) by a second-order expansion at t = 0. Consequence (4.7.7): Γ(P_t f) ≤ ρ/(e^{2ρt} − 1) for measurable |f| ≤ 1. Assertions (ii) and (iv) at ρ = 0 only, integrated against nonnegative C_c^∞ tests, for e^{-U} with smooth convex U.

items.label: Gradient bound with constant K
items.statement: The implications (ii)⇒(iii),(iv) of Theorem 4.7.2 persist if Γ(P_t f) ≤ Ke^{−2ρt}P_tΓ(f) with some K ≥ 1, giving e.g. P_t(f²) − (P_t f)² ≤ (K(1 − e^{−2ρt})/ρ) P_tΓ(f); only K = 1 returns CD(ρ, ∞).
items.note: Relevant for hypocoercive examples (Remark 3.3.22).

items.label: Small-time characterization of CD(ρ, ∞)
items.statement: Each assertion of Theorem 4.7.2 is equivalent to the existence of t₀ > 0 and c(t) = 2t − 2ρt² + o(t²) such that P_t(f²) − (P_t f)² ≤ c(t)P_tΓ(f) (respectively ≥ c(t)Γ(P_t f)) for all t ∈ (0, t₀) and f ∈ A₀.
items.note: Read off from the proof of Theorem 4.7.2. The book states the same c(t) for both directions; the expansion of (e^{2ρt} − 1)/ρ in (iv) is 2t + 2ρt² + o(t²), so the reverse case as printed needs review.

items.label: Poincaré under CD(ρ, ∞)
items.statement: Under the curvature condition CD(ρ, ∞) with ρ > 0, the Markov Triple satisfies P(1/ρ): Var_μ(f) ≤ (1/ρ) E(f) for every f ∈ D(E).
items.note: Let t → ∞ in (4.7.5) of Theorem 4.7.2, using Theorem 3.3.23 (μ finite when ρ > 0) and ergodicity P_∞ f = ∫f dμ (Sect. 1.8). Formally the case n = ∞ of Theorem 4.8.4. The semigroup argument is formalized abstractly (finite-time bound ‖f‖² − ‖P_t f‖² ≤ (1 − e^{-2ρt})/ρ ‖Tf‖² under ρ‖Ty‖² ≤ ‖Ay‖²) and for the Euclidean heat model, where ergodicity is now proved (2026-10-04: tendsto_norm_center_apply) and P(1/ρ) holds on the whole form domain (norm_center_sq_le_inv_mul); no general Markov-Triple CD(ρ, ∞) framework, so the relation stays partial.

items.label: Strongly log-concave measures: P(1/ρ)
items.statement: Let dμ = e^{−W}dx be a probability measure on the Borel sets of ℝⁿ, where W : ℝⁿ → ℝ is smooth with ∇∇W ≥ ρ Id for some ρ > 0. Then μ satisfies P(1/ρ): Var_μ(f) ≤ (1/ρ) ∫|∇f|² dμ.
items.note: Proof: L = Δ − ∇W·∇ with Γ(f) = |∇f|² (Sect. 1.11.3) and Γ₂(f) = |∇∇f|² + ∇∇W(∇f, ∇f) ≥ ρΓ(f) ((1.16.5)), so CD(ρ, ∞) holds and Proposition 4.8.1 applies. Also a consequence of Theorem 4.9.1. The weighted Riemannian analogue under Ric_g + ∇∇W ≥ ρg is stated without a separate proof. Local Lean proof (2026-10-04), a reviewed stronger statement: for ν = volume.tilted (−W) on any finite-dimensional real inner product space (ℝⁿ as EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), n = 0 included), W of class C² (the book: smooth) and ρ‖v‖² ≤ D²W(x)(v, v), ρ > 0, the literature Poincaré constant satisfies C_P(ν) ≤ 1/ρ (literatureConstant_le_inv_of_eq_tilted) and Var_ν(f) ≤ ρ⁻¹ ∫‖∇f‖² dν for smooth L² tests with L² gradient (smoothTest_holds_inv_of_eq_tilted). The tilted law has density e^{−W}/∫e^{−W}, so the book's normalized e^{−W} dx is the case ∫e^{−W} = 1. The Dirichlet-domain form Var(u) ≤ ρ⁻¹‖T̄u‖² holds for every u in the domain of the closed unit gradient, the closure of C_c^∞ in the energy norm, i.e. the book's D(E) (norm_center_sq_le_inv_mul, heat model ν = m.tilted (−U) for any Haar m), and the literature constant equals the optimal constant on that domain (closedWeightedOperator_id_constant_eq_literature). Route: ergodicity from ker T̄ = constants (WeightedGradient/Kernel.lean, Energy/Euclidean/ZeroGradient.lean) and strong convergence on (ker T)ᗮ (Analysis/Semigroup/Generated/Convergence.lean); log-concavity and full support of the tilted law (Density/Tilted.lean). Registered as the paper-target certificate thm:bakry-emery-poincare (owner review accepted 2026-10-04, relation stronger); the certificate's gaussian witness constructs the scaled Gaussian law and discharges every hypothesis, so the statement is not vacuous.

items.label: Dual form of Poincaré
items.statement: A Markov Triple satisfies P(C) for some C > 0 iff E(f) = ∫Γ(f) dμ ≤ C ∫(Lf)² dμ for every f ∈ D(L) (4.8.2).
items.note: ⇒ by Cauchy–Schwarz ∫f(−Lf) dμ ≤ Var_μ(f)^{1/2}‖Lf‖₂ and P(C); ⇐ via Λ(t) = ∫(P_t f)² dμ with Λ″ ≥ −(2/C)Λ′, as in the proof of Lemma 4.2.6. Under ESA, (4.8.2) is equivalent to E(f) ≤ C∫Γ₂(f) dμ on A₀ (4.8.3).

items.locator: Theorem 4.8.4 (Poincaré inequality under CD(ρ, n)), p. 215
items.label: Poincaré under CD(ρ, n)
items.statement: Under the curvature-dimension condition CD(ρ, n) with ρ > 0 and n > 1, the Markov Triple satisfies P(C) with C = (n − 1)/(ρn).
items.note: Integrate CD(ρ, n) and use ∫Γ₂(f) dμ = ∫(Lf)² dμ to get (4.8.2) with C = (n − 1)/(ρn). Includes the Lichnerowicz bound λ₁ ≥ ρn/(n − 1) (4.8.1), sharp on the sphere Sⁿ (CD(n − 1, n)).

items.label: Brascamp–Lieb inequality
items.statement: For a probability measure dμ = e^{−W}dx on ℝⁿ with W smooth and strictly convex, Var_μ(f) ≤ ∫(∇∇W)^{−1}(∇f, ∇f) dμ for every smooth compactly supported f.
items.note: Proof only sketched: vector-valued operator on H = L²(μ)ⁿ, commutation ∇Lf = (L − ∇∇W)∇f (4.9.2), Lemma 4.9.2 with A₁ = ε + M and A₂ = ε + M − L, g_ε = (ε − L)^{−1/2}f and ε → 0. Improves Corollary 4.8.2 when ∇∇W ≥ ρ Id.

items.label: Operator monotonicity of inversion
items.statement: Let A₁, A₂ be symmetric operators on a common dense domain D₀ of a Hilbert space H with ε⟨u, u⟩ ≤ ⟨A₁u, u⟩ ≤ ⟨A₂u, u⟩ for some ε > 0 and all u ∈ D₀. Then the Friedrichs extensions have bounded inverses of norm at most 1/ε, and ⟨A₂^{−1}u, u⟩ ≤ ⟨A₁^{−1}u, u⟩ for every u ∈ H.
items.note: Reduce to u = A₂v with v ∈ D(A₂) ⊂ D(A₁); with B = A₂ − A₁ ≥ 0 the claim is ⟨A₁^{−1}Bv, Bv⟩ + ⟨Bv, v⟩ ≥ 0.

items.label: Riemannian Brascamp–Lieb inequality
items.statement: On a weighted Riemannian manifold with L = Δ_g − ∇W·∇ and reversible probability μ with density e^{−W}, if Ric(L) = Ric_g + ∇∇W is positive definite everywhere, then Var_μ(f) ≤ ∫ Ric(L)^{−1}(∇f, ∇f) dμ for every smooth compactly supported f.
items.note: Proof only indicated: as for Theorem 4.9.1 with 1-forms and the commutation dLf = (L − Ric(L))df. Recorded here: the consequence (4.9.4) Var_μ(f) ≤ ∫|∇f|²/ρ(x) dμ and the Feynman–Kac (Bismut) representation (4.9.5)–(4.9.6) of Sect. 4.9.2, which uses Proposition 3.2.5.

items.label: Dirichlet eigenvalue and exit time
items.statement: For the Laplacian on a relatively compact open O ⊂ ℝⁿ with Dirichlet conditions and the Brownian exit time T, E_x(e^{λT}) < ∞ for λ < λ₀ and E_x(e^{λT}) = ∞ for λ ≥ λ₀, where λ₀ is the bottom of the spectrum of −Δ with Dirichlet conditions.
items.note: Heuristic martingale argument with the positive ground state; not a complete proof. The spectral reading of (4.10.1) ∫f² dμ ≤ C E(f), with best constant 1/λ₀, is recorded here.

items.label: Hyperbolic space spectral bound
items.statement: On hyperbolic space Hⁿ (n ≥ 2) in the upper half-space model with dμ = x_n^{−n}dx and Γ(f) = x_n²|∇f|², every smooth compactly supported f satisfies ∫ f² dμ ≤ (4/(n − 1)²) E(f).
items.note: Proof as for Proposition 4.4.1, from L x_n = −(n − 2)x_n, Γ(x_n) = x_n² and Cauchy–Schwarz (the written argument divides by n − 2). Optimality of 4/(n − 1)² is asserted ('one may check').

items.label: Essential spectrum and finite-rank defect
items.statement: If σ_ess(−L) ⊂ [σ₀, ∞) with σ₀ > 0, then for every r > 1/σ₀ there is a finite-dimensional subspace F ⊂ L²(μ) with ∫f² dμ ≤ r E(f) + ∫(Π_F f)² dμ for all f ∈ D(E) (4.10.2), Π_F the orthogonal projection onto F; conversely, if (4.10.2) holds for some r > 0 and some finite-dimensional F, then σ_ess(−L) ⊂ [1/r, ∞).
items.note: Converse by Weyl's criterion (Theorem A.4.4) and weak convergence of orthonormal sequences. Minimal Markov triple setting (Sect. 3.1).

items.label: Discrete spectrum gives weighted Nash
items.statement: If σ_ess(−L) = ∅, there exist a positive w ∈ L²(μ) and β : (0, ∞) → (0, ∞) with ∫f² dμ ≤ r E(f) + β(r)(∫|f|w dμ)² for all r > 0 and f ∈ D(E) (4.10.3); equivalently, there are a positive w ∈ L²(μ) and an increasing concave Φ : (0, ∞) → (0, ∞) with Φ(r)/r → 0 as r → ∞ such that ∫f² dμ ≤ Φ(E(f)) whenever ∫|f|w dμ = 1 (4.10.4).
items.note: w = Σα_k|f_k| over an eigenbasis, β(r) = n(r)α_{n(r)}^{−2}, Φ(r) = inf_{s>0}(rs + β(s)). Generalized weighted Nash inequalities, Sect. 7.4.3.

items.label: Weighted Nash with kernel: σ_ess bound
items.statement: If for some r > 0 and positive w ∈ L²(μ), ∫f² dμ ≤ r E(f) + (∫|f|w dμ)² for all f ∈ D(E) (4.10.5), and P_t has an L²-density kernel for some t > 0, then σ_ess(−L) ⊂ [1/r, ∞). In particular, if (4.10.3) holds for every r > 0 with some β(r) and P_t has an L²-density kernel for some t > 0, then the spectrum of −L is discrete.
items.note: Due to F.-Y. Wang. Compactness of the closure of P_t(G_w), G_w = {|g| ≤ w}, plus Weyl's criterion as in Proposition 4.10.3. The kernel hypothesis may be replaced by operator-norm approximation by kernel operators.

items.label: Persson operator
items.statement: Given an increasing sequence (A_k) of measurable sets with ∪A_k = E and μ(A_k) < ∞, L is Persson with respect to (A_k) if λ_ess = inf σ_ess(−L) equals sup_k λ_k, where λ_k = inf{E(f) : f ∈ D(E), f = 0 on A_k, ∫f² dμ = 1}.
items.note: The sequence (λ_k) is increasing; for a Persson operator, λ_k → ∞ gives a discrete spectrum.

items.label: Criterion for Persson operators
items.statement: If for each k there is ψ_k ∈ D(E) with values in [0, 1], ψ_k = 0 on A_k, ψ_k = 1 on A_{k+1}^c and Γ(ψ_k) bounded, and the embedding H¹(A_k) → L²(A_k, μ) is compact for each k, then L is Persson with respect to (A_k).
items.note: λ_ess ≤ sup λ_k holds for every exhaustion; the reverse inequality uses Weyl's criterion (Theorem A.4.4), compactness and the cutoffs ψ_k.

items.label: Persson: discreteness iff weighted Nash
items.statement: If L is Persson, the spectrum of −L is discrete iff there is a positive w ∈ L²(μ) such that for every r > 0 some β(r) > 0 gives ∫f² dμ ≤ r E(f) + β(r)(∫|f|w dμ)² for all f ∈ D(E).
items.note: ⇐: choose k(r) with β(r)∫_{A_k^c} w² dμ ≤ ½ to get λ_{k(r)} ≥ 1/(2r); ⇒ is Proposition 4.10.4.

items.label: Discrete spectrum criterion on ℝⁿ
items.statement: For L = Δ − ∇W·∇ on ℝⁿ (dμ = e^{−W}dx) with lim_{|x|→∞}(−ΔW(x) + ½|∇W|²(x)) = ∞, the spectrum of −L is discrete; the same holds on an open O ⊂ ℝⁿ if L is essentially self-adjoint on C_c^∞(O) and the limit holds at the boundary of O.
items.note: The Laplacian symbols are lost in the extracted text and are restored from the proof (R = −½ΔW + ¼|∇W|²). Proof: balls A_k, Proposition 4.10.7 with Rellich–Kondrachov (Theorem 6.4.3), ground-state transform f = g e^{W/2}; ESA on ℝⁿ by Corollary 3.2.2. The open-set proof uses an exhaustion {J ≤ k} not defined in the text. Example: c_α e^{−|x|^α}dx, α > 1, has discrete spectrum.

papers.title: Logarithmically-concave moment measures I
papers.result: Develops the Hessian metric and weighted Poincaré structure associated with log-concave moment measures.
papers.remaining: The paper's smooth moment-map geometry, Hessian metric and weighted geometric identities are not locally formalized. The separate bounded-isotropic moment-map producer and weak regular-source package used by the compact Letwin proof are restricted supporting results, not a formalization of this paper's smooth source theory.

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: mu is a log-concave probability measure on R^n with barycenter at the origin, supported on a bounded open convex set K (convex body), with density e^{-rho}, rho : K -> R convex, C^infinity, and bounded with all derivatives (condition (1)); psi : R^n -> R is the convex function, unique up to translation (normalised to be centered in Section 2), whose moment measure is mu, i.e. (nabla psi)_# e^{-psi(x)} dx = mu; under (1) psi is finite and C^infinity (condition (2), quoted from Wang-Zhu, Donaldson and Berman-Berndtsson) and solves the transport equation e^{-rho(nabla psi)} det Hess psi = e^{-psi} (display (3)). phi = psi^* is the Legendre transform, smooth with positive definite Hessian on K, (phi^{ij}) = (Hess phi)^{-1} and Einstein summation is used. M_mu^* = (R^n, Hess psi, e^{-psi} dx) and M_mu = (K, Hess phi, mu) are isomorphic weighted Riemannian manifolds via nabla psi. R(K) = sup_{x in K} |x| is the outer radius. Section 2 allows arbitrary centered convex psi with compactly supported moment measures; Section 4 allows a general potential V in place of psi and an open K; Section 3, Lemma 5.5 and Corollary 5.7 add the strict-convexity condition (star): smooth boundary of K with positive Gauss curvature and Hess rho >= eps_0 Id.
lemma_map.omitted: Remark 4.8 is omitted as purely expository (the stochastic language is a matter of taste and the arguments can be rephrased analytically, as in Grigor'yan Sections 7.4 and 8.4). The unnumbered Introduction properties (i)-(iii) of M_mu (stochastic completeness, Bakry-Emery-Ricci tensor at least half the metric after Kolesnikov Theorem 4.3, and first nonzero eigenvalue -1 with linear eigenfunctions), the quoted regularity facts (1) => (2), and the unnumbered Section 6 transport of the Brascamp-Lieb inequality to Var_mu(f) <= int phi^{ij} f_i f_j dmu are not listed, as no Lean declaration states them. The paper has no numbered Definitions, Facts, Claims, Conjectures or appendix statements; its five theorem-like environments share the section-wise theorem counter.

items.label: Laplacian bound for moment map
items.statement: Let mu be a log-concave probability measure on R^n with barycenter at the origin, supported on a bounded open convex set K with density e^{-rho}, rho convex, C^infinity, and bounded with all its derivatives on K (condition (1)), and let psi be the smooth convex function whose moment measure is mu. Then Delta psi(x) <= 2 R(K)^2 for every x in R^n, where R(K) = sup_{x in K} |x|.
items.note: Main theorem: it is the first statement of the paper, the result announced in the abstract (bounding the second derivatives of the toric Kahler-Einstein solution), and Section 5 is its proof; Corollary 1.2 and Proposition 6.1 are applications. Proof: under the strict-convexity assumptions (smooth K with positive Gauss curvature, Hess rho >= eps_0 Id), Corollary 5.7 at t = log 2 gives Tr (Hess phi)^{-1}(z) <= 2 Tr Cov(X_t^{(z)}) <= 2 R(K)^2 and Hess psi(x) = (Hess phi)^{-1}(nabla psi(x)); the general case follows by approximating mu by such measures mu_l, using Proposition 2.1 to get psi_l -> psi pointwise, Rockafellar Theorem 24.5 for the gradients, and the divergence theorem on small balls. Smoothness of psi (condition (2)) and the transport equation (3) are quoted from Wang-Zhu, Donaldson and Berman-Berndtsson. No Lean counterpart: the library has no moment measures, Legendre-dual Hessian metrics or Monge-Ampere equations.

items.label: Payne-Weinberger type Poincare bound
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.1, every mu-integrable smooth f : K -> R satisfies int f^2 dmu - (int f dmu)^2 <= 2 R(K)^2 int_K |nabla f|^2 dmu.
items.note: Proved at the end of Section 6: the Brascamp-Lieb inequality for e^{-psi}, transported by nabla psi, gives Var_mu(f) <= int phi^{ij} f_i f_j dmu (display (90)), and Theorem 1.1 yields (Hess phi)^{-1} <= 2 R(K)^2 Id. The constant 2 R(K)^2 is not optimal (Payne-Weinberger give 4 R(K)^2 / pi^2 for symmetric convex bodies). No Lean counterpart: no Lean theorem bounds Poincare.LocalSlope.Intrinsic.constant by an outer radius; such a statement would read Intrinsic.constant mu <= 2 R(K)^2 for laws with LogConcave mu and the regularity (1), and through Intrinsic.constant_eq_iInf_gradient_of_logConcave it would follow from this gradient form only after extending from smooth to locally Lipschitz tests. The definition alone does not state the item, so it is not mapped.

items.label: Continuity of the moment measure
items.statement: Let Omega be a compact subset of R^n and let psi, psi_1, psi_2, ... : R^n -> R be centered convex functions (int e^{-psi} = 1 and barycenter of e^{-psi} dx at the origin) whose moment measures mu, mu_1, mu_2, ... are supported in Omega. Then psi_l -> psi pointwise on R^n if and only if mu_l -> mu weakly, i.e. int b dmu_l -> int b dmu for every continuous b : Omega -> R.
items.note: (i) => (ii): local uniform convergence (Rockafellar Theorem 10.8), gradient convergence (Theorem 24.5) and dominated convergence via the linear lower bound from Lemma 2.2. (ii) => (i): nondegeneracy of mu (Cordero-Erausquin-Klartag Proposition 1), the uniform two-sided linear bounds of Lemma 2.3 with L = sup_{Omega} |x|, Arzela-Ascoli, the direction (i) => (ii), and uniqueness of moment-measure potentials (Cordero-Erausquin-Klartag). No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Linear growth of centered potentials
items.statement: If psi : R^n -> R is a centered convex function, then psi(x) >= n ||x||_psi + psi(0) - 2n for every x in R^n, where ||.||_psi is the Minkowski functional of K(psi) = {x : psi(x) <= 2n + inf psi}.
items.note: Proof: Fradelizi's inequality psi(0) <= n + inf psi for centered log-concave densities, then convexity along the ray through x / ||x||_psi. Stated as well known, proof given for completeness. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Two-sided linear bounds
items.statement: Let L, eps > 0 and let psi : R^n -> R be a centered, L-Lipschitz convex function with int |nabla psi(x) . theta| e^{-psi(x)} dx >= eps for every theta in S^{n-1}. Then alpha |x| - beta <= psi(x) <= L |x| + gamma for all x in R^n, with alpha, beta, gamma > 0 depending only on L, eps and n.
items.note: Proof: Fubini along lines gives int |nabla psi . theta| e^{-psi} = 2 int_{theta^perp} e^{-m_theta}, a convexity argument bounds this by 2^n e^{2n} / |I_theta|, so K(psi) is contained in B(0, C_n / eps); Lemma 2.2 then gives the lower bound and integrability gives psi(0) bounded above and below. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Hessian of psi is bounded
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.1, assume further (condition (star)) that K has smooth boundary with everywhere positive Gauss curvature and Hess rho >= eps_0 Id on K for some eps_0 > 0. Then sup_{x in R^n} ||Hess psi(x)||_op < +infinity.
items.note: A preliminary weak form of Theorem 1.1, needed in Lemma 5.5. Proof follows Caffarelli's contraction theorem: the maximum principle for the second difference delta_{theta theta}^{(eps)} psi, whose supremum is attained by Corollary 3.4, combined with the concavity inequality log det B <= log det A + Tr[A^{-1} B] - n and the transport equation, yields delta_{theta theta}^{(eps)} psi <= 4 eps^2 / eps_0. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Legendre dual is bounded
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Section 3, sup_{x in K} phi(x) < +infinity, where phi = psi^* is the Legendre transform.
items.note: Attributed to Berman-Berndtsson, proof reproduced: Morrey-Sobolev embedding on the convex domain K with int_K |nabla phi|^p dx < infinity for some p > n, from int_K |nabla phi|^p dmu = int |x|^p e^{-psi(x)} dx (pushforward) and boundedness of rho. Uses only the exponential decay of e^{-psi}, display (8). No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Gradient approaches support function gradient
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Section 3 (including (star)), lim_{R -> infinity} sup_{|x| >= R} |nabla psi(x) - nabla h_K(x)| = 0, where h_K(x) = sup_{y in K} x . y is the support function of K.
items.note: Analogue of Caffarelli's Lemma 4. Proof: with M = sup_K |phi| (Lemma 3.2), Legendre duality gives (nabla h_K(x) - nabla psi(x)) . x/|x| <= 2M/|x|, and positive Gauss curvature of the boundary converts this into |nabla h_K(x) - nabla psi(x)| <= alpha_K sqrt(2M/|x|) for |x| >= R_K. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Second difference attains supremum
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Section 3 (including (star)), for each fixed 0 < eps < 1 the supremum of delta_{theta theta}^{(eps)} psi(x) = psi(x + eps theta) + psi(x - eps theta) - 2 psi(x) over x in R^n and theta in S^{n-1} is attained.
items.note: Proof: Lemma 3.3 and the 0-homogeneity and continuity of nabla h_K show the second difference tends to 0 uniformly as |x| -> infinity, and it is nonnegative and continuous. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Explicit operator norm bound
items.statement: The proof of Proposition 3.1 gives sup_{x in R^n} ||Hess psi(x)||_op <= 4 / eps_0; arguing as in Caffarelli's erratum, the bound improves to 1 / eps_0.
items.note: The bound 4 / eps_0 is proved in the proof of Proposition 3.1; the improvement to 1 / eps_0 is asserted with details omitted. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Stochastic completeness criterion
items.statement: Let K be an open subset of R^n and V, psi : R^n -> R, rho : K -> R smooth with psi convex, inf_{|x| >= R} psi(x) -> +infinity as R -> infinity, e^{-rho(nabla psi(x))} det Hess psi(x) = e^{-V(x)} on R^n, and inf_{x in K} nabla rho(x) . x > -infinity. Then the weighted Riemannian manifold (R^n, Hess psi, e^{-V(x)} dx) is stochastically complete.
items.note: Stochastic completeness is defined as non-explosion of the Ito diffusion dY = sqrt(2) (Hess psi(Y))^{-1/2} dB - nabla rho(nabla psi(Y)) dt with generator L; the proposition is stated to follow from Proposition 4.5. Generalises Kolesnikov's setting. No Lean counterpart: no Riemannian metrics or SDEs in the library.

items.label: Log-concave case is stochastically complete
items.statement: When V = psi the manifold of Proposition 4.1 is M_mu^* = (R^n, Hess psi, e^{-psi} dx); if mu is log-concave with barycenter at the origin then nabla rho(x) . x >= rho(x) - rho(0) >= -n on K, so M_mu^* is stochastically complete whenever mu also satisfies condition (1).
items.note: Uses Fradelizi's inequality rho(0) <= n + inf_K rho and convexity of rho. This is property (i) of the Introduction; Section 5 transfers it to M_mu = (K, Hess phi, mu) via the isomorphism nabla psi. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Laplacian in moment coordinates
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Proposition 4.1, the Laplacian of (R^n, Hess psi, e^{-V} dx) is L u = psi^{ij} u_{ij} - sum_j rho_j(nabla psi(x)) u_j for every smooth u : R^n -> R, where (psi^{ij}) = (Hess psi)^{-1}.
items.note: Proof: logarithmic derivative of the transport equation e^{-rho(nabla psi)} det Hess psi = e^{-V} gives psi^{ij}_i = -psi^{jl} V_l + rho_j(nabla psi), substituted into L u = psi^{ij} u_{ij} - (psi^{ij}_j + psi^{ij} V_j) u_i (display (55)). No Lean counterpart: FunctionalInequalities.Analysis.BakryEmery.weightedLaplacian is the Euclidean-metric operator Delta f - <nabla U, nabla f>, not this Hessian-metric Laplacian, and is not mapped.

items.label: L psi bounded above
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Proposition 4.1 there is A >= 0 with (L psi)(x) <= A for every x in R^n; one may take A = max{0, n - inf_{y in K} nabla rho(y) . y}.
items.note: Proof: by Lemma 4.3, L psi = n - sum_j rho_j(nabla psi) psi_j, and nabla psi(x) lies in K. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Global non-exploding diffusion
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Proposition 4.1, for every z in R^n there is a unique process (Y_t)_{t >= 0} adapted to the Brownian filtration, almost surely continuous, with Y_t = z + int_0^t sqrt(2) (Hess psi(Y_s))^{-1/2} dB_s - int_0^t nabla rho(nabla psi(Y_s)) ds for all t >= 0.
items.note: Proof: local solutions up to the exit times T_k of {psi < k} (Kallenberg Theorem 21.3), Dynkin's formula with L psi <= A from Lemma 4.4, and Markov's inequality give P(T_k <= t) <= (2At + psi(z) + alpha)/(k + alpha) -> 0. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Symmetric smooth heat kernel
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Proposition 4.1, with nu = e^{-V(x)} dx, there is a smooth function p_t(x, y) (x, y in R^n, t > 0), symmetric in x and y, such that for every y in R^n and t > 0 the random vector Y_t^{(y)} of Proposition 4.5 has density x -> p_t(x, y) with respect to nu.
items.note: Proof: existence of the minimal heat kernel (Grigor'yan Theorems 7.13 and 7.20), then Ito's formula for v(t_0 - t, Y_t) with v the heat extension of a compactly supported test, the bounded local martingale being a martingale. The author notes it is standard but found no precise reference. No Lean counterpart; the library's heat semigroup KLS/LogConcave/HeatSemigroup is the Euclidean-metric L^2 semigroup and has no kernel.

items.label: Stationarity of nu
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Proposition 4.1, if Z is distributed according to nu = e^{-V(x)} dx and is independent of the Brownian motion, then Y_t^{(Z)} is distributed according to nu for every t >= 0.
items.note: Proof: Fubini with the symmetry of p_t and int p_t(x, z) dnu(z) = 1 (stochastic completeness). Implicitly nu is a probability measure. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Laplacian of M_mu
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.1, the operator L u(x) = phi^{ij}(x) u_{ij}(x) - x^i u_i(x) on smooth u : K -> R, with (phi^{ij}) = (Hess phi)^{-1} and phi = psi^*, is the Laplacian of the weighted Riemannian manifold M_mu = (K, Hess phi, mu): int_K phi^{ij} u_i v_j dmu = -int_K v L u dmu whenever one of the smooth u, v is compactly supported.
items.note: Proof: the dual transport equation det Hess phi(x) = e^{x . nabla phi(x) - phi(x) - rho(x)} gives phi^{ij}_j = x^i - phi^{ij} rho_j, then integration by parts as in Lemma 4.3. In particular L x^i = -x^i (Section 6). No Lean counterpart: FunctionalInequalities.KLS.LogConcave.integral_inner_gradient_eq is weighted integration by parts for the Euclidean Dirichlet form int <nabla f, nabla g> dnu with nu = m.tilted(-U); it does not state or restrict this Hessian-metric identity (the two coincide only if Hess phi = Id, which the dual transport equation excludes for a probability measure on a bounded K), so it is not mapped.

items.label: Power of phi^{11} supersolution
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.1, fix eps > 0 and let f(x) = phi^{11}(x) on K. Then L(f^eps) + eps f^eps >= 0 on K, with L the Laplacian of Lemma 5.1.
items.note: Proof: differentiating the logarithm of the dual transport equation twice gives L f = phi^{1j}_k phi^{1k}_j - phi^{11} + rho_{il} phi^{1i} phi^{1l} >= phi^{1j}_k phi^{1k}_j - f by convexity of rho; the chain rule for t -> t^eps and the Hilbert-Schmidt versus operator norm bound phi^{1j}_k phi^{1k}_j >= phi^{11}_j phi^{11j} / phi^{11} finish. Related to Gamma_2 >= Gamma/2 (property (ii), Kolesnikov); for eps >= 1/2 it follows from Bakry's Lemma 2.4. No Lean counterpart: FunctionalInequalities.Analysis.BakryEmery.gammaTwo and its Bochner bounds are for the Euclidean metric with drift nabla U, not the Hessian metric, and do not restrict this item.

items.label: Mean and second moment
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.1, for z in K let X_t = X_t^{(z)} solve dX_t = sqrt(2) (Hess phi(X_t))^{-1/2} dB_t - X_t dt, X_0 = z. Then E X_t = e^{-t} z for all t >= 0, and for every theta in S^{n-1}, e^{2t} E (X_t . theta)^2 >= (z . theta)^2 + 2 int_0^t e^{2s} E[(Hess phi)^{-1}(X_s) theta . theta] ds.
items.note: The process exists for all time by Section 4 (stochastic completeness of M_mu^*, Remark 4.2, transported to M_mu by the isomorphism nabla psi). Proof: e^t X_t is a bounded local martingale since K is bounded; for the second moment, the local martingale part of e^{2t}(X_t . e_1)^2 is bounded above, hence a submartingale by Fatou. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Equality in second moment
items.statement: Once Theorem 1.1 is established, equality holds in the second-moment inequality of Lemma 5.3, since the local martingale there is then bounded and hence a martingale.
items.note: A posteriori strengthening; not used later. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Reverse bound along diffusion
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.1, assume that K has smooth boundary with everywhere positive Gauss curvature and Hess rho >= eps_0 Id on K for some eps_0 > 0. For z in K, X_t = X_t^{(z)} and f = phi^{11}, f(z) <= e^t (E f^eps(X_t))^{1/eps} for all t, eps > 0.
items.note: Proof: Proposition 3.1 gives f <= M on K; Ito's formula for e^{eps t} f^eps(X_t) and Lemma 5.2 make the local martingale part bounded above, hence a submartingale. The strict-convexity assumptions are used only for the bound M, which Theorem 1.1 later supplies with M = 2 R(K)^2. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Small epsilon limit
items.statement: Only the case eps = 1 of Lemma 5.5 is used, although small eps is stronger; as eps -> 0 the right-hand side of Lemma 5.5 tends to exp(t + E log f(X_t)).
items.note: The limit is asserted as not too difficult, without proof. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Inverse Hessian bounded by covariance
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.1, assume that K has smooth boundary with everywhere positive Gauss curvature and Hess rho >= eps_0 Id on K for some eps_0 > 0. Then (Hess phi)^{-1}(z) <= e^{2t} / (2(e^t - 1)) Cov(X_t^{(z)}) as symmetric matrices, for every z in K and t > 0.
items.note: Proof: Lemma 5.3 and Lemma 5.5 with eps = 1 give e^{2t} E(X_t . e_1)^2 >= (z . e_1)^2 + 2 phi^{11}(z) int_0^t e^s ds, and E X_t = e^{-t} z converts the second moment into a variance. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Covariance bound without strict convexity
items.statement: If mu is a log-concave probability measure with barycenter at the origin satisfying condition (1), then (Hess phi)^{-1}(z) <= e^{2t} / (2(e^t - 1)) Cov(X_t^{(z)}) as symmetric matrices, for every z in K and t > 0.
items.note: Proof: as for Corollary 5.7, with the bound Hess psi <= M Id in the proof of Lemma 5.5 taken from Theorem 1.1 (M = 2 R(K)^2) instead of Proposition 3.1, so the strict-convexity assumptions are removed. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Moments of inverse Hessian
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.1, fix theta in S^{n-1} and let V = int (x . theta)^2 dmu(x). Then for every p >= 1, (int_K |((Hess phi)^{-1} theta . theta) / V|^p dmu)^{1/p} <= 4 p^2.
items.note: Proof: Corollary 5.8 at t = log 2 gives phi^{11}(z) <= 2 E(X_t^{(z)} . e_1)^2; stationarity of mu (Corollary 4.7 transported to M_mu) and Holder give E|phi^{11}(Z)|^p <= 2^p E|Z . e_1|^{2p}; Berwald's inequality for log-concave measures gives (E|Z . e_1|^{2p})^{1/(2p)} <= (2p / sqrt 2) sqrt V. Presented as a modest step towards bounding (Hess phi)^{-1} by Cov(mu) for KLS. No Lean counterpart.

papers.title: Moment measures
papers.result: A nonzero finite centered measure whose support spans the space is the moment measure of an essentially continuous convex potential, unique up to translation.
papers.remaining: The general finite-mass/unbounded existence-and-uniqueness Theorem 2 is not formalized. Its source-constant Lemmas 14–15, essential continuity (Proposition 10, Theorem 8) and uniqueness up to translation remain outside the local scope. Formalized supports include Proposition 12 attainment, Lemma 16, Lemma 17 in geometric form with a separate source-condition adapter, Legendre/truncation and first-variation tools, and the bounded isotropic source construction. For that bounded probability class, exists_momentMap_of_isotropic_of_ae_norm_le proves a normalized finite convex Lipschitz potential and the actual gradient pushforward; the bounded Euler–Lagrange identification is no longer a missing step. It does not establish the full source theorem or its uniqueness conclusion.

local_results.scope: Lemma 16 for finite measures
Lemma 17 with explicit interior-hull input
Proposition 12 truncation and convexification tools
Theorem 2 conditions give the interior-hull hypothesis
Coercivity, truncation and affine normalization for Proposition 12
Proposition 12 attainment (reviewed stronger)

Proposition 12 for a bounded isotropic source: capped LSC maximiser, real minimum, finite convex L-Lipschitz conjugate ψ with ∫ e^{−ψ} = 1 and probability density; weak normalized primal, not the push-forward or Theorem 2
Attainment of the Legendre supremum at interior points of the finite dual domain and maximizer = dual gradient (generic, any dimension)
(42) pointwise: d/dt (φ + t b)*(y) at 0 = −b(∇φ*(y)) for bounded continuous b, φ proper LSC, φ* differentiable at an interior y; not the integral Euler–Lagrange or push-forward

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: n ≥ 1. Convex functions ψ: R^n → R ∪ {+∞} are allowed to take the value +∞ (convexity is required where both values are finite; exp(−∞) = 0). For convex ψ with 0 < ∫ e^{−ψ} < ∞, μ_ψ is the measure with density e^{−ψ} on R^n and ∇ψ is defined almost everywhere in the interior of {ψ < +∞}. The Legendre transform is ψ*(y) = sup_{ψ(x)<∞} [x·y − ψ(x)]; ∂ψ is the subgradient; D²f is the Aleksandrov Hessian of a convex f; Supp(μ) is the closed support, conv its convex hull, H^{n−1} the (n−1)-dimensional Hausdorff measure, κ_n the volume of the Euclidean unit ball, S^{n−1} the unit sphere. Cited, unproved inputs: integrability of e^{−ψ} iff liminf_{|x|→∞} ψ(x)/|x| > 0 (display (7), from Klartag, Lemma 2.1), (13), Prékopa's inequality (17) and Dubuc's characterisation of its equality cases, the Brenier map and McCann's weak regularity (20), the Rogers–Shephard inequality, Fradelizi's inequality ψ(0) ≤ inf ψ + n at the barycenter, the functional Santaló inequality of Artstein–Klartag–Milman, Rockafellar's Theorem 10.9 and Berman–Berndtsson Lemma 2.7. Numbering: Theorem, Proposition, Lemma, Corollary, Remark, Notation, Fact and Conjecture share one global counter (theo); Definition has its own counter; no section-relative numbering and no appendix; no Corollary, Notation, Fact, Conjecture or Claim occurs. The printed numbers Definitions 1–2 and Theorem/Proposition/Lemma/Remark 1–17 were computed from the LaTeX counters and checked against the PDF text.
lemma_map.omitted: All 19 numbered statements of v1 are listed except Remark 11, a purely expository heuristic (the measure in Theorem 8 might become a distribution acting through the asymptotic slope of φ when ψ0 is not essentially continuous). Unnumbered displayed claims are not listed: the integrability criterion (7) and (13), the Legendre identity (12), the support identity (16) (stated without proof), the Prékopa inequality (17) for Legendre transforms (deduced from Prékopa's theorem), the example moment measures (simplex, Gaussian, sphere, cube (5)), the Monge–Ampère equation (4), the one-dimensional formula, the end-of-Section-2 observations on conv(Supp μ), and the Section 5 discussion of cone-volume and surface-area variants. Reviewed Lean candidates with no item mapped: FunctionalInequalities.KLS.LogConcave (KLS/Definitions.lean), FunctionalInequalities.KLS.IsBorellDensity and its lemmas (KLS/LogConcave/Density/BorellRepresentation/Basic.lean, Density/Bounds.lean), FunctionalInequalities.Probability.Line.prekopaLeindler (Probability/Line/BrunnMinkowski.lean) and FunctionalInequalities.Analysis.prekopaLeindler (Probability/BrunnMinkowski.lean); the finite-dimensional Prékopa–Leindler inequality is an available ingredient for (17) (with f = e^{−u0*}, g = e^{−u1*}, h = e^{−[(1−λ)u0+λu1]*}) but states neither (17) nor any numbered item.

items.label: Moment measure of a convex function
items.statement: For a convex ψ: R^n → R ∪ {+∞} with 0 < ∫ e^{−ψ} < ∞, the moment measure μ of ψ is the push-forward of μ_ψ = e^{−ψ(x)} dx under ∇ψ, i.e. ∫ b dμ = ∫ b(∇ψ(x)) e^{−ψ(x)} dx (display (2)) for every Borel b that is nonnegative or μ-integrable.
items.note: Translation of ψ leaves μ unchanged; adding λ to ψ multiplies μ by e^{−λ}. No Lean declaration. The library has extended-real convex potentials and the Legendre transform (Analysis/Convex/Legendre.lean) and the exponential-potential measure, mass and CEK functional (Probability/MomentMeasure/Basic.lean), but no gradient push-forward, moment-measure predicate or essential-continuity definition.

items.label: Essentially-continuous convex function
items.statement: A convex ψ: R^n → R ∪ {+∞} is essentially continuous if it is lower semicontinuous and its set of discontinuity points has zero H^{n−1}-measure; equivalently {ψ < ∞} = A ∪ B with A open convex and B ⊆ ∂A, H^{n−1}(B) = 0.
items.note: Every finite convex function is essentially continuous; in dimension one the notion equals continuity. No Lean declaration. The library has extended-real convex potentials and the Legendre transform (Analysis/Convex/Legendre.lean) and the exponential-potential measure, mass and CEK functional (Probability/MomentMeasure/Basic.lean), but no gradient push-forward, moment-measure predicate or essential-continuity definition.

items.label: Necessary conditions on moment measures
items.statement: If ψ: R^n → R ∪ {+∞} is convex and essentially continuous with 0 < ∫ e^{−ψ} < ∞, then its moment measure is not supported in any hyperplane and its barycenter lies at the origin.
items.note: Proof: barycenter 0 from the 'furthermore' part of Lemma 4; support not in a hyperplane through 0 by Lemma 6, hence not in any hyperplane since the barycenter is 0. These are the necessity half of the bijection announced before Theorem 2. No Lean declaration. The library has extended-real convex potentials and the Legendre transform (Analysis/Convex/Legendre.lean) and the exponential-potential measure, mass and CEK functional (Probability/MomentMeasure/Basic.lean), but no gradient push-forward, moment-measure predicate or essential-continuity definition.

items.label: Existence and uniqueness of moment measures
items.statement: Let μ be a Borel measure on R^n with 0 < μ(R^n) < ∞, not supported in a lower-dimensional subspace, and with barycenter at the origin (in particular with finite first moments). Then there is an essentially continuous convex ψ: R^n → R ∪ {+∞} whose moment measure is μ, and such ψ is unique up to translation.
items.note: The full existence-and-uniqueness theorem has no mapped Lean declaration. Proposition 12 attainment is formalized by KLS.CEK.exists_variational_maximum, and the bounded-source primal and Legendre first-variation tools are proved. For an isotropic probability law with an a.e. norm bound L, KLS.CEK.exists_momentMap_of_isotropic_of_ae_norm_le (KLS/CEK/MomentMap.lean) constructs a finite convex L-Lipschitz potential ψ with ∫ e^{−ψ} dx = 1 and the actual gradient pushforward (∇ψ)_#(e^{−ψ} dx) = μ; the bounded-source Euler–Lagrange identification is therefore available. This restricted producer does not state Theorem 2 for every nonzero finite measure satisfying the source hypotheses, define essential continuity, or prove uniqueness up to translation. The paper's uniqueness argument uses Theorem 8, equality in Prékopa's inequality and Dubuc's equality characterization; those conclusions are not supplied by the bounded producer.

items.label: Essential continuity along lines
items.statement: If ψ: R^n → R ∪ {+∞} is convex and essentially continuous, 0 ≠ θ ∈ R^n and H = θ^⊥, then for H^{n−1}-almost every y ∈ H the function t ↦ ψ(y + tθ) is continuous on R (with values in R ∪ {+∞}) and locally Lipschitz in the interior of the interval where it is finite.
items.note: Proof: the projection of the H^{n−1}-null discontinuity set onto H is H^{n−1}-null; convexity gives local Lipschitz continuity. No Lean declaration. The library has extended-real convex potentials and the Legendre transform (Analysis/Convex/Legendre.lean) and the exponential-potential measure, mass and CEK functional (Probability/MomentMeasure/Basic.lean), but no gradient push-forward, moment-measure predicate or essential-continuity definition.

items.label: Log-concave gradients are integrable
items.statement: If ρ: R^n → [0, ∞) is integrable and log-concave, then ∫ |∇ρ| < ∞. If moreover ρ = e^{−ψ} with ψ essentially continuous, then ∫ ∂^i ρ = 0 for i = 1, ..., n.
items.note: Proof: on each line t ↦ ρ(y,t) is unimodal, so ∫|∂_t ρ| dt ≤ 2 sup_t ρ(y,t), and the marginal infimum ψ1(y) = inf_t ψ(y,t) is convex with exp(−ψ1) integrable by (7); the vanishing integral follows from Lemma 3 and Fubini. Gives finite first moments of the moment measure. No Lean declaration: KLS/LogConcave/Density gives bounded Borell densities and exponential moments of the law, not integrability of ∇ρ.

items.label: Integration by parts inequality
items.statement: If ψ: R^n → R ∪ {+∞} is convex with 0 < ∫ e^{−ψ} < ∞, then x·∇ψ(x) is μ_ψ-integrable; if ψ is moreover essentially continuous, then ∫ x·∇ψ(x) dμ_ψ(x) ≤ n ∫ e^{−ψ}.
items.note: Proof: ∇ψ(x)·(x − x0) ≥ ψ(x) − ψ(x0) is bounded below; the divergence theorem on smooth convex compact K ∋ x0 inside {ψ < ∞} bounds the integral by n∫e^{−ψ}; Lemma 4 handles ∇ψ·x0. The paper notes equality holds but neither uses nor proves it. No Lean declaration. The library has extended-real convex potentials and the Legendre transform (Analysis/Convex/Legendre.lean) and the exponential-potential measure, mass and CEK functional (Probability/MomentMeasure/Basic.lean), but no gradient push-forward, moment-measure predicate or essential-continuity definition.

items.label: Support not in a subspace
items.statement: If ψ: R^n → R ∪ {+∞} is convex and essentially continuous with 0 < ∫ e^{−ψ} < ∞ and μ is its moment measure, then Supp(μ) is not contained in any proper linear subspace E ⊊ R^n.
items.note: Proof: if Supp(μ) ⊆ θ^⊥ then ∂_θ ρ = 0 a.e.; by Lemma 3, ρ is constant on almost every line in direction θ, so ∫ρ ∈ {0, ∞} by Fubini, a contradiction. No Lean declaration. The library has extended-real convex potentials and the Legendre transform (Analysis/Convex/Legendre.lean) and the exponential-potential measure, mass and CEK functional (Probability/MomentMeasure/Basic.lean), but no gradient push-forward, moment-measure predicate or essential-continuity definition.

items.label: Legendre transform is moment-integrable
items.statement: If ψ: R^n → R ∪ {+∞} is convex with 0 < ∫ e^{−ψ} < ∞, φ = ψ* and μ is the moment measure of ψ, then φ is μ-integrable.
items.note: Proof: φ(∇ψ(x)) = x·∇ψ(x) − ψ(x) μ_ψ-a.e. (12); x·∇ψ ∈ L¹(μ_ψ) by Lemma 5, and ψ ∈ L¹(μ_ψ) since ψ is bounded below and ψe^{−ψ} ≤ 2e^{−ψ/2} with (7) (display (15)). No essential continuity is assumed. No Lean declaration. The library has extended-real convex potentials and the Legendre transform (Analysis/Convex/Legendre.lean) and the exponential-potential measure, mass and CEK functional (Probability/MomentMeasure/Basic.lean), but no gradient push-forward, moment-measure predicate or essential-continuity definition.

items.label: Above-tangent form of Prékopa's inequality
items.statement: Let e^{−ψ0}, e^{−ψ1} be log-concave on R^n with 0 < ∫ e^{−ψ0} < ∞, ψ1 not identically +∞, and ψ0 essentially continuous; with φ_i = ψ_i*, log ∫ e^{−ψ0} − log ∫ e^{−ψ1} ≥ ∫ (φ0 − φ1) dμ̄ (display (18)), where μ̄ is the moment measure of ψ0 normalised to a probability.
items.note: Printed title 'Prékopa's theorem revisited'. Proof: Brenier map T = ∇f from e^{−ψ0} to e^{−ψ1}1_L (L a large ball), McCann's a.e. Monge–Ampère equation (20), log s ≤ s − 1 and the Legendre inequalities give (21); the integration by parts ∫(Δf − ∇ψ0·∇f) dμ_ψ0 ≤ 0 follows line by line from Lemma 9 using Lemma 3, and Lemma 5 controls the remaining term. Expresses −μ̄ as a subgradient of the convex functional J(u) = −log ∫ e^{−u*}. No Lean declaration. The library has extended-real convex potentials and the Legendre transform (Analysis/Convex/Legendre.lean) and the exponential-potential measure, mass and CEK functional (Probability/MomentMeasure/Basic.lean), but no gradient push-forward, moment-measure predicate or essential-continuity definition.

items.label: One-dimensional integration by parts
items.statement: If ρ = e^{−ψ} is an integrable, continuous, log-concave function on R, dμ_ψ = ρ dx, and f: R → R is convex and Lipschitz, then ∫ (f'' − f'ψ') dμ_ψ ≤ 0, with f'' the Aleksandrov (a.e.) second derivative.
items.note: Proof: Lebesgue–Stieltjes integration by parts for the bounded nondecreasing right derivative V = f', using that V' dx is the absolutely continuous part of dV. No Lean declaration: the one-dimensional integration-by-parts results in KLS/LogConcave/Line/SharpHardy.lean concern clipped Poincaré tests, not convex f.

items.label: Prékopa inequality forces essential continuity
items.statement: Let ψ: R^n → R ∪ {+∞} be lower semicontinuous and convex with ∫ e^{−ψ} = 1, μ its moment measure and φ = ψ*. If for every μ-integrable convex φ1 with ψ1 = φ1* one has log ∫ e^{−ψ} − log ∫ e^{−ψ1} ≥ ∫ (φ − φ1) dμ, then ψ is essentially continuous.
items.note: Converse to Theorem 8. Proof: near x0 in A = {x ∈ ∂{ψ<∞} : ψ(x) < ∞} write the boundary as a Lipschitz graph; test with φ_ε = max{φ, φ + ε(y·θ) − 1}: the right side is o(ε) by first moments (Lemma 4), while ∫e^{−ψ_ε} gains at least ε c0^{n−1} e^{−(k0+1)} H^{n−1}(A^{k0}), forcing H^{n−1}(A^{k0}) = 0. μ-integrability of φ_ε uses Proposition 7. No Lean declaration. The library has extended-real convex potentials and the Legendre transform (Analysis/Convex/Legendre.lean) and the exponential-potential measure, mass and CEK functional (Probability/MomentMeasure/Basic.lean), but no gradient push-forward, moment-measure predicate or essential-continuity definition.

items.label: Existence of a variational maximiser
items.statement: Let μ be a probability measure on R^n satisfying the assumptions of Theorem 2 and I_μ(f) = log ∫ e^{−f*} − ∫ f dμ for μ-integrable f: R^n → R ∪ {+∞}. Then there is a μ-integrable convex φ with ∫ e^{−φ*} = 1 and I_μ(φ) = sup_f I_μ(f) (display (38)), the supremum over all μ-integrable f.
items.note: Variational problem of Berman–Berndtsson. Proof: truncate a maximising sequence below, replace by biconjugates, normalise φ_ℓ(0) = inf φ_ℓ = 0; Lemma 15 and log t = o(t^{1/n}) bound sup_ℓ ∫e^{−φ_ℓ*} and sup_ℓ ∫φ_ℓ dμ; Lemma 17 extracts a limit with I_μ(φ) ≥ limsup I_μ(φ_ℓj). Formalized (KLS.CEK.exists_variational_maximum): for a probability measure μ on a finite-dimensional real inner product space (dimension 0 included) with finite first moment, barycenter 0 and no proper linear subspace of full measure, and any additive Haar measure dx, there is φ: E → (−∞, +∞] with convex real epigraph, lower semicontinuous and μ-integrable, with ∫ e^{−φ*} dx = 1 and I_μ(f) ≤ I_μ(φ) for every μ-integrable f (convex or not). Reviewed stronger: lower semicontinuity and the general Haar/space scope are added; no maximising sequence, bound or optimizer is supplied. Different route for the bounds: a measure-dependent polynomial conjugate-mass bound (exists_coercivity_of_centered_probability) replaces the particular constant of Lemma 15, and the normalisation subtracts a supporting affine function produced by Hahn–Banach separation. Adopted 2026-10-10 from the root-accepted CEK Proposition 12 candidate; clients research/audits/CEK/Proposition12Audit.lean and FunctionalLimitAudit.lean.

items.label: Maximiser and Prékopa connection
items.statement: By Prékopa's inequality the functional f ↦ I_μ(f) is concave, and strictly concave modulo affine functions, on convex functions finite near 0; and if μ is the moment measure of ψ0 then Theorem 8 forces φ0 = ψ0* to be a maximiser in (38).
items.note: Not purely expository: it asserts the concavity of I_μ (from (17)) and the maximising property of ψ0* (from Theorem 8), without separate proof. No Lean declaration. The library has extended-real convex potentials and the Legendre transform (Analysis/Convex/Legendre.lean) and the exponential-potential measure, mass and CEK functional (Probability/MomentMeasure/Basic.lean), but no gradient push-forward, moment-measure predicate or essential-continuity definition.

items.label: Volume–integral lower bound
items.statement: Let μ be a probability measure on R^n satisfying the assumptions of Theorem 2. There is c_μ > 0 such that every μ-integrable convex φ: R^n → R ∪ {+∞} with e^{−φ} integrable and φ(0) = 0 satisfies (∫ e^{−φ})^{1/n} (∫ [φ − inf φ] dμ + 1) ≥ c_μ; one may take c_μ = κ_n^{1/n} m_μ / (4 e^{1/n}) with m_μ = inf_{θ ∈ S^{n−1}} ∫ |x·θ| dμ(x) > 0.
items.note: Proof: with K = {φ ≤ 1}, Rogers–Shephard gives Vol(K − K) ≤ 4^n Vol(K), so K − K has inradius at most R_φ = 4κ_n^{−1/n} Vol(K)^{1/n}; convexity gives φ(x) ≥ |x·θ0|/R_φ + inf φ − 1 and ∫e^{−φ} ≥ Vol(K)/e. No Lean declaration. The library has extended-real convex potentials and the Legendre transform (Analysis/Convex/Legendre.lean) and the exponential-potential measure, mass and CEK functional (Probability/MomentMeasure/Basic.lean), but no gradient push-forward, moment-measure predicate or essential-continuity definition.

items.label: Coercivity of the variational functional
items.statement: Let μ be a probability measure on R^n satisfying the assumptions of Theorem 2, φ: R^n → R ∪ {+∞} μ-integrable and convex with φ(0) = 0, and ψ = φ*. Then ∫ φ dμ ≥ (c_μ / (2π)) (∫ e^{−ψ})^{1/n} − (n + 1), with c_μ the constant of Lemma 14.
items.note: Proof: ∫φ dμ ≥ 0 via a subgradient at 0 and the zero barycenter; after translating ψ to have barycenter 0, Fradelizi's inequality gives inf φ = −ψ(0) ≥ −n, Lemma 14 applies, and the functional Santaló inequality ∫e^{−ψ} ∫e^{−φ} ≤ (2π)^n of Artstein–Klartag–Milman concludes. No Lean declaration. The library has extended-real convex potentials and the Legendre transform (Analysis/Convex/Legendre.lean) and the exponential-potential measure, mass and CEK functional (Probability/MomentMeasure/Basic.lean), but no gradient push-forward, moment-measure predicate or essential-continuity definition. The adopted Proposition 12 proof uses a different, measure-dependent polynomial coercivity bound (Probability.MomentMeasure.exists_coercivity_of_centered_probability); the constant of this lemma is not formalized.

items.label: Pointwise bound by the integral
items.statement: Let μ be a finite Borel measure on R^n and K the interior of conv(Supp(μ)). For every x0 ∈ K there is C_{μ,x0} > 0 such that φ(x0) ≤ C_{μ,x0} ∫ φ dμ for every nonnegative μ-integrable convex φ: R^n → R ∪ {+∞}.
items.note: Proof: m_{μ,x0} = inf_θ μ{(x − x0)·θ > 0} > 0 by Fatou and compactness of S^{n−1}; integrate the supporting-hyperplane bound over a half-space; C_{μ,x0} = 1/m_{μ,x0}. Formalized with the source statement (exists_pos_le_mul_lintegral_toReal_of_convex_epigraph): for a finite Borel measure on a finite-dimensional real inner product space (dimension 0 included) and x0 in the interior of the convex hull of its support, one C > 0, chosen before φ, gives φ(x0) ≤ C ∫ φ dμ for every nonnegative extended-real φ with convex real epigraph, a.e.-measurable values and finite integral. Different route: the uniform halfspace bound (54) is proved for probability measures by a finite product of ball masses over a cover of the unit sphere, not Fatou, and transported to finite measures by normalization (m ≤ μ(R^n)); the point bound uses finiteness of φ near interior points of the support hull (mem_interior_setOf_ne_top_of_lintegral_ne_top) and a halfspace-or-global-minimum alternative for the strict sublevel set. Promoted 2026-10-09 from the root-accepted CEK integration candidate; clients research/audits/CEK/PointControlAudit.lean (mass-two boundary measure, dimension 0) and research/audits/BKL/ConvexSupportAudit.lean.

items.label: Compactness of normalised potentials
items.statement: Let μ satisfy the assumptions of Theorem 2 and let φ_ℓ: R^n → [0, ∞] be μ-integrable convex with φ_ℓ(0) = 0 and sup_ℓ ∫ φ_ℓ dμ < ∞. Then a subsequence φ_ℓj and a nonnegative μ-integrable convex φ satisfy ∫ φ dμ ≤ liminf_j ∫ φ_ℓj dμ and ∫ e^{−φ*} ≥ limsup_j ∫ e^{−φ_ℓj*}.
items.note: Proof: Lemma 16 gives pointwise bounds on K = int conv(Supp μ); Rockafellar Theorem 10.9 gives a pointwise convergent subsequence on K; extend φ radially to ∂K, use Fatou and monotone convergence for the first inequality, and a finite dense max-affine approximation of φ* for the second. Formalized in geometric form (MomentMeasure.exists_subseq_integral_bounds_of_convex_epigraph): for a finite Borel measure μ on a finite-dimensional real inner product space with 0 ∈ int conv(Supp μ) as an explicit hypothesis, and nonnegative φ_ℓ with convex real epigraph, φ_ℓ(0) = 0, a.e.-measurable values and sup_ℓ ∫ φ_ℓ dμ < ∞, one subsequence and one nonnegative convex μ-integrable limit satisfy both (56a) and (56b), the latter for every additive Haar measure; the limit is finite and attained on K, radially closed and +∞ off the closure of K, and finiteness of ∫ e^{−φ*} is derived (zero mass, a non-probability μ and dimension 0 included). Partial for the source item: the source assumes the conditions of Theorem 2. The adapter from a nonzero finite measure with finite first moment, barycenter 0 and no proper linear subspace of full measure to 0 ∈ int conv(Supp μ) is formalized (Probability.zero_mem_interior_convexHull_support_of_integral_eq_zero, adopted 2026-10-10), but no declaration states their composition in the source form. Promoted 2026-10-09 from the root-accepted CEK integration candidate; clients research/audits/CEK/Lemma17Audit.lean and ConjugateMassAudit.lean.

papers.title: Approaching the Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits and variance conjectures
papers.locator: Page 11; local source audit linked below
papers.result: Records C_P ≤ 4 tr(Cov), whose one-dimensional specialization is 4 Var, in a broader account of KLS and the variance conjecture.
papers.remaining: Only the one-dimensional bound is formalized here, by an independent proof. The high-dimensional trace bound, its original exact-constant attribution and optimality over all laws are not certified.

local_results.scope: One-dimensional 4 Var upper bound, including zero variance

papers.title: Perimeter as relaxed Minkowski content in metric measure spaces
papers.result: A Minkowski coarea inequality and identification of relaxed Minkowski content with BV perimeter.
papers.remaining: The complete lower/upper content, recovery and relaxation chain is formalized for finite Borel measures on arbitrary metric spaces. The new continuation proves the globally Lipschitz/global L1 bounded-support reduction of Remark 3.4 for every measurable finite-mass target under any Borel measure, the direct positive-level local-slope coarea upper bound under finite mass of a positive-support neighborhood (all levels for nonnegative functions), and perimeter at most lower content at measurable finite-mass targets. Under finiteness on bounded Borel sets, actual bounded measurable lower-recovery sets have finite mass and finite lower content term by term; indicators converge globally in L1 and lower contents converge to perimeter. The existing relaxed lower-content set infimum equals the perimeter at Theorem 3.6's measurable finite-mass target scope, including infinite perimeter and infinite total mass; convergence ensures eventual finite approximating-set masses without changing the class or excluding infinite-mass finite prefixes. Finite target mass and finite lower content imply a finite-mass positive neighborhood. Actual lower-to-upper radius recovery holds there, and a diagonal sequence gives bounded open upper-recovery sets with finite masses/contents and original global indicator L1 convergence. The existing relaxed upper infimum equals perimeter, hence the lower relaxation, at the published finite-mass target scope, including infinite perimeter by order. The full Lemma 3.2 chain is formalized with the actual right-radius liminf of integrated open-ball growth under nonnegativity and finite positive-support-neighborhood mass. Lemma 2.1 exposes the actual relaxed-upper <= lower-content bound at finite-mass Borel targets under any measure. Lemma 2.1's relaxed lower/upper-content equality is also formalized for every Borel measure at measurable finite-mass targets, and on proper metric spaces Remark 3.5's locally Lipschitz classes with global or compact-set L1 convergence have relaxation infima equal to the bounded-support perimeter at measurable finite-mass targets for every Borel measure (2026-10-01). The locally Lipschitz classes on nonproper spaces, nonconvex ambient/support transfer and general RCD comparisons remain pending. These local Lean results do not add ledger certificates; remote Lean verification is a separate check.

local_results.scope: Minkowski coarea inequality in the local Euclidean scope

Published finite-mass target / finite-on-bounded measure scope: bounded-support reduction, full coarea radius chain, lower-to-upper recovery, both actual recoveries and both relaxed identities; convex closed-support Cheeger identification

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: Metric space with a Borel measure finite on bounded Borel sets; contents are defined for Borel sets of finite measure.
lemma_map.omitted: Remarks 3.1, 4.1 and 4.4 are expository (literature context, Euclidean background and a cited counterexample) and are not separate formalization targets.

items.label: Lower content bounds relaxed upper content
items.statement: For a Borel set A of finite measure, the relaxed upper Minkowski content is at most the lower Minkowski content.
items.note: Holds for every Borel measure; the standing finiteness on bounded sets is not needed.

items.label: Relaxed lower and upper contents agree
items.statement: The relaxed lower and upper Minkowski contents coincide.
items.note: Measurable finite-mass targets under every Borel measure.

items.label: Minkowski coarea inequality
items.statement: For a nonnegative Lipschitz f with a finite-mass neighbourhood of {f > 0}, the integrated lower content of superlevel sets is at most the liminf of the integrated open-ball growth, which is at most the slope integral.
items.note: Both inequalities of the chain, with the actual open-ball supremum semigroup.

items.label: Perimeter by Lipschitz relaxation
items.statement: Per(A) is the infimum of liminf of slope integrals over Lipschitz approximants converging to the indicator of A in L¹.
items.note: The library perimeter uses bounded-support tests; lipschitzRelaxation_eq_perimeter_of_measure_lt_top identifies the two at finite-mass targets.

items.label: Truncation and bounded-support reduction
items.statement: Only approximants with values in [0, 1] and bounded positivity set need to be considered in Definition 3.3.
items.note: Measurable finite-mass targets under every Borel measure.

items.label: Locally Lipschitz variants agree
items.statement: The locally Lipschitz variants of the perimeter (L¹ or L¹_loc convergence) agree with Definition 3.3 on proper spaces, and on complete separable spaces by a non-elementary argument.
items.note: Proper spaces only. The complete separable case, cited from Di Marino's thesis, is not formalized.

items.label: Relaxed Minkowski content equals perimeter
items.statement: For every Borel set A with finite measure, the relaxed lower Minkowski content equals Per(A) of Definition 3.3.
items.note: Exact Definition 3.3 form, registered as the paper-target certificate thm:relaxed-minkowski-content-perimeter; the two library identities compose under the standing assumption.

items.label: Coarea with lower content
items.statement: Under the regularity assumption (4.2), the total variation of a nonnegative Lipschitz f equals the integrated lower content of its superlevel sets; lower content equals perimeter for almost every level, and lower and upper contents agree for unit-slope functions.
items.note: Needs the BV total variation of functions and the Fleming–Rishel coarea formula (4.1), which the paper cites.

items.label: Distance-function level sets
items.statement: Under a length assumption and (4.2), almost every level set of a distance function has equal lower content, upper content and perimeter, and has a Minkowski content.

items.label: Doubling coarea with Hausdorff gauge
items.statement: For a doubling measure and nonnegative Lipschitz f with finite-mass positivity set, the integrated gauge-Hausdorff measure of B ∩ {f = t} is bounded by the asymptotic Lipschitz integral and by twice the slope integral over B.
items.note: Needs the Carathéodory gauge measure and Vitali covering for doubling measures.

items.label: Perimeter lower bound on level sets
items.statement: On complete doubling spaces satisfying (4.2), almost every superlevel set has finite perimeter with perimeter measure at least half the gauge-Hausdorff measure on its essential boundary.

papers.title: Eldan’s stochastic localization and the KLS conjecture: Isoperimetry, concentration and mixing
papers.result: For isotropic log-concave laws, C_P = O(n^(1/2)), equivalently ψₙ = O(n^(1/4)); the paper also studies mixing and concentration.
papers.remaining: The quantitative localization theorem, covariance bounds and mixing results are not locally formalized.

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: Log-concave densities p on R^n with mean mu and covariance matrix A; isotropic means mean 0 and A = I. psi_p is the KLS constant, the reciprocal of the Cheeger constant: 1/psi_p = inf_S p(boundary S)/min(p(S), p(R^n minus S)) (Conjecture 1 display), so upper bounds on psi_p are lower bounds on expansion; psi_n in Appendix A is the supremum over isotropic laws on R^n (implicit). The repository's Isoperimetry.constant is 1/psi_p on the affine support (outer Minkowski content) and Isoperimetry.inverseScale is psi_p. kappa_p and rho_p are the log-Cheeger and log-Sobolev constants (Definitions 10, 9); D is the diameter of the support. c, C are universal constants and a <~ b means a <= C b; ||.||_op is the spectral norm. From Section 3 on the support of p is truncated to a ball of radius R > n (justified by Lemma 24 and Theorem 25), W_t is a standard n-dimensional Wiener process and p_t, mu_t, A_t are the localization of Definition 26 with control matrix C_t = I. The Stieltjes potential u(X) is defined by display (1.1), Tr((uI - X)^{-q}) = Phi with X <= uI, which the paper cites as Definition 1.1.
lemma_map.omitted: The three unnumbered remarks (after Theorem 17: the k = 2 case recovers Paouris' small-ball bound epsilon^{c sqrt n}; after Lemma 37: Theorem 12 verifies its hypothesis with k = 2; after Theorem 48: the 1/D log-Sobolev bound is tight by Section 8) are expository and summarized in the notes of Theorems 17, 48 and Lemma 37; the acknowledgement is unnumbered. Unnumbered displays (the quadratic-variation conventions of Section 2.1, d log p_t(x) after Lemma 27, the Stieltjes potential (1.1), the Markov-chain log-Sobolev constant rho(P) of Section 1.2 and the Euclidean-norm tail after Theorem 16) are not listed, except the defining display of psi_p in Conjecture 1, which Lean states.

items.label: KLS constant psi_p
items.statement: For a log-concave density p on R^n, 1/psi_p = inf over S of p(boundary S)/min(p(S), p(R^n minus S)), where p(boundary S) is the boundary measure (written as the integral of p over the boundary); psi_p is the reciprocal of the Cheeger constant, so upper bounds on psi_p are lower bounds on expansion.
items.note: Lean Isoperimetry.constant is h_mu = 1/psi_p, an infimum over measurable sets of mass in (0, 1) of the outer Minkowski content (liminf over open thickenings) divided by min(mu(B), 1 - mu(B)), computed on the affine support with its induced metric; Isoperimetry.inverseScale is Psi = h_mu^{-1} = psi_p, valued in [0, infinity]. The paper leaves the boundary measure and the admissible class of S unspecified, and uses the display only for densities on R^n.

items.label: KLS conjecture
items.statement: For every log-concave density p on R^n with covariance matrix A, 1/psi_p >= c/sqrt(||A||_op) for a universal constant c > 0; equivalently psi_p <= C for every isotropic log-concave p.
items.note: Open conjecture, not proved in the paper. Deliberately not mapped to FunctionalInequalities.KLS.kls.

items.label: KLS trace bound
items.statement: For every log-concave density p on R^n with covariance matrix A, psi_p <= C sqrt(Tr A) for a universal constant C; for isotropic p this is psi_p = O(sqrt n).
items.note: Quoted from KLS95; the displayed trace-covariance estimate has no mapped source-form declaration. The one-dimensional Minkowski counterpart is available as KLS.LogConcave.inv_minkowskiConstant_sq_le_three_mul_evariance (KLS/LogConcave/Line/CheegerVariance.lean). The separate BKL main line proves the dimension-free covariance-normalized Poincaré bound, and inverseScale_sq_le_pi_literature provides the Buser comparison. These results do not constitute a registered formalization of this paper's quoted trace-covariance statement or the KLS95 localization proof.

items.label: Thin-shell conjecture
items.statement: For X drawn from an isotropic log-concave density on R^n, sigma_p^2 = E[(||X|| - sqrt n)^2] <= C for a universal constant C.
items.note: Open conjecture; the text recalls sigma_p <= C psi_p and the Guedon-Milman bound sigma_p <= C n^{1/3}. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Slicing conjecture
items.statement: Every convex body of unit volume in R^n has a hyperplane section of volume at least a universal constant; equivalently L_K <= C for every unit-volume convex body K with covariance L_K^2 I.
items.note: Open conjecture; the text recalls L_p <= C sigma_p <= C psi_p (Eldan-Klartag, Ball). No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Cheeger implies Poincare
items.statement: For every isotropic log-concave density p on R^n and every smooth g, Var_p g <= C psi_p^2 E_p ||grad g||^2 for a universal constant C.
items.note: Quoted, not proved here; used in Lemmas 39 and 57 for non-isotropic laws as well. Lean proves C_P^lit(mu) <= 4 Psi(mu)^2 for every finite-dimensional log-concave law (no isotropy, explicit constant 4, Dirac laws included), which implies the theorem when psi_p is read as Isoperimetry.inverseScale and smooth g with finite energy are admissible local-slope tests.

items.label: Lipschitz concentration via psi_p
items.statement: For every L-Lipschitz g on R^n and isotropic log-concave p, P(|g(x) - E g| >= psi_p L t) <= exp(-c t) for a universal c > 0.
items.note: Quoted for context, not proved or used. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Norm deviation bound
items.statement: For every isotropic log-concave p on R^n and t >= 0, P(| ||x|| - sqrt n | >= t) <= exp(-c min(t^3/n, t)).
items.note: Quoted for comparison with Theorem 16; not proved or used.

items.label: CLT for convex sets
items.statement: For an isotropic symmetric convex set K with marginal densities g_theta of vol(K cap {x^T theta = s}) and g the standard Gaussian density, there are universal c_1, c_2 > 0 such that for every delta > 0 the set of theta in S^{n-1} with |int_{-t}^t g_theta - int_{-t}^t g| <= c_1(delta + psi_K/sqrt n) for all t has measure at least 1 - n e^{-c_2 delta^2 n}.
items.note: Quoted for context; not proved or used. The printed vol of a subset of S^{n-1} is the normalized spherical measure.

items.label: Log-Sobolev constant rho_p
items.statement: For a density p, rho_p is the largest rho such that (rho/2) int f^2 log f^2 dp <= int ||grad f||^2 dp for every smooth f with int f^2 dp = 1.
items.note: No log-Sobolev constant is defined in the Lean library.

items.label: Log-Cheeger constant kappa_p
items.statement: For a density p on R^n, kappa_p = inf over S of p(boundary S)/(min(p(S), p(R^n minus S)) sqrt(log(1/p(S)))).
items.note: The defining display is typeset after the definition environment. The text asserts rho_p = Theta(kappa_p^2) citing Ledoux; only kappa_p^2 <~ rho_p follows from Theorem 47 as quoted. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Previous log-Cheeger bound
items.statement: For a log-concave density p on R^n with support of diameter D, kappa_p >= c/D and rho_p >= c/D^2.
items.note: Quoted; superseded by Theorem 15 in the isotropic case.

items.label: KLS constant n^{1/4} bound
items.statement: For every log-concave density p on R^n with covariance matrix A, psi_p <= C (Tr(A^2))^{1/4} for a universal constant C; in particular psi_p <= C n^{1/4} for isotropic p, where psi_p is the reciprocal of the Cheeger constant of Conjecture 1.
items.note: Main theorem (the psi_n = O(n^{1/4}) bound). Proof (Section 4.3): Lemma 35 keeps Tr A_t^2 <= 8 Tr A_0^2, hence ||A_t||_op <= sqrt(8 Tr A_0^2), on [0, c_1/sqrt(Tr A_0^2)] with probability 0.99; Lemma 31 with T = min(1/(64 sqrt 8), c_1)/sqrt(Tr A_0^2) gives psi_p = O(T^{-1/2}). Requires the stochastic-localization calculus of Section 3; the Lean library has no stochastic calculus and no declaration states this bound, even for n = 1.

items.label: Slicing and thin-shell n^{1/4}
items.statement: For every isotropic log-concave density p on R^n, the isotropic constant L_p and the thin-shell constant sigma_p are O(n^{1/4}).
items.note: Called immediate: combine Theorem 12 with the quoted comparisons L_p <= C sigma_p <= C psi_p (Eldan-Klartag; sigma_p <= C psi_p is folklore). The printed statement says any log-concave p, but L_p and sigma_p are defined for isotropic p.

items.label: Ball walk warm-start mixing
items.statement: The ball walk for an isotropic log-concave density on R^n mixes from a warm start in O*(n^{2.5}) steps.
items.note: From Theorem 12 and the quoted O*(n^2 psi_p^2) warm-start bound of KLS97; no proof given.

items.label: Log-Sobolev bound 1/D
items.statement: For every isotropic log-concave density p with support of diameter D, kappa_p >= c/sqrt D and rho_p >= c/D for a universal constant c > 0.
items.note: The paper's main log-Sobolev result (called our main theorem in Section 1.3); tight by Lemma 54. kappa_p follows from Theorem 36, rho_p is Theorem 48.

items.label: Lipschitz large deviation
items.statement: For every L-Lipschitz g on R^n, isotropic log-concave p and t > 0, P(|g(x) - gbar| >= L t) <= exp(-c t^2/(t + sqrt n)), where gbar is the median or mean of g under p and c > 0 is universal.
items.note: Proof in Section 6.1: Theorem 12 gives a first tail estimate; truncation to balls makes the law almost isotropic with bounded diameter, and Theorem 36 then bounds d alpha_t/dt for alpha_t = log(1/p(E_t)). The printed gbar(x) means the constant gbar; renormalization of almost isotropic laws is asserted without proof.

items.label: Small ball probability
items.statement: If for some k >= 1, psi_p <= C (Tr A^k)^{1/(2k)} for every log-concave p with covariance A, then for every isotropic log-concave p on R^n and 0 <= epsilon <= c_1, P(||x||_2^2 <= epsilon n) <= epsilon^{c_2 n^{1-1/k}/k} with universal c_1, c_2 > 0.
items.note: Proved in Section 6.2: on an event of probability 7/10, ||A_t||_op <= 2 (Lemma 37), Tr A_t >~ n and p_t(E) >= e^{-O(nt)} p(E), and Paouris' Theorem 49 for the t-strongly log-concave p_t; with the k = 2 case of Theorem 12 it gives epsilon^{c sqrt n} (unnumbered remark). The printed proof says the diameter can be taken as 2 sqrt n by truncation.

items.label: Ball walk from any start
items.statement: The ball walk with step size delta = Theta(1/sqrt n) on an isotropic convex body K in R^n of diameter D mixes in O(n^2 D log log D) proper steps from any starting point at distance n^{-O(1)} from the boundary of K.
items.note: Follows from Theorem 50 and Theorem 1.2 of Kannan-Lovasz-Montenegro (quoted); no further proof is written.

items.label: Ito's formula
items.statement: For a semimartingale x and a C^2 function f, df(x_t) = sum_i (partial_i f)(x_t) dx^i + (1/2) sum_{i,j} (partial_ij f)(x_t) d[x^i, x^j]_t.
items.note: Standard stochastic calculus, quoted without proof. The Lean library has no stochastic calculus.

items.label: Reflection principle
items.statement: For a standard one-dimensional Wiener process W and a, t >= 0, P(sup_{0<=s<=t} W(s) >= a) = 2 P(W(t) >= a).
items.note: Standard, quoted without proof. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Time change of martingales
items.statement: Every continuous local martingale M_t can be written as M_t = M_0 + W_{[M]_t} for all t >= 0 for some Wiener process W.
items.note: Quoted without proof; as printed it omits the possible enlargement of the probability space when [M]_infinity < infinity. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Log-concavity is preserved
items.statement: The convolution of two log-concave functions is log-concave; in particular every linear image and every marginal of a log-concave density is log-concave.
items.note: Quoted. Lean proves only the invertible linear case in measure form: the image of a compact-set (Borell) log-concave law under a continuous linear equivalence of finite-dimensional inner-product spaces is log-concave. Convolution and marginals (non-invertible maps) are not stated; the Prekopa-Leindler inequality itself is in Probability/BrunnMinkowski.lean but does not state this lemma.

items.label: Reverse Holder moments
items.statement: For a log-concave density p on R^n and k >= 1, E_p ||x||^k <= (2k)^k (E_p ||x||^2)^{k/2}.
items.note: Folklore, quoted from Lovasz-Vempala. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Norm tail bound
items.statement: For every isotropic log-concave density p on R^n and t > 0, P_p(||x|| > t sqrt n) <= e^{-t+1}.
items.note: Quoted from Lovasz-Vempala; used only to justify truncating the support in Section 3.1.

items.label: Half-measure sets suffice
items.statement: The Cheeger constant of every log-concave density is attained (up to the infimum) on subsets of measure 1/2.
items.note: Quoted from Milman 2009 via concavity of the isoperimetric profile; not proved here. Used in Lemma 31 and Section 3.1. No Lean counterpart; the Lean halfConstant of MetricBV is a different (mass at most 1/2) normalization.

items.label: Stochastic localization with C_t = I
items.statement: For a log-concave p (with support in a ball of radius R > n), c_0 = 0 and dc_t = dW_t + mu_t dt, where p_t(x) = e^{c_t^T x - t||x||^2/2} p(x)/int e^{c_t^T y - t||y||^2/2} p(y) dy, mu_t = E_{p_t} x and A_t = Cov(p_t).
items.note: Eldan's localization with identity control matrix: the Gaussian factor e^{-t||x||^2/2} is deterministic and the SDE is n-dimensional with additive noise and bounded drift mu_t that is Lipschitz in c_t (derivative A_t); existence and uniqueness are cited from Oksendal Sec. 5.2. The truncation to a ball is justified by Lemma 24 and Theorem 25. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Density is a martingale
items.statement: For every x in R^n, dp_t(x) = (x - mu_t)^T dW_t p_t(x).
items.note: Proved in Section 4.4 by Ito's formula for q_t(x) = e^{c_t^T x - t||x||^2/2} p(x) and for V_t^{-1}, V_t = int q_t. The proofs then use that p_t(x), p_t(E) and the boundary measure p_t(boundary E) are true martingales and interchange d with spatial integrals, which the bounded support makes valid but is not argued.

items.label: Covariance SDE
items.statement: dA_t = int (x - mu_t)(x - mu_t)^T ((x - mu_t)^T dW_t) p_t(x) dx - A_t^2 dt; in particular d mu_t = A_t dW_t.
items.note: Proved in Section 4.4 by Ito's formula for A_t as a function of mu_t and p_t.

items.label: Mass of a half set
items.statement: For every E with p(E) = 1/2 and t >= 0, P(1/4 <= p_t(E) <= 3/4) >= 9/10 - P(int_0^t ||A_s||_op ds >= 1/64).
items.note: d[g]_t <= ||A_t||_op dt for g_t = p_t(E), then Dambis-Dubins-Schwarz, the reflection principle and P(N(0,1) > 2) <= 0.0228.

items.label: Gaussian-tilted isoperimetry
items.statement: If f is integrable log-concave and h = f e^{-t||x||^2/2}/int f e^{-t||y||^2/2}, then h is log-concave and h(boundary S) >= c sqrt t min(h(S), h(R^n minus S)) for every measurable S, i.e. psi_h <= C/sqrt t.
items.note: Quoted from CV2014 and implied by the paper's Theorem 46. For a probability law ν = volume.tilted (−W) with W ∈ C² and Hess W ≥ t Id, t > 0, the local ingredients are literatureConstant_le_inv_of_eq_tilted (C_P ≤ 1/t, KLS/LogConcave/HeatSemigroup/Curvature.lean) and inverseScale_sq_le_pi_literature (Ψ² ≤ π C_P). No declaration is mapped here to the composed source statement for an arbitrary integrable log-concave factor, including nonsmooth factors.

items.label: Covariance control gives KLS
items.statement: If p is log-concave and T > 0 satisfies P(int_0^T ||A_s||_op ds <= 1/64) >= 3/4 for the localization of Definition 26 started at p, then psi_p = O(T^{-1/2}).
items.note: For E with p(E) = 1/2: p(boundary E) = E p_T(boundary E) >~ sqrt T E min(p_T(E), p_T(E^c)) by Theorem 30, and Lemma 29 bounds the last expectation below. The martingale identity for the boundary measure needs only the inequality E p_T(boundary E) <= p(boundary E) (Fatou), which is the direction used. The display in the proof writes int_0^t for int_0^T.

items.label: Third-moment vector bound
items.statement: For log-concave p with mean mu and covariance A and every PSD C, ||E_p (x - mu)(x - mu)^T C (x - mu)||_2 <= C' ||A||_op^{1/2} Tr(A^{1/2} C A^{1/2}) for a universal C'.
items.note: Rank-one case by Cauchy-Schwarz and fourth moments of one-dimensional log-concave marginals, then spectral decomposition of C. Deterministic.

items.label: Third-moment tensor bound
items.statement: For log-concave p with mean mu and covariance A, E_{x,y ~ p} |<x - mu, y - mu>|^3 <= C (Tr A^2)^{3/2} for a universal C.
items.note: Deterministic: one-dimensional reverse Holder in y, then Lemma 23 for A^{1/2} x.

items.label: Ito formula for Tr A_t^2
items.statement: d Tr A_t^2 = 2 E_{p_t}[(x - mu_t)^T A_t (x - mu_t)(x - mu_t)^T] dW_t - 2 Tr(A_t^3) dt + E_{x,y ~ p_t}[((x - mu_t)^T (y - mu_t))^3] dt.
items.note: Proved in Section 4.4 from the matrix Ito formula and d[A_ij, A_ji]_t.

items.label: Potential Tr A_t^2 stays bounded
items.statement: For log-concave p with covariance A and its localization, there is a universal c_1 > 0 such that P(max_{t in [0,T]} Tr A_t^2 >= 8 Tr A_0^2) <= 0.01 with T = c_1/sqrt(Tr A_0^2).
items.note: Drift <= C' Phi_t^{3/2} by Lemma 33, martingale part ||v_t|| <~ Phi_t^{5/4} by Lemma 32 (the printed inequality drops the constant), then Ito for f(a) = -(a + Phi_0)^{-1/2}, Dambis-Dubins-Schwarz and the reflection principle.

items.label: Isotropic log-isoperimetry 1/D
items.statement: For an isotropic log-concave p with support of diameter D and measurable S (with p(S) <= 1/2), p(boundary S) >= c (log(1/p(S))/D + sqrt(log(1/p(S))/D)) p(S) for a universal c > 0.
items.note: Labelled lem:expand_p but typeset as a theorem. The printed statement omits p(S) <= 1/2, which the proof needs through Lemma 45. Proof in Section 5.5: martingale property, Theorem 46 at time T and Lemma 45, with the two admissible choices of T.

items.label: Spectral norm stays bounded
items.statement: If for some k >= 1, psi_p <= C (Tr A^k)^{1/(2k)} for every log-concave p with covariance A, there is a universal c such that for the localization of an isotropic log-concave p and 0 <= T <= 1/(c k n^{1/k}), P(max_{t in [0,T]} ||A_t||_op >= 2) <= 2 exp(-1/(cT)).
items.note: Potential Psi_t = -(u_t + 1)^{-3} for the Stieltjes potential u of display (1.1) with Phi = 2^{-k} n and q = ceil k, then Dambis-Dubins-Schwarz and reflection. The statement leaves isotropy of p implicit (u_0 = 3/2 uses A_0 = I). The remark after it records that Theorem 12 gives the hypothesis with k = 2.

items.label: Ito formula for Stieltjes potential
items.statement: For u_t = u(A_t) with u defined by Tr((uI - X)^{-q}) = Phi, X <= uI, du_t = alpha_t^T dW_t + beta_t dt with alpha_t = kappa_t^{-1} E_{tilde p_t}[x^T (uI - A_t)^{-(q+1)} x x] and beta_t/(q+1) bounded by the three displayed third-moment terms, kappa_t = Tr((uI - A_t)^{-(q+1)}) and tilde p_t the centred p_t.
items.note: Matrix Ito formula with the Hessian of Lemma 41 and Lemma 42 to merge the first Hessian term. The printed reference Definition 1.1 is display (1.1).

items.label: Anisotropic third-moment bound
items.statement: Under the hypothesis of Lemma 37, for log-concave p with mean mu and covariance A and PSD B1, B2, B3, |E_{x,y ~ p} prod_{i=1}^3 (x - mu)^T B_i (y - mu)| <= C Tr(A^{1/2} B1 A^{1/2}) (Tr (A^{1/2} B2 A^{1/2})^k)^{1/k} ||A^{1/2} B3 A^{1/2}||_op.
items.note: Uses Theorem 5 for the non-isotropic law of B2^{1/2} x together with the anisotropic KLS hypothesis (the printed exponent -1/2k is a sign typo for 1/2k); the reduction to isotropic p and diagonal B1 is by linear change of variables.

items.label: Drift and diffusion of u_t
items.statement: Under the hypothesis of Lemma 37 and q = ceil k, du_t = alpha_t^T dW_t + beta_t dt with ||alpha_t||_2 <= C u_t^{3/2} and beta_t <= C k u_t^4 Phi^{1/k}.
