items.note: Deterministic estimates of the coefficients of Lemma 38.

items.label: Derivatives of the Stieltjes potential
items.statement: Du(X)[H] = Tr((uI - X)^{-(q+1)} H)/Tr((uI - X)^{-(q+1)}), and D^2 u(X)[H1, H2] is given by the displayed four-term formula.
items.note: Implicit differentiation of display (1.1). Deterministic matrix calculus.

items.label: Trace shift inequality
items.statement: For positive definite A, symmetric Delta and alpha, beta >= 0, Tr(A^alpha Delta A^beta Delta) <= Tr(A^{alpha+beta} Delta^2).
items.note: Attributed to Eldan 2013. Lean states it for real square matrices over any finite index type, with A^α the continuous functional calculus cfc (· ^ α) A; the proof diagonalizes A and uses (a^α − b^α)(a^β − b^β) ≥ 0 in place of weighted AM-GM. Deterministic.

items.label: Quadratic variation of p_t(E)
items.statement: For fixed E and g_t = p_t(E), g_t is a martingale with d[g]_t <= D^2 g_t^2 dt and d[g]_t <= 30 ||A_t||_op g_t^2 log^2(e/g_t) dt, where D is the diameter of the support.
items.note: First bound from the support diameter, second from Holder with ell = log(e/g_t) and Lemma 23.

items.label: log(1/g_t) stays controlled
items.statement: For T, gamma >= 0, with probability at least 1 - 4 exp(-gamma^2/(2 T D^2)), for all 0 <= t <= T, log(1/g_0) - gamma <= log(1/g_t) <= log(1/g_0) + D^2 t/2 + gamma.
items.note: The proof cites (5.3) in Lemma 29; the bound is (5.3) of Lemma 43 (cross-reference error in the source).

items.label: g sqrt(log 1/g) is preserved
items.statement: There is a universal c such that for measurable E with p_0(E) <= 1/2 and 0 <= T <= c max(D^{-2} log(1/p_0(E)), 1/(log(1/p_0(E)) + D)), E[p_T(E) sqrt(log(1/p_T(E))) 1_{p_T(E) <= 1/2}] >= p_0(E) sqrt(log(1/p_0(E)))/5.
items.note: Two cases on T; the second applies Lemma 37 with k = 2 (hence relies on Theorem 12) using D >= sqrt n for isotropic laws; the proof cites (5.4) of Lemma 29 for Lemma 43 and mixes D and sqrt n in the time bound.

items.label: Gaussian-tilted log-isoperimetry
items.statement: If f is integrable log-concave, t >= 0 and h = f e^{-t||x||^2/2}/int f e^{-t||y||^2/2}, then for every S with h(S) <= 1/2, h(boundary S) >= c sqrt t h(S) sqrt(log(1/h(S))).
items.note: Quoted from Ledoux 1999 and reproved by the KLS localization lemma (reduction to one-dimensional needles e^{-gamma x - t x^2/2} on intervals) and three Gaussian tail cases. Implies Theorem 30. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Log-isoperimetry implies log-Sobolev
items.statement: If mu is absolutely continuous on R^n and mu(boundary A) >= phi mu(A) sqrt(log(1/mu(A))) for every open A with mu(A) <= 1/2, then int |grad f|^2 dmu >= c phi^2 int f^2 log f^2 dmu for every f with int f^2 dmu = 1.
items.note: Quoted, not proved.

items.label: Log-Sobolev for bounded isotropic laws
items.statement: For an isotropic log-concave p with support of diameter D and every f with int f^2 p = 1, int |grad f|^2 p >= (c/D) int f^2 log f^2 p.
items.note: Immediate from Theorems 47 and 36; tight by Lemma 54 (remark after it).

items.label: Small ball under subgaussian tails
items.statement: If p is log-concave with covariance A and subgaussian constant beta, i.e. E<x, theta>^{2k} <= beta^{2k} E g^{2k} for all theta and k, then for every y and 0 <= epsilon <= c_1, P(||x - y||^2 <= epsilon Tr A) <= epsilon^{c_2 beta^{-2} ||A||_op^{-1} Tr A}.
items.note: Quoted from Paouris 2012 (printed with the hypothesis written for unit theta implicitly and b for beta).

items.label: Speedy walk log-Cheeger
items.statement: For the speedy walk with steps delta <= C on an isotropic convex body K of diameter D, every subset of measure s with e^{-O(D/delta^2)} <= s <= 1/2 has expansion psi(s) >= c (delta/sqrt n)(sqrt(log(1/s)/D) + log(1/s)/D).
items.note: Standard three-set partition, the martingale property of p_t, Theorem 52 at time T and Lemma 45. Here psi(s) denotes the Markov-chain expansion, not the KLS constant.

items.label: Local conductance facts
items.statement: For a convex body K the local conductance ell(x) = vol(K cap (x + delta B_n))/vol(delta B_n) is log-concave and proportional to the speedy-walk stationary density; if K contains a unit ball, K' = {ell >= 3/4} has vol(K') >= (1 - 2 delta sqrt n) vol(K).
items.note: Stated without proof (standard facts from the ball-walk literature).

items.label: Gaussian-tilted three-set inequality
items.statement: For h as in Theorem 46 and a partition S1, S2, S3 of R^n with h(S1) <= h(S2) such that every u in S1, v in S2 has ||u - v|| >= d or d_h(u, v) >= d_h, h(S3) >= c min(d_h/sqrt n, d sqrt(t log(1/h(S1)))) h(S1).
items.note: Proof sketch: localization reduces to needles, then Theorem 46 or Lemma 3.8 of KLS97.

items.label: One-step coupling
items.statement: For x, y in K with ||x - y|| <= delta/sqrt n, d_TV(P_x, P_y) < 1 - d_ell(x, y).
items.note: Quoted.

items.label: Log-Sobolev lower-bound example
items.statement: For every 2 sqrt n <= D <= n/2 there is an isotropic log-concave distribution of diameter D whose log-Cheeger constant is O(1/sqrt D) and log-Sobolev constant O(1/D).
items.note: Truncated cone K_D; a slab S of measure e^{-Omega(D)} with expansion at most 2. The log-Sobolev part uses rho = Theta(kappa^2), cited from Ledoux. K_D is only asserted to be nearly isotropic.

items.label: Ball walk lower bound
items.statement: For every 2 sqrt n <= D <= n/2 there is an isotropic convex body of diameter D on which the ball walk needs Omega~(n^2 D) proper steps to mix.
items.note: Drift argument on the truncated cone from the slab start, using Claim 56; the proof takes delta = 1/sqrt n and D < 0.99 n.

items.label: Slices stay radially unimodal
items.statement: Started from the uniform law on the slab S, the ball-walk distribution on the cone at every time is spherically symmetric and unimodal on every cross-section.
items.note: Proved inside the proof of Lemma 55 by a one-step monotonicity argument.

items.label: Isotropic-only third-moment bound
items.statement: If psi_n <= C n^{1/(2k)} for all n for some k >= 2, then for log-concave p with mean mu, covariance A and PSD B1, B2, B3, the trilinear moment of Lemma 39 is at most C (log n)^{1-1/k} Tr(A^{1/2}B1A^{1/2}) (Tr(A^{1/2}B2A^{1/2})^k)^{1/k} ||A^{1/2}B3A^{1/2}||_op.
items.note: Appendix A: dyadic eigenvalue decomposition of B2 and the isotropic KLS bound for rank-r_i projections. psi_n (the supremum of psi_p over isotropic log-concave p on R^n) is not formally defined in the paper.

items.label: Spectral norm bound, isotropic KLS
items.statement: If psi_n <= C n^{1/(2k)} for all n for some k >= 2, there is a universal c such that for 0 <= T <= 1/(c k (log n)^{1-1/k} n^{1/k}), P(max_{t in [0,T]} ||A_t||_op >= 2) <= 2 exp(-1/(cT)).
items.note: Stated as the result of replacing Lemma 39 by Lemma 57 in Section 5.1; no separate proof.

papers.title: The Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits conjecture
papers.result: A guide to KLS formulations, geometric consequences and algorithmic motivation at the 2018 frontier.
papers.remaining: Use for orientation; its historical frontier is superseded by the later papers in the frontier table.

papers.title: Stein kernels and moment maps
papers.result: Constructs Stein kernels using moment maps, connecting Hessian geometry to probabilistic identities.
papers.remaining: The canonical moment-map Stein kernel is not locally formalized.

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: Probability measures on R^d; gamma is the standard Gaussian measure (gamma_1 in dimension one). A Stein kernel tau_mu : R^d -> M_d(R) for mu satisfies int x . f dmu = int <tau_mu, nabla f>_HS dmu for smooth vector-valued f (display (1) prints dnu for dmu), with tests in H^1(mu) when tau_mu is in L^2(mu) and mu has finite second moments; the Stein discrepancy is S(mu)^2 = inf_tau int |tau - Id|_HS^2 dmu. The moment map of a centered mu is a convex phi with (nabla phi)_# e^{-phi} dx = mu, equivalently the toric Kahler-Einstein equation e^{-phi} = rho(nabla phi) det(nabla^2 phi) (display (3)); phi^* is its Legendre transform. W_p is the p-Kantorovich-Wasserstein distance with Euclidean cost (the printed formula omits the 1/p power); mu_n is the law of n^{-1/2} sum_{i<=n} X_i for i.i.d. X_i ~ mu. Isotropic means centered with identity covariance.
lemma_map.omitted: Remark 2.2 is omitted as purely expository (it compares this kernel with the Courtade-Fathi-Pananjady construction and notes their earlier existence result under a Poincare inequality); the unnumbered Section 4 derivation of the weighted Poincare inequality Var_nu(f) <= int <tau nabla f, nabla f> dnu from Brascamp-Lieb and the unnumbered Section 5 transport of Stein kernels to non-Gaussian reference measures are not listed, as no Lean declaration states them; the paper has no numbered Definitions, Lemmas, Examples, Conjectures or appendix statements.

items.label: Existence of moment maps
items.statement: If mu is a centered measure on R^d with finite first moment, not supported on a hyperplane, then there is a convex function phi such that mu is the pushforward of the probability measure with density e^{-phi} under nabla phi; phi is called the moment map of mu.
items.note: Quoted from Cordero-Erausquin and Klartag without proof; the probability normalisation of e^{-phi} is implicit. No Lean counterpart: the library has no moment maps or Monge-Ampere objects.

items.label: Smoothness of moment maps
items.statement: If mu is supported on a compact (bounded) open convex set with a smooth density rho satisfying C^{-1} <= rho <= C on its support for some C > 0, then the moment map phi of Theorem 2.1 is smooth and finite on all of R^d.
items.note: Quoted from Berman and Berndtsson without proof (Caffarelli regularity). Equivalently phi solves the toric Kahler-Einstein equation e^{-phi} = rho(nabla phi) det(nabla^2 phi), display (3) of the PDF. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Moment map yields Stein kernel
items.statement: If mu has a Lebesgue density rho and the solution phi of e^{-phi} = rho(nabla phi) det(nabla^2 phi) is C^2 and finite on all of R^d, then tau = Hess phi(nabla phi^*) = (Hess phi^*)^{-1} is a Stein kernel for mu with respect to the standard Gaussian, and S(mu)^2 <= int |Hess phi - Id|_HS^2 e^{-phi} dx. In particular this applies when mu is supported on a compact convex set with density bounded above and below by positive constants.
items.note: Proof: Gaussian-type integration by parts against e^{-phi} (no boundary term since phi grows linearly, Klartag 2007 Lemma 2.1), test f = g(nabla phi), then the change of variables y = nabla phi^*(x). Main theorem: it is the construction announced first in the abstract, carries the LaTeX label main_thm_stein, and every later result (Corollary 2.4, Theorems 3.3 and 3.4, Section 4) is obtained from this kernel. No Lean counterpart: there is no Stein kernel, Stein discrepancy or moment map in the library; the scalar weighted integration by parts FunctionalInequalities.KLS.LogConcave.integral_inner_gradient_eq is a different identity (scalar Dirichlet form, compactly supported tests) and does not state this item.

items.label: Kernel is symmetric positive
items.statement: The Stein kernel of Theorem 2.3 takes values in symmetric positive definite matrices; in dimension one this explains why the explicit one-dimensional Stein kernel formula is nonnegative.
items.note: Immediate from tau = Hess phi(nabla phi^*) with phi convex and C^2, Hess phi > 0. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Bounded kernel, uniformly convex case
items.statement: If mu = e^{-V} dx with Hess V >= epsilon Id for some epsilon > 0, then mu has a Stein kernel tau with positive symmetric values and ||tau||_op <= epsilon^{-1} everywhere.
items.note: Kernel of Theorem 2.3; the bound ||Hess phi||_op <= 1/epsilon is Klartag's (2014) contraction estimate for moment maps, quoted without proof. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Stein kernel bounds W_p
items.statement: If tau is a Stein kernel for a probability measure mu on R^d, then for every p >= 2, W_p(mu, gamma) <= C_p (int ||tau - Id||_HS^p dmu)^{1/p} with C_p = (int |x|^p dgamma_1)^{1/p} = O(p).
items.note: Proved in Section 3.2 via the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck interpolation of Ledoux-Nourdin-Peccati (Proposition 3.4 there), Jensen, and the moment bound E||AZ||^p <= C_p^p ||A||_HS^p for symmetric A (Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund with sharp constant). The printed definition of W_p omits the 1/p power; the intended distance is (inf_pi int ||x-y||^p dpi)^{1/p}. No Lean counterpart (no Wasserstein distances in the library).

items.label: Klartag moment-map Hessian estimate
items.statement: If mu is a log-concave probability measure supported on an open bounded convex set with density bounded above and below, then its essentially continuous moment map phi is C^2 and, for all p >= 1 and theta in S^{d-1}, int |<Hess phi(nabla phi^*) theta, theta>|^p dmu <= 8^p p^{2p} (int (x . theta)^2 dmu)^p.
items.note: Due to Klartag (2014); Section 3.1 reproves it via Kolesnikov's curvature bound Ric >= 1/2 for (R^d, Hess phi, e^{-phi}) under the regularity of Theorem 2.2, the eigenfunction identities L partial_e phi = -partial_e phi and Gamma(partial_e phi) = partial_ee phi, the reverse local Poincare bound Gamma(P_t f) <= P_t(f^2)/(2(e^t-1)) (BGL Theorem 4.7.2) at t = ln 2, and log-Sobolev hypercontractivity of eigenfunctions (BGL Section 5.3). No Lean counterpart: the library's Bakry-Emery files work with the Euclidean metric and a fixed potential, not the Hessian metric of a moment map.

items.label: Continuous density suffices
items.statement: Klartag's results assume C^infinity smoothness via Berman-Berndtsson; since only C^2 smoothness of phi is needed, continuity of the density suffices.
items.note: Regularity relaxation asserted without proof; it underlies the continuous-density hypotheses of Theorems 3.3 and 3.4. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Log-concave CLT rate in W_p
items.statement: Let mu be an isotropic log-concave probability measure on R^d with strictly positive continuous density on its support, and mu_n the law of n^{-1/2}(X_1 + ... + X_n) for i.i.d. X_i ~ mu. Then for every p >= 2, W_p(mu_n, gamma) <= C~(p) d n^{-1/2}, with C~(p) depending only on p and growing like p^4.
items.note: Proof for compact support and density bounded below: the kernel of Theorem 2.3, its conditional averaging as a Stein kernel for mu_n (Courtade-Fathi-Pananjady Theorem 3.2), Jensen and Rosenthal (K_p = O(p)), Proposition 3.2 with isotropy (int (x.theta)^2 dmu = 1), then Proposition 3.1; explicit constant 2 K_p (1 + 8^p p^{2p})^{1/p} C_p; the general case by convex compact truncation. No Lean counterpart; FunctionalInequalities.KLS.LogConcave is only the log-concavity predicate, does not restrict this rate statement, and is not mapped.

items.label: Uniformly log-concave CLT rate
items.statement: Let mu = e^{-V} be isotropic with strictly positive continuous density on its support and Hess V >= epsilon Id for some epsilon > 0; with mu_n as in Theorem 3.3, for every p >= 2, W_p(mu_n, gamma) <= C(p) sqrt(d) / (epsilon n^{1/2}), with C(p) growing like p^4.
items.note: Proof omitted in the paper: same argument as Theorem 3.3 with the operator-norm bound of Corollary 2.4 replacing Proposition 3.2. The sqrt(d) dependence is sharp (product measures). No Lean counterpart.

papers.title: An almost constant lower bound of the isoperimetric coefficient in the KLS conjecture
papers.locator: Main bound, translated from the lower-bound convention for h
papers.result: ψₙ ≤ exp(C√(log n · log log n)) = n^o(1); hence C_P = n^o(1), breaking the polynomial barrier.
papers.remaining: The stochastic-localization bootstrap and the subpolynomial bound are not locally formalized.

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: Log-concave probability densities p on R^d (absolutely continuous, hence full-dimensional). ψ(p) is the Cheeger isoperimetric coefficient of (2), a lower-bound quantity (larger is better), with p⁺ the lower outer Minkowski content over closed ε-neighbourhoods; ρ(p) = ‖Cov_p‖_op; log is natural; KLS reads ψ(p) ≥ c/√ρ(p). ψ_d of (7) is the infimum of ψ(p)√ρ(p) over compactly supported log-concave densities on R^d. The repository's Isoperimetry.constant is ψ on the affine support and Isoperimetry.inverseScale is Ψ = 1/ψ, so Chen's lower bounds on ψ are upper bounds on Ψ. The localization statements (Lemmas 3–8) assume compact support and invertible covariance A, with d ≥ 3 where stated; q = ⌈1/β⌉ + 1 ≥ 3 for 0 < β ≤ 1/2; c denotes unspecified universal constants.
lemma_map.omitted: Figure 1 (proof diagram), the expository introduction (consequences for slicing, thin-shell, concentration and MCMC, and the cited bounds of Bourgain, Klartag, Eldan–Klartag and Eldan), the remark after Lemma 6 and the Notation paragraph are not items. Displays (1), (5)–(6), (8)–(14), (17), (19)–(22), (24), (27)–(28), (30)–(33) and (35) are definitions or proof steps recorded with the statements they define or prove. Appendix A contains only the proofs of Lemma 3 and (15)–(16); the paper has no numbered Definition, Proposition, Corollary or Remark environments, and a lemma commented out in the LaTeX source is not printed. Unnumbered displayed claims and cited tools are listed only where a local Lean declaration states them; 14 others (equations, cited SDE, Itô and Brascamp–Lieb tools) are not listed.

items.label: KLS conjecture
items.statement: There is a universal constant c > 0 such that every log-concave density p on R^d satisfies ψ(p) ≥ c/√ρ(p), where ρ(p) = ‖Cov_p‖_op is the spectral norm of the covariance and ψ is the coefficient of (2).
items.note: Quoted and open. The repository names a covariance-normalized Poincaré form (KLS.Conjecture, C_P ≤ C‖Cov‖_op); it is equivalent to this form through the proved comparisons C_P ≤ 4Ψ² and Ψ² ≤ π C_P, but no Lean declaration states Conjecture 1 itself and none is mapped.

items.label: Isoperimetric coefficient ψ(p)
items.statement: For a density p on R^d, ψ(p) = inf over S ⊂ R^d of p⁺(∂S)/min(p(S), p(S^c)), where p⁺(∂S) = liminf as ε → 0⁺ of (p({x : d(x, S) ≤ ε}) − p(S))/ε.
items.note: Lean takes measurable sets of mass in (0, 1), open thickenings and the induced metric on the affine support of an arbitrary finite-dimensional law, with value ⊤ in dimension zero; Isoperimetry.inverseScale is Ψ = 1/ψ. Agreement with the closed-neighbourhood, all-subsets convention of (2) is not stated in Lean.

items.label: Almost constant KLS lower bound
items.statement: There is a universal constant c such that for every log-concave density p on R^d and every integer ℓ ≥ 1, ψ(p) ≥ 1/([c·ℓ(log(d) + 1)]^{ℓ/2} d^{16/ℓ} √ρ(p)), where ρ(p) = ‖Cov_p‖_op.
items.note: Main theorem; the d^{-o(1)} form is its unnumbered corollary C1. Proof: truncate p to a ball B about its mean with p(B^c) ≤ 0.2, so ψ(p) ≥ ψ(ϱ)/2 for the compactly supported truncation ϱ (via P0), then apply Lemma 1; the needed ρ(ϱ) ≤ ρ(p)/p(B) ≤ 1.25 ρ(p) is used tacitly. In repository notation Ψ ≤ [cℓ(log d + 1)]^{ℓ/2} d^{16/ℓ}√ρ, and Cheeger's C_P ≤ 4Ψ² converts it to a Poincaré bound. No Lean statement.

items.label: Subpolynomial form d^{-o(1)}
items.statement: Taking ℓ = ⌈(log(d)/log log(d))^{1/2}⌉ in Theorem 1 gives a constant c' with ψ(p) ≥ d^{−c'(log log(d)/log(d))^{1/2}}/√ρ(p), i.e. ψ(p)√ρ(p) ≥ exp(−c'√(log d · log log d)) = d^{−o(1)}, for d large enough that log log d > 0.
items.note: The register's ψₙ ≤ exp(C√(log n log log n)) = n^{o(1)} is this bound in the inverse-scale convention.

items.label: Main bound for compact support
items.statement: There is a universal constant c such that every log-concave density p on R^d with compact support and every integer ℓ ≥ 1 satisfy ψ(p) ≥ 1/([c·ℓ(log(d) + 1)]^{ℓ/2} d^{16/ℓ} √ρ(p)).
items.note: Induction on ℓ: assuming ψ_k ≥ 1/(α_ℓ(log d + 1)^{ℓ/2} k^{β_ℓ}) for k ≤ d, Lemma 2 with α = α_ℓ(log d + 1)^{ℓ/2} and q ≤ 2/β_ℓ yields the step ℓ + 1; the bounds (24) give the stated form.

items.label: One bootstrap step
items.statement: If ψ_k ≥ 1/(αk^β) for all k ≤ d, with 0 ≤ β ≤ 1/2 and α ≥ 1, then for q = ⌈1/β⌉ + 1 there is a universal constant c with ψ_d ≥ 1/(c·q^{1/2} α log(d)^{1/2} d^{β − β/(8q)}).
items.note: q requires β > 0 (Lemma 5 assumes 0 < β). For d ≥ 3: for p(E) = 1/2, p(∂E) ≥ E p_{T₂}(∂E) ≥ (1/8)T₂^{1/2}‖A‖^{−1/2} min(p(E), p(E^c)) using GI, Lemmas 4–5 and B_t = tA^{−1} (the martingale identity for the boundary measure needs Fatou, giving the correct inequality direction). As printed, the right side is undefined at d = 1 (log 1 = 0); the d = 1, 2 cases from (3) hold with log(d) read as log(d) + 1, which is how Lemma 1 uses it.

items.label: Localization SDE well-posed
items.statement: If p is a density on R^d with compact support and invertible covariance A, the SDE dc_t = A^{−1/2}dW_t + A^{−1}μ_t dt, dB_t = A^{−1}dt, c₀ = 0, B₀ = 0, with p_t(x) ∝ exp(c_tᵀx − xᵀB_t x/2)p(x) and μ_t its mean, has a unique solution on [0, T] for every T > 0, and for each x, p_t(x) is a martingale with dp_t(x) = (x − μ_t)ᵀA^{−1/2}dW_t p_t(x).
items.note: Log-concavity is not assumed. Proved in Appendix A: Lipschitz coefficients from compact support, then Itô's formula for G_t(x) = exp(c_tᵀx − xᵀB_tx/2)p(x), V_t = ∫G_t and V_t^{−1}.

items.label: Half-mass set stays balanced
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Lemma 3, for every measurable E with p(E) = 1/2 and every t > 0, P(1/4 ≤ p_t(E) ≤ 3/4) ≥ 9/10 − P(∫₀ᵗ ‖A^{−1/2}A_sA^{−1/2}‖_op ds ≥ 1/64).
items.note: The integrand is printed with A_t; read A_s. Proof: d[g]_t ≤ ‖Q_t‖_op dt for g_t = p_t(E) by Cauchy–Schwarz, then Dambis–Dubins–Schwarz, the reflection principle and P(N > 2) < 0.023.

items.label: Spectral norm control
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Lemma 3, if ψ_k ≥ 1/(αk^β) for all k ≤ d with 0 < β ≤ 1/2 and α ≥ 1, then for q = ⌈1/β⌉ + 1, d ≥ 3 and T₂ = 1/(c·qα²log(d)d^{2β−β/(4q)}) with c universal, P(∫₀^{T₂} ‖A^{−1/2}A_tA^{−1/2}‖_op dt ≥ 1/64) < 4/10.
items.note: The proof takes T₁ = 1/(32768qα²log(d)d^{2β}) and T₂ = d^{β/(4q)}T₁/40, i.e. c = 1310720: probability ≤ 3/10 on [0, T₁] by Lemma 7 and ≤ 1/10 on [T₁, T₂] by (18), Lemma 8 and Markov. Log-concavity of p, not part of Lemma 3, is needed through Lemma 6.

items.label: Potential drift and diffusion bounds
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Lemma 5, dΓ_t = v_tᵀdW_t + δ_t dt with ‖v_t‖₂ ≤ 16qΓ_t^{1+1/(2q)} and δ_t ≤ min{64q²α²log(d)d^{2β−1/q}Γ_t^{1+1/q}, 2q²Γ_t/t}.
items.note: The 1/t bound is new relative to Lee–Vempala: ϱ_t, the law of A^{−1/2}(X − μ_t), is log-concave (linear images of log-concave laws) and more log-concave than N(0, I_d/t).

items.label: Potential stays small up to T₁
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Lemma 6, with h(a) = −(a + 1)^{−1/q} and T₁ = 1/(32768qα²log(d)d^{2β}), P(max_{t∈[0,T₁]} h(Γ_t) ≥ −(d + 1)^{−1/q}/2) ≤ exp(−(2/3)q log(d)) ≤ 3/10.
items.note: Γ₀ = d. Itô's formula for the concave h drops the correction; the proof gives exp(−(2/3)qα²log(d)d^{2β−2/q}), which implies the printed bound since βq ≥ 1 and α ≥ 1; d ≥ 3 and q ≥ 2 give ≤ 3/10.

items.label: Polynomial growth of E Γ^{1/q}
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Lemma 6, with f(a) = a^{1/q}, E f(Γ_{t₂}) ≤ E f(Γ_{t₁})(t₂/t₁)^{2q} for all t₂ > t₁ > 0.
items.note: Itô's formula for the concave f, the bound δ_t ≤ 2q²Γ_t/t and the asserted martingale property of ∫Γ_t^{1/q−1}v_tᵀdW_t give d E f(Γ_t) ≤ (2q/t)E f(Γ_t)dt, integrated by Grönwall.

items.label: Vector third-moment bound
items.statement: If p is log-concave with mean μ and covariance A, then for all positive semi-definite B, C, ‖∫B^{1/2}(x − μ)(x − μ)ᵀC(x − μ)p(x)dx‖₂ ≤ 16‖A^{1/2}BA^{1/2}‖_op^{1/2} Tr(A^{1/2}CA^{1/2}).
items.note: Eigen-decomposition of C, Cauchy–Schwarz and (29) with a = 4, b = 2.

items.label: Tensor bound from the hypothesis
items.statement: If ψ_k ≥ 1/(αk^β) for all k ≤ d with 0 ≤ β ≤ 1/2 and α ≥ 1, and p is log-concave on R^d with invertible covariance A, then for q ≥ 1/(2β), T_p(A^{q−2}, I_d, I_d) ≤ 128α²log(d)d^{2β−1/q}Tr(A^q)^{1+1/q}.
items.note: Standardize to the isotropic law ϱ, swap exponents by Lemma 12, expand A^q in eigenvectors and apply Lemma 13(2), then Hölder (called Cauchy–Schwarz). Effectively β > 0. Lemma 13 is applied to ϱ, which has compact support in the application.

items.label: Tensor bound under a Gaussian factor
items.statement: If τ > 0 and p is log-concave, more log-concave than N(0, τ^{−1}I_d), with invertible covariance A, then for q ≥ 3, T_p(A^{q−2}, I_d, I_d) ≤ (4/τ)Tr(A^q).
items.note: Eigen-decomposition of A, Brascamp–Lieb for the quadratics xᵀΔ_ix, Cauchy–Schwarz, Lemma 12 to raise A^{q−3}, then rearrangement.

items.label: Tensor exponent swap
items.statement: If p is log-concave on R^d, δ ∈ [0, 1] and A, B, C are positive semi-definite, then T_p(B^{1/2}A^δB^{1/2}, B^{1/2}A^{1−δ}B^{1/2}, C) ≤ T_p(B^{1/2}AB^{1/2}, B, C).
items.note: The proof does not use log-concavity, only finite third moments: both sides are sums of traces Tr(A^δΔ_iA^{1−δ}Δ_i) and Tr(AΔ_iΔ_i).

items.locator: Lemma 13, part 1 (Lee–Vempala, arXiv v2 Lemma 41; Eldan Lemma 6)
items.label: Δ-trace bound for projections
items.statement: If p is an isotropic log-concave density on R^d, v a unit vector and Δ = E(Xᵀv)XXᵀ, then Tr(ΔPΔ) ≤ 16ψ_{min(2r,d)}^{−2} for every orthogonal projection P of rank r.
items.note: Cauchy–Schwarz and Cheeger's inequality for the quadratic xᵀΔPx, which depends on a projection of rank ≤ min(2r, d). The ψ_k hypothesis of the lemma is not needed for this part; ψ_k is defined over compactly supported densities, which holds in the application.

items.label: Δ-trace bound for PSD weights
items.statement: If ψ_k ≥ 1/(αk^β) for all k ≤ d with 0 < β ≤ 1/2 and α ≥ 1, then with p, v, Δ as in part 1, Tr(ΔAΔ) ≤ 128α²log(d)(Tr A^{1/(2β)})^{2β} for every positive semi-definite A.
items.note: Groups the eigenvalues of A into J = ⌈log d⌉ exponential blocks plus a small remainder, applies part 1 and the hypothesis to each block, then Hölder.

items.locator: Proof of Lemma 13, step (ii) (Maz'ya; Cheeger; Milman Theorem 1.1)
items.label: Cheeger's inequality
items.statement: For a probability density with isoperimetric coefficient ψ, Var(g) ≤ 4ψ^{−2}E‖∇g‖² for locally Lipschitz g; equivalently the Poincaré constant satisfies C_P ≤ 4/ψ².
items.note: Lean proves C_P ≤ 4Ψ² (Ψ = 1/ψ) for finite-dimensional log-concave laws, and h² Var(g) ≤ 4∫‖∇g‖² for bounded C¹ Lipschitz g under every probability law with the Minkowski constant h. Chen applies it to an unbounded quadratic on a marginal; that instance is not separately stated in Lean.

papers.title: Sharp Cheeger–Buser type inequalities in RCD(K,∞) spaces
papers.locator: Cheeger–Buser comparison; log-concave specialization in Letwin, introduction
papers.result: Provides the sharp reverse-comparison input used to normalize ψ² and C_P; in the log-concave convention, 1/4 ≤ ψ²/C_P ≤ π.
papers.remaining: The numerical comparison is formalized for finite-dimensional log-concave laws. For the bounded-support metric BV test class, complement symmetry for finite measures, the half-mass/symmetric equality, the BV–Minkowski Cheeger identification for probability laws on normed spaces, and, for finite-dimensional log-concave laws, the identification of the BV Cheeger constant on the closed intrinsic support with the isoperimetric constant are formalized. Test-class equivalence is formalized for finite Borel measures (global Lipschitz/global L¹), and on proper spaces also for locally Lipschitz/global or compact-local L¹ approximants. The test-class comparison beyond this scope, constant identification on nonconvex supports, and the paper's RCD(K,∞) theorem remain unformalized.

local_results.scope: Both numerical inequalities for every finite-dimensional log-concave probability law, including zero-dimensional affine support and extended optima
Closed-support BV Cheeger constant equals the isoperimetric constant for finite-dimensional log-concave laws

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: RCD(K, ∞) metric measure spaces; h(X) is the min-denominator Cheeger constant and λ₁ = 1/C_P the spectral gap (λ₀ the bottom of the spectrum when m(X) = ∞). Finite-dimensional log-concave laws on Euclidean spaces are RCD(0, ∞) with m(X) = 1. Unnumbered proof steps (46) and (48) are listed because local Lean results state them.
lemma_map.omitted: Remark 1.3 (discreteness of the spectrum) is expository.

items.label: Sharp implicit Buser inequality
items.statement: On RCD(K, ∞) spaces with m(X) = 1, h(X) ≥ sup over t > 0 of (1 − e^(−λ₁t))/J_K(t), sharp for the Gaussian when K > 0; with m(X) = ∞, h(X) ≥ 2 sup (1 − e^(−λ₀t))/J_K(t). Here J₀(t) = 2√t/√π.
items.note: No implicit (supremum over t) form is stated locally; only the explicit π bound of Corollary 1.2 is proved, in the Euclidean log-concave case.

items.label: Explicit Buser inequalities
items.statement: For K > 0 and K/λ₁ ≥ c: λ₁ ≤ (π/2c)h²; for K = 0 and m(X) = 1: λ₁ ≤ (4/π)h² inf_T T/(1 − e^(−T))² < πh²; explicit bounds for K < 0 and for infinite measure.
items.note: The K = 0, m(X) = 1 case in its weaker displayed form λ₁ ≤ πh², i.e. Ψ² ≤ π C_P, for every finite-dimensional log-concave law; the sharper constant (4/π) inf_T T/(1 − e^(−T))², the K ≠ 0 cases and infinite measure are not formalized.

items.label: CD(K, ∞) condition
items.statement: Entropy is K-convex along some W₂-geodesic between any two measures of finite entropy.

items.label: RCD(K, ∞) condition
items.statement: CD(K, ∞) together with a quadratic Cheeger energy.

items.label: Isoperimetric gradient bound for the heat flow
items.statement: For f with values in [0, 1]: |D(H_t f)|² ≤ j_K(t)([I(H_t f)]² − [H_t(I(f))]²) with I the Gaussian isoperimetric profile; hence ‖|D H_t f|‖_∞ ≤ √(2/π)√(j_K(t))‖f‖_∞, with j₀(t) = 1/(2t).
items.note: Not stated locally. The local reverse Poincaré inequality gives |∇P_t f| ≤ ‖f‖_∞/√(2t), a weaker constant for the L^∞ gradient bound.

items.label: Spectral heat decay
items.statement: For mean-zero f ∈ L²: ‖H_t f‖₂ ≤ e^(−λ₁t)‖f‖₂.
items.note: Squared form with C = 1/λ₁ for the weighted-gradient heat semigroup of a smooth convex tilted law.

items.label: L¹ heat displacement with J_K
items.statement: ‖f − H_t f‖₁ ≤ J_K(t)‖|Df|‖₁ for bounded Lipschitz f.
items.note: K = 0 coefficient J₀(t) = 2√(t/π), for indicator data of smooth domains with relative perimeter under a smooth convex potential.

items.label: Monotone auxiliary function (K > 0)
items.statement: f₁(x) = √x / arctan(√(e^(Tx) − 1)) is increasing on (0, ∞) with f₁ ≥ 1/√T.
items.note: Both claims, with f₁ = buserRatioPos T; monotonicity is stated strictly, which implies the paper's "increasing".

items.label: Monotone auxiliary function (K < 0)
items.statement: f₂(x) = √x / log(e^(Tx) + √(e^(2Tx) − 1)) is decreasing on (0, ∞).
items.note: With f₂ = buserRatioNeg T; stated strictly, which implies the paper's "decreasing". The logarithm is identified with arcosh(e^{Tx}).

items.label: Bound under a lower bound on K/λ₁
items.statement: If K/λ₁ ≥ −c, an explicit lower bound for h(X) in terms of √λ₁ and c follows from Theorem 1.1 and Lemma 3.3.

items.label: Coarea inequality
items.statement: On a complete metric space with a measure finite on bounded sets, for bounded Lipschitz u ≥ 0 with M = sup u: ∫₀^M Per({u > t})dt ≤ ∫|∇u|dm, and almost every {u > t} has finite perimeter.
items.note: Finite measures and closed superlevel sets {u ≥ t}, for every globally Lipschitz u; the local-finiteness case is not stated in this form.

items.label: Cheeger inequality on metric measure spaces
items.statement: On a complete metric space with a measure finite on bounded sets: λ₁ ≥ h²/4 if m(X) < ∞, and λ₀ ≥ h²/4 if m(X) = ∞.
items.note: Finite-dimensional log-concave probability laws only, as C_P ≤ 4Ψ².

papers.title: Bourgain’s slicing problem and KLS isoperimetry up to polylog
papers.result: First polylogarithmic KLS bound: ψₙ = O((log n)^5), hence C_P = O((log n)^10).
papers.remaining: The localization covariance window and spectral argument are not locally formalized.

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: Log-concave probability measures on R^n, n ≥ 2 and n larger than a universal constant WLOG; c, C, C₁, C_q etc. are universal constants (C_q, C_p depending only on q, p) changing from line to line; log is natural. ψ_μ is the inverse Cheeger constant (the display before (7)), ψ_n = sup ψ_μ over isotropic log-concave μ on R^n (8) (G_n in Eldan, ψ_n^{-1} in Chen), C_P(μ) the Poincaré constant (5), σ_μ the thin-shell constant n σ_μ² = Var_μ(|x|²) (4), σ_n = sup σ_μ, κ_n² = sup_X sup_θ ‖E⟨X, θ⟩ X ⊗ X‖_HS² over isotropic log-concave X (23). From Section 2 on, μ is isotropic log-concave with smooth positive density ρ; μ_s = μ ∗ γ_s, P_s f = f ∗ γ_s, Q_s φ = P_s(φρ)/P_s ρ; L = Δ + ∇log ρ · ∇ (closure in L²(μ)) with spectral resolution −L = ∫λ dE_λ and spectral measures ν_f. Stochastic localization in the Lee–Vempala form: tilt process (18) dθ_t = dW_t + a(t, θ_t) dt, p_t ∝ e^{⟨θ_t, x⟩ − t|x|²/2} ρ, dp_t = p_t⟨x − a_t, dW_t⟩ (19), barycenter a_t, covariance A_t, time reversal t = 1/s; ‖A‖_q = Tr[A^q]^{1/q}, ‖·‖_op the operator norm. The repository's Isoperimetry.inverseScale plays the role of ψ_μ.
lemma_map.omitted: Remark 6.1 (non-optimality of the exponent and possible improvements) is purely expository and is not an item. Apart from the items for (3), (5), (7) and (14), the numbered equations (1)–(54) are definitions, cited results (Chen's bound (11), Eldan–Klartag (2), Eldan (10)/(24), the H^{-1} inequality (44)) or proof steps recorded inside the items that use them; claims outside numbered statement environments are listed only where a local Lean declaration states them (DLC, MOM, D3, D5, DPSI, E7, E14, UP). The thin-shell bound σ_μ² ≤ 4C_P(μ) (6), the definitions (4), (8), (23), finiteness of C_P for log-concave laws (Bobkov; KLS), and the unnumbered σ_n ≤ C(log n)^4 have no local Lean statement and are not listed. There is no appendix; Theorem, Lemma, Proposition, Corollary, Remark and Definition share the section-reset counter (Question has its own, unused), and no Definition, Conjecture, Question, Speculation or Problem environment is printed.

items.label: Log-concave probability measure
items.statement: A probability density ρ on R^n is log-concave if {ρ > 0} is convex and log ρ is concave on it; a probability measure on R^n is log-concave if it is supported in an affine subspace and has a log-concave density there.
items.note: Lean defines log-concavity by Borell's compact-set inequality on finite-dimensional real normed spaces. LogConcave.exists_isBorellDensity constructs a log-concave density of the intrinsic law on the affine support. The converse for an actual Haar density on a finite-dimensional real inner-product space is also proved: IsBorellDensity.compactLogConcave (KLS/LogConcave/Density/FromBorell.lean), via Prékopa–Leindler, without requiring an everywhere positive density. The mapped item records definitions and the intrinsic representation, rather than a single equivalence with the paper's affine-subspace definition.

items.label: Finite moments of all orders
items.statement: Every log-concave probability measure on R^n has finite moments of all orders.
items.note: The mapped declarations give intrinsic natural norm moments and the ambient second moment. Ambient exponential integrability is also available from KLS.LogConcave.exists_integrable_exp_norm_contDiffOn_logLaplace, and Probability.integrable_norm_pow_of_integrable_exp_norm converts a positive exponential moment into every natural norm moment (KLS/LogConcave/Density/BorellRepresentation/Moments.lean). Thus ambient higher moments are supported; this item retains its mapped component declarations rather than a standalone all-orders source statement.

items.label: Isotropic probability measure
items.statement: A probability measure μ on R^n with finite second moments is isotropic if ∫x_i dμ = 0 and ∫x_i x_j dμ = δ_ij for i, j = 1, …, n, i.e. it is centered with identity covariance.
items.note: Lean states the three conditions (MemLp id 2, zero mean, centered covariance operator equal to the identity) coordinate-free on any finite-dimensional real inner-product space; in orthonormal coordinates this is (3).

items.label: Poincaré constant C_P
items.statement: For a Borel probability measure μ on R^n, C_P(μ) is the smallest C ≥ 0 such that Var_μ(f) ≤ C ∫|∇f|² dμ for every locally Lipschitz f ∈ L²(μ).
items.note: Lean takes the infimum (in [0, ∞]) of finite constants valid for all finite-energy L² tests, with |∇f| replaced by the pointwise local slope, computed for the intrinsic law on the affine support; for locally Lipschitz tests the slope equals |∇f| almost everywhere, but agreement with the ambient definition (5) for singular laws is not stated.

items.label: Isoperimetric constant 1/ψ_μ
items.statement: For μ with log-concave density ρ on R^n, 1/ψ_μ = inf over open A ⊆ R^n with smooth boundary and 0 < μ(A) < 1 of ∫_{∂A} ρ / min{μ(A), 1 − μ(A)}; ψ_μ is the inverse Cheeger constant (larger is worse).
items.note: Isoperimetry.constant is the infimum of outer Minkowski content over measurable sets of mass in (0,1), divided by min{μ(B),1−μ(B)}, in the induced metric on the affine support; it is ⊤ in dimension zero and inverseScale is its inverse Ψ. The library also proves constant_eq_smoothConstant_intrinsic and inverseScale_eq_inv_smoothConstant_intrinsic (KLS/Geometry/Cheeger/Equality.lean), identifying these with the smooth relative-perimeter infimum on the interior of the intrinsic support for a Borell density. This item does not register a single equivalence with every ambient smooth-boundary convention in the paper.

items.label: Cheeger and Buser–Ledoux comparison
items.statement: For every absolutely continuous log-concave probability measure μ on R^n, 1/4 ≤ ψ_μ²/C_P(μ) ≤ 9; the left inequality (Cheeger) does not need log-concavity.
items.note: Lean proves C_P ≤ 4Ψ² and Ψ² ≤ π C_P (Ψ = Isoperimetry.inverseScale) for every finite-dimensional log-concave law, including singular and Dirac laws, in the Lean conventions of D5 and DPSI; the Buser constant π is sharper than 9. Cheeger without log-concavity is not stated in this form.

items.label: Polylogarithmic KLS bound
items.statement: For every n ≥ 2, ψ_n ≤ C (log n)^α, where ψ_n = sup ψ_μ over isotropic log-concave probability measures μ on R^n (equation (8)) and C, α > 0 are universal constants; the proof gives α = 5.
items.note: Main theorem. The proof shows σ_n ≤ C(log n)^4 (unnumbered), then applies Eldan's inequality (10)/(24), which is cited (its hard half is re-derived in Remark 5.5 only modulo a cited implication), and the H^{-1} inequality (44) cited from Barthe–Klartag Proposition 10; it also yields L_n ≤ C(log n)^4 in (12). Via (7) it gives C_P(μ) ≤ C(log n)^10 for isotropic log-concave μ. Reduction to a smooth positive density with σ_μ > σ_n/2 (41) is by Gaussian convolution and re-isotropization. No Lean statement.

items.label: Weighted integration by parts
items.statement: For μ with smooth positive density ρ and L u = Δu + ∇(log ρ)·∇u, ∫(Lu)v dμ = −∫∇u·∇v dμ for smooth u, v with one of them compactly supported.
items.note: Lean: for ν = m.tilted(−U) with U ∈ C¹ (so ρ ∝ e^{−U}, L = Δ − ⟨∇U, ∇·⟩), f ∈ C² compactly supported and g ∈ C¹, ∫⟨∇f, ∇g⟩ dν = ∫(−ℒf) g dν; only the case where the operator falls on the compactly supported function is stated.

items.label: Spectral mass below λ bound
items.statement: Let μ be a probability measure on R^n with smooth positive density, and f ∈ L²(μ) with ∫f dμ = 0 and ‖f‖_{L²(μ)} = 1. Then for all s, λ > 0, ⟨E_λ f, f⟩_{L²(μ)} ≤ C(‖Q_s f‖_{L²(μ_s)} + sλ) with a universal C; the proof gives C = 4.
items.note: E_λ is the spectral resolution of −L and Q_s φ = P_s(φρ)/P_sρ. The proof actually gives the stronger squared form ⟨E_λ f, f⟩ ≤ 4(‖Q_s f‖²_{L²(μ_s)} + sλ) (note ‖Q_s f‖ ≤ 1), which is the form used in (46). Section 3 assumes μ log-concave; the printed statement omits it, while the proof relies on Lemma 3.1 and on Klartag–Putterman facts (Q_s is a contraction with Q_s 1 = 1). Stochastic localization is not used here.

items.label: Localization martingale second moment
items.statement: For φ ∈ L¹(μ), s > 0 and t = 1/s, the process M_t = ∫φ p_t of Eldan's stochastic localization (19) started at the isotropic log-concave smooth density ρ satisfies E M_t² = ‖Q_s φ‖²_{L²(μ_s)}.
items.note: Uses Q_sφ(y) = ∫φ p_{t,ty} and that θ_t/t has law μ_s = μ ∗ γ_s (both cited from Klartag–Putterman). Applied coordinatewise it gives (21): E|a_t|² = ‖Q_s x‖²_{L²(μ_s)}.

items.label: Small-time Schatten moments of A_t
items.statement: There is a universal C such that for t ≤ (C κ_n² log n)^{-1} and q ≥ 1, E‖A_t‖_q^q ≤ C_q n, where A_t is the localization covariance, ‖A‖_q = Tr[A^q]^{1/q}, κ_n is given by (23), and C_q depends only on q.
items.note: Carries two LaTeX labels (lem_eldan, lem_1135), one printed number. Proved at the end of Section 5 from Corollary 5.4 and ‖A‖_q^q ≤ n‖A‖_op^q.

items.label: Cubic growth of E‖A_t‖₂²
items.statement: For 0 ≤ t₁ ≤ t₂ the localization covariance satisfies E‖A_{t₂}‖₂² ≤ (t₂/t₁)³ E‖A_{t₁}‖₂².
items.note: Proof: Itô's formula (37) for Tr(A_t²), the almost sure bound (38) Σ|H_ij|² ≤ (3/t) Tr(A_t²) from Lemma 4.2 (p_t is t-uniformly log-concave), then Grönwall. The case t₁ = 0 is vacuous as printed.

items.label: Barycenter second moment bound
items.statement: With t₁ = (C κ_n² log n)^{-1}, the localization barycenter satisfies E|a_t|² ≤ C₁ n t max{1, t³/t₁³} for all t > 0, with universal C, C₁.
items.note: Integrates (22) d/dt E|a_t|² = E‖A_t‖₂² with a₀ = 0, using Lemma 2.3 (q = 2) on [0, t₁] and Lemma 2.4 beyond t₁.

items.label: Deterministic Kim–Milman coupling
items.statement: The deterministic evolution (25) dθ_t = ½(a(t, θ_t) + θ_t/t) dt (the Kim–Milman map) is an alternative coupling: for 0 < t₁ < t₂, if θ_{t₁}/t₁ has law μ_{1/t₁}, then running (18) or (25) on [t₁, t₂] gives θ_{t₂}/t₂ with law μ_{1/t₂}.
items.note: Also speculates that all stochastic processes could be replaced by heat-semigroup differentiation and integration by parts. The coupling claim is cited from Klartag–Putterman.

items.label: Heat-flow norm lower bound
items.statement: Let μ be log-concave with smooth positive density and g ∈ H¹(μ) with ∫g² dμ = 1 and E = ∫|∇g|² dμ. Then ‖Q_s g‖²_{L²(μ_s)} ≥ exp(−sE) for all s > 0.
items.note: Proof: log-convexity of s ↦ ‖Q_s g‖² (its −log has non-increasing derivative R_g(s), with R_g(0) = E), cited from Klartag–Putterman Section 2 and Lemma 2.5, plus density of C_c^∞ in H¹(μ) (Barthe–Klartag appendix).

items.label: Projection lower bound for ⟨Af,f⟩
items.statement: Let A be a self-adjoint positive semi-definite operator on L²(μ) with ‖A‖ ≤ 1, f ∈ L²(μ) with ‖f‖ = 1, ε, β ∈ (0, 1], and g ∈ L²(μ) with ⟨Ag, g⟩ ≥ (1 − ε)β and β = ‖g‖² = ⟨f, g⟩. Then ⟨Af, f⟩ ≥ β/4 − ε.
items.note: Pure Hilbert-space spectral argument with r = 1 − 4ε/β; when ε > β/4 the conclusion is trivial, which the proof leaves implicit.

items.label: Conjectured operator bound P_sQ_s ≥ e^{sL}
items.statement: Proposition 2.1 would improve if P_s Q_s ≥ e^{sL} for all s > 0 (31), for which no counterexample is known; (31) holds weakly: Tr φ(P_s Q_s) ≥ Tr φ(e^{sL}) (32) for every continuous increasing φ : [0, 1] → [0, ∞) vanishing near 0.
items.note: The weak form (32) is sketched from Lemma 3.1 (⟨P_sQ_s f, f⟩ ≥ exp(s⟨Lf, f⟩) for unit f ∈ Dom(L)) plus unspecified spectral theory; (31) itself is an open question.

items.label: Bounded martingale representation
items.statement: If μ is a centered 1-uniformly log-concave probability measure on R^n and (B_t) a standard Brownian motion with B₀ = 0, there is an adapted process (Q_t) of symmetric matrices with 0 ≤ Q_t ≤ Id for all t ∈ [0, 1] almost surely and ∫₀¹ Q_t dB_t of law μ.
items.note: t-uniformly log-concave means density exp(−φ(x) − t|x|²/2) with φ convex. Proof via the Brenier map and Caffarelli's contraction theorem, heat smoothing P_{1−t}T and the Itô representation of the martingale (P_{1−t}T)(B_t); alternatively Eldan–Lehec with a time change.

items.label: Uniformly log-concave Poincaré inequality
items.statement: A 1-uniformly log-concave random vector satisfies the Poincaré inequality with constant 1; by scaling, a t-uniformly log-concave one has C_P ≤ 1/t.
items.note: The mapped declarations give the standard Gaussian bound 1 and its scaled bound r² in every finite dimension. Beyond Gaussian laws, literatureConstant_le_inv_of_eq_tilted (KLS/LogConcave/HeatSemigroup/Curvature.lean; certified as thm:bakry-emery-poincare) proves C_P ≤ 1/t for a law ν = volume.tilted (−W) with W ∈ C² and Hess W ≥ t Id, t > 0. The unrestricted nonsmooth uniformly log-concave formulation is not mapped here. The sharper Cordero-Erausquin–Fradelizi–Maurey bound 1/2 for functions with centered gradient used in Lemma 4.2 is not supplied by these results.

items.label: Cubic inner-product moment bound
items.statement: If t > 0, μ is a centered t-uniformly log-concave probability measure on R^n and X, Y are independent with law μ, then E⟨X, Y⟩³ ≤ (3/t) E⟨X, Y⟩² = (3/t) Tr(A²), where A is the covariance matrix of μ.
items.note: Reduce to t = 1 by scaling; Itô's formula (34) along X_t = ∫₀ᵗ Q_s dB_s, Cauchy–Schwarz, the Cordero-Erausquin–Fradelizi–Maurey Poincaré constant 1/2 for |QY|², and Q_t⁴ ≤ Q_t².

items.label: Constant in Lemma 4.2
items.statement: The constant 3 in Lemma 4.2 directly controls the exponent of the logarithm in Theorem 1.1 and is probably not optimal; in dimension one the inequality of Lemma 4.2 holds with constant 2.
items.note: The one-dimensional constant-2 claim is stated without proof.

items.label: Improved exponent in Chen's lemma
items.statement: Using the Cordero-Erausquin–Fradelizi–Maurey inequality, the exponent in Chen's Lemma 8 improves from 2q to q − 1 for q ≥ 3, and with it the case q = 3 of Chen's Lemma 8 can replace Lemma 2.4 in the proof of Theorem 1.1.
items.note: Stated without proof.

items.label: Scaling bound for κ_X
items.statement: If X is a centered log-concave random vector in R^n, then κ_X² ≤ ‖Cov(X)‖_op³ κ_n², where κ_X² = sup_{θ ∈ S^{n−1}} ‖E⟨X, θ⟩ X ⊗ X‖_HS² and κ_n² is its supremum over isotropic log-concave X in R^n.
items.note: Proof: homogeneity of degree 6 and adding an independent symmetric Gaussian Y with covariance Id − Cov(X) to make X + Y isotropic without changing third moments; uses that convolution preserves log-concavity.

items.label: Operator-norm tail at small times
items.statement: There is a universal C such that for every t ≤ (C κ_n² log n)^{-1}, the localization covariance satisfies P(‖A_t‖_op ≥ 2) ≤ exp(−(Ct)^{-1}).
items.note: Proof: Itô's formula for Φ_t = β^{-1} log Tr e^{βA_t} with β = 2 log n, reverse Hölder for log-concave measures, a stopping time at ‖A_t‖_op = 2 and Lemma 5.3; the explicit window used is t ≤ (32 κ_n² log n)^{-1}.

items.label: Martingale deviation inequality
items.statement: If (M_t) is a continuous martingale with M₀ = 0 and [M]_t ≤ σ² almost surely for a fixed t > 0 and σ > 0, then P(M_t ≥ u) ≤ exp(−u²/(2σ²)) for all u ≥ 0.
items.note: Proof: the exponential local martingale is a supermartingale by Fatou's lemma, then Markov's inequality.

items.label: Small-time operator-norm moments
items.statement: There is a universal C such that for t ≤ (C κ_n² log n)^{-1} and p ≥ 1, E‖A_t‖_op^p ≤ C_p, with C_p depending only on p.
items.note: Uses ‖A_t‖_op ≤ 1/t almost surely (p_t is t-uniformly log-concave) together with Lemma 5.2: E‖A_t‖_op^p ≤ 2^p + C^p p!.

items.label: Recovering Eldan's inequality
items.statement: Corollary 5.4 with p = 1 gives E∫₀^{t₁}‖A_t‖_op dt ≤ C′t₁ ≤ Ĉ/log n for t₁ = (C κ_n² log n)^{-1}, which implies ψ_μ² ≤ C̃ t₁^{-1}; hence ψ_n² ≤ C₁ κ_n² log n, the hard half of (24).
items.note: The implication from the integrated operator-norm bound to the isoperimetric bound is cited (Klartag's exposition of Chen, page 9), not proved.

items.label: H^{-1} reformulation via e^{sL}
items.statement: For centered f ∈ L²(μ), ‖f‖²_{H^{-1}(μ)} = ∫₀^∞ ⟨e^{sL} f, f⟩ ds, so (44) reads Var_μ(f) ≤ 2∫₀^∞ ‖e^{sL}∇f‖² ds (52); with Var_μ(f) = 2∫₀^∞ ‖∇e^{sL}f‖² ds (53) this gives, for log-concave μ, ∫₀^∞ ‖∇e^{sL}f‖² ds ≤ ∫₀^∞ ‖e^{sL}∇f‖² ds (54).
items.note: Contrasts (54) with the Bakry–Émery pointwise bound |∇e^{sL}f|² ≤ e^{sL}|∇f|²; the pointwise inequality |∇e^{sL}f|² ≤ |e^{sL}∇f|² is suspected false. Relies on the cited H^{-1} inequality (44) of Barthe–Klartag. No Lean statement.

papers.title: A slightly improved bound for the KLS constant
papers.result: Improves the logarithmic exponent: ψₙ = O((log n)^3.2226), hence C_P = O((log n)^6.4452).
papers.remaining: The refined localization growth estimate and resulting bound are not locally formalized.

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: Distributions on ℝⁿ, n ≥ 2; a ≲ b means a = O(b) with a universal implied constant (C, c universal unless they depend on q as stated). A log-concave density is nonnegative, integrates to 1 and has concave logarithm; α-strongly log-concave means p(x) = e^{−α‖x‖²/2} q(x) with q log-concave. Isotropic means mean 0 and covariance I. σ_n, κ_n and ψ_n are the suprema of σ_μ, κ_μ and ψ_μ (Definition 3) over isotropic log-concave μ on ℝⁿ. γ is the best constant in display (1.3), T_μ(I, I, I) ≤ (γ/α) Tr A² for every α-strongly log-concave μ with covariance A. a_t, A_t denote the mean and covariance of the stochastic-localization density p_t (Definition 4), and W_t is a standard Brownian motion in ℝⁿ.
lemma_map.omitted: All 27 numbered statement environments (one shared counter for Theorem, Definition and Lemma across sections and appendices) are listed. The numbered displays (1.1)–(1.3), (2.1)–(2.3), (3.1)–(3.3), (B.1), (B.2) are proof steps or the definition of γ and are absorbed into the listed items or the standing assumptions; Section 1.2 (heuristic re-derivation of the Klartag–Lehec bound) and Appendix A (localization heuristic and computer search suggesting γ ≈ 0.37 in dimension one) contain only unnumbered expository claims.

items.label: Klartag–Lehec polylog bounds
items.statement: σ_n ≲ log⁴ n and ψ_n ≲ log⁵ n, with universal implied constants.
items.note: Quoted background result; not proved in this paper. Section 1.2 re-derives it heuristically as σ_n ≲ log^{γ+1} n with γ = 3.

items.label: Improved thin-shell and KLS bounds
items.statement: There is a universal constant C such that for all n ≥ 2, σ_n ≤ C·log^{2.2226} n and ψ_n ≤ C·log^{3.2226} n, where σ_n and ψ_n are the suprema of the thin-shell and KLS constants over isotropic log-concave distributions on ℝⁿ.
items.note: The σ_n part is Theorem 22 with γ = 2√2 (Lemma 15) and the optimized q ≈ 3.058, giving η = (1 + 7√2 + √(53 − 4√2))/8 ≈ 2.22252; the ψ_n part adds one logarithm via ψ_n ≲ σ_n log n (Lemma 5). Not stated in Lean.

items.label: Thin-shell, κ and KLS constants
items.statement: For a distribution μ on ℝⁿ: σ_μ² = Var_μ(‖x‖²)/n, κ_μ² = sup_{‖θ‖=1} ‖E_μ[⟨x,θ⟩ x xᵀ]‖_F², and 1/ψ_μ = inf over open A ⊆ ℝⁿ with smooth boundary of ∫_{∂A} dμ / min(μ(A), 1 − μ(A)); σ_n, κ_n, ψ_n are the suprema of σ_μ, κ_μ, ψ_μ over isotropic log-concave μ on ℝⁿ.
items.note: The KLS-constant clause and isotropy are represented. Isoperimetry.constant is h_μ = 1/ψ_μ and inverseScale is ψ_μ, using outer Minkowski content and measurable sets on the affine support, with values ⊤ and 0 respectively in dimension zero. Isoperimetry.inverseScale_eq_inv_smoothConstant_intrinsic (KLS/Geometry/Cheeger/Equality.lean) also identifies the inverse scale with the smooth relative-perimeter infimum on the interior of the intrinsic support for a Borell density. The full source-definition bundle is not mapped: KLS.Isotropic records finite second moment, zero mean and identity covariance, while σ_μ, κ_μ and the dimensional suprema σ_n, κ_n, ψ_n have no local definitions in this map.

items.label: Eldan and LV stochastic localization
items.statement: For a log-concave density p on ℝⁿ, Eldan's process is dp_t(x) = p_t(x)(x − a_t)ᵀ A_t^{−1/2} dW_t and the Lee–Vempala (LV) process is dp_t(x) = p_t(x)(x − a_t)ᵀ dW_t, both with p_0 = p, where a_t and A_t are the mean and covariance of p_t; both are martingales in the space of densities.
items.note: Stochastic-calculus definition; outside the Lean library scope.

items.label: Eldan thin-shell to KLS reduction
items.statement: ψ_n² ≲ κ_n² log n ≲ σ_n² log² n, with universal implied constants.
items.note: Quoted; proved by Eldan via stochastic localization.

items.label: Three-matrix tensor T_μ
items.statement: For a log-concave distribution μ on ℝⁿ with mean a and symmetric matrices A_1, A_2, A_3, T_μ(A_1, A_2, A_3) = E_{x,y∼μ} ∏_{i=1}^{3} (x − a)ᵀ A_i (y − a) with x, y independent; the same notation T_p is used for a density p.

items.label: Chen tensor bound
items.statement: For every α-strongly log-concave μ with covariance A and every q ≥ 3, T_μ(A^{q−2}, I, I) ≤ (4/α) Tr A^q.
items.note: Quoted; superseded in this paper by the constant 2/α of Lemma 24.

items.label: Klartag–Lehec mean-growth criterion
items.statement: For a log-concave density p on ℝⁿ with LV process p_t and mean a_t, σ_p² ≲ ∫_{λ_1}^{∞} min_{t_λ > 0} { E‖a_{t_λ}‖²/(nλ²) + 1/(λ t_λ) } dλ, where λ_1 = Ω(ψ_p^{−2}) and the expectation is over the LV process.
items.note: Quoted; relies on the LV stochastic localization and the heat-flow argument of Klartag–Lehec.

items.label: Improved Poincaré for centered gradients
items.statement: For any α-strongly log-concave μ and any smooth f ∈ L²(μ) with ∫ f dμ = 0 and ∫ ∇f dμ = 0, ∫ f² dμ ≤ (1/(2α)) ∫ ‖∇f‖² dμ.
items.note: Quoted. The factor 1/(2α) (half the Brascamp–Lieb/Bakry–Émery constant) needs the extra centering ∫∇f dμ = 0; no Lean declaration states it.

items.label: Eldan process properties
items.statement: For Eldan's process with mean a_t and covariance A_t: da_t = A_t^{1/2} dW_t; dA_t = E_{x∼p_t}(x − a_t)(x − a_t)ᵀ(x − a_t)ᵀ A_t^{−1/2} dW_t − A_t dt; and if p_0 is 1-strongly log-concave then ‖A_t‖_op ≤ e^{−t}.
items.note: Quoted stochastic-calculus facts.

items.label: LV process properties
items.statement: For the LV process with mean a_t and covariance A_t: da_t = A_t dW_t; dA_t = E_{x∼p_t}(x − a_t)(x − a_t)ᵀ(x − a_t)ᵀ dW_t − A_t² dt; and p_t(x) ∝ exp(c_tᵀx − (t/2)‖x‖²) p_0(x) for a random process c_t.
items.note: Quoted stochastic-calculus facts; in particular p_t is (α + t)-strongly log-concave when p_0 is α-strongly log-concave.

items.label: Properties of T_μ
items.statement: For log-concave μ with covariance A and symmetric M, N: T_μ(M_1, M_2, M_3) ≥ 0 for positive definite M_i; T_μ(M, I, I) ≲ κ_n² Tr|A^{1/2} M A^{1/2}| ‖A‖_op²; T_μ(M, N, I) ≤ T_μ(|M|^s, I, I)^{1/s} T_μ(|N|^t, I, I)^{1/t} for s, t ≥ 1 with 1/s + 1/t = 1; and T_μ(N^{1/2}M^βN^{1/2}, N^{1/2}M^{1−β}N^{1/2}, C) ≤ T_μ(N^{1/2}MN^{1/2}, N, C) for PSD M, N, C and β ∈ [0, 1].
items.note: Quoted; the paper writes the interpolation exponent as α, renamed β here to avoid a clash with the convexity parameter.

items.label: Early-time LV covariance control
items.statement: For the LV process from an isotropic log-concave p_0 on ℝⁿ with covariance A_t, and T ≤ 1/(cκ_n² log n) for a large enough universal c, P[‖A_t‖_op ≥ 2 for some 0 ≤ t ≤ T] ≤ exp(−1/(cT)).
items.note: Quoted. The printed event reads "‖A_t‖_op ≥ 2 for 0 ≤ t ≤ T"; it is used as the probability that the bound fails at some time in [0, T].

items.label: Eldan decomposition, strongly log-concave
items.statement: For any 1-strongly log-concave μ on ℝⁿ with mean 0 and covariance A, μ is the law of ∫_0^∞ Q_t dW_t for an adapted process of positive definite matrices with 0 ⪯ Q_t ⪯ e^{−t/2} I and E Q_t² = e^{−t} A.
items.note: Strengthens Klartag–Lehec Lemma 4.1 by the identity E Q_t² = e^{−t}A; Q_t = A_t^{1/2} from Eldan's process. Stochastic ingredient.

items.label: Tensor bound with constant 2√2
items.statement: For any α-strongly log-concave μ on ℝⁿ with covariance A, T_μ(I, I, I) ≤ (2√2/α) Tr A²; hence the best constant γ in (1.3) satisfies γ ≤ 2√2.
items.note: Improves the Klartag–Lehec constant 3. The proof applies Itô's formula along x_t = ∫_0^t Q_s dW_s.

items.label: LV decomposition, strongly log-concave
items.statement: For any α-strongly log-concave μ on ℝⁿ with mean 0 and covariance A, μ is the law of ∫_0^∞ Q_t dW_t for an adapted process of positive definite matrices with 0 ⪯ Q_t ⪯ (α + t)^{−1} I and E Q_t ⪯ A.
items.note: Q_t = A_t from the LV process. Stochastic ingredient.

items.label: Growth of Tr A_t^q
items.statement: For α-strongly log-concave μ with covariance A, LV process covariance A_t and any q ≥ 3, E Tr A_t^q ≤ (1 + t/α)^{q(q−1)} Tr A^q; in particular the Q_t of Lemma 16 satisfies E Tr Q_t^q ≤ (1 + t/α)^{q(q−1)} Tr A^q.
items.note: Proof: Lemma 27 with b = 0, then Lemma 24 for the (α + t)-strongly log-concave p_t, then Grönwall.

items.label: Conditional tensor bound for spiked covariance
items.statement: Let μ be α-strongly log-concave with covariance A, 3 ≤ q ≤ 8 and ζ > 0 with Tr A^q ≤ α^{−(q−2)} ζ^{−1} Tr A². Then T_μ(I, I, I) ≤ 12 α^{−1} ζ^{−1/(2(q²−2))} Tr A²; equivalently, without the hypothesis, T_μ(I, I, I) ≤ 12 α^{−3} (α^q Tr A^q)^c (α² Tr A²)^{1−c} with c = 1/(2(q²−2)).
items.note: The final step bounds 3√2 · 2.8 ≤ 12. Implicitly needs ζ ≥ 1 so that the crossover time s* = ζ^{1/(q²−2)} − 1 is nonnegative.

items.label: Early-time bound on Tr Ā_t^q
items.statement: For the LV process from an isotropic log-concave p_0 on ℝⁿ supported in a ball of radius n, with Ā_t = (A_t − I)^+ and t_1 = 1/(cκ_n² log n) for a large enough c depending only on q, for all 0 ≤ t ≤ t_1 and q ≥ 3, E Tr Ā_t^q ≤ 1 + (Cqκ_n² t)^{q/2} n for a universal constant C > 0.
items.note: Proof uses Lemma 13 with t_1 ≈ (qκ_n² log n)^{−1} to make the failure probability at most n^{−(2q+1)}, and the support assumption to bound ‖A_t‖_op ≤ n².

items.label: Late-time bound on Tr A_t^q
items.statement: Under the setting of Lemma 19 with 3 ≤ q ≤ 4, E Tr A_t^q ≲ n for t_1 ≤ t ≤ t̂ := t_1 log^{1/(2q−2)} n, and E Tr A_t^q ≲ (t/t_1)^{q(q−1)} n / log^{q/2} n for t ≥ t̂, where t_1 = 1/(cκ_n² log n).
items.note: The first estimate is derived for t ≤ κ_n^{−2}; for t ≥ t̂ the proof restarts Lemma 17 from p_{t̂}, which is t̂-strongly log-concave.

items.label: Improved growth of E‖a_t‖²
items.statement: Under the setting of Lemma 19 and for 3 ≤ q ≤ 4, E‖a_t‖² ≲ nt + n t^{γ+1}/(t*)^γ for all t > 0, where t* := κ_n^{−2(q²−q)/(q²−2)} log^{−(2q²−3q)/(2(q²−2))} n and γ ≤ 2√2 is the constant of (1.3).
items.note: Uses Lemma 18 (second form, with α = t for p_t) up to t*, where E Tr A_t² ≲ n, and Lemma 15 after t*; d/dt E‖a_t‖² = Tr A_t² by Itô's formula.

items.label: Thin-shell bound with explicit exponent
items.note: The proof starts from an isotropic log-concave p_0 with σ_{p_0}² ≥ σ_n²/2 supported in a ball of radius n (truncation step not detailed) and solves 2η ≤ max{η + 1, αη + β}. Numerically η ≈ 2.222516 at q ≈ 3.0580.

items.label: Sub-logarithmic bound without gap
items.statement: If ψ_n ≲ σ_n, then σ_n ≲ log^η n with η = min_{3≤q≤4} (γ(q²/2 − 3q/4)/(q² − 2)) / (1 + γ(q − 2)/(q² − 2)); with γ = 2√2 and q = 3 this gives η ≤ (63√2 − 36)/82 ≤ 0.6476.
items.note: Conditional on the no-gap hypothesis; the proof also uses κ_n ≲ σ_n under that hypothesis. The unconstrained optimum q ≈ 2.4588 is outside the range of Lemma 21.

items.label: Tensor bound with constant 2
items.statement: For any α-strongly log-concave μ with covariance A and any q ≥ 3, T_μ(A^{q−2}, I, I) ≤ (2/α) Tr A^q.
items.note: Improves Lemma 7 by a factor 2; proof given for completeness.

items.label: Hessian of matrix trace functions
items.statement: If f is twice differentiable on (α, β) and (f′(b) − f′(a))/(b − a) ≤ θ (f″(b) + f″(a))/2 + φ for all α ≤ a < b < β, then for every symmetric X with spectrum in (α, β) and every symmetric H, ∂² Tr f(X)/∂X²|_{H,H} ≤ θ Tr(f″(X)H²) + φ Tr H².
items.note: Quoted.

items.label: Divided-difference bound for (x⁺)^q
items.statement: For φ(x) = x^q on x ≥ 0 and φ(x) = 0 otherwise, with q ≥ 3, every a < b satisfies (φ′(b) − φ′(a))/(b − a) ≤ (φ″(b) + φ″(a))/2.

items.label: Itô drift of Tr φ(A_t−bI)
items.statement: For log-concave μ on ℝⁿ, its LV process with covariance A_t, φ as in Lemma 26 and q ∈ {2} ∪ [3, ∞): d Tr φ(A_t − bI) = E_{x∼p_t}(x − a_t)ᵀφ′(A_t − bI)(x − a_t)(x − a_t)ᵀ dW_t − Tr(φ′(A_t − bI)A_t²) dt + ½ T_{p_t}(φ″(A_t − bI), I, I) dt, and hence d/dt E Tr φ(A_t − bI) ≤ ½ T_{p_t}(φ″(A_t − bI), I, I).
items.note: Printed as an identity although the second-order term is only bounded via Lemma 25, so the first display is effectively an inequality for the drift. Stochastic ingredient.

papers.title: Logarithmic bounds for isoperimetry and slices of convex sets
papers.result: ψₙ = O(√log n), hence C_P = O(log n), using an improved log-concave Lichnerowicz inequality.
papers.remaining: The improved Lichnerowicz estimate and stochastic localization remain unformalized locally.

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: Probability measures on ℝⁿ; log-concave means a log-concave density on an affine subspace; isotropic means mean 0 and covariance Id. C_P is the optimal Poincaré constant for locally Lipschitz tests, ψ_μ the inverse Cheeger (isoperimetric) constant with min{μ(A), 1 − μ(A)} denominator, ψ_n = sup ψ_μ over isotropic log-concave μ on ℝⁿ, λ(μ) = 1/C_P(μ) the spectral gap. t-uniformly log-concave: the density relative to μ proportional to e^{t|x|²/2} is log-concave (∇²ψ ≥ t·Id). From Section 2 on μ is regular (smooth positive e^{−ψ} with ε·Id ≤ ∇²ψ ≤ Id/ε and polynomial growth of ψ and its derivatives). C, c denote universal constants. Numbered displays used as proof inputs, and the unnumbered definition of ψ_μ (stated by a Lean declaration), are listed alongside all thirteen numbered statement environments.
lemma_map.omitted: No numbered statement environment is omitted; Remark 4.2 is substantive and is listed. The remaining numbered displays (1.1), (1.2) (Hensley–Fradelizi and Grünbaum facts quoted as background), (1.8) and (3.18) (restating or concluding listed items), the definitions (2.1)–(2.3) and the intermediate proof steps (2.7)–(2.12), (3.1), (3.3), (3.6), (3.8), (3.9), (3.11), (3.12), (3.15)–(3.17), (4.1)–(4.4) and (5.1)–(5.3) are absorbed into the listed items. Unnumbered or display-level claims are listed only where a local Lean declaration states them; 10 others are not listed.

items.label: Poincaré constant C_P
items.statement: C_P(X) is the infimum of C ≥ 0 with Var f(X) ≤ C·E|∇f(X)|² for every locally Lipschitz f: ℝⁿ → ℝ with E|∇f(X)|² < ∞; C_P(μ) = C_P(X) for X with law μ.
items.note: Intrinsic.constant is the extended (ENNReal) optimum of the local-slope Poincaré inequality for the intrinsic law on the affine support of a finite-dimensional law, with local slope in place of the a.e. gradient. Agreement with the paper's ambient a.e.-gradient formulation is not stated as a separate Lean theorem; for log-concave laws it equals the smooth-test optimum (KLS.LogConcave.smoothTest_constant_eq_localSlope).

items.label: Isoperimetric constant ψ_μ
items.statement: For μ with log-concave density ρ, 1/ψ_μ = inf over open A ⊆ ℝⁿ with smooth boundary and 0 < μ(A) < 1 of ∫_{∂A}ρ / min{μ(A), 1 − μ(A)}; this is finite and positive (Bobkov).
items.note: Isoperimetry.constant is h_μ = 1/ψ_μ and inverseScale is ψ_μ, defined with outer Minkowski content over measurable sets on the affine support, with values ⊤ and 0 respectively in dimension zero. constant_eq_smoothConstant_intrinsic and inverseScale_eq_inv_smoothConstant_intrinsic (KLS/Geometry/Cheeger/Equality.lean) provide the smooth relative-perimeter identification on the interior of the intrinsic support for a Borell density. This item does not map the complete ambient convention and the paper's separate positivity/finiteness assertions; its definition mapping remains partial.

items.label: Cheeger–Buser comparison
items.statement: For every μ with a log-concave density, 1/4 ≤ ψ_μ²/C_P(μ) ≤ π.
items.note: Both halves are proved for every finite-dimensional log-concave law, including degenerate and zero-dimensional ones: C_P ≤ 4Ψ² and Ψ² ≤ π C_P, with Ψ = Isoperimetry.inverseScale. The intrinsic smooth relative-perimeter identification is also proved by inverseScale_eq_inv_smoothConstant_intrinsic (KLS/Geometry/Cheeger/Equality.lean). The item retains its partial source relation because it does not register the complete identification with the paper's ambient smooth-boundary convention.

items.label: Log-concave Lichnerowicz inequality
items.statement: If t > 0 and μ is t-uniformly log-concave (μ has density ∝ e^{−t|x|²/2} times a log-concave function), then C_P(μ) ≤ 1/t.
items.note: The mapped declarations give the Gaussian instances r·G with constant r² and density proportional to exp(−s|x|²) with constant 1/(2s). The library also proves literatureConstant_le_inv_of_eq_tilted (KLS/LogConcave/HeatSemigroup/Curvature.lean; thm:bakry-emery-poincare): C_P ≤ 1/t for ν = volume.tilted (−W), W ∈ C² and Hess W ≥ t Id, t > 0, for the intrinsic literature constant in every finite-dimensional real inner-product space. The arbitrary nonsmooth log-concave-factor formulation of this item is not mapped; its recorded Gaussian fragment remains partial.

items.label: Slicing bound √log n
items.statement: For n ≥ 2, L_n ≤ C·√(log n) for a universal constant C > 0; equivalently every convex body in ℝⁿ of volume one has a hyperplane section of (n−1)-volume at least c/√(log n).
items.note: Immediate from Theorem 1.2 and (1.6).

items.label: KLS bound √log n
items.statement: For n ≥ 2, ψ_n ≤ C·√(log n) for a universal constant C > 0, i.e. every isotropic log-concave probability measure on ℝⁿ has ψ_μ ≤ C√(log n) (equivalently C_P(μ) ≤ C' log n by (1.4)).
items.note: Main theorem (abstract and title). Proof: choose μ with ψ_μ ≥ ψ_n/2, take t = cψ_n^{−2}/log n so that E√‖A_t‖ ≤ C by (3.13), check t ≤ c̄λ₀ via (1.4), apply Corollary 3.2 to get λ₀^{−1} ≤ C/√t ≤ C̃ψ_n√(log n), and close with ψ_n² ≤ 4ψ_μ² ≤ C̃λ₀^{−1} from (1.4). Dimension-dependent; not mapped to any Lean declaration.

items.label: Improved log-concave Lichnerowicz
items.statement: If t > 0 and μ is a t-uniformly log-concave probability measure on ℝⁿ, then C_P(μ) ≤ √(‖Cov(μ)‖_op / t) ≤ 1/t.
items.note: Reduction to regular μ by Lemma 2.1; then (2.7)–(2.8) with ∇²ψ ≥ t give λ²‖Cov‖ ≥ t. The right inequality is ‖Cov(μ)‖ ≤ C_P(μ) ≤ 1/t via (2.6) on linear functions and (1.7) (the printed last step reads 1/λ ≤ t, a typo for ≤ 1/t). No local statement.

items.label: Regular approximation
items.statement: If μ is an absolutely continuous log-concave probability measure on ℝⁿ and 0 < ε < t, there is a regular log-concave ν (smooth positive density e^{−ψ} with ε'·Id ≤ ∇²ψ ≤ Id/ε' for some ε' > 0 and ψ and all derivatives of polynomial growth) with C_P(ν) ≥ C_P(μ) − ε and ‖Cov(μ) − Cov(ν)‖_op < ε; if μ is t-uniformly log-concave then ν is (t − ε)-uniformly log-concave.
items.note: ν is the normalization of (ρ ∗ γ_δ)·γ_{1/δ}. The local GaussianSmoothing.smoothedProbabilityLaw_literatureConstant_le bounds the Poincaré constant of a Gaussian convolution from above (C_P(μ ∗ γ) ≤ C_P(μ) + 1/(2s)); the lemma needs the lower bound for convolution followed by Gaussian multiplication, so it is not a restricted case. The printed proof says 'covariance of ν ... close to that of ν' for 'of μ'.

items.label: Eigenfunctions are tempered
items.statement: For regular log-concave μ, every eigenfunction of L_μ = Δ − ∇ψ·∇ is μ-tempered: smooth, with every partial derivative bounded by C e^{−a|x|}/√ρ(x).
items.note: Proof in the Appendix via the Schrödinger operator −Δ + V, V = |∇ψ|²/4 − Δψ/2, and exponential decay of its eigenfunctions (Agmon et al.), plus Green's representation for derivatives.

items.label: Weighted integration by parts
items.statement: For regular log-concave μ = e^{−ψ}dx and μ-tempered u, v, ∫(Lu)v dμ = −∫⟨∇u, ∇v⟩ dμ with Lu = Δu − ∇ψ·∇u.
items.note: Lean proves ∫⟨∇f, ∇g⟩ dμ = ∫(−ℒf)g dμ for μ = m.tilted(−U) with C¹ potential U, C² compactly supported f and C¹ g on a finite-dimensional space: compact support of one factor replaces μ-temperedness and no convexity is needed.

items.label: Eigenfunction has preferred direction
items.statement: For regular log-concave μ = e^{−ψ}dx and an L²(μ)-normalized eigenfunction f ∈ F_μ of −L with eigenvalue λ(μ): |∫∇f dμ|² ≥ λ^{−1}∫⟨(∇²ψ)∇f, ∇f⟩ dμ, and |∫∇f dμ|² = λ²|∫f(x)x dμ(x)|² ≤ λ²‖Cov(μ)‖_op.
items.note: Bochner formula plus the Poincaré inequality (2.6) applied to each ∂ⁱf; the identity uses (2.4) with g(x) = ⟨x, θ⟩ and Cauchy–Schwarz.

items.label: Poincaré constant of θ_t
items.statement: C_P(θ_t) = C_P(tX + W_t) ≤ C_P(tX) + C_P(W_t) = t²/λ₀ + t, using subadditivity of C_P for independent sums, C_P(tX) = t²C_P(X) and C_P(W_t) = t.
items.note: Lean has the three ingredients for smooth-test constants: subadditivity under convolution of probability laws (constant_conv_le_add), the scaling bound Holds μ C → Holds (μ.map (r•)) (r²C), and Holds for r·G with constant r². The paper's locally Lipschitz constant agrees with the smooth-test one for log-concave laws (KLS.LogConcave.smoothTest_constant_eq_localSlope), which covers tX + W_t; the composed bound (3.7) is not stated as one theorem.

items.label: Variance decomposition along localization
items.statement: For regular log-concave μ, t > 0 and f ∈ L²(μ), E Var_{p_t}(f) ≤ Var_{p₀}(f) ≤ (2 + t/λ₀)·E Var_{p_t}(f), where λ₀ = λ(μ) = 1/C_P(μ).
items.note: Law of total variance from (3.5), then the Poincaré inequality for θ_t (3.7) applied to θ ↦ M_f(t, θ) with |∇_θ M_f|² ≤ ‖A(t, θ)‖·Var_{p_{t,θ}}(f) and ‖A‖ ≤ 1/t from (3.2). Only the fixed-time law of θ_t and (3.5) are used.

items.label: Spectral gap from localized gaps
items.statement: For regular log-concave μ, A > 0 and 0 < t < Aλ₀: λ₀^{−1} ≤ C(A + 1)·E λ_t^{−1} ≤ C(A + 1)·E√‖A_t‖_op / √t, with C universal, λ_t = λ(μ_{t,θ_t}) and A_t = A(t, θ_t).
items.note: Apply Lemma 3.1 to a near-extremal 1-Lipschitz f from (3.10) and use the Poincaré inequality for each p_t; the second inequality is (3.2).

items.label: H^{-1} Lichnerowicz variant
items.statement: If t > 0 and μ is regular, t-uniformly log-concave and centered, and R = sup over θ ∈ S^{n−1} of ‖⟨·, θ⟩‖²_{H^{−1}(μ)}, then λ(μ) ≥ (t/R)^{1/3}.
items.note: Proof from (2.7), (2.8), (2.12) and the definition of the H^{−1}(μ) norm.

items.label: Varentropy via H^{-1} inequality
items.statement: For regular log-concave μ = e^{−ψ}dx, −∫⟨L^{−1}∇ψ, ∇ψ⟩ dμ = n, and with the H^{−1}-inequality Var_μ(f) ≤ ‖∇f‖²_{H^{−1}(μ)} (for Lipschitz f with ∫∇f dμ = 0) this gives the Bobkov–Madiman/Nguyen varentropy bound Var_μ(ψ) ≤ n.
items.note: Substantive remark (alternative proof of the varentropy inequality), so it is listed.

items.label: Localized Bochner formula
items.statement: For regular log-concave μ = e^{−ψ}dx, u ∈ F_μ and t > 0, almost surely u ∈ F_{μ_t}, and ∫(Lu)² dμ + t∫|∇u|² dμ = E∫(L_t u)² dμ_t, where μ_t has density p_t and L_t = L_{μ_t}.
items.note: Bochner formula for μ_t with ∇²ψ_t = ∇²ψ + t·Id, then (3.5) and Fubini. Uses only the fixed-time law of p_t.

items.label: Gaussian convolution–multiplication swap
items.statement: For s, t > 0, p = st/(s + t), q = t²/(s + t), r = t/(s + t), S_r f(x) = rⁿf(rx), and measurable f with fγ_t integrable, (fγ_t) ∗ γ_s = S_r[(f ∗ γ_p)γ_q], γ_s the N(0, s·Id) density.
items.note: Completing the square.

items.label: Gaussian convolution keeps uniform log-concavity
items.statement: For s, t > 0 and an absolutely continuous 1/t-uniformly log-concave probability measure μ on ℝⁿ, μ ∗ γ_s is 1/(t + s)-uniformly log-concave.
items.note: Lemma 5.1 plus Prékopa–Leindler. The local GaussianSmoothing.smoothedProbabilityLaw_logConcave (log-concavity of the Gaussian convolution of a log-concave law) is the excluded limit t = ∞, not a restricted case.

papers.title: A note on Bourgain’s slicing problem
papers.result: Obtains an iterated-logarithmic slicing bound and localization estimates used in the later slicing and thin-shell work.
papers.remaining: The covariance process and Guan’s estimates are not locally formalized.

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: Measures on R^n (Euclidean, n ≥ 1) are non-degenerate log-concave probability measures with density ρ; isotropic means barycenter 0 and identity covariance; L = Δ + ⟨∇log ρ, ∇⟩, C_p is the locally Lipschitz Poincaré constant, ψ_μ uses open sets with smooth boundary and the surface integral of ρ, σ_μ^2 = Var_μ(|x|^2)/n, μ_s = μ * γ_s with γ_s of covariance s·Id; (p_t) is the Lee–Vempala stochastic localization dp_t = p_t⟨x − a_t, dB_t⟩ with covariance A_t; C is a universal constant changing between lines. The printed definition of t-uniform log-concavity (density e^{-φ − t|x|^2}) is a factor 2 off from its uses (p_t ∝ e^{-t|x|^2/2} with C_p ≤ 1/t), so the operative convention is ∇^2(−log ρ) ≥ t. Lean hypotheses closest to these are the definitions FunctionalInequalities.KLS.LogConcave (KLS/Definitions.lean, compact-set Borell form admitting degenerate laws) and FunctionalInequalities.KLS.Isotropic (KLS/Isotropic.lean); as definitions they state no numbered item.
lemma_map.omitted: Remark 4.4 is a purely expository comment on possibly removing |log λ| from (4.11) and is omitted; there are no Definition, Proposition, Fact, Claim or Conjecture environments, and the in-text references to Klartag's Theorem 1.3 and Klartag–Putterman Proposition 2.3 are citations, not statements of this paper.

items.label: Iterated-logarithm slicing bound
items.statement: There is a universal C > 0 such that L_n ≤ C log(log n) for all n ≥ 3, where (L_n)^{-1} = inf over convex K ⊆ R^n of volume one of sup over hyperplanes H of Vol_{n-1}(K ∩ H).
items.note: Main item: the paper calls it the main result of the note (title and abstract). Proof: Theorem 1.2 combined with the cited L_n ≤ C σ_n (Eldan–Klartag 2011, display (1.2)) and ψ_n ≤ C sqrt(log n) (Klartag 2023); neither cited bound is proved here. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Thin cell versus isoperimetry
items.statement: There is a universal C > 0 such that σ_n ≤ C log ψ_n, where n σ_μ^2 = Var_μ(|x|^2), σ_n and ψ_n are suprema of σ_μ and ψ_μ over isotropic log-concave probability measures on R^n, and 1/ψ_μ is the infimum of ∫_{∂A} ρ / min(μ(A), 1 − μ(A)) over open A with smooth boundary.
items.note: Proof reduces (via ψ_n ≥ ψ_1 ≥ sqrt(π/2) and Buser–Ledoux) to σ_μ ≤ C|log λ_μ| + C for n ≥ C (4.21), approximates μ by regular measures (Klartag 2023), obtains (4.10) from Lemma 2.1 and (1.4), (1.8), applies Lemma 4.3, and closes with the cited H^{-1} bound (4.24) from Klartag–Lehec 2022 (48). Uses stochastic localization; the Lean library has no σ_μ, ψ_n or σ_n counterpart.

items.label: Two-sided bound for E Tr(A_t^2)
items.statement: There is a universal C > 0 such that for every isotropic log-concave probability measure μ on R^n with n > C, the covariance A_t of the Lee–Vempala stochastic localization (1.3) started at the density of μ satisfies n/2 ≤ E Tr(A_t^2) ≤ 8n for t ∈ [0, e^{-1000}].
items.note: Proved in Section 3 by a finite induction over times t_{k+1} = |log t_k|^{-16} starting at t_1 = C_2^{-1}(log n)^{-2}, with f_k from Lemma 2.2 (r_0 = s_k, D_0 = |log t_k|^4). Cites κ_n^2 ≤ C log n (Klartag 2023), the operator-norm tail (3.2) from Klartag–Lehec 2022 Lemma 5.2, Lichnerowicz (1.11), and dA_t from Lee–Vempala 2024 Lemma 29. Stochastic calculus; no Lean counterpart.

items.label: Exponential-to-quadratic gluing function
items.statement: For D_0 > 4 and r_0 ∈ [7/3, 8/3] there are b ∈ [1/20, 1/5] and an increasing f ∈ C^2(R) with f(r) = e^{D_0(r − r_0)} for r ≤ r_0 − D_0^{-1}, f(r) = b r^2 for r ≥ r_0, and |f''(r)| ≤ D_0^2 f(r) for all real r.
items.note: Elementary real analysis: f is built by integrating a piecewise-linear second derivative and fixing parameters c, s, b by continuity. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Marginals keep uniform log-concavity
items.statement: For t ≥ 0, if μ is a t-uniformly log-concave probability measure on R^n (density e^{-φ(x) − t|x|^2} with φ convex), then its projection (marginal) onto any linear subspace is again t-uniformly log-concave.
items.note: Proof by the Prékopa–Leindler inequality (Brazitikos et al. 2014, Theorem 1.2.3). The case t = 0 is the classical marginal log-concavity; the Lean library has KLS.LogConcave as a definition but no marginal-projection theorem among the reviewed candidates.

items.label: Growth of E F_t
items.statement: For μ isotropic log-concave on R^n, D_0 > 4, r_0 ∈ [7/3, 8/3], f from Lemma 2.2 and F_t = Σ_i f(λ_{i;t}) over the eigenvalues of A_t, every t_0 ∈ (0, 1] gives E F_t ≤ (t/t_0)^{1000} E F_{t_0} for t ∈ [t_0, t_0 ∨ D_0^{-4}].
items.note: Proof by the Itô formula for eigenvalues (Klartag 2021; Klartag–Lehec 2022), a five-term decomposition of the drift, and a third-moment bound from Klartag's spectral-variance inequality (1.12) applied to a projected p_t via Lemma 2.3, plus Lichnerowicz (1.11). Display (2.23) of the proof is reused in Corollary 3.1. Stochastic calculus; no Lean counterpart.

items.label: Large-eigenvalue mass beyond log time
items.statement: Let N > 1, C_2 the constant of (3.2) and c̃ = 1 ∧ C_2^{-1}; there is C > 3 depending on N such that for μ isotropic log-concave on R^n with n ≥ C and t ∈ [c̃(log n)^{-2}, 1 ∧ N(log n)^{-1}], E Σ_{λ_{i;t} ≥ 8/3} λ_{i;t}^2 ≤ 20 e^{-10^{-4} N^{-1/2} (log n)^{1/2}} n.
items.note: The printed left side carries a redundant inner E. Proof uses f from Lemma 2.2 with r_0 = 8/3, D_0 = 2^{-1}10^{-3}N^{-1/2}(log n)^{1/2}, display (2.23) from the proof of Lemma 2.4, (1.11) and the cited tail bound (3.2). Not used elsewhere in the paper. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Gaussian convolution identities
items.statement: For μ isotropic log-concave with density ρ and ρ_s the density of μ * γ_s: ∫(|x|^2 − (1+s)n)^2 ρ_s = ∫(|y|^2 − n)^2 ρ + 2(s^2 + 2s)n for s ≥ 0, and −s^{-1} Id ≤ ∇^2 log ρ_s ≤ 0 for s > 0; if moreover ρ = e^{-φ} with φ smooth, then ∫ ∂_θ^2 φ dμ ≥ 1 for every unit vector θ.
items.note: Direct Gaussian computation, a conditional-variance formula for ∂_θ^2 log ρ_s (upper bound via Lichnerowicz or Prékopa–Leindler), and integration by parts with Cauchy–Schwarz. Only the right half of (4.2) is used later (Lemma 4.3). No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Dyadic Cauchy–Schwarz integral bound
items.statement: If h ≥ 0 is differentiable and non-increasing on [0, ∞), then for every integer N ≥ 0, ∫_0^{2^N} (s^{-1/2} ∧ 1)(−h'(s))^{1/2} ds ≤ h(0)^{1/2}(N+1)^{1/2}.
items.note: Dyadic splitting and Cauchy–Schwarz on each block. The proof integrates h' (fundamental theorem of calculus), implicitly needing h' integrable. No Lean counterpart.

items.label: Low-spectrum coordinate mass bound
items.statement: Let μ be a regular log-concave probability measure on R^n, g_k(x) = x_k, and assume Σ_k ∫|Q_s g_k|^2 dμ_s ≤ c_1^{-1}(s^{-1} ∧ 1)n for all s > 0 with some c_1 ∈ (0, e^{-1}), where Q_s u = P_s(uρ)/ρ_s; then Σ_k ∫|E_λ g_k|^2 dμ ≤ 10^2 c_1^{-2} λ|log λ| n for λ ∈ (0, e^{-1}), with E_λ the spectral projection of −L below level λ.
items.note: Regular means smooth positive density with ε Id ≤ ∇^2 φ ≤ ε^{-1} Id and polynomially growing derivatives. Proof uses the Klartag–Putterman Γ-calculus (1.9), Γ_2 formula (4.8), Bochner (4.9), the gradient contraction (4.18) and the Rayleigh-quotient bound (4.7) from Klartag–Lehec 2022 Lemma 3.1. Remark 4.4 notes the |log λ| factor might be removable. No Lean counterpart.

items.locator: Proof of Theorem 1.2, Buser–Ledoux inequality (Buser 1982; Ledoux 2004)
items.label: Buser–Ledoux comparison
items.statement: For an isotropic log-concave probability measure μ on R^n with first nonzero eigenvalue λ_μ of −L on L^2(μ), ψ_μ^2 ≤ 9 λ_μ^{-1}.
items.note: The mapped declaration proves Ψ² ≤ π C_P for every finite-dimensional log-concave law, where Ψ = Isoperimetry.inverseScale and C_P is the intrinsic local-slope constant, with extended values, no isotropy and π < 9.
