The library also identifies Ψ with the intrinsic smooth relative-perimeter inverse scale (inverseScale_eq_inv_smoothConstant_intrinsic, KLS/Geometry/Cheeger/Equality.lean) and C_P with the intrinsic locally Lipschitz gradient-form optimum (Intrinsic.constant_eq_iInf_gradient_of_logConcave, KLS/LogConcave/Poincare.lean). The paper's cited display additionally uses the first nonzero eigenvalue λ_μ; this item does not register that spectral identification and the complete ambient source convention. Its reviewed stronger coefficient refers to the local Ψ² ≤ π C_P estimate. The paper does not use the separate Cheeger half.

papers.title: Affirmative resolution of Bourgain’s slicing problem using Guan’s bound
papers.result: Every volume-one convex body has a hyperplane section of volume at least a universal positive constant. This resolves slicing, not KLS.
papers.remaining: The slicing theorem, M-ellipsoids and entropy-stability inputs are not locally formalized.

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: Isotropic means centered with identity covariance (probabilistic normalization), except that an isotropic convex body of volume one uses Bourgain's normalization Cov(K) = L_K^2 Id. L_K = (det Cov(K)/Vol_n(K)^2)^{1/(2n)}, L_n = sup_K L_K (2), and L_μ = e^{−Ent(μ)/n} det Cov(μ)^{1/(2n)} (3), taken on the affine hull of the support. Sections 2–3 fix an isotropic log-concave μ on R^n with stochastic localization θ_t (7), barycenter a_t and covariance A_t; Section 3 uses the Föllmer change of variables r = t/(t+1). c, C denote universal constants changing from line to line. Lean: FunctionalInequalities.KLS.Isotropic (KLS/Isotropic.lean: second moment, zero mean, identity covariance) and FunctionalInequalities.KLS.LogConcave (KLS/Definitions.lean: compact-set Borell log-concavity) match the paper's isotropy and log-concavity hypotheses but state no numbered item, so they are not mapped.
lemma_map.omitted: The source has no numbered definition, remark, claim or conjecture environment; all 13 numbered statements (Theorems 1.1–1.2, Lemmas 2.1–2.3, Proposition 2.4, Lemmas 2.5–2.6, Lemma 3.1, Corollary 3.2, Lemmas 3.3–3.5) are listed. Unnumbered or equation-numbered facts (Guan's bound (1), the bounds (4)–(6), the variance decomposition (9), d/dt EA_t = −EA_t^2 (10), A_t ≤ Id/t (11), the de Bruijn identity (45)–(46), the Bourgain–Klartag–Milman monotonicity L_m ≤ C L_n) are cited inputs, not listed. No item is mapped to Lean: the library has no stochastic localization, isotropic constant, entropy or Fisher information, and the Poincaré and Cheeger/Buser declarations (Poincare.LocalSlope.Intrinsic.constant, LogConcave.literatureConstant_le_four_mul_inverseScale_sq, LogConcave.inverseScale_sq_le_pi_literature) concern quantities the paper does not use.

items.label: Slicing: large hyperplane section
items.statement: For every convex body K ⊆ R^n with Vol_n(K) = 1 there is a hyperplane H with Vol_{n−1}(K ∩ H) > c, where c > 0 is a universal constant independent of n.
items.note: Geometric formulation; the paper derives it from Theorem 1.2 via the standard equivalence of slicing formulations (cited, e.g. Klartag–Milman, BGVV), not proved in the paper.

items.label: Isotropic constant uniformly bounded
items.statement: sup_{n ≥ 1} L_n < ∞, where L_n = sup_K L_K over convex bodies K ⊆ R^n and L_K = (det Cov(K) / Vol_n(K)^2)^{1/(2n)}; equivalently L_n ≤ C for a universal constant C.
items.note: Main theorem: this is the slicing theorem L_n ≤ C in its isotropic-constant form (Theorem 1.1 is its corollary). Proof (Section 4): Proposition 2.4 gives an isotropic log-concave ν in R^m, m ≥ n/4, with L_ν ≳ L_n and E A_{t0} ≥ Id/4; Lemma 3.3 turns this into c·Id ≤ EΓ_r ≤ Id for r ≥ ξ; Lemmas 3.4 and 3.5 bound the variance of Γ_r; Lemmas 3.1, 3.3(iii) and Corollary 3.2 then give D(ν‖γ1) ≤ Cm, hence Ent(ν) ≥ −Cm and L_ν ≤ C by (3). Combined with Ball's lower bound it gives 1/√(2πe) ≤ L_μ ≤ C for all log-concave μ (6). No Lean declaration: the library has no isotropic constant, entropy or slicing statement.

items.label: Drift orthogonality identity
items.statement: For isotropic log-concave μ on R^n with stochastic localization (θ_t, a_t) started at μ and every t > 0, E (a_t − θ_t/(1+t)) ⊗ θ_t = 0.
items.note: Proof via integration by parts for μ * γ_{1/t} and the Klartag–Putterman formula ∇ψ_s(y) = (y − a(t,θ))/s (13); stochastic localization is not formalized.

items.label: Projection increases expected covariance
items.statement: For a subspace E ⊆ R^n, with A_{E,t} the covariance process of stochastic localization started at μ_E = (Proj_E)_*μ, one has E A_{E,t} ≥ Proj_E · E A_t · Proj_E for every t > 0.
items.note: Proof: A_t has the law of Cov(X | X + √(1/t) Z), and conditioning on the coarser σ-field Proj_E(X + √(1/t) Z) increases expected conditional covariance.

items.label: Guan's bound on E Tr A_t²
items.statement: For isotropic log-concave μ on R^n and its stochastic-localization covariance process (A_t), E Tr[A_t^2] ≤ C n for every t > 0, with C a universal constant.
items.note: Quoted from Guan (Lemma 2.1 there), restating display (1); no proof in this paper.

items.label: Reduction to non-collapsing localization
items.statement: For n ≥ 10 there are an integer n/4 ≤ m ≤ n, a real t0 ∼ 1 and an isotropic log-concave ν on R^m with L_ν ≥ c L_n and E A_{t0} ≥ Id/4, where (A_t) is the covariance process of stochastic localization started at ν.
items.note: Proof uses also Bourgain–Klartag–Milman L_m ≤ C L_n (m ≤ n) to assume 6 | n and take m = n/3, ν = (Proj_E)_*μ with μ uniform on L_K^{-1}K for a maximizing isotropic K.

items.label: Marginals inherit maximal isotropic constant
items.statement: Let K ⊆ R^n be an isotropic convex body of volume one with L_K = L_n (n divisible by 6) and μ uniform on L_K^{-1}K; then for every subspace E with dim E = n/3 the marginal μ_E = (Proj_E)_*μ satisfies L_{μ_E} ≥ c L_n, c universal.
items.note: Proof by Milman's M-ellipsoids, the maximality bound Vol_k(K ∩ E)^{1/(n−k)} ≤ C of BKM Corollary 3.5, minimal ellipsoid sections and Fradelizi's central-section bound, combined with (5).

items.label: Large-eigenvalue subspace at time c0
items.statement: In the setting of Lemma 2.5 there is a subspace E ⊆ R^n with dim E = n/3 such that Proj_E · E A_t · Proj_E ≥ Proj_E/4 at t = c0 = min{1/(2C), 1}, where C is the constant of Lemma 2.3.
items.note: Uses E Tr A_{c0} ≥ n/2 from (10), (28)–(29) and E A_t ≤ Id from (9), then counts eigenvalues.

items.label: Föllmer drift energy is Fisher information
items.statement: For isotropic log-concave μ on R^n and r ∈ (0,1), with X_r = (1−r)θ_{r/(1−r)}, ν_r its law and v_r = (1+t)a_t − θ_t (t = r/(1−r)), E|v_r|^2 = J(ν_r‖γ_r); moreover E|v_r|^2 ≤ 4n/(1−r)^2.
items.note: Uses formula (13) from the proof of Lemma 2.1 and the variance decomposition (9); J is relative Fisher information and γ_r = N(0, r·Id).

items.label: Entropy as integrated drift energy
items.statement: For isotropic log-concave μ on R^n, D(μ‖γ1) = (1/2)∫_0^1 J(ν_r‖γ_r) dr = (1/2)∫_0^1 E|v_r|^2 dr, and D(μ‖γ1) = −Ent(μ) + (n/2) log(2πe).
items.note: Via the de Bruijn identity (45)–(46) (quoted from Klartag–Ordentlich) and a change of variables s = (1−r)/r.

items.label: Properties of the matrix process Γ_r
items.statement: With Γ_r = (1+t)A_t and r = t/(t+1): (i) (1−r)EΓ_r = EA_t; (ii) E v_r⊗v_r = (Id − EΓ_r)/(1−r), so 0 ≤ EΓ_r ≤ Id; (iii) d/dr E v_r⊗v_r = E(Id − Γ_r)^2/(1−r)^2; (iv) d/dr EΓ_r = (EΓ_r − EΓ_r^2)/(1−r); (v) Γ_r ≤ Id/r almost surely.
items.note: Also uses the variance decomposition (9), the derivative formula (10) and the Lichnerowicz bound A_t ≤ Id/t (11).

items.label: Shannon–Stam deficit stability bound
items.note: Quoted from Eldan–Mikulincer Lemma 2 with λ = 1/2; δ_KL(μ) = δ_KL(μ, μ) is the entropy deficit (57) of the Shannon–Stam inequality.

items.label: Entropy jump at most 2n
items.statement: For isotropic log-concave μ on R^n, δ_KL(μ) ≤ 2n.
items.note: Proof: δ_KL(μ) = Ent((X^{(1)}+X^{(2)})/√2) − Ent(X^{(1)}) by Corollary 3.2, then Ball–Nguyen's bound by −log f(0) + 2n and (4).

papers.title: The slicing conjecture via small ball estimates
papers.result: An alternative proof of slicing via small-ball estimates and Guan’s localization bound.
papers.remaining: The small-ball argument and slicing conclusion are not locally formalized.

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: X is a random vector in R^n; isotropic means E X = 0 and E XXᵀ = I_n; b-subgaussian means (E|(X − E X)·θ|^p)^{1/p} ≤ b√p for all p ≥ 1 and unit θ; t-strongly log-concave means log-concave relative to a Gaussian of variance 1/t. C_P(X) is the optimal Poincaré constant for locally Lipschitz f and Ψ_n² its supremum over isotropic log-concave X in R^n. Convex isotropic position: Vol(K) = 1, barycenter 0, ∫_K xxᵀ = L_K² I_n; L_n = sup L_K and L̃_n = sup_f sup_x f(x)^{1/n} over isotropic log-concave densities. Stochastic localization: f_{t,θ} ∝ e^{−t|x|²/2 + θ·x} f, dθ_t = a_{t,θ_t} dt + dB_t, with barycenter a_t and covariance A_t of μ_t. Constants c, c_0, c_1, C_0, C_1 = 8C_0², c_2, C_2 are universal. Numbering: one shared counter for Theorem, Definition, Lemma, Proposition, Corollary, Remark etc. (only Theorem, Lemma, Corollary and Remark occur, numbered 1–10, no section prefix); cited results use a separate lettered counter (Theorems A–C); no appendix.
lemma_map.omitted: All 13 numbered statements of v1 are listed (Theorems A–C, Theorem 1, Lemmas 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, Corollary 3, Remark 7); none is purely expository. Unnumbered displayed claims are covered in the items that use them: the easy direction (4) of the Dafnis–Paouris equivalence (Corollary 3), the Section 2.1 reduction to y = 0 and small diameter (Theorem 1), the tilt density (10) and SDE (11), the density SDE (12) and martingale identity (13), the Lichnerowicz bound A_t ≤ Id/t (14) (Lemma 10), and the M-position estimate (19) (Theorem C). No Lean declaration states any item: Isotropic and LogConcave are hypothesis predicates only, Poincare.LocalSlope.Intrinsic.constant is the per-measure Poincaré constant rather than Ψ_n², and the Cheeger/Buser comparisons literatureConstant_le_four_mul_inverseScale_sq and inverseScale_sq_le_pi_literature concern Cheeger–Poincaré relations that this paper does not use.

items.label: Subgaussian small ball bound
items.statement: If X is a b-subgaussian log-concave vector in R^n with covariance A, there is a universal c > 0 such that for every ε < c and y ∈ R^n, P(‖X − y‖² ≤ ε Tr A) ≤ ε^{c Tr(A)/(b² ‖A‖_op ‖A^{-1}‖_op)}.
items.note: Cited from Paouris (2012); not proved here.

items.label: Small ball with KLS loss
items.statement: For isotropic log-concave X in R^n there is a universal c_B > 0 such that for every y ∈ R^n and ε < c_B, P(‖X − y‖² ≤ εn) ≤ ε^{c_B n/(Ψ_n² log n)}, where Ψ_n² is the supremum of Poincaré constants of isotropic log-concave vectors in R^n.
items.note: Cited from Lee–Vempala; not proved here. Ψ_n² is the paper's sup of C_P over isotropic log-concave laws, which Lean does not define as a supremum (Poincare.LocalSlope.Intrinsic.constant is only the per-measure C_P), so nothing is mapped.

items.label: Optimal small ball estimate
items.statement: For isotropic log-concave X in R^n there is a universal c_0 > 0 such that for every ε < c_0 and y ∈ R^n, P(‖X − y‖² ≤ εn) ≤ ε^{c_0 n}.
items.note: Main item: the new result of the note (it removes the log n factor of Theorem B); Theorem C is then deduced from it in Section 3.2. Proof: Section 2.1 reduction (uses Lemma 5) to y = 0 and support of diameter √(C_1 n), C_1 = 8C_0²; then stochastic localization at time c_1 with Lemmas 8–10, 9, 6, 4. Printed constant c_0 = min(c, c_1^6/(256 e^{C_1}), c c_1^8 n/512) contains a stray n in the third term (should be c c_1^8/512). The Lean predicates FunctionalInequalities.KLS.Isotropic and FunctionalInequalities.KLS.LogConcave name its hypotheses only; no Lean statement asserts a small ball bound, so nothing is mapped.

items.label: Equivalent slicing formulations
items.statement: Bourgain's slicing conjecture is equivalent to sup_n L_n < ∞ and to sup_n L̃_n < ∞, where L_n is the supremum of L_K over convex bodies in convex isotropic position and L̃_n the supremum of sup_x f(x)^{1/n} over isotropic log-concave densities f on R^n.
items.note: Stated as well known with reference to Klartag's survey; no proof given. Isotropic constants are outside the Lean library.

items.label: Slicing conjecture
items.statement: sup_{n ∈ N} L_n < ∞.
items.note: Cited from Klartag–Lehec and re-proved in Section 3.2: an extremal K with L_K = L_n is in M-position, Vol(K ∩ √(C_2 n) B_2^n) > c_2^n (Bourgain–Klartag–Milman, cited), while Theorem 1 for the uniform law on L_K^{-1}K gives Vol(K ∩ L_K √(c_3 n) B_2^n) ≤ c_3^{c_0 n}; with c_3 = min(c_0, c_2^{1/c_0}) this yields L_n² < C_2/c_3.

items.label: Bootstrapped small ball
items.statement: For isotropic log-concave X in R^n there is a universal C'' > 0 such that for all ε > 0 and y ∈ R^n, P(‖X − y‖² ≤ ε² n) ≤ (C''ε)^n.
items.note: No separate proof: from Theorem C via Lemma 2 (bounded L̃_n) and P ≤ (C')^n Vol(ε√n B_2^n) as in display (4).

items.label: Projected Paouris estimate
items.statement: If X is b-subgaussian log-concave with covariance A, then for all y ∈ R^n and ε < c (the constant of Theorem A), P(‖X − y‖² ≤ ε Tr A) ≤ (4n‖A‖_op ε/Tr A)^{c Tr(A)³/(8n² b² ‖A‖_op²)}.
items.note: Proof projects onto the span of the top k = ⌊Tr A/(2λ_1)⌋ ∨ 1 eigenvectors, where λ_k ≥ Tr A/(2n), and applies Theorem A to X_E. The printed final exponent drops b² (it is restored in the statement).

items.label: Borell moment comparison
items.statement: There is a constant C_0 > 1 such that every log-concave real random variable Y and every p ≥ 2 satisfy (E|Y|^p)^{2/p} ≤ C_0 E|Y|².
items.note: Classical; quoted without proof. As printed, with one constant for every p ≥ 2, the statement is false: for a two-sided exponential Y, (E|Y|^p)^{2/p} / E|Y|² = Γ(p+1)^{2/p}/2 grows like p²/(2e²). The paper uses it only with p = 4 (the covariance bound after (eq_290)), where it holds; the standard form is (E|Y|^p)^{1/p} ≤ C p (E|Y|²)^{1/2}.

items.label: Strong log-concavity gives subgaussianity
items.statement: A t-strongly log-concave random vector (log-concave relative to the Gaussian of variance 1/t) is 1/√t-subgaussian.
items.note: Proof via Hargé's inequality Cov_γ(f, g) ≤ 0 for log-concave f and convex g, applied with g(x) = (x·θ)^p after reducing to t = 1 and E X = 0.

items.label: Weaker subgaussian constant suffices
items.statement: A c''/√t-subgaussian bound with a universal c'' would suffice; by Prékopa–Leindler each marginal X·θ of a strongly log-concave X is strongly log-concave, so one-dimensional Caffarelli contraction or a log-Sobolev inequality with Herbst's argument also gives it.
items.note: Proof sketch only.

items.label: Guan trace lower bound
items.statement: If the stochastic localization starts at an isotropic log-concave μ, there is a universal c_1 > 0 with E Tr(A_{c_1}) ≥ c_1 n.
items.note: Cited from Guan (2024), whose proof uses Klartag's improved Lichnerowicz inequality; not proved here.

items.label: Set shrinkage along localization
items.statement: If μ has support of diameter D and (μ_t) is its stochastic localization, then for every measurable S, t ≥ 0 and λ > 1, μ(S) ≤ e^{D² t/2} μ_t(S)^{1/λ} with probability at least 1 − 1/λ.
items.note: From d[g]_t ≤ D² g_t² dt for g_t = μ_t(S), Itô's formula E log(1/g_t) ≤ log(1/g_0) + D² t/2 (display (17)) and Markov's inequality.

items.label: Large covariance trace event
items.statement: Under the reduced setting of Section 3.1 (isotropic log-concave μ with support of diameter √(C_1 n)), the event E_0 = {Tr A_{c_1} ≥ c_1 n/2} has P(E_0) ≥ c_1²/2.
items.note: Proof: split E Tr A_{c_1} ≥ c_1 n over E_0 and its complement using the almost sure bound A_{c_1} ≤ Id/c_1 (display (14), log-concave Lichnerowicz).

papers.title: Isoperimetric inequalities in high-dimensional convex sets
papers.result: A detailed entry point to stochastic localization, KLS and slicing up to the period covered by the notes.
papers.remaining: Reading guide; the July 2026 frontier requires the newer sources in the frontier table.

papers.title: Thin-shell bounds via parallel coupling
papers.result: For isotropic log-concave X, E(‖X‖ − √n)² ≤ C with a universal constant, via parallel coupling.
papers.remaining: The coupling construction and dimension-free thin-shell theorem are not locally formalized; thin shell alone does not remove the KLS logarithms.

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: Log-concave measures may be degenerate (log-concave density on an affine subspace); isotropic means barycenter 0 and Cov = Id; C, c denote universal constants that change from line to line. From Section 2 on, μ is a compactly supported probability measure on R^n whose support affinely spans R^n, with logarithmic Laplace transform Λ_t(θ) = log ∫ exp(⟨θ, x⟩ − t|x|²/2) dμ(x), tilts dμ_{t,θ}/dμ = exp(⟨x, θ⟩ − t|x|²/2 − Λ_t(θ)), μ_θ = μ_{0,θ}, barycenter a(t, θ) = ∇Λ_t(θ) and covariance A(t, θ) = ∇²Λ_t(θ), bounded by a constant C_μ. B is a standard Brownian motion in R^n with B_0 = 0 and (F_t) its natural filtration. Section 3 writes K for the interior of the convex hull of supp μ. Section 4 adds log-concavity, giving A(t, θ) ≤ Id/t (display (36)); Sections 5–6 assume μ isotropic, compactly supported and log-concave, with θ_t = G_{t,B}(0), stochastic localization μ_t = μ_{t,θ_t}, a_t = a(t, θ_t), A_t = A(t, θ_t) with eigenvalues λ_1(t) ≥ ... ≥ λ_n(t) > 0 and eigenvectors u_i(t). ‖f‖_{H^{-1}(μ)} = sup{∫ f g dμ : g ∈ C_c^∞, ∫|∇g|² dμ ≤ 1} for centered f ∈ L²(μ); |M| is the Hilbert–Schmidt norm and W_p the L^p Wasserstein distance. Numbering: one shared counter within sections for Theorem, Definition, Lemma, Proposition, Corollary and Remark (no Question, Conjecture, Speculation or Problem occurs; no appendix).
lemma_map.omitted: All 37 numbered statements of v2 are listed (no numbered statement is purely expository; Remarks 3.7, 3.9, 3.10, 4.8 and 4.9 each assert a mathematical claim, mostly without proof). Unnumbered displayed claims are covered in the items that use them: the Gaussian and cube examples (2), the cited Bochner-type H^{-1} inequality (6) and its consequence (7) used for Theorem 1.1, the uniform tilt bounds (11)-(13), the log-concave Lichnerowicz bound (36)-(37), the von Neumann trace inequality (50) used for Proposition 4.6, Guan's estimate E Tr A_t² ≤ Cn (56), the short-time operator-norm bounds (58)-(59), the covariance SDE (65), and the conditions (71) and (75)-(76) on f. Equation numbers were recomputed from the LaTeX and checked against the PDF.

items.label: Thin-shell variance bound
items.statement: If X is an isotropic log-concave random vector in R^n (mean zero, Cov(X) = Id), then Var(|X|²) = E(|X|² − n)² ≤ C n with a universal constant C > 0.
items.note: Main item: the paper calls it its main result and it is the thin-shell conjecture in the variance form; the abstract's form E(|X| − √n)² ≤ C is the immediate Corollary 1.2. Derived from Theorem 1.4 via the cited Bochner-type inequality ‖f‖²_{L²(μ)} ≤ Σ‖∂_i f‖²_{H^{-1}(μ)} (display (6), Barthe–Klartag and Klartag 2010) applied to f = |x|² − n, giving display (7). Tight up to C (C = 2 Gaussian, 4/5 cube). No Lean declaration: FunctionalInequalities.KLS.Isotropic only encodes the isotropy hypothesis (finite second moment, zero mean, identity covariance), and no repository statement bounds Var(|X|²), even in dimension 1.

items.label: Thin shell for the norm
items.statement: If X is an isotropic log-concave random vector in R^n, then Var(|X|) ≤ E(|X| − √n)² ≤ C with a universal constant C.
items.note: Follows from Theorem 1.1 and E(|X| − √n)² ≤ n^{-1} E(|X|² − n)²; this is the normalization displayed in the abstract.

items.label: Stretched-exponential thin-shell deviation
items.statement: For every isotropic log-concave X in R^n and every t > 0, P(||X| − √n| ≥ t) ≤ P(||X|² − n|/√n ≥ t) ≤ C exp(−c√t), with universal constants C, c > 0.
items.note: No proof is written; the paper combines Theorem 1.1 with the Bourgain / Nazarov–Sodin–Volberg reverse Hölder inequalities for polynomials of log-concave vectors. Stated to be suboptimal for large t.

items.label: H^{-1} bound for coordinates
items.statement: If μ is an isotropic log-concave probability measure on R^n, then Σ_{i=1}^n ‖x_i‖²_{H^{-1}(μ)} ≤ C n with a universal constant C, where ‖f‖_{H^{-1}(μ)} = sup{∫ f g dμ : g ∈ C_c^∞(R^n), ∫|∇g|² dμ ≤ 1}.
items.note: Proof in Section 6: the compactly supported case follows from Corollary 4.10 with t = 1 and Theorem 6.2; the general case uses weak lower semicontinuity of μ ↦ ‖x_i‖²_{H^{-1}(μ)} = sup_φ ∫(2x_iφ − |∇φ|²) dμ and approximation by re-isotropized restrictions to balls.

items.label: Pathwise flow and its derivative
items.statement: For μ compactly supported with affinely spanning support and any continuous path w with values in R^n, the equation θ_t = x + w_t + ∫_0^t a(s, θ_s) ds has a unique solution for every x ∈ R^n; θ_t(x) is jointly continuous in (t, x) and smooth in x, and M_t(x) = θ_t'(x) is jointly continuous, C¹ in t > 0, and the unique solution of M_0 = Id, dM_t/dt = A(t, θ_t(x)) M_t.
items.note: Proof by Picard–Lindelöf (Hartman) using the uniform bounds |a| ≤ C_μ and 0 ≤ A ≤ C_μ Id from compact support. Deterministic, no stochastic calculus.

items.label: Flow map G_{t,w}
items.statement: For t ≥ 0, x ∈ R^n and a continuous path w, G_{t,w}(x) is the value at time t of the unique solution of θ_t = x + w_t + ∫_0^t a(s, θ_s) ds from Lemma 2.1.

items.label: Continuity and adaptedness of flow
items.statement: The map (x, w) ↦ (G_{t,w}(x))_{t≥0} into C([0, ∞), R^n) (topology of locally uniform convergence) is continuous, and for fixed t ≥ 0 and x the map w ↦ G_{t,w}(x) is F_t-measurable for the natural filtration of the coordinate process.
items.note: Proof by Gronwall: |G_{t,w}(x) − G_{t,w̃}(x̃)| ≤ e^{C_μ t}(|x − x̃| + sup_{s≤t}|w_s − w̃_s|).

items.label: Lipschitz bound for the flow
items.statement: For t ≥ 0 and every continuous path w, the map G_{t,w}: R^n → R^n is e^{C_μ t}-Lipschitz, where C_μ bounds the covariance of all tilts of μ.
items.note: Read off from the Gronwall estimate in the proof of Lemma 2.3.

items.label: Law of the driven flow
items.statement: Fix x ∈ R^n and let X have law μ_x (the exponential tilt dμ_x/dμ ∝ e^{⟨x,·⟩}) and be independent of the standard Brownian motion B; then the process (G_{t,B}(x))_{t≥0} has the same law as (x + B_t + tX)_{t≥0}.
items.note: Proved through non-linear filtering: E[X | G_t] = a(t, x + tX + B_t) (Cameron–Martin), and the innovation process is a Brownian motion by Lévy's characterization; the x = 0 case is the Girsanov argument of Klartag–Lehec 2022, Proposition 6.7. Uses Brownian motion and martingale theory.

items.label: Large-time limit is the tilt
items.statement: For every x ∈ R^n, G_{t,B}(x)/t converges almost surely as t → ∞ and the limit has law μ_x.
items.note: Using one Brownian motion for all x gives the parallel coupling of the tilts μ_{x1} and μ_{x2}.

items.label: Flow maps are expanding diffeomorphisms
items.statement: For every t ≥ 0 and every continuous path w, the map G_{t,w}: R^n → R^n is a diffeomorphism and is expanding: |G_{t,w}(x) − G_{t,w}(y)| ≥ |x − y|.
items.note: Section 3 is a digression not used for the thin-shell proof. Invertibility by solving the integral equation backwards; expansion from convexity of Λ_t.

items.label: Time-shifted flow map
items.statement: For t_1, t_2 ≥ 0, a continuous path w and x ∈ R^n, G_{t_1,t_2,w}(x) = θ_{t_2}, where θ_t = x + w_t + ∫_0^t a(t_1 + s, θ_s) ds; this is the flow of Definition 2.2 for the reference measure μ_{t_1,0}.

items.label: Semigroup property of flows
items.statement: For every continuous path w and t_1, t_2 ≥ 0, G_{t_1+t_2,w} = G_{t_1,t_2,σ_{t_1}(w)} ∘ G_{t_1,w}, where (σ_{t_1}(w))_t = w_{t+t_1} − w_{t_1} is the shift.
items.note: Proof by concatenating solutions.

items.label: Barycenter map onto K
items.statement: For a compactly supported μ with affinely spanning support and every t ≥ 0, θ ↦ ∇Λ_t(θ) is a diffeomorphism from R^n onto K, the interior of the convex hull of the support of μ.
items.note: Standard; the paper cites Eldan–Klartag, Lemma 2.1, and proves it by strong convexity and Legendre duality. The printed display of Λ*(ξ) writes Λ(ξ) for Λ(θ).

items.label: Martingale diffeomorphisms S_{t,w}
items.statement: For a continuous path w and t ≥ 0, S_{t,w} = ∇Λ_t ∘ G_{t,w} ∘ (∇Λ_0)^{-1}, and for t_1, t_2 ≥ 0, S_{t_1,t_2,w} = ∇Λ_{t_1+t_2} ∘ G_{t_1,t_2,w} ∘ (∇Λ_{t_1})^{-1}; with S_t = S_{t,B} and S_{t_1,t_2} = S_{t_1,t_2,B}.

items.label: Martingale diffeomorphism process
items.statement: For μ compactly supported with affinely spanning support and K the interior of the convex hull of its support: (a) almost surely every S_t: K → K is a diffeomorphism with S_0 = Id; (b) for fixed ξ ∈ K, (S_t(ξ)) is a martingale converging almost surely to S_∞(ξ), whose law is the unique exponential tilt of μ with barycenter ξ; (c) (S_t(ξ)) is a time-inhomogeneous Markov process with E[f(S_{t_1+t_2}(ξ)) | F_{t_1}] = P_{t_1,t_2} f(S_{t_1}(ξ)) for bounded continuous f, where P_{t_1,t_2} f(ξ) = E f(S_{t_1,t_2}(ξ)).
items.note: Digression; not used in the thin-shell proof. Uses Brownian motion, martingales and the Markov property.

items.label: Boundary extension of S_t
items.statement: Under mild regularity assumptions and strict convexity of K, S_t extends to a homeomorphism of the closure of K with S_t = Id on ∂K for all t ≥ 0, almost surely.
items.note: Claim stated without proof in the paper.

items.label: Barycenter process is martingale
items.statement: For x ∈ R^n, with θ_t = G_{t,B}(x) and a_t = a(t, θ_t), the process (a_t) is a martingale and its limit as t → ∞ has law μ_x.
items.note: Via a_t = E[X | G_t] for X ~ μ_x independent of B and martingale convergence.

items.label: Stochastic localization as martingale
items.statement: For every bounded test function φ, the process ∫ φ dμ_{t,θ_t} is a martingale, so the measure-valued process (μ_{t,θ_t}) is a martingale; it is Eldan's stochastic localization of μ.
items.note: Stated without proof; also introduces terminology.

items.label: Generator of S_t(ξ)
items.statement: The Markov process (S_t(ξ)) is a time-inhomogeneous diffusion with generator L_t f(ξ) = ½ Tr[∇²Λ_t((∇Λ_t)^{-1}(ξ)) ∇²f(ξ)] for suitable f: K → R.
items.note: Proof omitted in the paper.

items.label: Monotone normalized flow distance
items.statement: If μ (compactly supported, affinely spanning support) is log-concave, then for every continuous path w and x, y ∈ R^n, |G_{t,w}(x) − G_{t,w}(y)|/t is non-increasing in t ∈ (0, ∞).
items.note: Uses the log-concave Lichnerowicz bound A(t, θ) ≤ Id/t (displays (36)-(37), cited).

items.label: Wasserstein bound via parallel coupling
items.statement: If μ is log-concave (with the standing compact-support assumption) and θ_t^x = G_{t,B}(x), then for all x, y ∈ R^n, 1 ≤ p < ∞ and t > 0, W_p(μ_x, μ_y) ≤ t^{-1}(E|θ_t^x − θ_t^y|^p)^{1/p}.
items.note: Optimal-transport coupling statement; the coupling is the parallel coupling of Corollary 2.6.

items.label: Infinitesimal Wasserstein bound
items.statement: If μ is log-concave (compactly supported) and M_t = G_{t,B}'(0), then for every v ∈ R^n and t > 0, limsup_{ε→0+} W_2(μ, μ_{εv})/ε ≤ (E|M_t v|²)^{1/2}/t.
items.note: Dominated convergence using Lemma 2.4.

items.label: H^{-1} norm via W_2
items.statement: For a centered compactly supported probability measure μ on R^n and every v ∈ R^n, ‖⟨x, v⟩‖_{H^{-1}(μ)} ≤ limsup_{ε→0+} W_2(μ, μ_{εv})/ε.
items.note: No log-concavity needed. The last display of the proof writes ⟨x, u⟩ for ⟨x, v⟩.

items.label: H^{-1} sum via derivative
items.statement: If μ is centered, compactly supported and log-concave, then for every t > 0, Σ_{i=1}^n ‖x_i‖²_{H^{-1}(μ)} ≤ t^{-2} E|M_t|², where M_t = G_{t,B}'(0) and |M| = (Tr M*M)^{1/2} is the Hilbert–Schmidt norm.

items.label: Product-integral Hilbert–Schmidt bound
items.statement: If (A_t)_{t≥0} is a continuous path of symmetric positive-definite n×n matrices with eigenvalues λ_1(t) ≥ ... ≥ λ_n(t) > 0 and M solves M_0 = Id, dM_t/dt = A_t M_t, then |M_t|²_{HS} ≤ Σ_{i=1}^n exp(2∫_0^t λ_i(s) ds) for every t > 0.
items.note: Deterministic matrix inequality; proof uses the von Neumann trace inequality and the min-max principle (both cited, unnumbered).

items.label: Majorization Gronwall comparison
items.statement: Let μ_1(t), ..., μ_n(t) and λ_1(t) ≥ ... ≥ λ_n(t) be non-negative continuous functions on [0, ∞) with Σ_{i≤k} μ_i(t) ≤ Σ_{i≤k}[1 + 2∫_0^t μ_i(s)λ_i(s) ds] for all t ≥ 0 and k ≤ n; then Σ_{i≤k} μ_i(t) ≤ Σ_{i≤k} exp(2∫_0^t λ_i(s) ds) for all t ≥ 0 and k ≤ n.
items.note: Elementary induction on k, formalized along the paper's proof. Lean drops the hypothesis μ_i ≥ 0, which the proof never uses, so the statement is slightly stronger; indices are 0, …, n − 1 and λ_i is written ℓ i. The final display of the proof writes λ_i(t) inside the ds-integral for λ_i(s).

items.label: Jensen form of the bound
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 4.6, Jensen's inequality gives |M_t|² ≤ t^{-1}∫_0^t Tr[e^{2tA_s}] ds.
items.note: The paper notes that the sharper Proposition 4.6 is what the proof needs.

items.label: Tilt distances under Gaussian convolution
items.statement: For a log-concave probability measure μ on R^n, the standard Gaussian γ, θ_1, θ_2 ∈ R^n and p ≥ 1, W_p(μ_{θ_1}, μ_{θ_2}) ≤ W_p((μ*γ)_{θ_1}, (μ*γ)_{θ_2}).
items.note: Proof omitted; the paper indicates it follows from the parallel couplings and A_t ≤ Id/t. Tilts are implicitly assumed to exist.

items.label: H^{-1} bound by eigenvalues
items.statement: If μ is compactly supported, centered and log-concave, then for every fixed t > 0, Σ_{i=1}^n ‖x_i‖²_{H^{-1}(μ)} ≤ t^{-2} E[Σ_{i=1}^n exp(2∫_0^t λ_i(s) ds)], where λ_1(s) ≥ ... ≥ λ_n(s) > 0 are the eigenvalues of A_s = ∇²Λ_s(G_{s,B}(0)).
items.note: Main novelty of the paper (parallel coupling + transport interpretation of H^{-1}).

items.label: Few large eigenvalues, stopped
items.statement: Let μ be isotropic, compactly supported and log-concave, A_t its stochastic-localization covariance process with eigenvalues λ_1(t) ≥ ... ≥ λ_n(t), and τ any stopping time for the Brownian filtration; then for every t > 0, Σ_{i=1}^n P(λ_i(t∧τ) ≥ 3) ≤ C n exp(−t^{−α}) with universal C, α > 0, and the proof gives α = 1/8.
items.note: Multi-scale iteration with t_k = 2^{−8k}t, D_k = t_k^{−1/4}, r_k ∈ [2, 3]; also uses the qualitative bound P(τ_* ≤ t) = o(t^k) for τ_* = inf{t : ‖A_t‖_op ≥ 2} (display (59), cited). The τ ≡ ∞ case essentially follows from Guan.

items.label: Guan's three-tensor bound
items.statement: Let t > 0 and X be a centered t-uniformly log-concave random vector in R^n with covariance eigenvalues λ_1, ..., λ_n, orthonormal eigenvectors v_1, ..., v_n and X_i = ⟨X, v_i⟩; then for 1 ≤ k ≤ n and u > 0, Σ_{i,j=1}^n (E X_i X_j X_k)² 1{max(λ_i, λ_j) ≤ u} ≤ 4 t^{−1/2} u^{3/2} λ_k.
items.note: Proof uses the improved Lichnerowicz inequality C_P(Y) ≤ √(u/t) (Klartag 2023) for Y = Proj_E X and Prékopa–Leindler (both cited, unnumbered). No Lean declaration: Poincare.LocalSlope.Intrinsic.constant could express C_P(Y), but no repository theorem states the improved Lichnerowicz bound or this lemma.

items.label: Itô drift of trace functionals
items.statement: For every C² function f: [0, ∞) → R and stopping time τ, d/dt E Tr f(A_{t∧τ}) = ½ Σ_{i,j} E[|ξ_{ij}(t)|² (f'(λ_i(t)) − f'(λ_j(t)))/(λ_i(t) − λ_j(t)) 1{t<τ}] − E[Σ_i λ_i(t)² f'(λ_i(t)) 1{t<τ}], where ξ_{ij}(t) = ∫⟨x − a_t, u_i(t)⟩⟨x − a_t, u_j(t)⟩(x − a_t) dμ_t(x) and the quotient means f''(λ_i) when λ_i = λ_j.
items.note: Uses the stochastic differential equation dA_t = Σ_i H_{i,t} dB_{i,t} − A_t² dt (display (65), cited), Itô's formula and the Daleckii–Krein formula; stochastic calculus.

items.label: Gronwall drift bound for f
items.statement: Let f: [0, ∞) → [0, ∞) be C², increasing, with f(x) = x² for x ≥ r and f'' ≤ D² f, where D > 1 and r ∈ [2, 3]; then for every stopping time τ and t > 0, d/dt E Tr f(A_{t∧τ}) ≤ C(1/t + D²/√t) E Tr f(A_{t∧τ}) with a universal C.
items.note: The pathwise inequality (73) is credited to Guan and re-proved; uses λ_i(t) ≤ 1/t and t-uniform log-concavity of μ_t.

items.label: Existence of test functions f_{D,r}
items.statement: For every D > 1 and r ∈ [2, 3] there is a C², positive, increasing f = f_{D,r}: [0, ∞) → R with f(x) = e^{D(x−r)} for x ≤ r − 1/D, f(x) = x² for x ≥ r, and f'' ≤ (12D)² f on [0, ∞).
items.note: Elementary construction; the last step is left as an exercise in the paper.

items.label: Stopping-time tail and moment
items.statement: For μ isotropic, compactly supported and log-concave, τ_k = inf{t > 0 : λ_k(t) ≥ 3}, k = 1, ..., n, and t > 0: P(τ_k ≤ t) ≤ C_1 (n/k) exp(−t^{−α}) and E τ_k^{−2} ≤ C_2 (1 + log(n/k))^β, with universal constants, α = 1/8 and β = 16.

items.label: Exponential eigenvalue integral bound
items.statement: If μ is an isotropic, compactly supported, log-concave probability measure on R^n and λ_i(t) are the eigenvalues of A_t = ∇²Λ_t(G_{t,B}(0)) as in Corollary 4.10, then E[Σ_{i=1}^n exp(2∫_0^1 λ_i(t) dt)] ≤ C n with a universal C.
items.note: Variant of Guan's bound E Tr A_t² ≤ Cn; uses λ_k(t) ≤ 1/t (display (36)) and summability of (1 + log(n/k))^16.

papers.title: Digesting the proof of the sharp thin-shell inequality
papers.result: For isotropic log-concave X: Var(‖X‖²) ≤ 8n and ‖T₃(X)‖²_HS ≤ 4n. The constants are sharp.
papers.remaining: The moment-Hessian estimate, third-order tensor identities and sharp conclusions are not locally formalized. A trace bound is not a universal matrix bound.

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: X is an isotropic log-concave random vector in R^n (E X = 0, Cov(X) = Id) with law μ; T(X) = (E X_i X_j X_k) and ‖·‖_HS is the Hilbert–Schmidt norm; ‖f‖_{H^{-1}(μ)} = sup{∫ f g dμ : g ∈ C_c^∞, ∫ |∇g|² dμ ≤ 1}. From Section 2 on (the regularity assumptions of Klartag 2023, Logarithmically-concave moment measures I): μ is supported on a bounded open convex K with density ρ = e^{−V}, V smooth convex with all derivatives bounded; ψ is the smooth strictly convex function whose moment measure is μ (Cordero-Erausquin–Klartag), ν = e^{−ψ} dx, (∇ψ)_# ν = μ, H = ∇²ψ, solving the Monge–Ampère equation ρ(∇ψ) det ∇²ψ = e^{−ψ} (5); the weighted manifold M*_μ = (R^n, ∇²ψ, ν) has weighted Laplacian L u = ψ^{ij} u_ij − (V_i ∘ ∇ψ) u_i, carré du champ Γ(u, v) = ψ^{ij} u_i v_j and Dirichlet form E. Cited, unproved inputs: the H^{-1} inequality Var(|X|²) ≤ 4 Σ ‖x_i‖²_{H^{-1}(μ)} (2), the sharp Poincaré inequality (7)-(8) on M_μ, M*_μ, the trace bound tr H ≤ 2R(K)² (10), LH + H ≥ 0 (12), and the weak lower semicontinuity of Σ ‖x_i‖²_{H^{-1}(μ)}. Numbering: one shared counter within sections for Theorem, Definition, Question, Lemma, Example, Conjecture, Speculation, Proposition, Corollary, Remark and Problem; the appendix is Section A; no Definition, Question, Conjecture, Speculation, Proposition or Problem occurs, and Section 2 has no numbered statement.
lemma_map.omitted: All 17 numbered statements of v1 are listed (Theorems 1.1, 1.2, 1.4, 1.5, Corollary 1.3, Lemmas 3.1-3.5, 3.7, 4.2, A.1-A.3, Example 3.6, Remark 4.1); none is purely expository, and Remark 4.1 asserts the Stein-kernel interpretation. Unnumbered or cited displayed claims ((2), (8), (10), (11), (12), the Stein identity (23) and the approximation arguments) are recorded in the notes of the items that use them; no Lean declaration states any of them. Labels and equation numbers were recomputed from the LaTeX counters and checked against the PDF text.

items.label: Sharp thin-shell variance bound
items.statement: For every isotropic log-concave random vector X in R^n (E X = 0, Cov(X) = Id), E(|X|² − n)² = Var(|X|²) ≤ 8n. Equality holds when X_1, ..., X_n are i.i.d. standard centered exponential variables with density e^{−x−1} on [−1, ∞).
items.note: Main item: the abstract and title designate the sharp thin-shell inequality Var(|X|²) ≤ 8n as the paper's result. Proof: the cited H^{-1} inequality Var(|X|²) ≤ 4 Σ_i ‖x_i‖²_{H^{-1}(μ)} (display (2), from Klartag 2010 and Barthe–Klartag 2020, not proved here) combined with Theorem 1.4; equality via E Z^4 = 9 for Z = E − 1. No Lean declaration: FunctionalInequalities.KLS.Isotropic (KLS/Isotropic.lean) only encodes the isotropy hypothesis, and no repository statement bounds Var(|X|²) or defines the H^{-1}(μ) norm or the exponential law.

items.label: Sharp third-moment tensor bound
items.statement: For every isotropic log-concave random vector X in R^n, the third-moment tensor T_ijk = E[X_i X_j X_k] satisfies ‖T‖²_HS = Σ_{i,j,k} (E X_i X_j X_k)² ≤ 4n, with equality for i.i.d. standard centered exponential coordinates.
items.note: Proved first under the regularity assumptions of Section 2 (Bessel's inequality for the orthonormal ψ_k in L²(ν) and display (22)), then for general μ by the regularisation 1_{B(0,R)} e^{−ε|x|²/2} (μ * γ_δ), re-isotropised, with convergence of moments up to order four. No Lean declaration states a third-moment bound; the Gaussian files under Poincare/Gaussian enter only through the convolution regulariser and do not state this item.

items.label: Sharp bounds for convex bodies
items.statement: If X is isotropic and uniformly distributed on a convex body in R^n, then Var(|X|²) ≤ 4n(n+1)²/((n+3)(n+4)) and ‖T(X)‖²_HS ≤ 4n(n−1)(n+2)/(n+3)²; both are attained by the uniform distribution on an isotropic regular simplex.
items.note: Apply Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 in dimension k = n + 1 to the cone vector of Lemma 4.2; sharpness via the representation (GX, G) = Σ_r E_r (v_r, 1) for a simplex with vertices v_r. No Lean declaration.

items.label: Sharp H^{-1} coordinate bound
items.statement: If μ is the law of an isotropic log-concave random vector in R^n, then Σ_{i=1}^n ‖x_i‖²_{H^{-1}(μ)} ≤ 2n, where ‖f‖_{H^{-1}(μ)} = sup{∫ f g dμ : g ∈ C_c^∞(R^n), ∫ |∇g|² dμ ≤ 1}; equality holds for i.i.d. standard centered exponential coordinates.
items.note: Under the regularity assumptions, the moment-map Stein identity (23) ∫ y_i g dμ = ∫ Σ_j τ_ij ∂_j g dμ with τ = H ∘ (∇ψ)^{-1} (justified with the Euclidean cutoff ζ_R from the proof of Lemma A.3) and Cauchy–Schwarz give the bound ∫ ‖τ‖²_HS dμ ≤ 2n; the general case uses the regular approximations from the proof of Theorem 1.2 and the weak lower semicontinuity of the functional from the proof of Klartag–Lehec 2025, Theorem 1.4 (cited). Equality follows from T11's exponential example and display (2). Improves the non-sharp constant of Klartag–Lehec 2025. No Lean declaration.

items.label: Second trace moment of H
items.statement: If X is isotropic log-concave in R^n and its law μ satisfies the regularity assumptions of Section 2 (μ supported on a bounded open convex K with density e^{−V}, V smooth convex with all derivatives bounded), and ψ is the convex function whose moment measure is μ, ν = e^{−ψ} dx and H = ∇²ψ, then ∫ ‖H(x)‖²_HS dν(x) ≤ 2n.
items.note: The paper's main technical estimate: N_2 = D_2 + A_2 + Q_2 ≥ 2D_2 and D_2 ≥ N_2 − n give N_2 ≤ 2n (display (22)). Depends on the moment-measure construction (Cordero-Erausquin–Klartag 2015) and the Monge–Ampère equation (5), which the repository does not formalize. No Lean declaration.

items.label: Exact identity LH+H = A+Q
items.statement: Under the regularity assumptions, with A = H(∇²V ∘ ∇ψ)H and Q_ij = tr(H^{-1} ∂_i H H^{-1} ∂_j H), the matrix fields A and Q are positive semi-definite and LH + H = A + Q entrywise, where Lu = Σ ψ^{ij} u_ij − Σ (V_i ∘ ∇ψ) u_i is the weighted Laplacian of the manifold (R^n, ∇²ψ, ν).
items.note: Refines the cited inequality LH + H ≥ 0 (display (12), Klartag 2023 moment measures Lemma 5.2); proved by differentiating log of the Monge–Ampère equation (5) twice. Not mapped to FunctionalInequalities.Analysis.BakryEmery.gammaTwo_nonneg (Analysis/BakryEmery/Bochner/Basic.lean): that is the Euclidean Bochner bound Γ₂ ≥ 0 for a convex potential, whereas L here carries the Riemannian metric ∇²ψ and the identity is specific to the Monge–Ampère potential.

items.label: Pointwise formula for L tr(H²)
items.statement: Under the regularity assumptions, pointwise on R^n, L tr(H²) = 2[−tr(H²) + d_2 + a_2 + q_2], where d_2 = ψ^{ab} tr(∂_a H ∂_b H), a_2 = tr(HA) and q_2 = tr(HQ) are non-negative.
items.note: Leibniz rule for L applied to Σ H_ij² together with Lemma 3.1. No Lean declaration (the repository's BakryEmery.weightedLaplacian_mul is the Euclidean product rule).

items.label: Integrated trace identity
items.statement: Under the regularity assumptions, d_2, a_2, q_2 are ν-integrable and N_2 = D_2 + A_2 + Q_2, where N_2 = ∫ tr(H²) dν and D_2, A_2, Q_2 are the ν-integrals of d_2, a_2, q_2.
items.note: Uses the cited boundedness tr H ≤ 2R(K)² (display (10), Klartag 2023) and the gradient bound Γ(G) ≤ 4G d_2 for G = tr(H²) (display (20)) to verify the hypotheses of Lemma A.2. No Lean declaration.

items.label: Poincaré bound for entries of H
items.statement: Under the regularity assumptions, N_2 − n ≤ D_2.
items.note: Applies the cited sharp Poincaré inequality Var_ν(u) ≤ ∫ ψ^{ij} u_i u_j dν on (R^n, ∇²ψ, ν) (display (8), Klartag 2023) to each bounded finite-energy entry H_ij (via Lemma A.1), and ∫ H dν = Id (display (11), justified by Lemma A.3). Not mapped to FunctionalInequalities.Poincare.LocalSlope.Intrinsic.constant (Poincare/LocalSlope/Basic.lean) or Solutions.LemLinearTestLower.certificate (solutions/LemLinearTestLower.lean): both concern the Euclidean Poincaré constant of a law, not the weighted Riemannian inequality (8) with metric ∇²ψ.

items.label: Cyclic identity q_2 ≥ d_2
items.statement: Pointwise, in coordinates with H(x) = diag(λ_1, ..., λ_n), q_2 − d_2 = (1/6) Σ_{a,i,j} ψ_aij² [(λ_a − λ_i)² + (λ_i − λ_j)² + (λ_j − λ_a)²]/(λ_a λ_i λ_j) ≥ 0; consequently Q_2 ≥ D_2.
items.note: The new elementary observation enabling the bootstrap; uses only the symmetry of ∇³ψ and cyclic averaging. No Lean declaration.

items.label: Exponential equality case for H
items.statement: For the standard centered exponential law in dimension one, ψ(t) = e^t − t, dν = e^{−e^t + t} dt, H(t) = e^t and ∫ H² dν = 2; for n independent copies, ∫ ‖H‖²_HS dν = 2n, so Theorem 1.5 is sharp.
items.note: Explicit computation via s = e^t. No Lean declaration.

items.label: Third moments as cubic derivatives
items.statement: Under the regularity assumptions, for all i, j, k, T_ijk = ∫ y_i y_j y_k dμ(y) = 2 ∫ ψ_ijk dν = 2 ∫ (H_ij − δ_ij) ψ_k dν.
items.note: D_2 < ∞ (Lemma 3.3) with H ≤ 2R(K)² Id gives ψ_ijk ∈ L²(ν), so the identities (35)-(36) of Lemma A.3 apply; then (∇ψ)_# ν = μ and ∫ ψ_k dν = 0. No Lean declaration.

items.label: Moment-map Stein kernel
items.statement: Under the regularity assumptions, the matrix field τ = H ∘ (∇ψ)^{-1} of the Stein identity (23) is the moment-map Stein kernel of μ, so Theorem 1.5 gives a Stein kernel whose squared Hilbert–Schmidt norm has μ-integral at most 2n.
items.note: Interpretive remark with a mathematical claim; the connection between moment maps and Stein kernels is attributed to Fathi. No Lean declaration (the repository defines no Stein kernel).

items.label: Cone construction moment formulas
items.statement: If X is isotropic and uniform on a convex body K ⊆ R^n, k = n + 1, G ~ Gamma(k, 1) is independent of X, and Y = (GX/√(k(k+1)), (G − k)/√k) ∈ R^k, then Y is isotropic and log-concave, Var(|Y|²) = (k+3)/(k(k+1)) · [(k+2) Var(|X|²) + 4k²] and ‖T(Y)‖²_HS = (k+2)²/(k(k+1)) ‖T(X)‖²_HS + 12 − 8/k.
items.note: Standard conical integration (cf. Klartag, Mahler paper, Lemma 2.1) with the moments of G. No Lean declaration: FunctionalInequalities.KLS.Isotropic would only express the isotropy conclusion as a predicate; nothing states the lemma.

items.label: Energy cutoffs and finite-energy domain
items.statement: Under the regularity assumptions there are χ_R ∈ C_c^∞(R^n) with 0 ≤ χ_R ≤ 1, χ_R → 1 in L²(ν) and ν-a.e., and E(χ_R, χ_R) ≤ CA/R with A < ∞ depending only on V and K; consequently every bounded smooth F with ∫ Γ(F) dν < ∞ lies in D(E), has Dirichlet energy ∫ Γ(F) dν, and satisfies the Poincaré inequality (8).
items.note: χ_R = η(ψ/R), using L ψ ≤ A and integration by parts (9) on the Riemannian manifold. No Lean declaration: the repository's operator-core and cutoff results (KLS/LogConcave/HeatSemigroup) concern the Euclidean form ∫ |∇f|² dν.

items.label: Vanishing integral of LG
items.statement: If G, S are smooth on R^n with 0 ≤ G ≤ B, S ≥ 0, LG = 2(S − G) and Γ(G) ≤ 4BS for some B < ∞, then S ∈ L¹(ν) and ∫ LG dν = 0.
items.note: Not mapped to FunctionalInequalities.KLS.LogConcave.integral_weightedLaplacian_eq_zero (KLS/LogConcave/HeatSemigroup/Generator.lean): that states ∫ ℒf dν = 0 for the Euclidean weighted Laplacian Δf − ⟪∇U, ∇f⟫ and compactly supported C² f, whereas here L uses the metric ∇²ψ, G is not compactly supported, and the integrability of S is part of the conclusion.

items.label: Euclidean integration-by-parts identities
items.statement: If ∇ψ and H = ∇²ψ are bounded on R^n, then ∫ ψ_ij dν = ∫ ψ_i ψ_j dν for all i, j; if in addition ψ_ijk ∈ L¹(ν), then ∫ ψ_ijk dν = ∫ ψ_ij ψ_k dν and ∫ ψ_i ψ_j ψ_k dν = 2 ∫ ψ_ijk dν, where dν = e^{−ψ} dx.
items.note: Proved with Euclidean cutoffs ζ_R(x) = ζ(x/R) and dominated convergence. Not mapped to FunctionalInequalities.Analysis.BakryEmery.integral_inner_gradient_tilted (Analysis/BakryEmery/IntegrationByParts/Basic.lean) or FunctionalInequalities.KLS.LogConcave.integral_inner_gradient_eq (Generator.lean): those state ∫ ⟪∇f, ∇g⟫ dν = ∫ (−ℒf) g dν for compactly supported C² f against a tilted Haar law, a tool for the cutoff step, while the lemma concerns the non-compactly-supported functions ψ_i, ψ_ij and the passage R → ∞.

papers.title: The KLS constant is O(log^(1/4) n)
papers.result: For isotropic log-concave X and symmetric M, Var(XᵀMX) ≤ 8‖M‖²_HS = 2 E‖∇(XᵀMX)‖². For n ≥ 2, ψₙ = O((log n)^(1/4)), hence C_P = O(√log n).
papers.remaining: Formalized: the compact counterpart of Theorem 1.2 with the exact constant 8. letwinCompactBound : LetwinCompactBound gives, for every n > 0, every compactly supported isotropic log-concave law and every self-adjoint quadratic form (singular and indefinite included), variance at most 8 times the squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm; it is the supporting certificate thm:letwin-compact-quadratic-bound. Its proof reduces the compact case to the regular class 1_K e^{-W} dx (the compact case of Lemma A.1) and works at one actual weak C^{1,1} moment witness of that class: bounded moment-map existence and pushforward (Lemma 2.1 for bounded laws), the weak Monge-Ampere identities (Lemma 2.4 in weak form), Lemma 2.3 for that potential, the weak trace contraction and Theorem 2.5's bound E tr(B Hess u B Hess u) <= 2 tr(B^2) for every real symmetric B in weak form, and the bounded-Lipschitz source Stein identity; then the Gaussian product coupling with the compact dual bound, the H^-1 step on the Gaussian-smoothed law (Proposition 2.8), the spectral noise energy and the singular extension (Lemma A.2, stronger form). Not formalized: Theorem 1.1; the noncompact Theorem 1.2 and the full Lemma A.1; Theorem 2.5 and Lemma 2.2 as stated for the smooth moment map; the target Stein kernel of Lemma 2.7; and general finite-mass or unbounded moment-map existence and uniqueness. The other supporting results keep their recorded scopes in the lemma map. No Letwin paper-target certificate is registered, so the paper is not covered.

local_results.scope: Lemma A.3 (weighted directional IBP, any direction) and the finite identity (2.12) with arbitrary real weights

Lemma 2.3 in conditional generic form: for any smooth potential with ν = e^{-φ} m a probability law and isotropic gradient law (∇φ)_* ν, with Hessian integrability, the mean Hessian is the identity; the smooth moment-map producer of Lemma 2.2 and its source regularity class are not formalized (for the actual R0 source potential, under C1/Lipschitz-gradient hypotheses, the mean Hessian Id is produced by lem:letwin-regular-moment-weak-mean-hessian without asserting full smoothness)

Definition 2.6 (compact-test Stein kernel, HS norm), (2.19) H^{-1} norm as an extended supremum, A.7 (locally Lipschitz extension and Cauchy–Schwarz) and Lemma 2.9 for full-dimensional log-concave laws; no kernel construction, no Theorem 1.1/1.2 coverage

Lemma 2.7 analytic part for a given normalized convex potential with isotropic gradient image and injective gradient: the Hessian kernel is a symmetric PSD integrable Stein kernel with mean Id; moment-map existence, strict PD and HS-L² open

Proof of Theorem 1.2, p. 14, covariance step preceding (2.21): Cov(|M|^{1/2} X) = |M| for isotropic X and every real symmetric M (singular, indefinite, dimension zero; reviewed stronger than the invertible reduction); not (2.21), Theorem 2.5 or Theorem 1.2

Theorem 2.5 extension step from PSD to all symmetric B under an arbitrary measure, conditional on the PSD bound as a named hypothesis (integrability for B derived); not the PSD bound, the moment map or Theorem 2.5

Lemma A.6 support only: density of compact smooth diffusion images in the centered classes of L²(ν) for a log-concave ν = m.tilted(−U), C¹ U, any finite dimension; not Brascamp–Lieb, A.6, the moment map or Theorem 2.5

Lemma A.6 supports only: compactly supported ordinary weighted-diffusion coercivity ∫∇²U(∇u,∇u) dμ ≤ ∫(ℒu)² dμ (C² U, any finite dimension) and the inverse-quadratic Young inequality for positive definite H on any finite index type; not Brascamp–Lieb, A.6, the moment map or Theorem 2.5

Lemma A.6 for a given potential: log-concave ν = m.tilted(−U), Hess U positive definite everywhere, C¹ f ∈ L²(ν); finite-energy (C² U) and extended-energy (C^∞ U, right side in [0,∞]) forms, bounded tests, any dimension, sharp for the Gaussian; not the source moment map or A.6 for the source law
Lemma A.6 energy facts: operator Young inequality, nonnegativity, coordinate form and continuity of ⟨∇f,H⁻¹∇f⟩

Theorem 2.5 support only: the pointwise trace identity (2.8) for smooth φ, any V and every constant real B (no PSD, commutation or Monge–Ampère premise); not the Lemma 2.4 substitution, (2.10), the tensor comparison or the trace bound

(2.9)–(2.10) for a given smooth PD potential with the Monge–Ampère relation and local V, every constant B; nonnegative remainders and L tr(BHBH) + 2 tr(BHBH) ≥ 0 pointwise for PSD B and V convex on open K; not the A.4/A.5 integration, the source moment map or the trace bound
PSD Frobenius pairing, trace of a PSD product and trace-weighted Gram positivity (matrix support for (2.10))

Lemma A.4, real-variable part only: profile η(t) = smoothTransition(2 − t) with derivative support and bound, smooth majorant w ≥ |η″| vanishing for t ≤ 0 and t ≥ 3, monotone exhaustion η(a/(n+1)) ↑ 1 and η(a/R) ↑ 1 for real R > 0, tail primitive q_R(t) = R⁻¹∫_{t/R}^3 w (R > 0), affine rescaling of derivatives; the cutoffs η((φ − min φ + 1)/R), their compact support and the O(1/R) defect bound are lem:letwin-a4-cutoffs

Lemma A.4 for every potential in the source class (smooth convex φ with bounded gradient image, V smooth near its closure, Monge–Ampère, PD Hessian, ∫e^{−φ} = 1; any finite dimension, any Haar measure): cutoffs for every real R ≥ 1 with ∫|Lχ_R| dν ≤ C/R and the natural-index C/(n+1) form; the moment-map properties are hypotheses, the moment map is not constructed

Lemmas A.4–A.5 applied to the explicit uniform-interval potential (V ≡ log(2√3), gradient range in (−√3, √3); pushforward to the uniform law not proved; not the general moment-map producer) with the nonconstant f = tanh²(√3y/2): Lf ∈ L¹(ν) and ∫Lf dν = 0; gradient range inclusion only, no pushforward; not Theorem 2.5 or 1.2
At a gradient differentiability point of a C1 potential, identify the coordinate Hessian with D(gradient u) and prove Hermitian symmetry; all finite dimensions, no C2 assumption.

Inverse-Hessian entries times measurable bounded compactly supported functions are integrable, from a Lipschitz gradient, continuous F and det = exp F a.e.; no C1/C2 or PosDef premise; all finite dimensions.

Both original weak C1,1 generator identities of (2.2) for the a.e. Monge-Ampere solution, w C1 with Lipschitz gradient and eta C2 compactly supported; no C2 u or w; supports Theorem 2.5, not the trace bound or Theorems 2.5/1.2.

Integrability of the weighted squared shifted-Hessian density for continuous u with Lipschitz gradient and continuous compact eta; every shift and dimension.

For a G-Lipschitz gradient, total Hessian entries are L2 on every compact set and cutoff products with continuous compact chi are globally L2; no differentiability premise, all finite dimensions.

From the original potential data (u, V, G, LF, K and the a.e. PD/log-det/cap data) and the original global centered-difference bound, a produced C >= 0 bounding the squared global L2 translation difference of chi*H_ij by C t^2 for all nonzero |t| <= 1; C1 compact chi, arbitrary v, i, j and dimension. The C t^2 bound is a conclusion; the centered-difference bound is an input.

Not determinant/inverse calculus, evolution or the trace bound.
