Let J_i be compactly supported fluxes in L2 on every compact set and F a compactly supported locally integrable forcing with int sum_i J_i d_i psi = -int F psi for every compactly supported C1 test psi. Then every globally bounded locally integrable eta whose coordinate weak derivatives a_i are in L2 on every compact set satisfies: each J_i a_i and F eta is integrable and int sum_i J_i a_i = -int F eta, in every dimension. The shared compact-local tools used here (products with compactly supported L2 functions, compact C1 multiplier data, compact L-infinity bounds of continuous functions and local integrability from compact L2 bounds) are public in the same owner.

Let A be a matrix field with measurable entries bounded by M and coordinate weak derivatives DA_k in L2 on every compact set. For every real matrix B, tr(B A B A) is globally bounded and locally integrable, with weak coordinate derivatives 2 tr(B A B DA_k) in L2 on every compact set. For every real matrix S and every direction v along which the entries of H (bounded by M) have weak derivatives DH that are L2 on compact sets, every entry of S H S is bounded explicitly and has weak derivative the corresponding entry of S DH S, again L2 on compact sets. All finite dimensions.

Let u be C1 with Lipschitz gradient, V be C1, the exponent -u + V(grad u) be globally Lipschitz, det Hess u = exp(-u + V(grad u)) almost everywhere, and the inverse Hessian entries be essentially bounded on every compact set. Let chi be a compactly supported C1 cutoff with Lipschitz gradient whose inverse-Hessian generator tr((Hess u)^-1 Hess chi) - DV(grad u)(grad chi), weighted by e^{-u}, is integrable. Then for every globally bounded locally integrable eta with coordinate weak derivatives a_i in L2 on every compact set, both pairings below are integrable and int eta (tr((Hess u)^-1 Hess chi) - DV(grad u)(grad chi)) e^{-u} = -int sum_ij (Hess u)^-1_ij a_i d_j chi e^{-u}.

This is the weak counterpart of the trace contraction (2.8)/(2.10) in the proof of Letwin Theorem 2.5. Let H, R and E be matrix fields, T a tensor field and rho a continuous weight. Assume H has globally essentially bounded entries, the entries of T and of the fluxes J_ija = sum_b R_ba T_bij are L2 on every compact set, E is locally integrable, and rho sum_a J_ija (psi T_alk + d_a psi H_lk) tested against every compactly supported C1 psi equals minus the integral of rho E_ij psi H_lk. Then for every real matrix B, the density g = 2 tr(B H B E) + 2 sum_ij R_ij tr(B T_i B T_j) is locally integrable and, for every compactly supported C1 psi, the contracted flux sum_j (sum_i R_ij 2 tr(B H B T_i)) d_j psi weighted by rho integrates to minus the integral of rho g psi, with all terms integrable. All finite dimensions; no Hessian, potential or source premise.

For positive semidefinite matrices B, H, R, W and symmetric matrices T_i, with G_R the trace Gram matrix (G_R)_ij = tr(R T_i R T_j), the quantity 2 tr(B H B (-H + H W H + G_R)) + 2 sum_ij R_ij tr(B T_i B T_j) + 2 tr(B H B H) is nonnegative.

For a positive definite H, a symmetric B and a fully symmetric three-tensor T, sum_ij (H^-1)_ij tr(B T_i B T_j) <= tr(B H B G), where G_ij = tr(H^-1 T_i H^-1 T_j); this is Letwin (2.12) in trace-Gram coordinates. For positive semidefinite B and W and positive definite H, the quantity D = sum_ij (H^-1)_ij tr(B T_i B T_j) satisfies 0 <= D and 4 D <= g + 2 tr(B H B H), where g = 2 tr(B H B (-H + H W H + G)) + 2 D is the weak trace density.

For the actual source law, under the exact original R0 hypotheses (n > 0, isotropic 1_K exp(-W) dx with K compact and convex with nonempty interior, W smooth and kappa-uniformly convex), the same u, L, LF, T and the same common cutoff family as the weak cutoffs (whole earlier payload retained) satisfy, for every r >= 1 and every globally bounded locally integrable eta with coordinate weak derivatives in L2 on every compact set, the rough inverse-Hessian cutoff-generator identity. No source premise is added.

Let U be C1 with int e^{-U} = 1, v be smooth and compactly supported, and eta be globally bounded and locally integrable with coordinate weak derivatives a_i in L2 on every compact set. Then eta Lv and sum_i a_i d_i v are integrable for the tilted measure e^{-U} dx and int eta Lv dnu = -int sum_i a_i d_i v dnu, where L is the ordinary weighted Laplacian; no inverse-Hessian object is used.

On a finite-dimensional real inner product space, let U be C1 and globally Lipschitz with Lipschitz gradient and integrable e^{-U}. For every smooth compactly supported f, <D(grad U) grad f, grad f> and (Lf)^2 are integrable for the tilted measure and the integral of the first is at most the integral of the second. This is the Lipschitz-gradient sibling of compact_ordinary_diffusion_coercivity.

This is Letwin Lemma A.6 at C^{1,1} regularity for a given potential. Let nu = e^{-U} dx be a log-concave probability measure with U C1, globally Lipschitz, with Lipschitz gradient, int e^{-U} = 1 and almost everywhere positive definite coordinate Hessian. For every globally bounded locally integrable eta with coordinate weak derivatives a in L2 on every compact set and nu-integrable inverse-Hessian energy <a, (Hess U)^-1 a>, Var_nu eta <= int <a, (Hess U)^-1 a> dnu. The Hilbert-closure helpers it shares with the scalar Brascamp-Lieb owner are public there.

For symmetric S and D and arbitrary A, sum_ij (S A S)_ij (S D S)_ij = tr((S S) A (S S) D). For symmetric S, arbitrary R and symmetric T_k, the entrywise quadratic forms of the vectors ((S T_k S)_ij)_k against R sum to sum_kl R_kl tr((S S) T_k (S S) T_l). All finite dimensions.
Under a probability measure, for an almost everywhere symmetric random matrix H with L2 entries and symmetric mean M, sum_ij Var(H_ij) = int tr(H H) - tr(M M). All finite dimensions.

This is the weak C^{1,1} form of Letwin Theorem 2.5 for a given potential, with positive semidefinite B. Let nu = e^{-U} dx with U convex, C1, globally Lipschitz, with Lipschitz gradient, int e^{-U} = 1 and almost everywhere positive definite Hessian; let T be a weak Hessian tensor in L2 on every compact set, and let the inverse Hessian entries be essentially bounded on every compact set. Assume as hypotheses that the Hessian entries are nu-integrable with mean Id, that D = sum_kl (Hess U)^-1_kl tr(B T_k B T_l) is nu-integrable and that the half-energy bound int D dnu <= (1/2) int tr(B Hess U B Hess U) dnu holds. Then tr(B Hess U B Hess U) is nu-integrable and its integral is at most 2 tr(B B). The mean and half-energy inputs remain visible hypotheses; only the actual source producer discharges them.

For an arbitrary measure and finite index type, let H have measurable entries and be positive semidefinite almost everywhere. If tr(A H A H) is integrable with integral at most 2 tr(A A) for every positive semidefinite A, then the same holds for every symmetric B, singular or indefinite. This is the almost-everywhere version of symmetric_trace_integral_extension.

If g is the weak directional derivative of f along v against compactly supported C1 tests and f and g are globally integrable, then int g = 0. Every dimension, including zero, and every direction. The proof body is the accepted S1 API output, copied verbatim.

Let U be globally Lipschitz with int e^{-U} = 1 and eta be bounded and globally Lipschitz. For every direction v, D_v eta and eta D_v U are integrable for the tilted measure e^{-U} dx and int D_v eta dnu = int eta D_v U dnu. All dimensions.

For C1 functions u and f and a point y where grad u is differentiable, d_i (f o grad u)(y) = sum_j (Hess u)_ij(y) (grad f)_j(grad u(y)). This is the C1 counterpart of chain_coordinate; all dimensions.

Let u be C1 and globally Lipschitz with Lipschitz gradient and int e^{-u} = 1, and let nu = e^{-u} dx. For every C1, bounded and globally Lipschitz test f and every coordinate i, d_i u f(grad u) and sum_j (Hess u)_ij d_j f(grad u) are nu-integrable and int d_i u f(grad u) dnu = int sum_j (Hess u)_ij d_j f(grad u) dnu. This is the latent source coupling identity behind Lemma 2.7 at C^{1,1} regularity; no Stein kernel is constructed and no target inverse is used.

Let P be a measure on a latent space, Z a measurable map with P.map Z = mu for a probability law mu, and F a latent field in L2(P). If a smooth compactly supported h satisfies the latent source identity int <x, v> h dmu = int <F, grad h(Z)> dP, then (int <x, v> h dmu)^2 <= (int |F|^2 dP) (int |Dh|^2 dmu). Arbitrary latent space and all dimensions. The source identity and the L2 field remain inputs; this is the compact dual Cauchy-Schwarz step that supplies the dual bound directly, without a target Stein kernel.

Under gaussianLaw s with s > 0, in every dimension, for every C1, bounded and globally Lipschitz f and every direction v, <x, v> f and D_v f are integrable and int <x, v> f = (2 s)^-1 int D_v f. This supports the Gaussian smoothing step; no product coupling is asserted.

For the actual source law, under the exact original R0 hypotheses (n > 0, isotropic 1_K exp(-W) dx with K compact and convex with nonempty interior, W smooth and kappa-uniformly convex), there is ONE weak normalized convex globally Lipschitz moment potential u, with constants L, LF and weak Hessian tensor T, that retains the whole earlier payload: R0 regularity (C1, 16/kappa-Lipschitz gradient, 4/kappa centered-difference bound, almost everywhere positive definite Hessian with log-det equation and 16/kappa cap), the weak tensor, first Monge-Ampere and inverse fields, mean Hessian Id under nu = e^{-u} dx, the weak evolution identities, bounded testing, the weak cutoffs and rough cutoff testing, the weak trace contraction, A.5 conservativity int g dnu = 0 and the half energy int D dnu <= (1/2) int tr(B H B H) dnu for every positive semidefinite B. It adds: for EVERY real symmetric B, tr(B H B H) is nu-integrable and int tr(B H B H) dnu <= 2 tr(B B) (Theorem 2.5 with the exact constant 2, weak C^{1,1} form for this witness); the weighted integration by parts int D_v eta dnu = int eta D_v u dnu for every bounded globally Lipschitz eta; and the coordinate source Stein identity for every C1, bounded and globally Lipschitz test. This is not the smooth moment map of Lemma 2.2, not a constructed Stein kernel, and not Theorem 1.2 or the constant-8 bound.

Finite real-matrix trace identities over any finite index type: tr((A + tI)^T (A + tI)) = tr(A^T A) + 2t tr A + n t^2; invariance of tr((AQ)^T AQ) under a symmetric involution Q; tr(SHS) = tr(S^2 H); and tr((SHS)^T SHS) = tr(S^2 H S^2 H) for symmetric S, H.

For symmetric invertible M with B = sqrt(M^2), S = sqrt B and Q = sign M: B and S are positive semidefinite, Q is symmetric, B^2 = M^2, S^2 = B, SQS = M, Q^2 = I, S is invertible, Q acts self-adjointly and S defines a self-adjoint continuous linear equivalence.
Every symmetric real matrix A over a finite index type is the limit of the symmetric invertible matrices A - r_k I, with 0 < r_k < 1/(k+1) outside the finite real spectrum of A.
For a matrix field H with integrable entries and mean Id under a measure, tr(B H) is integrable with integral tr B for every matrix B.
For a symmetric continuous linear operator A and any finite orthonormal basis b, the sum over i, j of <A b_i, b_j>^2 equals tr(A o A).
For complete real inner product spaces, a continuous linear S, z and f differentiable at Sx + z, the gradient of y -> f(Sy + z) at x is S* grad f(Sx + z).

The Euclidean action of real n x n matrices equals the Euclidean linear map of the matrix and is multiplicative, additive, homogeneous and unital; (A e_i)_j = A_ji and the sum of |A e_i|^2 is tr(A^T A).
If grad u is Lipschitz on R^n, then y -> Hess u(y) v is in L2 of every finite measure, for every v.

Coordinate form sum A_ij x_i x_j = <Ax, x>; the sandwich <Q(Sx), Sx> = <(SQS)x, x> and invariance of the variance of the quadratic form under the pushforward by symmetric S; and e(H(e* v)) + t v = (SHS + tI) v for a self-adjoint equivalence e with the operator of S.
For symmetric invertible M with B = sqrt(M^2), S = sqrt B, Q = sign M, every symmetric H and real t: the sum over i of |(SHS + tI) Q e_i|^2 equals tr(BHBH) + 2t tr(BH) + n t^2.

For probability measures on arbitrary measurable spaces and a measurable, a.e. symmetric matrix field with integrable entries, mean Id and the input trace bound int tr(B'HB'H) <= 2 tr(B'^2) for every symmetric B', the integrated energy of the shifted action is at most 2 tr(M^2) + 2t tr B + n t^2 for symmetric invertible M. No log-concavity or Hessian hypothesis.
If f is in L4 with values in a real inner product space and A is continuous linear, then <A f, f> is in L2.
For a probability measure and finitely many real L2 functions f_i, if the coefficients c_{k,i} converge to b_i then the variance of sum_i c_{k,i} f_i converges to that of sum_i b_i f_i.
For a probability law on R^n with finite fourth moment and matrices A_k -> A, the variance of sum (A_k)_ij x_i x_j converges to that of sum A_ij x_i x_j.

For every probability law on R^n (every n) with finite fourth moment and every real C: if Var(sum B_ij x_i x_j) <= C tr(B^2) for all symmetric invertible B, then for all symmetric B. Stronger than Letwin Lemma A.2 (no isotropy or log-concavity, arbitrary C); proved through B - r_k I outside the spectrum, not M + eps P_0. It does not establish the bound.
For probability laws mu, nu on a complete separable real inner product space with finite fourth moments, nu centered, and continuous linear A, Var_mu <Ax, x> <= Var_{mu * nu} <Ax, x>.
gaussianLaw s (s > 0) has a fourth moment, and fourth moments pass to Gaussian smoothings and to continuous linear images of a probability measure.
For s > 0, bounded globally Lipschitz C1 h and a, v: int <z, v> h(a + z) = (2s)^-1 int D_v h(a + z) under gaussianLaw s, both integrable.
If g pushes the probability measure rho to mu, S is continuous linear and s > 0, then rho x gaussianLaw s pushed by (y, z) -> S(g y) + z is the Gaussian smoothing of S_# mu.

For a log-concave probability law with full affine support, a continuous linear equivalence S and s > 0, the Gaussian smoothing of S_# mu is e^{-W} dx with W smooth and convex, and the smoothed probability law is log-concave.

For C1 globally Lipschitz u with Lipschitz gradient and int e^{-u} = 1: the source Stein identity in a direction v for bounded Lipschitz C1 tests f, and its affine form for tests h(S grad u + z) with continuous linear S.

For s > 0, on P = (e^{-u} dx) x gaussianLaw s with Z = S grad u + z: the latent fields are in L2(P), the source and noise pairings are integrable, and int <Z, v> h(Z) dP = int (<S* v, Hess u S* grad h(Z)> + (2s)^-1 D_v h(Z)) dP for bounded Lipschitz C1 h.

With grad u pushing e^{-u} dx to mu, s > 0 and nu_s the Gaussian smoothing of S_# mu: (int <x, v> h d nu_s)^2 <= int |S Hess u S* v + (2s)^-1 v|^2 dP * int |Dh|^2 d nu_s for smooth compactly supported h.
If a <= b + c (2s)^-1 + d ((2s)^-1)^2 for every s > 0, then a <= b.
For a probability law with finite fourth moment, continuous linear A and s > 0, Var <Ax, x> is at most its variance under the Gaussian smoothing.

For log-concave mu with full affine support equal to grad u_# (e^{-u} dx) with u as above, a continuous linear equivalence S, self-adjoint Q and s > 0: the variance of <Qx, x> under the Gaussian smoothing of S_# mu is at most 4 times sum_i int |S Hess u S* Q e_i + (2s)^-1 Q e_i|^2 dP, via the H^-1 inequality on the smooth convex smoothed law.

If a probability law mu has density 1_K e^{-W}, with K closed convex and W continuous convex, then 1_K e^{-W} is a Borell density of mu, so mu is log-concave; in particular every regular-class probability law is log-concave.
For every measure mu on R^n: if Var(sum M_ij x_i x_j) <= 8 tr(M^2) for every symmetric M, then mu satisfies LetwinQuadraticBound.

Exact R0 hypotheses (n > 0, isotropic 1_K e^{-W} dx, K compact convex with nonempty interior, W smooth and kappa-uniformly convex): Var(sum M_ij x_i x_j) <= 8 tr(M^2) for every symmetric M, hence LetwinQuadraticBound. Regular-class case of Letwin Theorem 1.2.

letwinCompactBound : LetwinCompactBound: for every n > 0, every compactly supported isotropic log-concave law and every self-adjoint form (singular and indefinite included), variance at most 8 times the squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm in the standard orthonormal basis. Exact compact counterpart of Letwin Theorem 1.2, certified in source form; the noncompact theorem is not covered.

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: Probability measures on R^n, n >= 2; log-concave means a log-concave density on the affine hull of the support (Borell); isotropic means mean 0 and covariance Id. C_P is the optimal Poincare constant for locally Lipschitz tests, psi_mu the inverse isoperimetric (Cheeger) constant with min{mu(A), 1 - mu(A)} denominator over smooth-boundary open sets, psi_n = sup psi_mu over isotropic log-concave mu on R^n. Throughout Section 2 and Appendix A (except Lemmas A.1, A.2 and the general Stein-kernel statements Definition 2.6, Proposition 2.8, Lemmas 2.9 and A.7) mu is regular: dmu = e^{-V} 1_K dx with K bounded open convex and V smooth convex near the closure of K; phi is its moment map, nu = e^{-phi} dy, (phi^{ij}) = (Hess phi)^{-1}, L f = phi^{ij} d_ij f - (V_i o grad phi) d_i f, Einstein summation. C denotes absolute constants. All 18 numbered environments share one per-section counter (Theorem 1.1-1.2; Lemma 2.1-2.4, Theorem 2.5, Definition 2.6, Lemma 2.7, Proposition 2.8, Lemma 2.9; Lemma A.1-A.7) and are listed; the unnumbered definitions, the comparison display and the conjecture statement of Section 1 are listed because Lean declarations state them.
lemma_map.omitted: The paper has no Remark, Corollary, Fact, Claim or Conjecture environment. Omitted unnumbered material: the expository discussion after Theorem 1.2 (sharpness of the constant 2 for the isotropic exponential vector with M = Id, recorded in the note of T12, and the Bobkov-Chistyakov-Gotze second-order correlation consequence), Eldan's parameter kappa_n (defined inside the proof of Theorem 1.1, recorded in the note of T11), the Notation and AI Disclosure subsections, the footnote to Theorem 2.5, and the motivating remarks before Lemma 2.3 and before the proof of Theorem 1.2. Display (2.3) is now listed as E23. Numbered displays (1.2)-(2.22) are recorded with the statements they belong to: (1.2) in T12, (2.1) in LA3, (2.2)-(2.3) in the note of L22, (2.4)-(2.6) in L24, (2.7)-(2.17) in T25, (2.18) in D26, (2.19)-(2.20) in P28, (2.21)-(2.22) in T12 and LA2; the unnumbered covariance display preceding (2.21) on p. 14 is CZ14.

items.label: Isotropic random vector
items.statement: A random vector X in R^n (or its law mu) is isotropic if E X = 0 and Cov(X) = Id.
items.note: Lean states the three conditions (MemLp id 2, zero mean, centered covariance operator equal to the identity) coordinate-free on any finite-dimensional real inner-product space; in orthonormal coordinates this is the paper's definition (finite second moments are implicit in the paper).

items.label: Poincare constant C_P
items.statement: C_P(mu) is the infimum of C >= 0 such that Var_mu f(X) <= C E_mu |grad f(X)|^2 for every locally Lipschitz f: R^n -> R with E_mu |grad f|^2 <= 1; testing linear functions gives C_P(mu) >= 1 for isotropic mu.
items.note: Intrinsic.constant is the extended (ENNReal) optimum of the local-slope Poincare inequality for the intrinsic law on the affine support of a finite-dimensional law, with local slope in place of the a.e. gradient. Agreement with the paper's ambient gradient formulation is not a separate Lean theorem; for log-concave laws it equals the smooth-test optimum. The bound C_P >= 1 for isotropic laws is not stated in Lean.

items.label: Isoperimetric and KLS constants
items.statement: For mu with log-concave density rho, 1/psi_mu = inf over open A with smooth boundary and 0 < mu(A) < 1 of the integral of rho over the boundary of A divided by min{mu(A), 1 - mu(A)}; psi_n = sup psi_mu over isotropic log-concave probability measures mu on R^n.
items.note: Isoperimetry.constant is h_μ = 1/ψ_μ and inverseScale is ψ_μ, using outer Minkowski content over measurable sets on the affine support, with values ⊤ and 0 respectively in dimension zero. constant_eq_smoothConstant_intrinsic and inverseScale_eq_inv_smoothConstant_intrinsic (KLS/Geometry/Cheeger/Equality.lean) give the smooth relative-perimeter identification on the interior of the intrinsic support for a Borell density. The complete ambient smooth-boundary convention is not registered by this definition mapping, and ψ_n, the supremum over isotropic laws, has no declaration in the map.

items.locator: Section 1, unnumbered display (Cheeger; Buser, Ledoux; De Ponti and Mondino)
items.label: Cheeger and Buser comparison
items.statement: For every log-concave probability measure mu on R^n with a density, 1/4 <= psi_mu^2 / C_P(mu) <= pi.
items.note: Quoted, not proved in the paper. Lean proves both halves for every finite-dimensional log-concave law, including degenerate and zero-dimensional ones, as C_P <= 4 Psi^2 and Psi^2 <= pi C_P with Psi = Isoperimetry.inverseScale (Minkowski-content convention). Partial only because Psi is not identified in Lean with the smooth-boundary psi_mu. The proof of Theorem 1.1 uses only the Buser direction psi_n^2 <= C sup C_P(mu).

items.locator: Section 1, statement of the KLS conjecture (unnumbered)
items.label: KLS conjecture
items.statement: There is an absolute constant C > 0 such that every isotropic log-concave probability measure mu on R^n, in every dimension, satisfies C_P(mu) <= C; equivalently sup_{n >= 2} psi_n <= C.
items.note: Conjecture is a definition (a Prop), not a proof. It is the covariance-normalized form: one NNReal constant C with C_P^lit(mu) <= C ||Cov(mu)||_op for every n (including n = 0) and every log-concave law with finite second moment, singular affine supports included. For isotropic laws ||Cov|| = 1 gives the paper's form; the affine/isotropic equivalence is proved separately in Lean (KLS/LogConcave/Isotropic.lean), and the psi_n form needs ECMP. The paper does not prove the conjecture.

items.label: KLS constant O(log^{1/4} n)
items.statement: For every n >= 2, psi_n <= C log^{1/4} n for an absolute constant C > 0, where psi_n = sup psi_mu over isotropic log-concave probability measures on R^n; equivalently C_P(mu) <= C' sqrt(log n) for every isotropic log-concave mu on R^n.
items.note: Main theorem: it is the title and abstract claim and the only bound on the KLS constant psi_n; Theorem 1.2 is the new quadratic-form inequality from which it is derived. Proof (Section 1): for M = E<X,theta> X (x) X, Cauchy-Schwarz and Theorem 1.2 give ||M||_HS^4 <= 8 ||M||_HS^2, so Eldan's parameter kappa_n <= 2 sqrt 2; then the bound C_P(mu) <= C kappa_n sqrt(log n) is attributed to tracing Klartag 2023 (Theorem 1.3, Corollary 3.2 and the discussion after (3.13)) - the paper says it is not the final bound Klartag states and does not prove it - and finally psi_n^2 <= C sup C_P(mu). That traced bound is the unverified external step of this review. No Lean statement of psi_n or of this bound exists; the Lean Buser comparison covers only the last step. Unrefereed July 2026 preprint; the AI disclosure credits ChatGPT with the Appendix A regularity arguments.

items.label: Quadratic-form Poincare inequality
items.statement: If X ~ mu is an isotropic log-concave random vector in R^n and M is any symmetric n x n matrix, then Var(<MX,X>) <= 2 E|grad <MX,X>|^2 = 8 Tr(M^2) (equation (1.2)).
items.note: Proof (end of Section 2): reduce to the regular class (Lemma A.1) and invertible M (Lemma A.2); push mu forward by |M|^{1/2} to eta, whose Stein kernel |M|^{1/2} tau_mu |M|^{1/2} has E||tau_eta||_HS^2 <= 2 Tr(M^2) by Theorem 2.5 with B = |M|; apply Proposition 2.8 to F(z) = <sgn(M) z, z> - Tr M and Lemma 2.9 to each partial derivative. Sharpness of the constant 2 (isotropic exponential vector, M = Id) is asserted as an exercise. The paper calls it the KLS conjecture for quadratic forms. Local supports include the covariance step CZ14 (p. 14, ⇑) and the compact reduction to the smooth uniformly convex regular class by letwinCompactBound_of_regularClass. Exact compact counterpart (2026-10-16): letwinCompactBound : LetwinCompactBound is proved for every n > 0, every compactly supported isotropic log-concave law and every self-adjoint operator (singular and indefinite included) with the exact constant 8 and the standard-orthonormal-basis Hilbert-Schmidt normalization, and certified in source form (thm:letwin-compact-quadratic-bound, solutions/ThmLetwinCompactQuadraticBound.lean). It applies letwinCompactBound_of_regularClass to regularClass_letwinQuadraticBound, whose proof takes one weak C^{1,1} Stein witness of the actual regular-class moment potential with its exact-2 trace bound (weak form of Theorem 2.5, see T25), the Gaussian product coupling with the compact dual bound in place of the transported Stein kernel of Lemmas 2.7/2.9, the H^-1 inequality on the C2 convex Gaussian-smoothed law (see P28), the spectral sign/noise energy identity, noise removal and the singular extension (see LA2). Not formalized: the noncompact statement (every isotropic log-concave law, through the full Lemma A.1), the transported Stein kernel and trace identity (2.21), and the smooth source moment map. The item stays partial.

items.locator: Proof of Theorem 1.2, p. 14 (unnumbered display preceding (2.21))
items.label: Covariance of the transported vector
items.statement: For isotropic X ~ μ and symmetric M, reduced to invertible M by Lemma A.2, Z = |M|^{1/2} X and η = (|M|^{1/2})_# μ satisfy Cov_{Z∼η}(Z) = |M|.
items.note: Reviewed stronger covariance part (Stage 1, Astra v5, independently accepted 2026-10-10): every real symmetric M, singular and indefinite included, and dimension zero, without the invertible reduction. The companion identity of the same display, ⟨MX, X⟩ = ⟨sgn(M) Z, Z⟩, is not part of this item and is pending: no declaration states it (only the matrix factorization |M|^{1/2} sgn(M) |M|^{1/2} = M, in Analysis/Matrix/Sign.lean). Display (2.21) itself, the Stein-kernel Hilbert–Schmidt trace identity on p. 15, is not formalized; T12 stays partial.

items.label: Existence of moment maps
items.statement: If mu is a Borel measure on R^n with 0 < mu(R^n) < infinity, support not contained in a proper linear subspace and barycenter at the origin, then there is an essentially continuous convex phi: R^n -> R cup {+infinity} with (grad phi)_#(e^{-phi(y)} dy) = mu, unique up to translation phi_1(y) = phi_0(y - y_0).
items.note: Quoted from Cordero-Erausquin and Klartag, Theorem 2. Local restricted existence: for an isotropic bounded source law in positive dimension, exists_momentMap_of_isotropic_of_ae_norm_le constructs a finite convex Lipschitz potential u with integral exp(-u) = 1 and the actual gradient pushforward. This is not general finite-mass/unbounded existence or uniqueness up to translation, so the numbered source statement remains partial.

items.label: Regularity of the moment map
items.statement: Under the regularity assumptions of Lemma A.1, the moment map phi of Lemma 2.1 is finite and smooth on R^n with positive definite Hessian everywhere, grad phi: R^n -> K is a diffeomorphism, and the Monge-Ampere equation rho(grad phi) det Hess phi = e^{-phi}, i.e. log det Hess phi = -phi + V(grad phi), holds pointwise.
items.note: Quoted from Klartag 2014. For an isotropic regular law 1_K exp(−W) dx in positive dimension, K compact convex with nonempty interior, W globally smooth and W − (κ/2)‖·‖² convex with κ > 0, exists_regular_moment_potential produces a finite convex Lipschitz normalized potential u with the actual gradient pushforward, u ∈ C¹, a 16/κ-Lipschitz gradient, a.e. positive definite Hessian, log det Hess u = −u + W(∇u) a.e. and Hess u ≤ (16/κ) Id a.e. secondDifference_le_of_map_gradient gives u(x+h) + u(x−h) − 2u(x) ≤ (4/κ)‖h‖²; exists_regular_moment_weak_tensor supplies compact-local L² weak derivatives of the Hessian entries at the same source witness. These are the weak regularity inputs used by the compact constant-8 proof. Global smoothness, everywhere positive definiteness, a gradient diffeomorphism and the full pointwise source Lemma 2.2 are not supplied, so the source item remains partial.

items.label: Hessian of phi has mean Id
items.statement: Under the regularity assumptions of Lemma A.1 (isotropic dmu = e^{-V} 1_K dx, K bounded open convex, V smooth convex near the closure of K), moment map phi and nu = e^{-phi} dy, E_{Y~nu} Hess phi(Y) = Id.
items.note: For a given smooth convex normalized potential φ whose gradient pushforward is isotropic, integral_hessian_eq_inner_of_isotropic_map derives Hessian-entry integrability and mean Hessian Id by cutoff integration by parts; the mapped conditional bilinear identities are also proved. For the actual regular source of L22, exists_regular_moment_weak_inverse_mean_hessian (KLS/CEK/MomentRegularity/WeakHessian.lean) proves the same mean-Hessian identity for the constructed C¹ potential with Lipschitz gradient, retaining the common potential, weak tensor and first Monge–Ampere/inverse data. Thus this actual weak-source identity is proved, rather than an assumed input. The paper's smooth moment-map producer and full source class are not constructed, so the numbered source item remains partial.

items.label: Product rule for the diffusion generator
items.statement: For the generator L = Σ_ij A_ij ∂_ij − Σ_i b_i ∂_i (in the source, A = (∇²φ)⁻¹ on the moment-map side), L(fg) = f Lg + g Lf + 2 Σ_ij A_ij ∂_i f ∂_j g.
items.note: The Leibniz rule is formalized for an arbitrary real coefficient field A, symmetric at each point without a positivity premise, arbitrary drift b and C² functions in the standard orthonormal basis. hessianInverseOperator_mul also specializes it to A = (Hess φ)⁻¹ and b = ∇V ∘ ∇φ for a given potential. Actual-source weak Monge–Ampere and trace estimates are available under L24 and T25. The smooth moment map of Lemma 2.2 for the full source class is not constructed; this generic product rule does not assert that missing regularity or the full smooth Theorem 2.5.

items.label: Twice-differentiated Monge-Ampere equation
items.statement: Under the regularity assumptions, for all i, j: L(d_ij phi) + d_ij phi = (Hess phi Hess V(grad phi) Hess phi)_ij + phi^{ac} phi^{bd} d_abi phi d_cdj phi, and both matrices on the right are positive semidefinite at every point.
items.note: For a given smooth potential φ with positive definite Hessian satisfying the zero-order Monge–Ampere equation, the mapped declarations prove Jacobi differentiation (2.4), the inverse-Hessian derivative (2.5), the second evolution identity (2.6), and positivity of its curvature and Gram terms under the stated local smoothness and convexity of V. For the actual regular source of L22, exists_regular_moment_weak_first_derivative, exists_regular_moment_weak_inverse and exists_regular_moment_weak_hessian_evolution (KLS/CEK/MomentRegularity/WeakHessian.lean) prove weak (2.4), weak (2.5) and weighted weak (2.6) at one constructed C¹ potential with Lipschitz gradient. They retain the same weak tensor, compact-local L² derivative bounds and compact-local essential inverse bounds; no C² potential, given inverse formula or global inverse bound is added. The generic rough-curl, Piola and weighted-flux identities supply the weak calculus. Weak trace contraction (2.8)/(2.10) and matrix positivity/comparison are also proved and consumed by the actual-source T25 trace bound. The source item remains partial because the full smooth moment map of Lemma 2.2 and the corresponding unrestricted smooth-source Lemma 2.4 are not constructed.

items.label: Key moment-map Hessian bound
items.statement: Under the regularity assumptions of Lemma A.1 (isotropic dmu = e^{-V} 1_K dx, K bounded open convex, V smooth convex near the closure of K), moment map phi and nu = e^{-phi} dy, every symmetric n x n matrix B satisfies E_{Y~nu} Tr(B Hess phi(Y) B Hess phi(Y)) <= 2 Tr(B^2).
items.note: Partial counterpart: the paper's Theorem 2.5 for the smooth moment map is not formalized; full smooth Lemma 2.2 regularity remains outside the registered scope. For a given smooth potential with positive-definite Hessian and the zero-order Monge-Ampere relation, the pointwise trace evolution (2.8)-(2.10), inverse-Hessian integration by parts and matrix positivity/comparison identities are proved with the stated local regularity of V. Equation (2.12) has a finite symmetric-tensor counterpart for arbitrary real weights. The generic integral_trace_quadratic_le_two_mul_trace_sq retains mean-Hessian and half-energy inputs as hypotheses. For the actual weak C^{1,1} moment witness of the regular source class, n > 0, exists_regular_moment_weak_stein_coupling produces an integrable trace quadratic with integral at most 2 tr(B^2) for every real symmetric B, including singular and indefinite B. Its source hypotheses produce the weak third derivatives, weak Hessian evolution, bounded H1 testing, cutoffs, conservativity and weak Brascamp-Lieb inputs at one witness; these are not extra target assumptions. The AE Jordan extension passes the PSD estimate to all symmetric B. This weak actual-source estimate is consumed by the compact constant-8 endpoint (T12), whose Gaussian product coupling and H^-1 step are formalized with their own scopes. It is a supporting weak counterpart, not the unrestricted smooth source theorem. The complete supporting declarations and their retained hypotheses are listed below.

items.label: Stein kernel
items.statement: For a centered random vector W ~ lambda in R^n, a measurable matrix-valued tau_lambda with entries locally integrable under lambda (up to lambda-a.e. equality) is a Stein kernel if E[W_i f(W)] = E[sum_j tau_lambda(W)_ij d_j f(W)] for every f in C_c^infinity(R^n) and every i (equation (2.18)); it is symmetric if tau_lambda(u) is symmetric for lambda-a.e. u.
items.note: Formalized as the compact-test coordinate Stein predicate on ℝⁿ: a centered finite-first-moment law, measurable locally integrable matrix entries and the identity on C_c^∞ tests, with separate a.e.-symmetry and Hilbert–Schmidt norm definitions. These declarations define the kernel contract; they do not construct the source law's moment-map kernel.

items.label: Moment map gives Stein kernel
items.statement: Under the regularity assumptions, tau_mu(x) = Hess phi((grad phi)^{-1}(x)) is a symmetric Stein kernel for mu that is positive definite mu-a.e., and tau_mu(X) = Hess phi(Y) in the coupling Y ~ nu, X = grad phi(Y).
items.note: Quoted from Fathi 2019. For a given smooth convex normalized potential φ with isotropic gradient pushforward and injective ∇φ, the mapped construction gives a target Stein kernel via a measurable left inverse, symmetric PSD integrable entries, mean Id and τ(∇φ(y)) = Hess φ(y); the Gaussian instance is τ = Id. This construction does not supply the arbitrary-law moment map, strict positive definiteness or the HS-L² bound of the full source route. At the actual weak regular-source witness, exists_regular_moment_weak_stein_coupling instead proves the source identity ∫ ∂_i u f(∇u) dν = ∫ Σ_j (Hess u)_ij ∂_j f(∇u) dν for C¹ bounded globally Lipschitz f, with u ∈ C¹ globally Lipschitz and ∇u Lipschitz. The compact constant-8 endpoint uses that latent identity and a Gaussian product coupling; it does not construct τ = Hess u ∘ (∇u)⁻¹ on the target law. The source Lemma 2.7 therefore remains partial.

items.label: H^{-1} variance inequality
items.statement: If W ~ lambda is log-concave and f: R^n -> R is locally Lipschitz with f, d_i f in L^2(lambda) and E d_i f(W) = 0 for every i, then Var f(W) <= sum_i ||d_i f||_{H^{-1}(lambda)}^2, where ||g||_{H^{-1}(lambda)} = sup E[g h] over locally Lipschitz h in L^2(lambda) with E|grad h|^2 <= 1 (equation (2.19)).
items.note: Quoted from Barthe–Klartag; λ need not be isotropic. The mapped variance_le_sum_of_partial_dual_bounds proves the H⁻¹ variance bound for ν = e^{−W} dm with W convex and C². gaussian_smoothed_quadratic_variance_le_latent_energy uses this proved form on the actual Gaussian-smoothed law in the compact constant-8 argument. The source statement for a general log-concave law remains outside this C² scope.

items.label: Stein kernel bounds H^{-1} norm
items.statement: If W ~ lambda is centered, log-concave, full-dimensional with finite second moments and tau_lambda is a symmetric Stein kernel with E||tau_lambda(W)||_HS^2 < infinity, then ||x -> <x,v>||_{H^{-1}(lambda)}^2 <= E|tau_lambda(W) v|^2 for every v in R^n.
items.note: The kernel-based dual estimate is formalized for a full-dimensional log-concave law with an a.e. symmetric Stein kernel τ and |τ|_HS ∈ L²: the centered linear function has finite H⁻¹ norm and its squared norm is at most ∫‖τ(x)v‖² dμ, using the full locally Lipschitz unit-energy test class; isotropy is not required. A separate generic bound compact_linear_pairing_sq_le_of_source_identity derives compact dual control from a latent source identity, a measurable pushforward and an L² latent field. For the compact endpoint, gaussian_product_compact_dual_bound supplies that control through the Gaussian product coupling. Neither the generic kernel-based estimate nor this latent route constructs the source law's moment-map target kernel; their hypotheses and the item's recorded partial relation are retained.

items.label: Reduction to regular measures
items.statement: To prove Theorem 1.2 it suffices to treat isotropic mu = e^{-V} 1_K dx with K bounded open convex and V smooth convex on a neighbourhood of the closure of K; every isotropic log-concave mu is the limit of such isotropic mu_eps in the sense that E_{mu_eps} p -> E_mu p for every polynomial p of degree at most four.
items.note: The passage of the quadratic bound through degree-at-most-four moment convergence is formalized. The compact source reduction is also formalized: if every positive-dimensional isotropic law 1_K exp(-W) dx, with K compact convex with nonempty interior and W globally smooth and uniformly kappa-convex for kappa > 0, satisfies LetwinQuadraticBound, then LetwinCompactBound holds. The proof uses Gaussian smoothing, ball conditioning and whitening with converging moments. The regular-class bound is an explicit retained premise; approximation of every noncompact isotropic log-concave law in the full source statement is not supplied by this compact reduction. Partial source coverage; not Theorem 1.2. (2026-10-16) For compact laws the retained regular-class premise is now discharged by regularClass_letwinQuadraticBound, giving letwinCompactBound (see T12); the noncompact approximation is still not formalized, so the entry stays partial.

items.label: Reduction to invertible M
items.statement: It suffices to prove (2.22), Var_mu(<MX,X>) <= 8 Tr(M^2), for invertible symmetric M; the general case follows from M + eps P_0 with P_0 the projection onto ker M, using fourth moments.
items.note: Formalized (⇑ stronger form, different route, 2026-10-16): for every probability law on EuclideanSpace R (Fin n), every n including zero, with finite fourth moment and every real C, a bound Var(sum B_ij x_i x_j) <= C tr(B^2) for all symmetric invertible B extends to all symmetric B (symmetric_matrix_variance_bound_of_isUnit). No isotropy or log-concavity is needed. The proof approximates B by B - r_k Id with 0 < r_k < 1/(k+1) outside the finite real spectrum (exists_symmetric_isUnit_matrix_sequence) and passes to the limit with the fourth-moment variance continuity (tendsto_variance_quadratic_matrix_forms); the source perturbation M + eps P_0 is not used. The reduction alone does not establish the bound; the regular-class application supplies its own fourth moment and invertible bound.

items.label: Integration by parts under nu
items.statement: Under the regularity assumptions, for fixed i and smooth f, g with (d_i f) g, f d_i g, f g d_i phi and f g in L^1(nu): E_nu[(d_i f) g] = E_nu[f (d_i phi g - d_i g)] (equation (2.1)).
items.note: Proof: cutoff chi_R and dominated convergence. Lemma A.3 formalized as weighted directional integration by parts for any fixed direction with the four source L¹ premises (⇑ reviewed different route: Mathlib directional IBP, no moment-map regularity).

items.label: Cutoffs with small generator
items.statement: Under the regularity assumptions there are chi_R in C_c^infinity(R^n), for all large R, with 0 <= chi_R <= 1, chi_R increasing to 1 and ||L chi_R||_{L^1(nu)} = O(1/R).
items.note: For a given smooth convex normalized φ satisfying the L22 moment-map properties, exists_scaled_cutoffs_hessianInverseOperator constructs smooth compactly supported height cutoffs for every real R ≥ 1, with values in [0,1], monotonicity, limit 1 and ‖Lχ_R‖_{L¹(ν)} ≤ C/R. The minimum, compact sublevels, bounded self-generator and energy estimate are derived; exists_cutoffs_hessianInverseOperator gives the natural-index form. The reviewed stronger relation refers to this supplied smooth-potential theorem's scale and ambient scope. Applying that smooth theorem to the paper's law still requires the unconstructed smooth moment-map producer. The actual regular-source weak counterpart is available separately: exists_scaled_weak_inverse_hessian_cutoffs and exists_weak_inverse_hessian_cutoffs (Analysis/BakryEmery/IntegrationByParts/InverseHessian/WeakCutoff.lean) give C¹ cutoffs with Lipschitz gradient, the literal integrable generator and the same C/R defect from the stated weak Monge–Ampere data. exists_regular_moment_weak_cutoffs applies them at the common regular-law witness. These weak cutoffs support the compact proof but are not C^∞ cutoffs.

items.label: Mean zero of L f
items.statement: If f in C^infinity(R^n) cap L^infinity(nu) and L f + c f >= 0 for some c > 0, then L f in L^1(nu) and E_nu L f = 0.
items.note: The smooth operator theorem integrable_and_integral_hessianInverseOperator_eq_zero_of_cutoffs retains a cutoff sequence as a premise, with the specified support, [0,1] bounds, limit 1, integrable generators and vanishing L¹ defect. It proves conservativity for smooth bounded f with Lf + cf ≥ 0, c > 0; the generic core is integrable_and_integral_eq_zero_of_cutoff_defect. LA4 supplies such cutoffs for a given source-class smooth potential, but their general smooth composition is not a mapped theorem; the uniform-interval client checks one concrete potential. For the actual weak regular-source witness, bounded weak testing and C¹ cutoffs are constructed, and exists_regular_moment_weak_stein_coupling carries ∫g dν = 0 for the weak trace density of every PSD B without assuming global L¹ integrability of g as an input. That actual consumption is proved; the item retains the separate smooth theorem's cutoff premise and partial source scope.

items.label: Brascamp-Lieb for nu
items.statement: Under the regularity assumptions every bounded smooth f: R^n -> R satisfies Var_nu f <= E_nu[phi^{ab} d_a f d_b f], the right side possibly infinite.
items.note: The scalar Brascamp–Lieb inequality is proved for a given potential with everywhere positive definite Hessian and C¹ tests: finite energy for a C² potential and possibly infinite energy for a smooth potential. scalar_brascamp_lieb_weak_finite_energy also proves the weak counterpart for a normalized C¹ globally Lipschitz potential with Lipschitz gradient and a.e. positive definite Hessian, and globally bounded weak tests with compact-local L² derivatives and integrable inverse-Hessian energy. Its supports include weighted-diffusion range density, the C¹,¹ Bochner identity, coercivity and weak integration by parts. The weak form is consumed by the actual regular-source trace argument. The full source statement for the law's smooth moment map, including its smooth producer and possibly infinite energy, is not asserted by that weak finite-energy counterpart.

items.label: Extended Stein identity
items.statement: If W ~ lambda is centered, full-dimensional, log-concave with finite second moments and tau_lambda is a symmetric Stein kernel with E||tau_lambda(W)||_HS^2 < infinity, then for every v the identity E[<W,v> f(W)] = E<tau_lambda(W) v, grad f(W)> holds for every locally Lipschitz f with f, grad f in L^2(lambda), whence |E[<W,v> f(W)]| <= (E|tau_lambda(W) v|^2)^{1/2} (E|grad f(W)|^2)^{1/2}.
items.note: The compact-test Stein identity extends to locally Lipschitz f with f, ∇f ∈ L²(μ) for μ absolutely continuous with respect to volume and with finite second moment, using compact smooth approximation in the graph norm and the Cauchy–Schwarz bound. The log-concave full-dimensional adapter derives absolute continuity and the second moment. The declarations retain their supplied Stein-kernel hypotheses; they do not construct the target kernel of L27.

papers.title: Presenting a proof of the Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits conjecture
papers.locator: Theorem 1.1 (through Theorems 3.1 and 4.1 and Proposition 7.1); first dependencies Lemmas 2.1, 2.2, 3.4, 3.6, Corollaries 3.5, 3.7 and conditional Lemma 4.2
papers.result: Claims C_P(μ) ≤ C for every isotropic log-concave μ in every dimension (the KLS conjecture with a universal constant): Taylor coefficients of tilt averages bounded by cumulant bounds along Eldan localization give the criterion of Theorem 3.1. Not peer reviewed.
papers.remaining: Theorem 1.1 is certified in the source form (thm:bkl-poincare) through the accepted cutoff route, with separately certified Theorems 3.1 and 4.1 and Proposition 7.1. Theorem 3.1 uses closed-generator-domain iterates and an approximate first eigenfunction; its operator-form supporting estimates, the regular-law adapter and the required exponential moments are proved. Proposition 7.1 includes the complete assembly (107), retaining the paper's universal cumulant hypothesis, which Theorem 4.1 supplies in the final composition. The finite-horizon cutoff (95) (lem:bkl-cutoff-energy) and the all-order Theorem 4.1 (thm:bkl-cumulant-bound, K = 153) are closed with the proved compact Letwin constant-8 theorem and compact-to-general approximation. The deterministic posterior calculus, covariance inverse/root, canonical standardization, generator identities, cutoff process, Lyapunov estimates and energy induction are proved in their recorded scopes. Remaining source boundaries are the smooth temperate inverse in Lemma 2.1, existence of the exact first eigenfunction (19), exact constant-8 Lemma 4.2 for every isotropic law, the uncut Eldan strong solution/uniqueness/non-explosion and literal stochastic identities (68)–(73), Lemmas 4.3, 5.1 and 5.2 along that uncut process, and the infinite-horizon source (95). Letwin's noncompact theorem is also separate. The paper is covered in the exact main-theorem sense, not as a formalization of every intermediate source statement.

lemma_map.standing_assumptions: Probability measures on Rⁿ, n ≥ 1. Log-concave means a log-concave density; isotropic means mean 0 and covariance Id. C_P(μ) is the least constant in Var f ≤ C∫|∇f|² for locally Lipschitz f ∈ L²(μ). A measure is regular if dμ = e^{−V}dx with a Id ≤ ∇²V ≤ b Id (0 < a ≤ b) and every derivative of V of polynomial growth; 𝒜 is the algebra of smooth functions all of whose derivatives grow polynomially and 𝒜₀ its mean-zero part; L = Δ − ⟨∇V, ∇⟩ and λ₁ = 1/C_P. Tensors carry the Hilbert–Schmidt norm |·|; S_q averages over the permutations of the first q indices. μ_z, F_f and T_d are defined in (26)–(28).
