items.label: Dimension-free Poincaré constant
items.statement: There is a universal C such that every isotropic log-concave probability measure μ on Rⁿ (every n ≥ 1) has C_P(μ) ≤ C; equivalently ‖Cov μ‖_op ≤ C_P(μ) ≤ C‖Cov μ‖_op for every log-concave μ (6).
items.note: Main theorem (title and abstract). Proof (p. 30): Theorem 4.1 with b = K^d (d!)² and Proposition 7.1 give |T_d f|² ≤ (2K)^d‖f‖² for d ≥ 2, d = 1 by isotropy, then Theorem 3.1 with R = √(2K) after the regular approximation of Section 2. Certified in the source form (2026-10-17, stage 4; thm:bkl-poincare, solutions/ThmBklPoincare.lean): one C > 0, chosen before every n ≥ 1 and every isotropic log-concave law on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), with Intrinsic.constant μ ≤ C and no compactness, regularity or moment premise; bound is IsotropicBound C on every finite-dimensional inner product space. Producer: KLS.BKL.Localization.theorem11 (KLS/BKL/Poincare.lean) applies localSlope_le_of_cumulantBound_all (the p. 30 reduction for isotropic regular laws with the Section 2 regular approximation and weak-limit passage; C_{3.1} fixed before K) to theorem41 letwinCompactBound, so C = 2·C_{3.1}·K. Relation alternative, as for T41: the same statement through the owner-selected cutoff localization route and the compact-to-general passage instead of the uncut Eldan process (whose identities (68)–(73) are not formalized), with the harmless extension of bound to every finite-dimensional inner product space; same is kept for statements proved along the source route. The right-hand inequality of (6) is the project target: FunctionalInequalities.KLS.kls : KLS.Conjecture (KLS/Target.lean, statement unchanged) is KLS.BKL.Localization.conjecture, through conjecture_of_cumulantBound and the affine/isotropic reduction with the same constant; the left inequality of (6) is lambdaMax_le_constant (linear tests). The conditional localSlope_le_of_cumulantBound_all, conjecture_of_cumulantBound and conjecture_of_letwinCompact are unchanged. The paper is covered in the exact main-theorem sense; intermediate statements keep their recorded scopes.

items.label: Centered inverse of the generator
items.statement: For regular μ (a Id ≤ ∇²V ≤ b Id, every derivative of V of polynomial growth) and g ∈ 𝒜₀ (smooth, polynomial growth, mean zero) there is a unique u ∈ 𝒜₀ with -Lu = g; ‖u‖ ≤ λ⁻¹‖g‖ and ∫|∇u|² = ∫gu ≤ λ⁻¹‖g‖² (20); the bounds (23)–(24) for ∇₀u; the componentwise tensor version.
items.note: Restricted operator-domain counterpart: in the heat model ν = m.tilted(−U), U ∈ C², log-concave with full-dimensional support, and any C ≥ C_P(ν), every centered g ∈ L²(ν) has exactly one centered u in the domain of the closed generator A = T̄†T̄ = −ℒ with Au = g, ‖u‖ ≤ C‖g‖, ‖T̄u‖² = ⟨g, u⟩ ≤ C‖g‖² and ‖∇₀u‖ ≤ √C‖g‖ (generic part: Analysis/Semigroup/Generated/Inverse.lean). C = C_P recovers λ⁻¹ in positive dimension. The existence of a smooth temperate inverse for every g ∈ 𝒜₀ (preservation of 𝒜₀) is not proved; the tensor version is proved only as the componentwise operator-domain counterpart below, not as a smooth 𝒜₀-preserving tensor inverse. On 𝒜 the energy bound corresponding to (20) holds: ∫‖∇h‖² ≤ C ∫‖ℒh‖² for temperate tensor fields, with the Poincaré inequality on 𝒜 (integral_sq_sub_integral_le_of_hasTemperateGrowth). Bridge to the class 𝒜 (2026-10-07): for U of temperate growth with all exponential moments, the L² class of every f of temperate growth lies in D(T̄) with T̄[f] = [∇f] and in D(A) with A[f] = [−ℒf]; hence a centered temperate solution of −ℒu = g is the centered operator-domain inverse of [g]. The existence of a temperate solution for g ∈ 𝒜₀ is not proved. Componentwise tensor lift (2026-10-07): for G-valued centered g ∈ L²(ν; G) and an orthonormal basis b of G, exactly one family of centered u_k in the generator domain with A u_k = ⟨b_k, g⟩, and Σ_k‖u_k‖² ≤ C²‖g‖² (existsUnique_centered_adjointComp_eq_components; the Parseval identity for the components is FunctionalInequalities.L2.sum_norm_sq_compLp_innerSL). For a regular potential (12) the scalar and componentwise inverses hold with C = 1/a (RegularPotential.existsUnique_centered_adjointComp_eq, RegularPotential.existsUnique_centered_adjointComp_eq_components). The existence of smooth (temperate) representatives of the inverse on 𝒜 remains open.

items.label: Partial symmetrization of tensors
items.statement: Let d ≥ 1 and T a tensor with at least 3d indices, invariant under the permutations of its first d indices and of its next 2d indices. Then |T| ≤ 4^d |S_{2d} T| (Hilbert–Schmidt norms; S_q averages over the permutations of the first q indices).
items.note: Source form on Coord n k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k → Fin n) (Hilbert–Schmidt norm), every n including 0, every k ≥ 3d, trailing indices fixed; d = 0 is included (the source assumes d ≥ 1, a hypothesis its proof never uses). The proof is the source one: identity (25) for every family indexed by d-subsets (sum_norm_sq_sum_subset_eq), the factor C(2d, d) (norm_le_choose_mul_norm_blockAverage, for every orthogonal permutation representation) and C(2d, d) ≤ 4^d.

items.label: Taylor-coefficient criterion
items.statement: Let μ be a centered regular log-concave measure with Cov μ ≤ Id and R ≥ 1 with |T_d f| ≤ R^d‖f‖_{L²(μ)} for all f ∈ L²(μ) and d ≥ 1 (29). Then C_P(μ) ≤ C R².
items.note: Formalized in the source form and certified (thm:bkl-taylor-criterion, solutions/ThmBklTaylorCriterion.lean): ∃ K, for every regular potential V on ℝⁿ (RegularPotential, BKL (12)) with centered law, Cov ≤ Id, R ≥ 1 and (29) in the Hilbert–Schmidt norm of the standard basis, C_P ≤ K R². Proved by the operator route (on the closed-generator domain): iterates in D(A) and an approximate first eigenfunction instead of (19); the library constant K = 100 (9·2^20)² differs from the source's. Hypotheses discharged in dimension zero and, for the standard Gaussian on ℝ¹ with R = 8, in dimension one (KLS/BKL/GaussianTaylor.lean).

items.label: Near-symmetric gradient
items.statement: With χ_i = ‖∇²h_i − α_{i+1}∇h_{i+1}‖², there is a tensor field T̃ symmetric in its first two indices with ‖∇₀h_{i+1} − T̃‖ ≤ √(χ_i/λ₁).
items.note: Partial counterpart (generalized implication for a supplied pair): for temperate tensor fields g, h with −ℒh = α∇₀g (30) under μ = m.tilted(−V) (V temperate, all exponential moments, μ a probability measure), any λ > 0 with λ ≤ α² when α ≠ 0 (the source's (32) with λ = λ₁, which needs Lemma 2.1 on 𝒜), there is T symmetric in its first two indices (T = α⁻¹∇₀(∇g), or 0 when α = 0) with ‖∇₀h − T‖²₂ ≤ χ/λ — the square of (38) — and ‖∇₀h − T‖² integrable; the normalization (33) is not needed. The source iterates on 𝒜 are not constructed (the operator route below constructs them in D(A)). In the heat model ν = m.tilted(−U) (U temperate, all exponential moments, C ≥ C_P(ν), so λ₁ ≥ 1/C) the premise is discharged: for a temperate pair satisfying (30) and (33) with ∇h ≠ 0, 1 ≤ Cα² (the source's (32) when C = C_P), and Lemma 3.2 holds with the bound Cχ (λ = 1/C ≤ λ₁ for C > 0, equality for C = C_P) and no further premise (exists_symm_integral_norm_sq_sub_le_mul). Operator route (on the closed-generator domain): for the iterates (30)–(31) built componentwise in the operator domain D(A) of the heat-model generator from any centered h₁ ∈ D(A), with λ = 1/C for any C ≥ C_P(ν) (λ = λ₁ when C = C_P): Lemma 3.2 with bound C χ_i.

items.label: Energy drops
items.note: Partial counterpart for supplied iterates: under the normalization (33) alone, v_i − v_{i+1} = ‖∫∇h_i‖² for a pair, and v_0 = v_N + Σ_{k<N}‖∫∇h_k‖² along any sequence of temperate tensor fields (values in G k), for μ = m.tilted(−V) a probability measure with all exponential moments. The value v_1 = λ₁ of the source needs the first eigenfunction, which is not constructed (the operator route below uses v₁ ∈ [λ, 1.1λ] for an approximate eigenfunction). Operator route (on the closed-generator domain): for the iterates (30)–(31) built componentwise in the operator domain D(A) of the heat-model generator from any centered h₁ ∈ D(A), with λ = 1/C for any C ≥ C_P(ν) (λ = λ₁ when C = C_P): (35) and (36), with v₁ in place of λ₁.

items.label: Approximate symmetry of iterates
items.statement: For 2 ≤ q ≤ i and 0 < α_j² ≤ 2λ₁ (i − q + 2 ≤ j ≤ i): ‖∇₀h_i − S_q∇₀h_i‖² ≤ (C^q/λ₁) Σ_{j=i−q+1}^{i−1} χ_j.
items.note: Case q = 2 only, for a supplied pair satisfying (30) (and (33) in the heat-model form): ‖∇₀h − S₂∇₀h‖²₂ ≤ χ/λ under λ ≤ α², and ≤ Pχ in the heat model with P ≥ C_P (λ = 1/P for P > 0) — the source bound with coefficient 1 in place of its universal C_src² ≥ 1 — since S₂ is the nearest tensor symmetric in the first two indices (norm_sub_symmetrizeFirstTwo_le). On 𝒜 (supplied pairs) the cases q ≥ 3 are not formalized; the operator route below proves every q. Operator route (on the closed-generator domain): for the iterates (30)–(31) built componentwise in the operator domain D(A) of the heat-model generator from any centered h₁ ∈ D(A), with λ = 1/C for any C ≥ C_P(ν) (λ = λ₁ when C = C_P): Lemma 3.3 for every 2 ≤ q ≤ i under 0 < α_j² ≤ β/C (the source has 2λ₁), with the constant 4q⁴max(1,β)^q C; (42), (43) and (44) are proved on the way.

items.label: Bochner step
items.statement: ‖Lh_i‖² ≥ ‖Lh_{i+1}‖² + χ_i + a v_i (the only substantial use of log-concavity).
items.note: Partial counterpart (generalized implication for supplied iterates; the source sequence on the paper class is not constructed): for every pair g = h_i, h = h_{i+1} of temperate tensor fields satisfying the Poisson relation (30) −ℒh = α∇₀g and the normalization (33), with ∇²V ≥ a, the orthogonality ⟨∇²g, ∇h⟩ = α‖∇h‖², (39), (46), (47) and (45) are derived from (15)/(16) (no division by α, so α = 0 is included); derivative energies use the coordinate gradient gradCoord (PiLp 2, Hilbert–Schmidt over the derivative and all trailing indices, derivative index first). The construction of the source iterates (Lemma 2.1 on 𝒜, the first eigenfunction, the normalization (31)) is not addressed. Operator route (on the closed-generator domain): for the iterates (30)–(31) built componentwise in the operator domain D(A) of the heat-model generator from any centered h₁ ∈ D(A), with λ = 1/C for any C ≥ C_P(ν) (λ = λ₁ when C = C_P): Lemma 3.4 and (47) (curvature a of ∇²U, any real a).

items.label: Vanishing of v_N
items.statement: v_N → 0 as N → ∞ (summation of Lemma 3.4 when a > 0).
items.note: Partial counterpart (generalized implication for supplied iterates): for nonnegative sequences satisfying (45) with a > 0, Σ v_i < ∞, Σ χ_i < ∞ and v_N → 0; and for every sequence of temperate tensor iterates h_k (values in G k, linked by linear isometries PiLp 2 (Fin n → G k) ≃ G (k+1)) satisfying (30) and (33), the energies ‖∇h_k‖² are summable and tend to 0. The existence of the source iterates on 𝒜 is not addressed (the operator route below constructs them in D(A)). Operator route (on the closed-generator domain): for the iterates (30)–(31) built componentwise in the operator domain D(A) of the heat-model generator from any centered h₁ ∈ D(A), with λ = 1/C for any C ≥ C_P(ν) (λ = λ₁ when C = C_P): Corollary 3.5 and Σχ_i ≤ ‖Lh₁‖².

items.label: Taylor tensors of the generator
items.statement: For u ∈ 𝒜 (scalar or tensor-valued): T_1(−Lu) = ∫∇u dμ (49) and T_{d+1}(−Lu) = S_{d+1} T_d(∇u) for d ≥ 1 (50).
items.note: Formalized in a reviewed stronger form (Codex review 3, 2026-10-07): for scalar and tensor-valued u ∈ 𝒜 (Mathlib HasTemperateGrowth; values in any finite-dimensional real normed space F, whose indices trail and are not symmetrized), with ℒu = Δu − Du(∇V) componentwise, the derivative index of T_d(Du) after its d Taylor indices (uncurryRight) and S_{d+1} on these d + 1 arguments, every d ≥ 0, for μ = m.tilted(−V) with V ∈ C¹, ∇V of polynomial growth and all exponential moments. The source assumes μ regular (a Id ≤ ∇²V ≤ b Id, every derivative of V polynomially bounded), which implies these hypotheses; that implication is reviewed, not a Lean adapter. A zero measure (e^{−V} not integrable) makes the identities trivial. The scalar case is also proved for compactly supported C² u. The symmetry of ∇ⁿF needed for S_{d+1} is proved for C^∞ maps (iteratedFDeriv_comp_perm_of_contDiff); Mathlib states it only for analytic maps. Also for every F in the generator domain D(A) of the heat model ν = m.tilted(−U), U ∈ C¹, all exponential moments (taylorTensor_adjointComp_eq, operator route of 2026-10-07).

items.label: Taylor tensors of the iterates
items.note: Formalized in a reviewed stronger form: for every tensor field h of temperate growth and every g, α with −ℒh = α∇₀g (the relation (30) defining h_{i+1} from h_i, with ∇₀u = Du − ∫Du, centeredFDeriv), every d ≥ 1, the symmetrization S_{d+1} acting on the first d + 1 indices and the trailing indices untouched. The existence and normalization (31) of the source iterates on 𝒜 (Lemma 2.1 on 𝒜) remain unproved there; the operator route below proves Corollary 3.7 for the iterates in D(A). Operator route (on the closed-generator domain): for the iterates (30)–(31) built componentwise in the operator domain D(A) of the heat-model generator from any centered h₁ ∈ D(A), with λ = 1/C for any C ≥ C_P(ν) (λ = λ₁ when C = C_P): Corollary 3.7 for d ≥ 1, as coefficient arrays.

items.label: Taylor-tensor recursion
items.statement: For d ≥ 1 and 2d ≤ i ≤ N: |T_d(∇₀h_i)|² ≤ (Cλ₁)^d |T_{2d}(∇₀h_{i−d})|² + (C^d R^{2d}/λ₁) Σ_{j=i−2d+1}^{i−1} χ_j.
items.note: Operator route (on the closed-generator domain): for the iterates (30)–(31) built componentwise in the operator domain D(A) of the heat-model generator from any centered h₁ ∈ D(A), with λ = 1/C for any C ≥ C_P(ν) (λ = λ₁ when C = C_P): Lemma 3.8 under (29) and α_j² ≤ β/C, with the explicit constant 2^20 max(1,β)² in place of the source's universal C.

items.label: Summation bound
items.statement: Σ_{i ≤ N} p_i ≤ λ₁² + 2λ₁ Σ_{i<N} |T_1(∇₀h_i)|².
items.note: Step (61) for a supplied pair: if −ℒh = α∇₀g (30) with h temperate under μ = m.tilted(−V) (V temperate, all exponential moments), then ∫Dh = αT_1(∇₀g) and ‖∫∇h‖² = α²Σ_i‖T_1(∇₀g)(e_i)‖² (Hilbert–Schmidt), i.e. p_{i+1} = α²|T_1(∇₀h_i)|² when combined with (35) and (33). The first step for a supplied eigenfunction is also proved: if ℒf = −λf, ∫f = 0 and ∫⟨e, x − b⟩² ≤ K|e|² (K ≥ 0 is assumed for convenience; it is redundant), then |∫∇f|² ≤ λ²K‖f‖² (p_1 ≤ λ₁² for ‖f‖ = 1, Cov ≤ Id); audited on the Gaussian with f = ⟨c, ·⟩, which attains equality (the audit proves the inequality; mean zero and covariance ≤ 1/ρ derived from (15) and the Poincaré inequality on 𝒜). On 𝒜 the existence of the first eigenfunction, the use of (54) and the summation (60) are not formalized; the operator route below proves (60) in the route form and its use (via (54) with α² ≤ 3λ) in the final argument of Theorem 3.1. Operator route (on the closed-generator domain): for the iterates (30)–(31) built componentwise in the operator domain D(A) of the heat-model generator from any centered h₁ ∈ D(A), with λ = 1/C for any C ≥ C_P(ν) (λ = λ₁ when C = C_P): Lemma 3.9 in the form Σ_{k<N} p_k ≤ ‖Lh₁‖² + (β/C) Σ |T₁(∇₀h_k)|² under Cov ≤ Id (for an exact eigenfunction ‖Lh₁‖² = λ₁², β = 2 is the source).

items.label: Analytic continuation
items.statement: The Taylor bound (29) continues F_f analytically to a complex ball of radius 1/R; no complex-analytic proof of Theorem 3.1 is known.
items.note: Not on the proof path.

items.label: Cumulant bounds
items.statement: There is a universal K ≥ 1 such that every isotropic log-concave μ on Rⁿ and m ≥ 2 satisfy R^μ_m ≤ K^{m−1}((m−1)!)² Id, where ⟨R_m u, u⟩ = |κ_m(u, ·, …, ·)|² and κ_m = ∇^mΛ_μ(0).
items.note: Certified in the source form (thm:bkl-cumulant-bound, solutions/ThmBklCumulantBound.lean): one universal K ≥ 1, with witness 153, bounds every order m = d + 1 ≥ 2, every dimension including zero and every isotropic log-concave law by Σ_J κ_m(u,e_J)² ≤ K^{m−1}((m−1)!)²‖u‖². There is no extra compactness, Letwin, moment, energy or induction premise. The proof uses the certified finite-horizon cutoff (95), the actual compact Letwin constant-8 theorem and cumulantBound_of_compact. The cutoff induction closes its base case, the Lemma 5.1 generator bound (lemma51Bound), the Lyapunov/boundary estimates, the induction step cutoffEnergyClaim_succ and the claim-to-compact-cumulant passage; these are proved inputs, not outstanding obligations. Supporting deterministic results include the local cumulants and CGF jets, the partition expansion (74), its grouping with (72), and the Section 6 envelope/absorption arithmetic. The shared theorem41, theorem41Compact and cumulantBound_of_letwinCompact keep their explicit LetwinCompactBound premise; cumulantBound_153 discharges it with letwinCompactBound. Relation alternative: the conclusion is obtained through cutoff diffusion and compact-to-general approximation rather than the uncut Eldan process. The uncut process and literal stochastic identities (68)–(73) remain unformalized; the KLS/Poincaré endpoint is the separate T11 certificate.

items.label: Third cumulant
items.statement: For isotropic log-concave μ: R^μ_3 ≤ 8 Id.
items.note: The mapped source-scope estimate is conditional on LetwinQuadraticBound for the given isotropic log-concave law: the exact quadratic variance bound 8 implies R_3 ≤ 8 Id in every orthonormal basis, with the exponential radius derived from log-concavity. The all-radii analytic counterpart is also available. For compactly supported isotropic log-concave laws, cumulantBoundCompact_two_of_letwinCompact with the proved letwinCompactBound supplies the exact R_3 ≤ 8 Id base used and discharged in lem:bkl-cutoff-energy. Letwin's noncompact Theorem 1.2 and the exact constant-8 Lemma 4.2 for every isotropic law are not formalized; the separately proved all-order Theorem 4.1 does not assert that exact constant. The source item therefore retains its conditional premise and partial relation.

items.label: Cumulant dynamics
items.statement: For m ≥ 3, along Eldan’s process dκ_m(t) = κ_{m+1}(t)(·, …, ·, A_t^{−1/2}dB_t) − (mκ_m(t) + L_m(t))dt.
items.note: The deterministic spatial expansion (74), grouped as 2m κ_m + 2 L_m with (72), is formalized at a fixed compactly supported law. generator_cumulant_posterior proves the corresponding generator identity 𝓛κ_m = −(mκ_m + L_m) for compactly supported isotropic priors. The finite-horizon cutoff route consumes this identity through Dynkin's formula and closes the certified cutoff (95). The source's uncut process, the Itô differential of (71), the stochastic integral term κ_{m+1}(t)(·,…,·,A_t^{−1/2} dB_t), and hence the literal stochastic differential (73) are not formalized. The item remains a partial generator/cutoff counterpart.

items.locator: Equations (72) and (74), pp. 20–21 (spatial step of the proof of Lemma 4.3)
items.label: Grouped drift expansion
items.statement: For m ≥ 3 and the compactly supported law at time t with invertible covariance A_t, ∇^m⟨v_t, A_t⁻¹ v_t⟩(0)[h] = Σ_{∅≠J⊊[m]} ⟨κ_{|J|+1}(h_J,·), A_t⁻¹ κ_{m−|J|+1}(h_{Jᶜ},·)⟩ (74), and grouping the 2m summands with |J| ∈ {1, m−1} (each equal to κ_m(h)) and the complementary pairs gives 2m κ_m(h) + 2 L_m(h), where (72) defines L_m(h) as the sum over J ∋ 1 with 2 ≤ |J| ≤ m − 2.
items.note: Reviewed stronger form at a fixed law (Stage 1, Astra v5 grouped proof with the Astra v6 ordered-mask partition, independently accepted 2026-10-10): every compactly supported probability law with invertible covariance, every m ≥ 3, repeated directions allowed, and ANY representative slot i₀ (the source keeps the representative containing 1); the raw (74) holds for any continuous linear M. Deterministic only: the stochastic differential (73) is Lemma 4.3.

items.label: Drift inequality
items.statement: For m ≥ 3 the drift of E_m(t) = |κ_m(t)(u)|²_t satisfies E_m ≥ ½E_{m+1} − Cm²E_m − 2⟨κ_m(u), L_m(u)⟩_t.
items.note: Generator form (Claude-controller batch 12, 2026-10-13; the cutoff-only route replaces the Itô drift by the generator of the posterior parameter diffusion): generator_cumulantEnergy_ge proves, for every compactly supported isotropic log-concave prior, r ≥ 2 (m = r + 1 ≥ 3), every direction u and every parameter p = (c, Q) with Q symmetric positive semidefinite, 𝓛E_m(p) ≥ ½E_{m+1}(p) − 17(r+1)²E_m(p) − 2⟨κ_m(u), L_m(u)⟩_p, i.e. (80) with the explicit constant C = 17. It assumes CumulantBoundCompact 2 8, the compact-support form of the Lemma 4.2 bound (79); this input is proved (cumulantBoundCompact_two_of_letwinCompact with letwinCompactBound) and discharged in lem:bkl-cutoff-energy. The source lemma concerns the Itô drift along the uncut process, which is not formalized; hence partial. Supporting results: the algebraic bound drift_expression_ge (SlotAction.lean), the generator chain rule and the noise bound (NoiseBound.lean).

items.label: Integrated drift bound
items.statement: For m ≥ 3 with ∫E E_m < ∞ and ∫E|L_m(u)|²_t < ∞: the integrated bound (92).
items.note: Cutoff form only (Claude-controller batch 11, 2026-10-13; the cutoff-only route replaces the paper's stopping-time integrability assumptions): along a ball-cutoff Eldan process, Dynkin's identity for the C^∞ posterior cumulant energy E_m and Cauchy–Schwarz give the integrated bound (92)–(93) with weights γ_R², under two explicit hypotheses: the drift inequality (80) of Lemma 5.1 (h51) and the Section 6 bound (104) (hL, the statement of sqrt_lowerDrift_energy_le). Both hypotheses are discharged in the certified cutoff form of (95) (lem:bkl-cutoff-energy: h51 by generator_cumulantEnergy_ge, (104) inside the induction step). The source lemma concerns the uncut process on the infinite horizon under its integrability assumptions, which is not formalized, so the entry stays partial.

items.label: Cumulant energy induction
items.statement: For every compactly supported isotropic log-concave μ on Rⁿ and every unit vector u, E_m(0) + ½∫₀^∞ E E_{m+1}(t) dt ≤ b_m = K^{m−1}((m−1)!)² for m ≥ 3, along Eldan’s process; the induction starts at m = 2 from (78).
items.note: Finite-horizon cutoff form, certified (lem:bkl-cutoff-energy, solutions/LemBklCutoffEnergy.lean, 2026-10-17). For every d ≥ 1 (m = d + 1), every dimension, every compactly supported isotropic log-concave prior, unit u, ε > 0 and T ≥ 0, there is R₀ such that for every R ≥ R₀ and every actual cutoff Eldan process (the strong solution of (67) with ball-cutoff coefficients on any Brownian setup with a usual filtration), E_{d+1}(0) + ½ ∫∫₀ᵀ γ_R² E_{d+2} ≤ (d!)² 153^d + ε. The proof uses the actual compact constant-8 theorem letwinCompactBound and no assumed inequality, induction step, Lyapunov estimate or process existence. Kept from the source: the factor ½, the normalization b_m of (94), a universal K (= 153) and every dimension. Different: a finite horizon with a tolerance ε and all sufficiently large cutoff radii instead of ∫₀^∞, the cutoff weight γ_R² inside the integral, the cutoff process instead of the uncut Eldan process, and the order range including m = 2. The uncut process (strong solution, uniqueness, non-explosion) and the literal stochastic identities (68)–(73) are not formalized, so the relation is partial; Theorem 4.1 is item T41.

items.label: Suspension
items.statement: For d ≥ 2: if R^ν_{d+1} ≤ b Id for every isotropic log-concave ν in every dimension, then every isotropic regular log-concave μ has |T_d f|² ≤ 2b/(d!)²‖f‖² for all f ∈ L²(μ).
items.note: Formalized in the source form and certified (prop:bkl-suspension, solutions/PropBklSuspension.lean): d ≥ 2, b > 0 and the paper's universal hypothesis CumulantBound d b give |T_d f|² ≤ 2b/(d!)² ‖f‖² for every L² function of every isotropic regular log-concave law in every dimension. The assembly (107) is norm_coordTensor_taylorTensor_sq_le_two_mul. Its proof includes the Laplace noise, the suspension law with density (109), log-concavity under (110), exponential integrability, local log-Laplace smoothness, isotropy from (108), (111)–(112), the Hilbert–Schmidt step, β → ∞ and (113) for smooth normalized functions. Continuity and linearity of T_d on L², the density extension to the affine-orthogonal class, the linear-function cumulant identity and the affine decomposition complete (107) with the exact factor 2. The universal cumulant hypothesis is part of Proposition 7.1 itself, not a remaining proof gap; the separately certified Theorem 4.1 supplies it in the final KLS assembly.

items.label: Regular log-concave measures
items.statement: μ is regular if its density is e^{−V}, V smooth with every partial derivative of polynomial growth and a Id ≤ ∇²V ≤ b Id with a, b > 0; the paper reduces Theorem 1.1 to regular μ by approximation.
items.note: Same (Codex reviews RE and final): RegularPotential V a b records only the assumptions of (12) (HasTemperateGrowth, 0 < a, a‖v‖² ≤ ∇²V(v,v) ≤ b‖v‖²) on any finite-dimensional real inner product space (the source's b > 0 follows in positive dimension; in dimension 0 any b is allowed); derived in Lean: strong convexity, Gaussian domination of e^{−V}, integrability and positive normalizer, the probability law volume.tilted(−V), all exponential moments, polynomial growth of ∇V, log-concavity and full support; the scalar/tensor (48)–(50), (15), (16) with curvature a, and the operator-domain Lemma 2.1 with C = 1/a then hold with every analytic premise discharged. Regular approximation (p. 5), formalized state as of 2026-10-08: (i) Gaussian smoothing of a law with a Borell density is a producer of regular potentials V_s + δ/2‖·‖² with δ·Id ≤ ∇² ≤ (2s+δ)·Id (upper Hessian through the Gaussian posterior, polynomial growth of all derivatives through uniform quantitative Borell moments of the centered posterior), whose law is the two-step law and is log-concave; (ii) the smoothed laws have covariance Cov μ + Id/(2s) and converge to μ weakly and in mean, second moment and covariance; the quadratic tilts have covariances converging to Cov μ; (iii) the joint Gaussian-then-quadratic approximation: along a selected diagonal, the laws of the produced regular potentials converge weakly to μ with means, raw second moments and covariance operators converging; (iv) the regular class is stable under affine maps and isometries, every regular law centers and whitens to an isotropic regular law, and a Poincaré bound for isotropic regular laws on ℝⁿ transfers to every finite-dimensional space; (v) conditional transfer: a universal bound K for isotropic regular laws gives C_P ≤ K‖Cov‖ for every regular law; (vi) the weak-limit transfer of a Poincaré bound with converging constants to the literature constant of a log-concave limit. (vii) the final passage: a bound for isotropic regular laws on ℝⁿ (n > 0) implies the bound for every isotropic log-concave law in every finite-dimensional space (KLS.LogConcave.isotropicBound_of_euclidean_regular_isotropic_bound), so the Section 2 reduction of Theorem 1.1 to isotropic regular laws is complete. The whitened-sequence convergence is not needed and not claimed. Theorem 1.1 itself is certified separately (T11, thm:bkl-poincare); its regular case uses Theorem 4.1.

items.label: Tilts, tilt averages and Taylor tensors
items.statement: μ_z has density e^{⟨x,z⟩ − Λ_μ(z)}, F_f(z) = ∫ f dμ_z and T_d f = (1/d!)∇^dF_f(0).
items.note: expTilt μ z = μ.tilted ⟨z, ·⟩ is the source density when 0 < ∫e^{⟨z,x⟩}dμ < ∞; taylorTensor is the continuous multilinear map (1/d!)∇^dF_f(0), whose default operator norm is not the source Hilbert–Schmidt norm. Smoothness of F_f is proved for every f ∈ L²(μ) under all exponential moments (Tilt/SquareIntegrable.lean), with ∇^d of the Laplace-type integral given by weighted moments. In an orthonormal basis the coefficient array of T_d f (coordTensor, Analysis/Tensor/Coefficients.lean) is a symmetric element of Coord n d with the Hilbert–Schmidt norm, which bounds the operator norm (norm_le_norm_coordTensor); symmetrizeML is S_d of the array.

items.label: Integration by parts on 𝒜
items.statement: For u, v ∈ 𝒜: ∫(Lu)v dμ = −∫⟨∇u, ∇v⟩ dμ = ∫u(Lv) dμ.
items.note: Formalized in a reviewed stronger form (Codex review 4) for scalar u, v and for tensor fields (values in a finite-dimensional real inner product space, ⟨∇u, ∇v⟩ = Σ_i ⟨Du(e_i), Dv(e_i)⟩) of temperate growth, μ = m.tilted(−V) with V ∈ C¹, ∇V of polynomial growth and all exponential moments (the source assumes μ regular; the implication is reviewed, not a Lean adapter).

items.label: Integrated Bochner formula on 𝒜
items.statement: For u ∈ 𝒜: ∫(Lu)² dμ = ∫‖∇²u‖²_HS dμ + ∫⟨∇²V ∇u, ∇u⟩ dμ.
items.note: Formalized in a reviewed stronger form (Codex review 4): proved for scalar u of temperate growth and μ = m.tilted(−V) with V of temperate growth and all exponential moments (convexity and the Hessian bounds of a regular measure are not needed), together with the curvature form ∫‖∇²u‖²_HS + ρ∫‖∇u‖² ≤ ∫(Lu)² under ∇²V ≥ ρ used in Lemma 3.4; ‖∇²u‖²_HS is written in the standard orthonormal basis (hessianSqStdBasis). Tensor fields: ∫‖ℒu‖² = ∫Σ_{i,j}‖∇²u(e_i,e_j)‖² + ∫Σ_{i,j}∇²V(e_i,e_j)⟨Du(e_i), Du(e_j)⟩ and the tensor curvature form are proved (TensorBochner.lean). On the generator domain D(A) of the heat model (U of temperate growth, all exponential moments): the weak first derivatives lie in D(T̄), the weak Hessian is symmetric and Σ_i‖T̄∂_iF‖² + ρ‖T̄F‖² ≤ ‖AF‖² under ∇²U ≥ ρ (operator route of 2026-10-07; the identity form of (16) on D(A) is not stated).

items.label: Tilted generator identity
items.statement: F_{−Lu}(z) = ⟨z, F_{∇u}(z)⟩ for every z.
items.note: Formalized in a reviewed stronger form (Codex review 4): for scalar and tensor-valued u ∈ 𝒜 (vector form F_{−ℒu}(z) = F_{Du}(z) z, ℒu = Δu − Du(∇V)), μ = m.tilted(−V) with V ∈ C¹, ∇V of polynomial growth and all exponential moments (the source assumes μ regular; that implication is reviewed, not a Lean adapter), by integration by parts under each tilt with a scaled bump cutoff and dominated convergence; also for compactly supported C² scalar u. Also for every F ∈ D(A) in the heat model, as an identity of L² classes (tiltAverage_adjointComp_eq, operator route of 2026-10-07).

items.locator: Equation (67), p. 19 (unnumbered display) and the compact stage before it
items.label: Localization posterior and its parameter dependence
items.statement: μ_t has density proportional to e^{⟨c_t,x⟩ − ½⟨Q_t x,x⟩} dμ with (c_0,Q_0) = (0,0); the parameters evolve by dc = A⁻¹a dt + A^{-1/2} dB, dQ = A⁻¹ dt.
items.note: The mapped results supply deterministic posterior calculus and the cutoff process used by the accepted BKL route. For compactly supported priors, every finite parameter pair (c,Q), including Q = 0 and signed Q, gives a probability posterior with bounded norm moments, the same null sets, support and affine support, and smooth joint parameter dependence. A separate coercive-Q calculus handles polynomial statistics of arbitrary probability priors. For compact isotropic priors, posterior covariance is positive and invertible at every finite pair, its inverse and drift are smooth, and its principal inverse square root is positive self-adjoint, locally Lipschitz, basis independent and satisfies σ² = Cov⁻¹ and σ Cov σ = Id. The actual transported-law standardization is proved by Isotropic.exists_inverseSqrt_equiv_isotropic_standardized (KLS/BKL/Posterior/Standardization.lean): the same principal root transports the centered posterior to an isotropic law. For log-concave priors and symmetric PSD Q, posterior log-concavity and the stated explicit dimension-dependent standardized sixth-moment bound are proved; log-concavity is not claimed for negative Q. The posterior-expectation generator cancels at the source inverse-covariance rate. Covariance Cauchy–Schwarz, whitening variance, trace/third-moment bounds, the uniform posterior covariance-radius bound, the bounded-test noise estimate and the deterministic standardized entry identity behind (69) are also proved; they do not assert the literal stochastic covariance equation. For the cutoff equation, globally Lipschitz bounded coefficients, a strong solution on every Brownian setup with a usual filtration (exists_isEldanCutoff), Dynkin's identity for C² functionals (IsEldanCutoff.dynkin), Q positive semidefinite along the path (IsEldanCutoff.ae_Q_posSemidef), and the cumulant-energy/generator estimates used in cutoff (95) are formalized. These results use the vendored stochastic calculus and feed the certified lem:bkl-cutoff-energy. What remains unformalized is the uncut Eldan construction (strong solution, uniqueness and non-explosion), its literal stochastic identities (68)–(71), their uncut stochastic-integral and martingale conclusions, and any claimed rotation of the Brownian driver in (75)–(77). The cutoff results do not assert those uncut statements.
